what: Computes the minimum spell-charge cost for a spell opening at its initial spell level, using the formula ceil(ratio × SL² × 1.9 / (SL + 1)) × 2 − 1.
ev: It computes a spell's charge cost through the same 1.9 price arithmetic (Rules.Fn1485Price) and applies a guild-level floor, but it uses the current spell level and a floored integer product, not the C++ ceil(ratio × SL_init² × 1.9 / (SL_init + 1)) × 2 − 1 formula.

what: Decides whether the owner may choose a body to carry, allowing it only when the carry slot is empty or holds a companion (slot index below kCompanionSlots), and refusing when a morgue body is held.
ev: Its opening guard `who.CarryingCompanion < four && who.CarryingCharacter == ""` repeats the C++ slot-below-kCompanionSlots test, but it is embedded in a routine that picks and assigns a companion to carry and returns message lines, not a standalone bool predicate, and it also checks for a carried character.

what: Converts the legacy boolean "Identified" save flag into an identification level, mapping true to fully identified (All) and false to Unknown, per the SRD's c32 section.
ev: No candidate converts a bool to an IdLevel (true to All, false to Unknown); the closest, CityWindow's IdLevelName, maps an int to a display name, and the others either take an IdLevel as input or compare against All.

what: Returns the highest per-category spell maximum across a guild's spell-max table, which sets the guild's overall spell ceiling for the game's casting rules.
ev: No candidate returns the maximum of a guild's per-category SpellMax values; the closest, Rules.BestGuildAD, takes the highest guild attack and defense across memberships, and the spell-related candidates test individual categories or levels rather than taking a maximum over the table.

what: Handles the player's roster command by building a description of the current party and appending a "Not in party" line for each character left behind, returning the combined text as the reply.
ev: No candidate builds a party description, appends "Not in party" lines, or returns that text as a reply; the nearest, LookAround.cs `order.Roster`, merges saved and in-memory party records into an ordered list but produces no reply text and does not isolate the characters left behind.

what: Converts a companion's alignment value to the game's Align type by subtracting one from its enum index, the inverse of itemAlignOf.
ev: No candidate maps a companion alignment to a game alignment by subtracting one from its enum index; the closest, OriginalSaves.cs `SlotFrom`, casts a saved alignment integer straight to `ItemAlignment` with no offset, and it works on items, not companions.

what: Tests whether a body's dungeon level is deeper than kFetchMaxDungeonLevel, returning true when it is within reach for the fetch spell.
ev: No candidate tests a body's dungeon level against kFetchMaxDungeonLevel; the closest, CastHere's fetch filter, requires the body to be on the leader's level, and Outcome.ForSpell compares a teleport level to MaxDungeonLevel but returns a fall or rock outcome, not a fetch reach result.

what: Returns the monster spell band for a monster, which is assumed to run from level 1 up to the monster's found level (minimum 1), since the real band rule is not in this SRD part.
ev: ChooseSpell derives a spell-level window from the monster's LevelFound (low = two thirds of LevelFound, top = LevelFound + 1, filtered by school), which is related to the C++ band (low 1, top = max(levelFound, 1)) but uses different bounds and also picks a spell, so it does not match the function's output.

what: Computes a character's Protect ailment level from their guild level as half the guild level, rounded down by truncation, plus one.
ev: Recompute sets `c.Protection = c.Guild.Level / 2 + 1` when the Protect bit is set, which is the same guild-level-halved-plus-one rule as the C++ function (integer division truncates like `Int()` for non-negative levels), though it is inline in a larger method rather than a standalone helper.

what: Rolls a drift check for a companion by comparing a random draw scaled by 200 against the given drift value, returning true when the drift threshold is met.
where: Mordor.Core/CompanionMood.cs CompanionMood.Step.Round (Candidate 3, with Step.Drift as its drift-threshold helper)
ev: Candidate 3 contains the same `rng.NextDouble() * 200 < Drift(...)` comparison that the C++ `driftCheck` performs, but it is embedded in a larger routine that also applies the binding change, builds messages, and rolls a leave check, so it is not a standalone drift check; no candidate is a standalone function that just returns `NextDouble() * 200 < drift`.

what: Clears the standing combat order for a party member when a fight ends, leaving that member's CombatSetting unchanged.
ev: Both reset the member's standing order to none and leave the Combat Setting alone, since `Clear()` only touches the order object and `CombatSetting` lives on `Character`; the C++ takes a member index while `Clear()` is called per member, a small structural difference.

what: Thief-style theft: takes a roll-determined amount of the victim's on-hand gold, leaves the remainder floored at zero, and posts a "Gold was stolen" message to the player.
ev: GoldToSteal computes the same take (the roll, or the whole purse when the roll is larger), but it does not debit the victim's gold, floor the remainder at zero, or post the "Gold was stolen" message, so only part of thiefRobs is covered.

what: Returns the archive HP gained when a character reaches a given level in a guild: Warriors get a flat average per level up to level 28, Nomads get a bonus at levels 29 and up (with a post-cap amount past their max level), and Wizards get a post-target amount past their target level, with other cases yielding 0.
ev: Both return the hits gained on reaching a level in a guild, using the guild's flat per-level amount below its cap and a fixed amount past it, but LevelUp adds random rolls, a constitution bonus, and a rule that another guild's standing suppresses the gain, none of which the C++ lookup has.

what: Resolves which monster a chest's lead monster counts as when it is taken by another monster: -2 if the lead is mistaken for another monster, 389 (Shadow Ninja) becomes 307 (Ninja) for a taker with See Invisible, and otherwise the lead's own id is kept.
ev: It shares the -2 "unknown monster" branch and the invisibility check against the taker's See Invisible, but it returns -2 for an invisible lead the taker cannot see, whereas the C++ returns the lead's id (389) in that case and maps 389 to 307 only for a see-invisible taker, and it has no 389→307 mapping at all.

what: Picks the creature the party's attention falls on for R97 "LeadGroup": the first monster if any monsters are in combat (returning null if none are alive), otherwise the first waiting creature, or null if there is none.
ev: No candidate picks the R97 lead creature (first monster if any are alive, otherwise first waiting creature); the closest, `DungeonWindow.ShowChest`'s `ChestLead` and `RefreshCombat`'s aimed-group logic, pick for different purposes.

what: When a character loses levels, it reports the event and the number of levels lost, but does not change hit points because the per-level AH hit amounts are not modelled.
ev: Both handle losing levels and removing the hits those levels gave, but ForfeitQuest actually subtracts MaxHits per lost level (using AvgHits/LateHits and a random slice), whereas the C++ stub only emits an event and leaves hit points unchanged because the per-level amounts are unmodelled.

what: Returns the on/off display text for one of the twelve game option checkboxes, reading its stored "1" or "0" value from the session and mapping it to "on" or "off".
ev: The C++ function maps a stored "1"/"0" game option flag to "on"/"off" display text, and none of the eight candidates reads a boolean setting or produces on/off text (the closest, DpsMeterMod.Draw.View and Kaizen's RowDrag.Build, deal with mod UI, not game option checkboxes).

what: Enforces the engine's minimum cost by returning the greater of the computed cost and the minimum, so a spell or action never costs less than the floor.
ev: No candidate raises a cost to a minimum floor; the closest, `OptionsWindow.Volume`, uses `Math.Clamp` on a slider value to both 0 and 100, and `WindowLayout.Minimum` sets a minimum window size, not a cost.

what: Rolls a d100 against the monster's computed hit chance (from its attack and the character's defense) and returns whether the monster's attack hits.
ev: HitThreshold computes the same monster-versus-defence hit chance that the C++ roll is compared against, but it is a related version rather than an exact match: its hit test is written as a miss when the roll is at or above the threshold (so a hit is roll < threshold, where the C++ accepts roll <= chance), its 2..98 clamp and formula may differ from the C++ `monsterHitChance`, and the C++ roll function itself (`monsterHitRoll`) is not in the candidates.

what: Sets a character's death state, zeroes their current hit points, and increments their death count, without producing any message for the player.
ev: SetDead zeroes hits and increments Deaths like the C++ function, but it hardcodes the death state to ordinary instead of taking it as a parameter, and it also logs the death and plays the DIE sound, which the C++ function does not do.

what: Counts how many monsters in the encounter still have hit points above zero, i.e. the foes still alive in the fight.
ev: Capture counts each group's standing members with `list.Where(m => m.Group == g && m.Alive).Count()` and stores that as GroupCount, which is part of what the C++ does, but it works per group inside a larger room-record update and never returns a total of living foes across the encounter.

what: Computes the gold dropped when a slime is killed, as a random amount scaled by dungeon level, the monster's attack and level, and the guild level (divided by the guild level, floored at 1).
ev: The closest candidate, Combat.cs FillGroup, also awards gold from a monster group but uses the monster's GoldFactor and LevelFound with a log-scaled random term, not the slime formula's dungeon-level, attack, level and guild-level scaling, and no candidate computes the slime formula.

what: Computes the attack-versus-defence term for melee combat, Int((Def - Att)/2) divided by 4 with truncation toward zero, as specified by rule R19 of the Mordor SRD.
ev: Fn0DEE computes the same term, `Floor(((def - atk) / 2.0) / 4.0)`, which equals the C++ nested Int for integer inputs, but only as one step inside the larger damage function, not as a standalone attack-versus-defence term.

what: Recounts how many creatures in monster group gi still have hit points above zero and stores that as the group's livingCount, which the combat rules use to track surviving monsters.
ev: Its local `Alive(int g)` counts the living members of group index `g`, which is part of what recountGroup does, but it is a lambda inside a spell routine and never stores the result as a group livingCount; RefreshCombat's per-group `Count(m => m.Alive)` is similar but display-only.

what: Rolls a rescue check by drawing a random number and returning true if it falls under the given percentage chance.
ev: It uses the same `rng.NextDouble() * 100` percentage roll compared against a threshold, but it returns true when the roll is above `level * 4` (the complement of the C++ `< chance` test) and derives the threshold from level rather than taking it as a parameter.

what: Grants a crest its spell, if the crest has one in the table, by returning that spell with its charges and the caster's current spell level, and posts a "Crest grants a spell" message.
ev: No candidate maps a crest to its granted spell, charges, and the caster's spell level; Guildmasters.AwardCrest and CrestFor only award or find the crest item, and Castables.Castables lists spells from pack items without granting one.

what: Depth Perception (SpellEffect 12) announces to the party the dungeon level they are currently standing on, as the spell's applied effect.
ev: No visible candidate announces the party's dungeon level as a Depth Perception effect; `DungeonState.NoteDepth` only records the deepest level reached, and `IsUtility` merely lists DepthPerception as a category, while `box.CastHere` (the likely home of that case) is cut off before any depth branch.

what: Registers the "look" typed command on the Dungeon screen, binding it to the cmdLook handler so the player can describe the square they stand on.
ev: The C++ function only registers a typed "look" command on the Dungeon screen; no candidate registers or dispatches a command, and the nearest one (DungeonWindow.Mdi.cs RefreshAreaLook) lists the characters on the party's square for the F2 Area List rather than describing the square.

what: Rolls a number of drain trials (scaled by the attacker's level), lets each trial be resisted by the target's drain resistance or Constitution-based save, and collects Table E drain picks for each trial that fails.
where: Mordor.Core/MonsterAttack.cs CombatEngine.GroupAttacks (closest, but it only lists drain as one step in a monster group's turn)
ev: None of the candidates performs the drain trials, the target's drain-resistance and Constitution-save checks, or the Table E pick draws; GroupAttacks only names drain in its doc comment and its drain code is not shown.

what: When a won combat round's display ends, it clears the fight's standing orders, marks the round as no longer in progress, and reports each key the player pressed during the hold so the host can replay them in order.
ev: EndCombat clears the party's orders and ends the won fight, like the C++ endFight call, but it does not replay the queued keys or clear the queue (that is in DungeonWindow.HoldUntil), and it adds spoils, room stamping and boss handling the C++ function does not show.

what: Decides whether the alignment-choice prompt is shown during the seer's (T-L) fee/gate flow, asking only when more than one alignment is stocked, which is a placeholder guess for an unstated original condition.
ev: `Asks => Stocked > 1` is the same condition as the C++ `stockedAlignmentCount > 1`, though `Offer` also carries the enabled-button and chosen-alignment logic that the C++ function does not.

what: Lets a character who has already joined a guild make it their active guild again, failing if the guild ID is invalid or the character has not joined it.
ev: Both find an already-joined guild and make it the active one, returning false when the character hasn't joined it; they differ only in taking a guild name instead of an index, with no ID validation and no "reacquainted" message.

what: Reports whether the dungeon is a shareware/limited build by comparing the dungeon level count against the full game's level count (kFullDungeonLevelCount).
ev: The C++ function compares a dungeon level count against kFullDungeonLevelCount to flag a limited build, while the closest candidate, LimitedVersion.Clamp (Mordor.Core/LimitedVersion.cs), only clamps a requested level against the limited build's last level and does not report whether the build is limited.

what: Charges a gold amount to the character, drawing from gold on hand first and then from the bank, and fails without charging if the character's total purse cannot cover it.
ev: Pay charges the cost from gold on hand first and then the bank, and returns false without charging when the purse can't cover it, matching chargeGold for positive amounts, but it differs for negative amounts (Pay adds gold to the hand where chargeGold returns true and changes nothing), it rounds the bank's part to a whole number, and it refuses on overflow.

what: Covers a party shortfall by drawing gold from the other members' bank accounts in member order (skipping the payer, capped at the party size), and returns how much was actually covered.
ev: It draws the shortfall from the other members' bank accounts in party order, skipping the payer, as the C++ does, but it credits the payer's gold on hand, skips dead or dungeon-level members, and is all-or-nothing (null when not fully covered) instead of returning the partial amount covered.

what: Reports whether the guild log has grown past its cleaning threshold, which is fifty entries per guild across the whole log (with at least one guild counted).
ev: It returns `All(savesDir).Count > KeepOnClean * Math.Max(1, guildCount)`, which matches the C++ logic of counting the whole log against fifty per guild with at least one guild, assuming `KeepOnClean` is fifty.

what: Compares a breather's power against a target's power and returns +1 if the breather is much stronger (more than 5/4 of the target), -1 if much weaker (less than 3/4 of the target), or 0 if the two are in between, for the breath relation rule [c28].
ev: It applies the same "much stronger or much weaker by a quarter" comparison, but on guild levels to pick a 80/20/50 firing chance rather than on power to return a +1/0/-1 relation.

what: Returns true when the dungeon level falls within the range 12 to 15 (inclusive), the only levels where the mythical Pariah monster can spawn.
ev: No candidate checks whether a dungeon level falls in the Pariah's 12-15 spawn range; the nearest, Outcome.ForSpell (Teleporting.cs), bounds-checks a level against the dungeon's depth for a teleport, which is a different purpose.

what: Decides whether the R62 look-ahead perception feature is active, returning true only when the NoPerceptionMessages option is off and the character is not lost.
where: Mordor.App/DungeonWindow.axaml.cs, DungeonWindow.LookAheadLines (the containing class is inferred from the file name)
ev: Its first two lines are the same gate as the C++ function (return nothing if NoPerceptionMessages is set or the character is lost), but the method then goes on to run the perception roll, write to the automap, and return the lines, so it does more than the C++ predicate, which only returns a bool.

what: Returns a character's alignment as an integer, which the item-use code reads when checking whether an item's alignment restriction applies to that character.
ev: No candidate returns a character's alignment as an integer for an item-use check; the alignment-related candidates either read the item's alignment flags (Possible, RollAlignment, AddOne, SlotFrom), use alignment for monster engagement (EngageChance) or guild eligibility (RefreshGuilds), or handle monster penning (Count, Key).

what: Loads a saved game session from text, validating the format version and end marker, then replaces the session's game state with the loaded state while leaving the data tables and RNG untouched.
ev: No candidate loads a saved game session, validates a format version and end marker, or replaces game state while keeping data tables and RNG; the closest, Mordor.Mod.Cartographer/MapNotes.cs WaypointShape.Load, loads JSON map notes with error recovery but does not do the same job.

what: Decides whether a dead character's body counts as lying in the city for the party's purposes: it must be dead, not the viewing character, on dungeon level 0, and not being carried by any party member.
ev: The candidate applies the same four tests as isBodyInCity (dead, not the viewing character, DungeonLevel == 0, and not carried by any party member) as a LINQ filter over all saved characters, rather than as a per-body predicate.

what: For each mod root, it sorts the subfolders case-insensitively by name and emits a "mod.discovered" event for each folder that contains a mod.json, leaving the actual reading and loading of mods to the host.
ev: Discover does the same case-insensitive ordering of each root's subfolders and the same check for mod.json, but it also reads the manifest, rejects duplicate ids and records the result, which the C++ leaves to the host and reports only as a "mod.discovered" event.

what: Returns the race experience multiplier (R14 T1) for a given raw Exp value, using the tabulated values for 4 through 9, 1.0 for 3 or less, and an approximation for anything higher.
ev: No candidate maps a raw Exp value to a race multiplier; the closest, MdrLoader.LoadRaces, only loads each race's stored ExpFactor, and the Fn12A1/Fn13ED/ExpAwarded candidates compute experience thresholds and awards, not this multiplier.

what: Lowercases a single ASCII uppercase letter (A–Z) to its lowercase form for the case-insensitive name matching used when the seer looks for a person by the start of their name, following the original BASIC routine.
ev: Match does the case-insensitive start-of-name comparison that seerLower exists to support, using `StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase` rather than a per-character ASCII lowercase helper, so it is a related version and no candidate lowercases a single character.

what: Computes the percentage chance of a monster's breath attack succeeding by comparing the top guild level against the monster's level, giving 50% by default, 80% if the guild is more than a quarter stronger than the monster, and 20% if it is more than a quarter weaker.
ev: Its breath block sets chance to 50, raises it to 80 if the top guild level exceeds monLvl + monLvl/4.0, then lowers it to 20 if the top level is below monLvl - monLvl/4.0, in the same order as the C++ function, but it is inlined in a larger method rather than being a standalone helper.

what: Looks up the guild name for a character's active guild from the loaded game data, returning an empty string if the guild index is out of range.
ev: No candidate maps the active guild (by index) to its display name; the closest, GuildData.ByName in Mordor.Core/GuildData.cs, goes the opposite way (name to definition) and throws on a miss instead of returning an empty string.

what: Returns how many days a character's age advances when raised from the dead after a failed raise, at 84 days for stoned, 124 for rock, and 54 otherwise.
ev: Both map a stoned death to a stoned age constant, a rock death to a rock constant, and everything else to the ordinary constant, differing only in taking an int cause-of-death instead of a DeathState enum.

what: Resets a chest's trap state to "not trapped" at the start of each chest generation pass, while leaving the lock untouched, per the game's chest-generation rules.
where: Mordor.Core/Combat.cs Fight.TrapSprung (the method's name and summary are not given in the candidate text; `TrapSprung` is the name shown)
ev: TrapSprung does the same state change as the C++ function (`ChestTrap = 0` and the lock is left alone), but it runs when a trap goes off rather than at the start of each chest generation pass, and no candidate clears the trap on generation.

what: Caps the number of hits a purchased companion gets at the definition's maximum, returning the lower of the rolled hits and the definition's hits.
ev: No candidate caps a companion's hits at the definition's maximum; the nearest, Combat.cs carries.AcceptJoin, takes the front monster's rolled hits and maximum uncapped, and the other candidates also assign hits without any min() against the definition.

what: Computes the proc threshold for a monster's special effect by taking the attacker's guild level and the owner's guild level, plus the monster's levelFound, and clamping the result to the spec's lo/hi bounds (rule R31).
ev: It computes the same expression, 100·ln(1+attacker/k)·ln(floor+1) − 100·ln(1+defender/999), clamped to lo/hi, with the same inputs; the only difference is that k and the clamp bounds are hardcoded per backstab flag rather than passed in a ProcSpec.

what: Opening a spell list in Mordor sets the character's Att value for the active guild to zero, then runs the cast check, which turns Fight and Defend into None while keeping any queued spell.
ev: It sets Att to False as the first step of mdrcharCheckCast, turns Fight and Defend into None, and keeps a queued spell, which matches the C++ `Att = 0` followed by `checkCast`, though the candidate omits the rest of the check's tests and the C++ call site lives in SpellListChecked (candidate 3).

what: Returns how many party-record slots are available for the roster, computed as the smallest of the party member count, inventory count, and companion count.
ev: No candidate computes the minimum of the party member, inventory, and companion counts as a slot capacity; the closest, `RoomRoster.Strangers` and `LookAround.Roster`, deal with counting bystanders and ordering the roster, not capacity.

what: Handles a click on a store buy row in the Mordor town store by applying the same alignment choice rule (R11) to that row's shelf counts.
ev: ClickRow applies the same alignment rule (`AlignmentChoice.For` over the row's per-alignment stock, then `offer.Chosen(chosenAlign)`), but it is a monster-pen UI click handler (FRMCITYC) that also enables buttons and awaits a frame pick, not the store-buy shelf function that returns just the choice.

what: Classifies a spell as Either (usable in and out of combat) for Teleport and Remove Paralysis, NonCombat for spells with zero Damage2 or a local Heal category, and Combat otherwise.
ev: UseOf returns Either for Teleport or CureParalysis, NonCombat when Damage2 is 0 or the category is the heal school, and Combat otherwise, which matches the C++ branch order exactly (assuming HealSchool corresponds to kCategoryHealLocal).

what: Quotes a character's revival price, works out whether the guild pays for it, and flags whether the payer must be asked, based on the character's top guild level.
ev: No candidate computes a revival fee, decides whether the guild pays, or flags that the payer must be asked based on top guild level; the closest, CityWindow.ShowDead, is a dead-character screen that offers Hire Rescuers and never prices a revival, and Candidates 1 and 2 are truncated in the provided text, so their remaining bodies were not visible.

what: Returns the spell level at which an item's magical spell is cast, computed from the item's level and the user's spell level via casting3's itemSpellLevel formula.
ev: Both return the item's own spell level when it is positive and otherwise the caster's spell level, but the C++ takes a stored `user.spellLevel` field and its casting3 formula isn't shown, while CastLevel derives the fallback from `Rules.SpellLevel(c.Guild.Level)`.

what: Removes every stored mod setting matching a given mod id and key, and marks the store as dirty only if something was actually removed.
ev: This candidate removes a single (mod id, key) setting from the store and only writes/notifies when the key exists, which matches the C++ core, but it differs in that it removes one key rather than filtering a list, and it also writes to disk and raises a Changed event, which the C++ function does not do.

what: Reports a wall collision by showing an "OUCH" message through the context's say hook, with no game-text body, as a plugin-style output hook.
ev: StepForward's else branch plays `Audio.Play("OUCH")` with no text when a move hits a wall, which matches reportWallHit's behavior, but StepForward also handles the successful move, map recording, and label updates, so it is a larger function that contains the same wall-bump output.

what: Applies a chest trap's hit damage (R4) to a character by replacing their current hit points with the result of hitsAfterChestTrap, which the game's rules then adjust (R5).
ev: Spring's cases 3 and 4 apply the chest's hit damage to `c.CurHits` with the same round-half-to-even step the C++ R5 adjustment describes, but they sit inside a larger function that also computes the damage, handles poison, disease, and teleport, and takes no separate damage input.

what: Recalculates a Mordor item's identification level when it is passed by exchange (not drag and drop), using the recipient's INT, WIS and top guild level as a placeholder skill against a reference item's level, then caps the result.
ev: It reproduces the same quirk, storing the identification level of the item named by LevelScale rather than the held item, but it uses the ReadableLevel formulas instead of the C++ placeholders, keeps a guard that only raises the stored level, and has no capIdentifyLevel step.

what: Rolls whether a stoning effect lands on a target by checking the target's stone resistance and then a chance derived from the stoner's Constitution and level, following the game's documented stoning formula.
ev: No candidate implements the two-step stoning roll (resistance check, then a chance from stoner CON and level), but CompanionStrikes' doc comment describes a stone's constitution test in the companion-attack path, and the body is truncated so the test itself can't be confirmed.

what: Converts a guild parameter value into a percentage by dividing it by the guild's divisor (kGefDivisor, 8) and multiplying by 100, per the R14 rule.
ev: No candidate divides a guild parameter by 8 and multiplies by 100; the closest, Bars.Percent and DpsView.Percent, compute a clamped or rounded share of a fraction or whole with different constants and semantics, and the rest are unrelated to the guild-parameter rule.

what: Decides whether a character is eligible to join the party from the current floor and area, returning false if they are already a member, the party is empty, or they are on a different level or area; dead characters still count as eligible.
ev: It excludes current members, requires the character's dungeon level to equal the current level and their area to equal the current area (read through `savedArea`), and keeps dead characters, matching the C++ checks; the C++ `party.size <= 0` guard is absent, but it is implied by calling the method on a party, and the extra level-range check is a minor difference.

what: Computes the chance that a companion's stone succeeds, from the companion's Constitution and the level at which it was found, capped at a fixed maximum (SRD rule R30).
ev: No candidate computes a stone success chance from CON and the level found (`con * ln(max(con, floor))/ln(2.5) - levelFound`, capped at 95); the closest, `SpellEffect.CompanionRaiseChance`, uses `85 + monsterCon` capped at 98 for raising a dead companion, and the rest are different raise, paralysis, or critical formulas.

what: Charges the Seer's fee from the player's gold on hand first and then from their bank balance for any shortfall, announcing a message if the fee cannot be fully paid.
ev: Pay uses the same on-hand-then-bank order, but it is all-or-nothing (returns false and takes nothing when the purse is short) and has no "fee could not be fully paid" message, whereas chargeSeerFee takes whatever it can and reports the shortfall.

what: Each tick with no monster in front, rolls a flat 10% chance to print a "distant sound" message to the player, and returns whether it fired.
ev: It makes the same flat 10% roll when nothing is in front, but it plays one of three random sound effects instead of printing the "distant sound" text message, and it adds dead-leader and waiting-state gates the C++ does not have.

what: Decides whether a creature of body size `bodySize` can be picked up by a carrier of size `carrierSize`, returning true when the size difference is at most 1 (per rule R37.3).
ev: No candidate applies a body-size-versus-carrier-size test (`bodySize - carrierSize <= 1`); the closest, DungeonWindow.axaml.cs `PickUpBody`, handles pickup eligibility (dead, paralysed, Hide, already carried) but never compares sizes.

what: Rolls a spit-odds mishap for a companion, and if it triggers, picks a random party member other than the owner to be struck, then reports the friendly-fire event to the player.
ev: It makes the same spit-odds mishap roll, draws a party victim, and returns no victim when the draw hits the owner, but it does not emit the friendly-fire message or return the bool the C++ function does; Combat.cs CompanionRound.CompanionTurn repeats the same draw inline as one step of a larger turn.

what: Computes the gold price the store charges to buy a companion, based on the companion's base value and how many of that alignment are penned, using the engine's logarithmic price formula.
where: Mordor.Core/Confinement.cs Confinement.PriceToBuy (the class name is my inference from the file; the candidate shows only the method)
ev: It applies the same floor of 10 on base value, the same stock = min(penned - 1, cap), the same 1.5·value / (ln(stock+1) + 1.15) formula, and rounds half to even, with 0 returned when nothing is penned.

what: Adds two X87 extended-precision values, aligning their exponents and rounding the 64-bit mantissa result half-to-even, as the Mordor currency and arithmetic rules (R29) require.
ev: X87.Round does only the final step, rounding an exact m * 2^e to a 64-bit mantissa half-to-even, with no exponent alignment, addition, subtraction, carry, or sticky-bit handling, so no candidate performs the X87 addition itself.

what: Announces to the player that their character has enough experience to make a level, but only on the change where XP first crosses the level's requirement.
ev: GiveExperience has the same crossing test (announce "enough to make a level" only when the total was not enough before and is enough after, using ExpForNextLevel), but it is embedded in pin-clamping logic, and a change that also reaches the pin sets `hadEnough = true` and suppresses the announcement, which the standalone C++ function would still emit.

what: Emits a warning message to the player (via ctx.say) that stored guild Att/Def values from a save or data file are being ignored and recomputed from guild level, with the guild and stored values attached as arguments.
ev: The C++ function only emits the "Stored guild Att/Def ignored" warning via ctx.say, and no candidate emits a message or warns about stored guild values at load time; the closest candidates (Rules.GuildAD, Rules.BestGuildAD) recompute guild Att/Def from level but do not warn.

what: Maps each cast refusal reason to whether it clears the spell's item slot, per the R5 table: true for NonCombat, AntiMagic, CombatOnly, and TooLongPeaced, false otherwise.
where: Mordor.Core/CastGate.cs Refusal.ClearsItemSlot (the `ClearsItemSlot` property on the `Refusal` record)
ev: It returns true for exactly RefusalKind.NonCombat, AntiMagic, CombatOnly and TooLongPeaced and false otherwise, the same mapping as the C++ switch.

what: Resolves one monster's turn-ending attack by running the pre-attack step, then melee (skipped if the monster cast a spell), then the post-attack step, which includes electrocution for spellcasters, against a chosen party member.
ev: No candidate runs the pre-attack, melee-unless-spell, post-attack sequence against a chosen victim; the nearest, CompanionTurn, sequences a companion's breath, spit and blow, and MonsterAttacks handles group targeting, with neither having this pre/melee/post structure or the castSpell skip.

what: Rolls the R56 defection check for an opposed companion, with a percent chance of defecting if the companion is Evil (kDefectChanceEvil) or Neutral (kDefectChanceNeutral) and never defecting if Good.
ev: Outcome.Check rolls the same 75% chance for Evil and 15% for Neutral with no chance for Good, but it reads the creature's alignment rather than the companion's, and it also includes a distance rule, a forced-turn path, and a refusal check that the C++ function lacks.

what: Handles the player's pen-sell command for a companion, refusing empty or invalid slots, running the confinement sale, and producing the reply text that reports the gold received and that the slot is now empty.
ev: No candidate performs the pen sale, clears the slot, or builds the reply; CityWindow.IdEnter only previews the sell price (`pen.PriceToSell`) and CompanionSlots.Remains only keeps an empty slot's record for the save.

what: Computes the total gold needed to reach a given level by summing the gold required for each level from 1 up to that level, scaled by a gold factor, per the wiki's R16 formula.
ev: It returns only the gold for the single next level, `Rules.Fn12B2(Guild.Level, ...)`, which is roughly one term of the C++ loop; no candidate sums GoldForNextLevel over levels 1..L to produce a cumulative total, and it uses the game's fn12B2 rather than the wiki's goldNextLevelWikiL2 formula.

what: Decides whether the "Cast on Who?" target prompt applies to spell effects 0 and 18, returning true only when the caster has companions to target (per SRD c34).
ev: WhoToAsk decides whether the "Cast on Who?" prompt applies to the heal case (Damage/Cure) and gates it on `Damage2 > 0` (the original's M5B33 check) rather than on whether the caster has companions, so it does not return false when there are no companions as `needsWhoPrompt` does.

what: Decides whether a character may open a treasure chest, currently refusing only when the character is dead (per the original game's DeathState check), without the port's additional CurHits <= 0 refusal.
ev: Its first check, `if (_ch.IsDead) return;`, is the same DeathState-only test as `canOpenChest` and omits the CurHits <= 0 refusal, but the method also refuses for paralysis, a missing chest, and magic locks, and then runs the opening itself, so it does more than the C++ predicate.

what: Returns whether a companion creature turns (changes allegiance) against its owner, based on the alignment relationship between the creature and the owner, per rule R36.
ev: Its first step, `turns = Math.Abs(theirs - mine) > 1`, matches the C++ alignment-distance test, but Check then adds random Evil (75%) and Neutral (15%) turn rolls and a forced override, so its outcome differs from the C++ function's deterministic result.

what: Refuses to set default combat orders while in combat or while monsters are in the area, and otherwise fills in the party's empty combat orders with the default.
ev: ApplyDefaultOrders fills only the empty orders with the default, matching the C++ apply step, but has no refusals; the refusals appear only in DungeonWindow's OnPartyOptions (in-combat message) and HandlePartyKey's Key.O case (monsters-in-area message), and both of those then open the dialog instead of applying defaults.

what: Uncurses an equipped cursed item in the player's pack by clearing its curse flag, refusing with a message if the item is not cursed or not equipped.
ev: Refusal reproduces the two early-return checks (not cursed, then not equipped) and returns null when the uncurse should proceed, but it does not clear the slot curse flag or produce the "The curse is lifted." outcome that the C++ function does.

what: Returns the fight's gold as the victory payout, unless a chest is still left in the room, in which case the payout is zero.
ev: AwardSpoils pays the fight's gold only when `ChestClass == 0` (no chest left) and otherwise pays nothing, which is the same decision as `chestLeft ? 0 : fightGold`, though it is a void method that pays from fight state rather than returning a value.

what: Denies a teleporter square's destination when the build is limited and the destination level is deeper than the build's last level.
ev: It returns `On && z2 > LastLevel`, which is the same test as the C++ `limitedBuild && destLevel > lastLevel` and, like it, does not check level 0.

what: Rolls a random bonus of 1 to (CON − 16) hit points when a character's Constitution is above 16, and returns 0 otherwise.
ev: LevelUp contains the same CON-over-16 bonus of 1 to CON-16 (`(int)(rng.NextDouble() * (CON - 16)) + 1`), but only as one step inside a larger level-up calculation and gated by extra conditions (below the guild's hit cap and ahead of other guilds), and no candidate exposes the bonus as a standalone function.

what: Merges a legacy library record into the Morgul record, raising the grade to the higher value, adding sighting counts and death counts (capped at short.MaxValue), taking the newer place and date, and keeping the first recorder's name.
ev: Candidate 1 applies the same rules in the same order: the name is taken when Known is 0, Known rises to the higher value, NSeen and NDeaths are added (NDeaths capped at short.MaxValue), a non-empty Location and a later LastSeen replace the old ones, and Id is taken when it is 0, with MonId left alone, as in the C++ function.

what: Computes a player's chance of finding a dead body during rescue searches as max(16 − level, 0.1), adding 16 − level again when the easy-find option applies, so levels above 16 can yield a negative chance.
ev: The chance line inside DaysUntilFound uses the same 16 - level base, the same 0.1 floor applied before the easy-find addition, and the same unclamped `+= 16 - level`, but it is only one step of a larger day-by-day search loop and the function does not return the chance on its own.

what: Sells a party member's pack item to the General Store, paying the reference sell price in gold to the seller and shelving the item in the store if the store accepts it, otherwise refusing or clearing the slot as appropriate.
ev: SellPrice computes the same reference sell payout that doSell's sellQuote pays, and ShelvesSale matches the shelving test, but no single candidate pays the seller, clears the pack slot, and shelves the item as doSell does.

what: Computes the party factor for experience awards, reducing the per-member share by 4% for each additional party member beyond the first (1.0 solo, 0.96 for two, 0.92 for three, 0.88 for four).
where: Mordor.Core/Rules.cs Rules.ExpAwarded (ChestExp in the same file uses the identical inline formula)
ev: Both candidates compute the same `1 - (partySize - 1) * 0.04` factor, but only as an intermediate step inside a larger experience calculation, not as a standalone function that returns the factor.

what: Sets or clears a character's Defend order in Mordor: when turned on, the character's order becomes Defend and their swing count is reset to zero so they stop attacking, and when turned off, the Defend order is removed if it is currently active, with a message to the player either way.
ev: SetOrder sets the selected character's order kind to Defend or None, which covers part of the on/off behavior, but it also engages waiting monsters, never resets a swing count, and emits no message, while ClearAtt only clears Fight or Defend and returns a bool, so neither matches the full function.

what: Computes the damage of an archive breath attack from the monster's guild level, rolling a random value in a range scaled by the target's resistance percentage (halved, then applied as a reduction).
ev: Kind.Raw computes a breath-specific pre-resistance damage from attacker and target levels, but it uses a different range and rounding formula (Range/4 share, ×0.7) and does not apply the R37 log-based minimum, the Minimum*2 spread, or the resistance halving.

what: Decides whether a melee swing's aim must be re-chosen, returning true when the aimed group index is invalid or the group is no longer standing (SRD R2, R3, R5).
ev: Retarget applies the same test (target index invalid, or its group has no living member) and then moves the aim, but it mutates the order and returns nothing instead of returning the bool that aimMustMove does.

what: Given the gap between a character's level and an item's level in the Mordor game, it returns the chance-of-identifying level (0 for no gap or better, 1 for a small shortfall, 2 for a moderate one, 3 for a large one).
ev: The final line applies the same thresholds as the C++ mapping (gap >= 0 gives 0, gap <= -15 gives 3, gap <= -5 gives 2, else 1), but IdLevelRoll takes a character, monster, and item and computes the gap itself, whereas the C++ function takes the gap as its input.

what: General Cure removes poison and disease from the target character and announces "Cured."
ev: Apply's Cure case clears poison and disease on the target, as castGeneralCure does, but its doc comment also has the general cure heal each target (spell 18), which the C++ function does not do, and the "Cured." message is not visible in the truncated snippet.

what: Returns the Guild level equivalent of a spell, computed as twice the spell level minus one (rule R31).
ev: No candidate computes spellLevel * 2 - 1; Rules.SpellLevel is the inverse mapping (guild level to spell level, Int(level / 2 + 0.5)), so it is related but does not do the same thing.

what: Returns true when monsters are on the square but not engaged with the player, meaning they are not coming after the player (rule R7, the "peaced" state).
ev: No candidate is a standalone `monstersPresent && !engaged` predicate, but CastGate.Refuse's peaced branch (`!monstersPresent` else `!engaged && s.Level > PeacedSpellLevel`) and its doc comment both encode the same peaced state, embedded in a larger spell-refusal routine.

what: Converts a currency amount stored in 1/10000 gold into whole gold and formats it as text for display in the confinement (pens) screens.
ev: GetIntCurrency does the same `/ 10000` conversion from 1/10000 gold to whole gold, but it returns a long and does no text formatting, so it lacks the `confNumText` display step that the C++ function performs.

what: Computes a character's chance to resist a melee paralysis attack as their paralysis resistance plus Constitution, capped at 95.
ev: It is a paralysis resistance roll that takes CON and resistance as inputs, but it is a per-tick wear-off check against the monster's guild level with a logarithmic formula and a 5-90 clamp, not the C++ `min(Res(c,8) + CON, 95)` melee chance.

what: Moves gold from the bank into the player's hand without checking the amount, so a negative withdrawal is accepted and can leave the hand with negative gold and the bank with extra.
ev: Its withdrawal branch does the same unchecked-sign arithmetic (hand += amount, bank -= amount) and explicitly lets a negative withdrawal through, but it also refuses withdrawals above the account balance or from an already-negative account, which the C++ function does not.

what: Returns the experience points needed to reach the character's current level in their guild, which is 0 at level 1 and otherwise the threshold computed by fn12A1 for the level below, based on the character's race.
ev: The candidate returns `Rules.Fn12A1(Guild.Level - 1, ...)`, which gives 0 at level 1 because the loop doesn't run, and otherwise the same threshold for the level below, matching the C++ function; it uses the character's active guild rather than an explicit guild parameter, a small structural difference.

what: Returns the guild level of the character's currently active guild, or 0 if no guild is active or the guild index is out of range.
ev: No candidate returns the active guild's level with a 0 fallback; MeetsUseLevel reads the active guild's level (`Guild.Level`) only in its class-restricted branch, and the other candidates use the highest level across all guilds (MaxGuildLevel, TopGuildLevel) or take a level as a parameter (ChestExp).

what: Decides whether CastGate monsters are flagged, returning true while combat is still going on or while any monsters are waiting, and false only once combat is over with nothing waiting.
ev: CheckCast computes `monsters = _combat is { IsOver: false } || _waiting is { Count: > 0 }`, which is the same predicate as `!combatOver || waitingCount > 0`, but it is inline in CheckCast rather than a separate method.

what: Returns true when a spell or effect code falls in the charm range 75 to 99, marking it as one of the game's charm effects.
ev: The only candidate that tests `spell.Effect is >= 75 and <= 99` is MonsterSpellHits, but it is inlined in a damage calculation rather than being a standalone predicate, and the other candidates either check Category (IsCharm) or use different effect ranges (SpecialFor, ResistKind, OpensLockUpTo).

what: Decides whether a monster can join a character based on alignment, where Neutral monsters can join any character and other monsters must match the character's alignment.
ev: No candidate decides whether a monster may join a character; the closest, Rules.EngageChance, uses alignment pairing only to set the chance that a monster attacks, and the other candidates handle pens, turning, display, or alignment conversion.

what: Picks a monster class at random from the set of classes allowed by the spawn mask, weighting each allowed class equally via the double-count quirk, and falls back to a fully random class when the mask allows none.
ev: Generate is a line-for-line port of the encounter routine that appears to contain the class pick (its comments mention a class pick writing into `v` at indices 0..n-1), but the excerpt is cut off before any spawn-mask class selection or double-count weighting is visible, so the match is unconfirmed; the other candidates pick a location, a random class without a mask, or a list of classes, not a mask-filtered class.

what: Returns the scope in which a movement spell can be cast, making it usable in combat only when the spell's table row is flagged as combat-usable (only Teleport, per the comment), and non-combat otherwise or if the spell has no row.
ev: UseOf also classifies Teleport as usable in combat (returns Either), but it derives the result from the spell's Effect and Damage2 rather than a per-row combatMarked flag, it has no movement-spell row lookup or NonCombat fallback for missing rows, and it also makes CureParalysis Either.

what: Parses a binary guild-log file byte by byte into a list of GuildLogEntry records, each holding a guild index, a day serial stamp, and a text message, dropping any truncated tail.
ev: It skips the header count, reads the same record layout (int32 guild, int64 day, int32 length, text), and drops a truncated tail, matching readGuildLog; it differs only in decoding text as UTF-8 rather than raw bytes and in how it handles a missing file.

what: Handles the player's guild log cleaning command: if the log is over its threshold, it archives all but the newest kept entries to guildlog.text, rewrites the log with only those, and tells the player how many entries were removed.
ev: Entry.Clean keeps the newest KeepOnClean entries, appends the discarded ones to GUILDLOG.TXT (when writeText is set), rewrites the log with only the kept entries, and returns the removed count, which matches glClean's core behavior; the threshold check is split out into Entry.NeedsCleaning and the reply strings are produced by the caller, which are structural differences only.

what: Decides whether a character of a given level may receive an advancement award, which is allowed only when the level is at or below the cap and is a multiple of the award interval (the exact game meaning of these values is still unknown).
ev: GuildADSingle applies the same gate (`l <= g.AdMaxLevel` and `l % every == 0`) for levels up to HitsCapLevel, but it is a loop that totals awards rather than a yes/no check, it clamps AdEvery to at least 1 instead of returning false, and above the cap it uses the AdInterval modulus instead.

what: Computes a level's experience-point requirement from the R13 research formula (scaled by guild GEF and race factor), returning 0 for level 1 or below.
ev: It returns the experience for the current level via `Rules.Fn12A1(Guild.Level - 1, ...)` with zero at level 1, and Candidate 5's `Fn13ED` implies `Fn12A1(n)` is the requirement for level n+1, so it matches the C++ inputs and zero-at-low-level behavior, but the C++ is a closed-form research approximation while `Fn12A1`'s body is not shown and may differ in detail.

what: Looks up the author's minimum item level for a given drop level (1-16), clamping out-of-range values, which determines the lowest level an item can be generated at when dropped.
ev: RollDrop computes the drop band from ItemDropLevel by halving it with banker's rounding (low = round(level/2, ToEven)) and applies chest-class shifts, which is the same banding idea as the C++ author's minimum-level list, but it never performs a table lookup of minimum levels and its formula differs from the C++ list (which deliberately uses the listed values), so it is only a related version and not the same function.

what: Decides whether a data file may be deleted, allowing deletion only for files classed as non-vital (provisional rule, since the SRD deletion rule was not supplied).
ev: No candidate decides whether a data file may be deleted by its class; the closest, Backups.cs `Copy`, removes character and party files during a restore to match the source, which is a different rule, and the TitleWindow `OnDelete` candidate only deletes the loaded character's record after confirmation.

what: Computes the chance that an archive stone effect triggers, starting from 100 plus the spawn level and subtracting a CON-based penalty (CON·ln(CON)·1.09), clamped to a minimum floor value.
ev: No candidate uses the `(100 + spawnLevel) - CON*ln(CON)*1.09` formula with a minimum of 5; the closest, `Rules.MorgueRaiseChance` (`35*(CON/4.5)+40`), is a different raise-chance formula with no spawn level or logarithm.

what: Asks the host to hold the display for a melee result by emitting a "Melee hold" message with the requested duration in milliseconds, since the core never reads the clock itself.
ev: HoldKeys takes a seconds-long timed hold and then replays queued keypresses, so it performs a timed wait like meleeHold's requested hold, but it holds keyboard input rather than emitting a "Melee hold" request for a melee result with milliseconds, and no candidate does that.

what: Rolls a random number and returns true if it falls under the leave threshold (the check that passes when the roll times 200 is less than leaveValue), which decides whether a companion leaves the party.
ev: ChanceToLeave computes the percent chance of a companion leaving, which is the kind of leaveValue the C++ check consumes, but no candidate draws a random number or compares it against a threshold as leaveCheck does.

what: Sends the caster of a spell (the "ethereal portal" effect) into solid rock by setting that party member's death state to Rock and logging a message, provided the caster slot is valid.
ev: It sets the rock death state (CauseOfDeath = Rules.DeathRock) and logs the rock message for the same Ethereal Portal rock branch, but it kills every member from the caster onward (and the whole party for slots 0-1) rather than only the caster, and it is a movement handler that also writes the automap, where the C++ function only sets the caster's death state and logs.

what: Returns the number of dungeon levels in the loaded game data (one per floor), with the build argument ignored because the limited build's restriction is enforced elsewhere in the R59 clamp and R67/R68.
ev: Check computes `levels = MdrLoader.LoadDungeon(P("MDATA11.MDR")).Count` as one step of a folder check, which is a related dungeon-level count, but no candidate simply returns the loaded game data's floor count, and none ignores the build argument as the C++ does.

what: On the first switch-on of a lifecycle mod, it loads the mod once (emitting a "Host calls Load" message), then emits "Host calls OnEnable" and marks the mod active, while plain mods are simply activated with no hooks.
ev: Switch matches the lifecycle path (Load then OnEnable on first switch-on, and OnEnable without a second Load after an earlier switch-off), but it leaves a plain non-lifecycle mod unactivated until the next start, whereas firstSwitchOn sets `mod.active = true` for plain mods.

what: Records the player's chosen text for a mod option under a given key, writing it straight into the mod settings store without checking it against the declared options.
ev: It writes the given option text straight to `_store.Write(_id, key, option)` with no check against the declared options, which matches the C++ `setChoice` quirk (candidate 4, `SetText`, does the same write but is not a choice setter).

what: Stores a boolean mod setting by converting it to the text "1" or "0" and writing it through modSettingWrite, so the flag can be saved and read back later.
ev: It converts the bool to text and writes it through the store like the C++ function, but it stores "True"/"False" where the C++ stores "1"/"0", so the saved settings.ini text differs.

what: Returns the trimmed name of a guild by index, or the bare number as text if the index is out of range.
where: Mordor.Core/GuildData.cs GuildData.ByName (with Mordor.Core/Character.cs is.SetActiveGuild as a related lookup)
ev: The C++ function returns the trimmed guild name by index, or the number as text when the index is out of range, while no candidate does that; ByName goes the other way (name to GuildDef, throwing when not found), and the other candidates only look up guilds by name or index without producing a name string or a fallback.

what: Spends spell points by adding the given amount to the character's current spell points, capped at their maximum, as from a Scroll of Spells or Tome of Spells.
ev: It caps current spell points at the maximum (`Math.Min`) but never adds an incoming amount, and the C++ function's add-then-cap behaviour is not in any candidate.

what: Decides whether a fallen character's body can be recovered for rescue: it is never recoverable while in rock, always recoverable if dead, and for a living body only when current hits are at or below the rescue fraction (20%) of max hits.
ev: Report returns a recoverable (true) outcome for a dead body not in rock and for a living body at or below 20% of max hits, and a non-recoverable (false) outcome for a body in rock or a living body above that threshold, which is the same rule as bodyRecoverable, though it also takes a foundAtAll flag and reports the result as a message.

what: Sets the forced-settle bit in the flags when the source is a teleporter square, the Teleport spell, or a chest teleporter trap, so the game's forced-settle rule (R89) applies.
where: Mordor.App/DungeonWindow.axaml.cs DungeonWindow.TeleporterSquare (candidate 6; the chest-trap case is in DungeonWindow.ChestTeleport, candidate 5)
ev: The candidates set the forced-settle flag (`_forceSettle`) for the teleporter square and the chest Teleporter trap at their call sites rather than through a source-keyed helper, and no visible candidate sets it for the Teleport spell (ArriveBySpell in candidate 3 does not), so only two of the three sources match.

what: Handles the Confinement pens command by listing each penned monster with its alignment, count, and current buy price in gold, or reporting that the pens are empty.
ev: PriceToBuy computes the per-item buy price from the penned count (half again the value, divided down by the log of the count), which matches only the `penBuyPrice` part of cmdPens, while no candidate builds the numbered pen listing with names, alignment, counts, and gold text or handles the empty-pens message.

what: Re-acquaints a character with a guild they have already joined by making it their active guild, returning false if they never joined it (free of cost, per R13.1).
ev: The candidate returns false when the guild is not in the character's Guilds list and otherwise moves it to the front as the active guild, matching the C++ joined check and call to setActiveGuild, though its doc comment's mention of experience and level-up gains is not in the code and the C++ setActiveGuild body is not shown.

what: Computes the monster grade for a library lookup in the Mordor game: if the reader has skill 0 and the monster is 15 or more levels above them, the grade is 1, otherwise it is derived from an ID-level roll.
ev: The candidate rolls with `CombatEngine.IdLevelRoll(reader, def, item, false)` and maps the roll to a grade (0→4, 1→3, 2→2, else 1), matching the C++ roll-and-grade path, but none of the candidates has the skill-0 / 15-level gate that returns grade 1 first.

what: When a rescued character arrives, their age advances by the days they waited, and they are moved to dungeon level 0 and area -1, leaving their X and Y coordinates unchanged.
ev: CarryHome adds `days` to `body.Age`, sets `DungeonLevel = 0` and `Area = -1`, and leaves X and Y untouched, which is the same operation as the C++ `applyRescueArrival`.

what: Builds the starting Hall of Records for a new game by copying each record kind's seeded starting value into the hall, which is used when no saved hall file exists.
ev: Fresh() builds a new Hall with the twelve seeded starting values, the same outcome as defaultHallOfRecords(), though it also sets holder names and day 0, which the C++ version omits.

what: Decides whether a slime attack hits by comparing a roll against a base value plus a bonus that scales with dungeon level.
ev: No candidate decides whether a slime attack hits by comparing a roll to a base plus a dungeon-level-scaled threshold; the only slime references (Candidate 2's comment about the quicksand pack-slot roll and Candidate 1's trap code) are unrelated.

what: Sanctuary, once Set Sanctuary has been cast, returns the party to the stored location and ages the caster by a fixed number of days; with no stored location it prints "Nothing happens" and fails.
ev: AgeBy covers only the "caster ages" half of castSanctuary (it is listed as a Sanctuary caller in its doc comment), while the candidate that actually implements Set Sanctuary's stored-location return is Mordor.Core/SpellThrown.cs Companion.Apply, which only records the caster's square on cast and never returns the party, so no candidate performs the full return-to-stored-location-and-age behavior.

what: Shifts a 128-bit unsigned value left by n bits, carrying bits across the 64-bit halves, which the X87 extended-precision arithmetic uses to align mantissas.
ev: No candidate performs a 128-bit left shift with carry across the two 64-bit halves; the closest, CompanionSlots.Left, just returns a companion record, and the rest are name formatting, mod-file parsing, or gold transfer.

what: Returns the target character's defence value for companion blows, deliberately without adding any protection bonus, per the SRD source notes.
where: Mordor.Core/Combat.cs Combat.CompanionStrikes (class name not shown in the excerpt)
ev: CompanionStrikes uses the target's defence with no Protection term for companion blows, matching the C++ rule, but it computes that defence via DefenseOf/pdef.Def rather than returning the stored `combat.defence` field, and the candidate's own comment says that field excludes Protection.

what: Computes the guild-level factor for a character as 333/(333+g), with negative guild levels clamped to 0, so the factor is 1.0 at guild 0 and falls toward 0 as guild level rises.
ev: Rules.ChestExp and Rules.ExpAwarded both contain the same 333/(333+g) factor inline (as `1 / (1 + guildLevel / 333.0)`), but no candidate computes that factor standalone, and none clamps negative guild levels to 0 as the C++ function does.

what: Returns the Constitution stat used for a companion's raise-dead rule (R16.3), taking the companion's own CON score when its monster definition exists and a fixed fallback value otherwise.
ev: No candidate looks up a companion's monster definition, returns its CON or falls back to 10; the closest, Morgue.CompanionChance and CompanionRaiseChance, take CON as an input and compute a raise chance from it.

what: Resolves a player's disarm attempt on a chest in the game: on success it awards experience to the acting member and clears the trap, on failure it clears the trap and reports that it went off, returning a message for the player.
where: Mordor.App/DungeonWindow.axaml.cs DungeonWindow.OpenChest (with Mordor.Core/Rules.cs Rules.ChestExp for the award formula)
ev: Both cover the same disarm-or-spring roll and the experience award for a successful disarm, with the first party member's guild level discounting it, but the candidates do not clear the trap on failure with a "goes off" message, and they do not take the C++ function's explicit `(success, member)` inputs, since the roll happens internally.

what: Determines the verb shown for a spell's effect in the game: a kill spell (effect 100) reads "KILLED", a charm spell (effect 80–99) reads "CHARMED", and any other spell uses its data-file verb index, or NONE if the spell or index is invalid.
ev: No candidate maps a spell's effect to a verb (KILLED for effect 100, CHARMED for 80-99, otherwise the data verb index); Combat.cs CastDamage (candidate 4) only mentions "verb from gv0972$(M5B12)" in a doc comment about caption wording, and SpellInfo.SpecialFor (candidate 7) returns descriptive text rather than a verb.

what: Resting in town cures poison by clearing the character's poison level to zero and showing the player a "The poison leaves you in town" message, doing nothing if they are not poisoned.
ev: RestInCity clears poison (through EndAilmentsAndSpellResists) as part of resting in town, but it also heals hits, adds age, and restores spell points, and it has no "poison leaves you in town" message, while CurePoison (candidate 1) clears the same poison state but is the spell/Cure path rather than the town rest.

what: Lists the indices of dead characters whose death was caused by rock (a stoning-type death state) and who are on the party leader's dungeon level and in the city area, which is the candidate set for the fetch spell's target selection.
ev: The FETCH branch filters the saves for dead characters with CauseOfDeath == Rules.DeathRock, DungeonLevel equal to the leader's level, and SavedArea(c) == 0, which is the same predicate as the C++ fetchCandidates, though CastHere also excludes the caster by name and returns names through a picker rather than indices.

what: Computes the whole seconds to add to the play clock for one step, returning zero while the game is paused and otherwise the elapsed time since the last tick, per SRD rule R27.
ev: It implements the same rule (add elapsed time only when not paused, and refresh the last-tick time either way), but it works per party member on float seconds with midnight wraparound and keeps a 4-decimal fraction, whereas the C++ takes ms inputs and returns whole seconds via integer division.

what: Charges the player the Seer's wiki-locate fee and then rolls a percentage chance (kWikiSuccessPercent, a placeholder value) to decide whether the requested name is found, leaving the location at 0 even on success because no target table is available.
ev: It shares the pay-a-fee-then-locate-by-exact-name flow, but it matches monsters or items through Seer.Match with a fee from Seer.Fee and has no percentage success roll, and no candidate implements the wiki locate.

what: Casting the Ethereal Portal spell walks the party into solid rock, killing the whole party if the caster is in slot 0 or 1, or only the caster and the members behind them if the caster is in slot 2 or later.
ev: Both kill the whole party when the caster is in slot 0 or 1, and only the caster and later members when the caster is in slot 2 or later, with the same stop-at-the-hang deviation; the candidate also writes rock onto the automap, which the C++ leaves out because its SquareState fields are missing.

what: Rolls a d100 for a slime attack, returning a value from 1 to 100 that is compared against the hit threshold (50 + dungeon level × 2) to decide whether the slime hits.
ev: No candidate rolls a slime value or uses the 50 + level×2 slime hit threshold; Rules.HitThreshold (fn0DEE's to-hit formula) is the nearest, but it is a different rule with a different formula, and the other candidates only make generic Int(Rnd*100)+1 rolls for unrelated checks.

what: Subtracts damage from a character's current hit points and floors the result at zero, so a character's hit points never go negative.
ev: It subtracts the damage from `CurHits` and floors the result at zero, exactly as `applyDamage` does, but it also yields an "Ouch"/"Aigh!" combat line for party members unless `silent` is set, which the C++ function does not do.

what: Checks a mod's manifest against the chapter 21 validation rule (F1), returning the first problem found: a blank id, an id containing forbidden characters, a blank assembly, or a blank entry type, or None if the manifest is valid.
ev: No candidate checks the id, assembly, or entry type for blank or forbidden characters; ModHost.Discover only reads a precomputed `m.Problem` (the check itself would be in ModManifest's `Problem` property, which isn't among the candidates), and ModManifest.Read just deserializes the file.

what: Decodes the raw bytes of a guild log file into a list of guild log records (guild index, day serial, and text), reading records until the data runs out and dropping any truncated record at the end.
ev: It ignores the 4-byte header count, reads each record as an int32 guild, int64 day, and int32 length followed by the text, stops at a truncated record, and returns an empty list for a missing or short file, matching the C++ decoder (the only differences are UTF-8 decoding versus raw bytes, and a caught exception versus an explicit bounds check on a partial header).

what: Checks whether a spell is being cast on an anti-magic square and, if so, marks that square and tells the player "Anti-Magic area!", blocking the cast.
ev: CheckCast blocks the cast on an anti-magic square, records the anti-magic bit on the map, and gives the "Anti-Magic area!" refusal, but it also blocks on extinguisher squares (which the C++ deliberately excludes) and wraps the whole cast gate, so the outcome differs.

what: Returns true when the shelf is on floor 0 and has at least one unaligned item stocked, which decides whether the shop sells unaligned goods at the item's price.
ev: PriceOf returns the list price whenever the item's floor is 0, which covers the floor test, but it omits the C++ `alignCounts[0] > 0` condition and no candidate returns the boolean predicate itself.

what: When a new companion is placed into a slot, it inherits the name of the companion who previously occupied that slot.
ev: When `keepSlotName` is true, `Add` sets the new companion's `Name` to `_left[at].Name`, the name left in the slot it is placed into, which is the same outcome as the C++ `keepSlotName` returning the previous occupant's name.

what: Returns true only when the character is in town (dungeon level 0) and not dead, which is the gate that decides whether the city rest can run.
ev: It computes the same predicate from the same inputs (`dungeonLevel == 0 && !dead`), but it decides whether frmCityMain or frmDungeonMain is shown at start rather than gating the city rest, and the rest-related candidate (RestInCity) runs for dead characters too, which conflicts with the C++ gate.

what: Computes the gold needed to advance from level n to n+1 under the game's R16 formula, 30.1 × n² × (1 + ggf/10), rounded half-up, where ggf is a gold-gain factor that scales the result.
where: Mordor.Core/Rules.cs Rules.Fn12B2 (called for the current guild by Mordor.Core/Character.cs Character.GoldForNextLevel)
ev: Fn12B2 sums (2i-1)·30.1 for i = 1..level, which equals 30.1·level² and is then multiplied by (1 + Gold/10), the same cumulative formula as the C++ closed form, though its per-step rounding and x87 arithmetic can shift the result by a gold piece in edge cases.

what: Computes a player's proc chance for a special combat effect (crit or backstab) from guild level, monster level, a coefficient, and weapon ability, then clamps it between a floor and a cap.
ev: The candidate has the same formula, ability term, weapon term with max, floor condition (`guildLevel > 0 || weaponHasIt`), and cap as playerProcChance, differing only in that it takes the divisor, weapon log, floor, and cap as separate parameters and names the coefficient `mod`.

what: Handles the typed `combine` command in the game: it checks the argument count, party member number, and slot numbers (refusing repeated slots and slot 1 or out-of-range slots with player-facing messages), then hands the valid request to combineApply.
ev: It repeats cmdCombine's one-based slot range rule (refuses slot 1 and anything past the pack size), but it belongs to the swap command, not combine, and it has no member check, no repeated-slot refusal, and no combineApply call.

what: Returns true only when a rock-death is undone by the Resurrect raise kind, so that Resurrect is the sole way to reverse death from rock in the game's rules.
ev: For rock deaths, the candidate permits a raise only when the effect is Resurrect (22) and refuses every other raise, which is the same rule as `rockUndoneBy`, though the candidate returns a refusal message rather than a bool and also covers the morgue case.

what: Spends one charge from the owner's item in the given pack slot to pay for a companion's cast, refusing with "Out of charges." if the slot is invalid or the item has none left.
ev: Both check for remaining charges and decrement one (via Spellbook.SpendCharge), but ItemCharge has no invalid-slot check and, when charges are gone, it removes the order and prints a different message instead of refusing with "Out of charges." (Castable.SpendCharge in Mordor.Core/Spells.cs decrements and possibly removes the item but has no refusal path.)

what: Charms up to the capped number of monster groups' front creatures matching the given monster class, marking them charmed, non-hostile, and their groups Peaced, and reports success or failure.
ev: The candidate builds the Companion a charm creates from a struck monster, which is related to charming, but nothing among the candidates marks the group's front creature charmed, non-hostile, and its group Peaced in place as the C++ does.

what: Returns the dungeon level the teleporter should load, using the leader's current level if it falls within the valid range of dungeon levels and otherwise falling back to the party's level.
ev: ForSquare applies the same rule (leader's level used when 1 ≤ level ≤ dungeon.Count) to choose the level its draws read from, but it is inlined in a teleport-destination routine, returns no standalone loaded level, and falls back to the current `fromLevel` rather than `party.dungeonLevel`.

what: Returns true when a newbie lead (character level 1 or below) faces a monster whose guild level exceeds the newbie monster cap, so that monster is excluded from the encounter.
ev: No candidate excludes a monster by comparing a newbie lead's level (<=1) against a guild-level cap; the candidates cover chest finds, loot drops, the Library sighting record, ability chance, and critical/backstab chance.

what: Computes the gold a character accrues per level from a guild's gold factor (GGF), which the code simplifies to 30.1 × GGF per level, with the level cancelling out under the assumed reading.
ev: Rules.Fn12B2 implements the full fn12B2 from MAINMOD2.BAS, a cumulative loop over levels with a per-step multiplier and a Gold/10 term, while the C++ function returns the single term 30.1 × GoldFactor under an assumed reading (l03A8 = 0, no loop, no Gold/10).

what: On arrival in town, guild-marked items in pack slots 1 through 39 have their charges restored to their maximum (guild item recharge, rules R62 and R63).
ev: It loops over pack slots 1 to PackSize-1 (slot 0 skipped), and for each guild-issued item with fewer charges than the item's maximum it sets the charges back to that maximum, the same as townRecharge; it also returns a town message, which the C++ function lacks.

what: Checks whether a trap placed by the trap table's Floor bit mask applies on a given dungeon level, returning false for any level outside 1 to 31.
ev: Librarian.Bit is a bare `(mask & (1L << b)) != 0` test, which matches the core bit read in floorMaskPlaces, but it lacks the `dungeonLevel - 1` offset and the 1..31 range guard that define the C++ function.

what: Applies the chest gold floor rule: if a group's gold is under 500, it is replaced with a random whole-gold amount from 2 to 501.
where: Mordor.Core/Rules.cs GroupGold (candidate 1; candidate 2, Mordor.Core/Combat.cs FillGroup, has the same floor inline)
ev: Both contain the same rule, "if gold < 500, replace with Int(Rnd*500)+2", but only as one step inside larger group-gold computations, and the floor is applied before the count scaling, so no candidate is a standalone equivalent of applyChestGoldFloor.

what: Returns true only when a character's combat order is None, implementing rule R4 that the combat setting applies only to characters with no order.
ev: No candidate is the pure predicate, but ApplyDefaultOrders and Sub0BDE both gate on "if (o.Kind != OrderKind.None) continue;", which is the same no-order condition as R4, and then apply the setting to those characters.

what: Computes the shortfall a payer must cover for a cost, equal to the cost minus the payer's purse and floored at zero.
ev: It computes the same shortfall, `VbCurrency.SubtractSaturating(cost, payer.Purse)` (cost minus purse, floored at zero), but only as the first step of planning gifts from other party members, and it returns a gift list rather than the shortfall amount.

what: Applies one monthly-style drift tick to a companion's binding value: if the binding isn't yet "for life," a random roll against the drift score may nudge it one step toward zero.
ev: Round contains the same steps as companionsDriftTick (ForLife check first, then one `NextDouble() * 200` roll against the drift score, then one notch toward zero), but it computes the drift score itself via Drift, is not a standalone tick returning bool, and also handles leaving, messages, and the leave chance.

what: Attempts a shop purchase by placing the item in the buyer's first free inventory slot if one exists and the buyer has enough gold, deducting the price and reporting the result to the player.
ev: It performs only the first step of storeBuy, the scan for the first free pack slot (skipping slot 0, returning -1 when full), but none of the gold check, the deduction, the item placement, or the messages.

what: Decides whether a newbie lead is rejected for a party, returning true when the lead's guild level is above the newbie cap, the lead is not the exempt table index, and the viewer counts as a newbie in that area.
ev: No candidate rejects a newbie lead by comparing its guild level to a newbie cap with an exempt table index, though Candidate 3 (Combat.cs whatever.Generate) is truncated and I could not see its full body.

what: Announces to the player via a message that a companion has been dropped, printing the message before any size check so it appears even when the new body is rejected.
ev: Run emits a "dropped X to carry Y" line before the monster-size test, matching the C++ ordering, but it is built inline during a carry-swap with different wording and no standalone announce function.

what: Clears the paralysed status, its paralysis level, and its paralysis round counter when the character reaches the city gate, while leaving lost stats unrestored, and sends the "paralysis leaves you" message.
ev: Unparalyse zeroes the paralysis level like the C++ does, but it also restores the stat part (ADShift) that the C++ deliberately leaves lost, and it has no round-counter clear or message; the city-gate candidate EndAilmentsAndSpellResists explicitly excludes paralysis.

what: When a character casts a spell, this sets their combat protection value to whatever protection the spell level grants, per the SRD's cast-time protection rule [c27].
where: Mordor.Core/SpellEffect.cs SpellEffect.ApplyToCharacter (the Protect case; SpellThrown.cs Companion.Apply describes the same rule)
