ev: Both set the caster's protection from the cast's spell level as `Int(spellLevel / 2) + 1`, written after the recompute, which matches the C++ `protectionFromCast(spellLevel)` assignment, though the candidate also sets the state bit and recomputes, and the candidate text is truncated before the full body.

what: Records the protection level granted to a character when a protection spell is cast by storing it in the character's ailments data, with the effect's magnitude still unresolved.
ev: The Protect branch writes the protection number at cast time, as the C++ does, but it computes the value itself (`Int(casterSpellLevel / 2) + 1`) and sits inside a larger function that also handles the other spell states, while the C++ is a one-line setter that takes the level as an argument.

what: Fear trap (Trap 9) releases each eligible occupied companion from its slot, clears the carried-companion index, and announces how many companions fled, returning that count.
ev: It releases the carried companion from its slot and resets the carry index to -1, but it is a player put-down action with no fear check, no loop over all slots, no count returned, and no "scared away" announcement, so it covers only part of fearTrap.

what: Computes the archive spell level needed to reach a desired cost, using the formula ceil(StartSpellLevel × SpellPointRatio × BaseMod² × 1.9 / (DesiredCost + 1)), returning 0 if the divisor is zero.
where: Mordor.Core/Spells.cs Spellbook.Cost (candidate 1, `it.Cost`; closest by name but computes the reverse direction)
ev: No candidate computes an archive spell level from a desired cost. Candidate 1 is the forward cost function (spell level to points via Rules.Fn1485Price), the inverse of the C++ R31 formula, and the others are gates, heal selection, installer parsing, or healing amounts.

what: Decides whether a character is eligible to join the party, which requires that they are not already a member and are at the leader's location (or anywhere in town when the party is in town).
where: Mordor.Core/Party.cs Party.WhyCannotJoin (the inline filter in Mordor.App/CityWindow.axaml.cs CityWindow.AskToJoin is the closest match to the exact predicate)
ev: Both candidates test "not already a member" and "same place as the leader," but neither is the bare predicate: WhyCannotJoin also refuses full parties, dead characters, and oppositely aligned ones and returns a reason string instead of a bool, while the CityWindow lambda `Members.All(m => m.Name != c.Name) && SamePlace(Leader, c)` matches the C++ logic only inside a larger UI method.

what: Rolls d100 and returns true when the roll is below 50 + 2 × dungeon level, deciding whether the slime effect takes hold on the player.
ev: No candidate handles the slime effect; Rules.QuicksandTakesSomething (Rules.cs) has a similar level-scaled d100 check, but it decides whether quicksand takes an item, not whether slime takes hold.

what: Sends the "DRAGON" attack-cry message to the owner when a melee companion hits a party member without killing them, as a mishap event under rule R32.3.
ev: CompanionCry emits one sound on its own line to the owner or victim under the No Party Sound guard, which is the same mechanism as the C++ call, but it does not name "DRAGON" or the melee-hit-without-kill trigger, and the CompanionStrikes body that would make that call is cut off in the excerpt.

what: Routes a typed player command to the matching feature handler for the current screen (combat, dungeon, or town), registering features first and returning whether a handler was found and whether it succeeded.
ev: No candidate parses a typed command string, looks up a handler by screen and verb, or returns a found/succeeded result; the closest, CityWindow.axaml.cs CityWindow.OnToolCommand, only switches over toolbar enum values for the town screen and returns void.

what: Computes the number of days a character must spend resting to recover, based on the percentage of hit points missing (zero days at full HP, 31 days at zero HP, rounded half-even).
ev: The method's comment gives the same rest-age formula, `(100 - Hits/MaxHits*100) / 3.25`, but its body never computes or returns the day count, and nothing in the candidates applies half-even rounding to it, so it only partly matches `restAgeCostDays`.

what: Switches the character's active guild in Mordor, saving the current experience into the outgoing guild's membership record and loading the incoming guild's stored experience into the character.
ev: Both make an already-joined guild the active one, but the C# version moves that membership to the front of the `Guilds` list and needs no experience copy because experience is stored on each membership, whereas the C++ copies experience between the character and guild slots.

what: Computes the published spell cost for a spell by multiplying the rated level, ratio, and rate, scaling by 1/10, and flooring the result (with an epsilon correction so values like 209 become 208).
ev: Both floor an exact product of the rated level, a rate, and a 1/10 scale with an epsilon-style correction, but Fn1485Price also multiplies by 19 (the `1.9#` factor), divides by the spell level `sl`, and takes `u4` and a separate rate, while the C++ ignores `spellLevel` and uses only `ratio * rate / 10`.

what: Forwards a member-roster load request for a named party member into the session, returning success and a reply string for the player.
where: Mordor.Core/Party.cs Party.LoadFor (and Mordor.Core/Party.cs Roster.RosterPath for the roster file lookup)
ev: The C++ function is a one-line forward to `rosterLoadMember`, which loads a named member into the session with a reply; LoadFor is the closest match in that it loads a roster by leader and reports each member's pass/fail by name, but it is a full join-party routine with alignment and death checks rather than a simple load-by-name forward, and no candidate is a direct forwarding wrapper for a named member.

what: Decides whether a monster group has gone stale, meaning it was never stamped or its timestamp is more than twice the respawn interval away from the current time, so it can be pruned.
ev: RefillDue's `Math.Abs(nowSec - stamp) > t * 2 || stamp == 0` test matches groupStale's core condition, but RefillDue applies it only to a standing group and then combines it with a second one-respawn-time test to decide whether to refill, so it does not return the stale flag by itself.

what: Rolls a hostility check against a threshold computed from the base value and Charisma (floored at 1, via the logarithmic formula T = trunc(base − 7.5·ln(cha))), returning true when a d100 draw is strictly below that threshold.
ev: EngageChance computes the same truncated threshold `(int)(b - 7.5 * Math.Log(Math.Max(1, charisma)))`, but it derives `b` from an alignment pairing instead of taking it as input and never performs the d100 draw or strict comparison that hostileRoll returns.

what: When a monster is killed, the killer's active guild monster quest is marked Done if its target matches that monster, and a completion message naming the character is produced.
ev: It has the same core check (Defeat quest, not done, target equals the monster id) and marks it done, but it loops over every party member rather than only the killer, and its messages and counter differ from the C++ version's single `guild.quest_done` message.

what: Applies a monster spell's damage to the leading party members (up to the spell's affect group plus one), subtracting the spell's damage from each one's current hits, and returns that damage.
ev: No candidate applies a monster spell's damage to up to AffectGroup+1 leading party slots and returns it; Rules.SpellDamage and CompanionSpellOnParty compute damage for a caster, and CompanionCasts damages one mishap victim, while Rules.SpellDamage's comment points to MonsterAttack.MonsterSpellHits, the likely real counterpart, which is not among the candidates.

what: Toggles an item's equipped state in the player's pack, refusing if the character is paralysed, the slot is invalid or empty, or the item isn't wearable, and blocking removal of a slot-cursed item while clearing the curse on successful unequip; equipping applies the item's curse.
ev: The candidate performs the same equip/unequip toggle, cursed-unequip refusal, unequip curse clearing, and equip curse application, but it also adds a WearRefusal check (stat-minimum refusal) that the C++ function does not apply, and the paralysis check lives in the caller (OnPackEquip) rather than in the toggle.

what: Builds the text listing of all game options for the player, showing each boolean and integer setting, the last backup date, and every party member's character options.
ev: It shows only the "Last Backup was on" line (via `_o.LastBackupLine`) as a UI label, with no listing of the game's boolean and integer options or the per-member character options that the C++ function builds as text.

what: Returns the player's deepest dungeon level for the R7 step 7 replenish rule, using the saved deepest level if one is recorded (greater than 0) and otherwise falling back to the map's deepest level.
ev: The candidate's comment says "the saved deepest, or the map's when none is saved", but the code is truncated after `DungeonState.Load(SavesDir).DeepestReached`, so the map fallback is never shown.

what: Computes a companion's chance to leave its owner, combining the monster's guild level, the owner's top guild level, the binding value, the companion's natural Charisma, and how wounded it is, then clamps the result between 0 and the maximum leave chance.
ev: The formula matches the C++ step for step (24·ln(M+1) − 2b − 4·ln(top/10+1) − Cha/2, halved, plus 15·missing/max, halved, clamped to 0–90), with minor differences in the rounding of b (ToEven here) and the maxHits ≤ 0 guard (the C++ guards it, the C# divides by zero).

what: Returns whether a computed value falls within the VB Long range (-2147483648 to 2147483647), so the GoldFromTag conversion can treat out-of-range gold amounts as overflow.
ev: CLng performs the same VB Long range check against int.MaxValue and int.MinValue, but it runs that check after rounding inside a larger string-parsing routine and returns null instead of a bool, so a value like 2147483647.4 passes there while fitsLong rejects it.

what: Returns true when a character's fear effect releases, which happens only if the character still has hit points above zero and is not under the ForLife status.
ev: No candidate handles a fear effect or releases one; Companion Round (Mordor.Core/CompanionMood.cs CompanionMood.Round) uses a similar Hits > 0 and ForLife guard, but on companion binding and departure rather than fear.

what: Maps a d6 draw to a Table E drain result: draws 1 to 5 drain the matching stat index by 1, draw 6 drains MaxHits by 2, and anything else drains nothing.
ev: None of the eight candidates maps a d6 draw to a stat drain (1 to 5 drains a stat by 1, 6 drains MaxHits by 2); they cover item, monster, seer, automap, loot, and spell logic.

what: Settles a forced area change on the same floor by storing the room, saving the character, putting down carried bodies, reporting nearby monsters, clearing the engaged-combat flag, and then running the arrival step.
ev: It matches the C++ block's sequence (store room, free monster round, save characters, prune dead, Arrived), but it runs MonstersRound where the C++ does not, never clears the engaged flag (the C++ sets `party.engaged = false`), and has no look-around report.

what: Charm forces a monster to join the party when the spell's damage exceeds the monster's remaining hit points.
ev: Charmed builds the companion a charm makes and its doc comment says the original charms whatever the damage would have killed, which states the same rule, but no candidate contains the `damage > remainingHits` comparison itself, and the truncated CastSpell may hold it.

what: Sets an item's identification level from a legacy boolean flag (identified maps to All, unidentified maps to Unknown) unless a modern known-level field is already present, in which case it does nothing.
ev: No candidate maps a legacy boolean to All/Unknown when no modern known-level field is present; the closest, Party.cs `moves.ReadGiven`, raises an item's known level from the reader's ability instead.

what: Maps a mod API member (toggle, Has/Remove, choices, table/list settings, settings window, OptionDescriptions) to the Mordor mod API version that introduced it, returning -1 for unknown or out-of-range members.
ev: No candidate maps a member index to its introducing API version or returns -1 for unknown members; the closest matches (Has and Remove at version 8, GetChoice at 10, MigrateSettings at 11) only mention a version in their doc comments.

what: Reports whether a key lookup in the game's data tables succeeded by inverting the "read was null" flag, so a key counts as present when the read returned a value.
ev: `Has(key) => _store.Read(_id, key) != null` returns true exactly when the read returns a value, which matches the C++ `!readWasNull`; the C++ takes a precomputed flag while the candidate performs the read itself.

what: Returns whether the Open key is enabled, which in game terms is true only when the trap label is showing, so a hidden trap panel blocks opening the chest.
ev: The C++ function is a one-line pass-through returning whether the trap label is showing, and no candidate does that: ShowChest and OpenChest handle the chest panel and trap logic, but none exposes an "Open key enabled" check equivalent to returning the trap-label visibility state.

what: Returns the total crit damage bonus for a companion by adding +4 if the crit-bit-10 flag is set and +1 if the crit-bit-11 flag is set in its special-property flags (R28).
ev: Its doc comment says a companion's critical and backstab are bits 10 and 11 of its special attacks, worth +4 and +1, and it checks `Bit(def.SpecialAttackFlags, 10)`, but the candidate is cut off and it is a full strike routine rather than a standalone bonus function that sums those two values.

what: Returns the base damage for an electrocution attack by passing the acid-modifier value for the given monster and character guild levels into the shared second-block damage roll, which uses one random draw.
ev: No candidate computes electrocution base damage or the shared second-block roll; the closest is Combat.cs left.CompanionSpits (acid spit via SpecialHits.Raw with Kind.AcidSpit), but that is the acid path, and GroupAttacks only lists electrocution in its caption order without calculating it.

what: Computes the chance that a character's archive (spawned item or record) ages, as 100 plus twice the spawn level minus 2.5 times the Constitution, truncated to an integer.
ev: No candidate computes `100 + 2*spawnLevel - 2.5*CON` for an archive-aging chance; the closest, `Rules.RaiseConLossChance` (a CON-based chance of 50 - 2*CON), is a different formula for a different purpose.

what: Realigns a stored item to a chosen alignment by charging a gold fee from the character's purse, then marking the item as aligned to that alignment.
where: Mordor.App/CityWindow.Store.cs CityWindow.Realign (candidate 1; the fee calculation alone is in Mordor.Core/StoreStock.cs StoreStock.RealignCost)
ev: Candidate 1 charges the same fee from the purse and sets the item's alignment, but it adds a Yes/No confirmation and refuses equipped items (which the C++ does not), and it never sets an `aligned` flag, which the C++ does set to true.

what: Computes the damage a monster's breath attack deals to a target from the monster's level and the target's level, returning zero if the result is negative.
ev: The breath branch computes the same base term, `VbInt(monLvl * Math.Log(monLvl + 1))`, but the excerpt cuts off before any subtraction of the target's level, the halving, or the zero clamp, so I can't confirm the full formula matches.

what: Declares a new mod toggle on a manifest, adding it to the declared settings unless a toggle with the same key (matched case-insensitively) already exists, in which case the existing toggle wins and the code default is ignored (R17).
ev: Both look up an existing toggle by key case-insensitively, leave it in place if found, and otherwise append a new toggle, with the existing one winning over the code default; the C++ returns a bool and the C# returns the toggle, which is a structural difference only.

what: Builds the switch settings for a Full or Limited (shareware) build of Mordor, turning on the limited-version title, ordering notices, and take-denied and dead-chute messages only in the Limited build, per the SRD's switch table.
ev: Apply turns the limited-build mode on or off from the folder's verdict, which covers only the limited-versus-full switch, while the C++ function sets about nine separate switches per build (goodbye box, take-denied, dead-chute lines, ordering notices, and others) and no candidate builds that full set.

what: Decides whether a monster offers to join the character, returning true when the character's active level is at least the monster's guild level.
where: Mordor.Core/Combat.cs Combat.FillGroup (the join-offer block at MONSMOD.BAS:1948-1967)
ev: FillGroup's join-offer section is the only candidate that decides who offers to join, but the candidate text is cut off before the comparison, so I can't confirm it tests the character's active level against the monster's guild level as the C++ function does; MonsterGuildLevel (candidate 4) supplies the monster-side value but makes no comparison.

what: Decides whether a character dies of old age by returning true once their age in days reaches the race's maximum age (a deterministic placeholder for the unsupplied R42 step 2f formula).
ev: Both decide whether a character dies of old age from their age and race lifespan, but the C++ placeholder is deterministic (dies at or past the maximum age), while DiesOfOldAge is a random roll that starts at 98% of lifespan, following the original FRMDUNM.BAS formula.

what: When a companion is released from its owner (the companion drop, rule R15.2/R17), this clears the companion's occupied flag and resets its owner to none for every companion whose owner is a valid party slot.
ev: DropCompanion releases a single companion slot and clears the carry, which is the same release action as the C++ loop body, but it does not loop over all companions or check the owner range, and would.CompanionsDrift loops over companions and releases the ones that leave, but only through mood logic.

what: Moves the party one square forward in the facing direction onto the ethereal portal's destination, then kills any living member whose new square is solid rock (DeathState::Rock) and shows a rock message.
ev: StepThrough matches the core of the C++ function (step one square forward in the facing direction, then test that new square for rock and report it), but it does not kill living members or show the rock message, and it wraps at the map edge, which the C++ does not do; the C++ also moves every member's location and applies DeathState::Rock in the same pass, which no candidate does as a single function.

what: Returns the text a mod has stored under a given key for that mod, or an empty string if nothing is stored.
ev: GetText returns the stored text for the key, or "" when nothing is stored, which matches the C++ result; it gets the mod id from its bound instance rather than as a parameter, and the underlying ModSettingsStore.Read does the same lookup but returns null instead of "".

what: Decides whether a character can cast a level-0 item spell, returning the first failing reason among not knowing the spell, lacking the guild level to reach it, or missing required stats, or no refusal if all pass.
ev: For `itemLevel == 0` it runs the same ordered checks (known via a guild with a rate and a spell ceiling reaching the level, then guild level reaching the spell level, then required stats) and returns NotKnown, SpellLevel, or Stat, with the stat check only partly visible in the truncated candidate.

what: Reports whether a character is dead by checking that their death state is anything other than Alive, which the game's rules use to gate actions like looting, climbing, and chest opening.
ev: The method returns early on `_ch.IsDead`, the same dead-or-not gate that `isDead` expresses, but the predicate itself (the `Character.IsDead` definition) is not among the candidates.

what: When the quicksand hazard (R73) fires, it picks a random item slot from 1 to 39 and reports the quicksand message if that slot holds an item, though the outcome itself is left unimplemented.
ev: The candidate rolls a random pack slot on quicksand and removes an item from it, which is related to the C++ slot roll, but the C++ function only reports that the slot is occupied and does not destroy anything, and the candidate's slot range (1 to 39) is produced differently from `pickItemSlot`.

what: Implements R25 of the Mordor rules by returning false when a monster group has a live join offer, so that group does not roll for engagement.
ev: No candidate decides whether a group rolls for engagement; they only display the join offer (JoinLine), accept it (AcceptJoin), generate or store it (FillGroup, Finish, Capture, Take), or wait on it (ShowWaiting, JoinTheFight), and none returns a roll gate based on JoinOffer.

what: Computes a character's experience points needed to reach a given level in Mordor, using the R13 formula scaled by the guild's EP factor and the race factor, without rounding.
ev: Fn12A1 gives the XP needed to leave a level (so `Fn12A1(L-1)` matches the C++ result for level L) using the original loop with Currency rounding, while the C++ function is the unrounded R13 closed form, and Fn12A1's own docstring says that closed form is off by one in 12 of 16,800 cases.

what: Computes the hit points a guild member gains on level-up or advance: the fixed maximum-hits value at or above the guild's max level, otherwise a base increment plus a 2/3-chance random bonus and the Constitution bonus.
ev: It implements the same level-up hits rule (MH at or past the cap, otherwise AH plus a 2-in-3 random slice plus a CON bonus), but it adds a rule that gives nothing when another guild is already ahead, uses a different chance draw, and limits the CON bonus to CON above 16 and below the cap, where the C++ applies ConHitsBonus to any guild below ML.

what: Computes the natural logarithm of a value, used by the game's melee rules (per VB Ln) in formulas such as the scaled-magnitude and protection calculations.
ev: The C++ `lnOf` is a bare natural log, and no candidate computes one; `GroupGold` and `ProtectionBonus` call `Math.Log` only inside larger game formulas (gold scaling and the fn13FE protection bonus), so they do not do the same thing.

what: Rolls a percentage check against the chance of recognising an item, computed from the character's skill and whether the item is in darkness.
ev: The candidate computes the same recognise chance from skill and darkness that the C++ wrapper passes to `rng.percent`, but no candidate performs the percentage roll itself, so the tick check is only partly covered.

what: Returns true when a chest trap either kills the whole party or teleports them, which means the chest's gold and treasure payout is cancelled (rule R33).
ev: The candidate handles both outcomes, returning early on a teleport (`ChestTeleport`) and before the gold and treasure step when the party is killed, but it is a full chest-opening routine rather than the boolean predicate `trapStopsPayout`, and no candidate returns the kill-or-teleport check on its own.

what: Returns true when a companion's spell aimed at foes is blocked because the caster itself has magic immunity, per the rule R34 quirk noted in the source.
ev: For a companion caster (`compDef != null`), this method zeroes the damage when `MonsterProperty.Has(compDef, 2)` is true, which is the same caster-own-magic-immunity test as the C++ predicate, but it is embedded in a damage calculation rather than returned as a standalone blocked flag.

what: Parses a typed gold amount for the Library/bank transfer, accepting decimal or &H hex forms, rounding fractions half-to-even as VB's CLng does, and refusing values outside the Long range.
ev: CLng is the same VB CLng conversion (trim blanks, &H/&O hex, whole-string parse, half-to-even rounding, Overflow to null), but it accepts thousands separators under the current culture, which the C++ refuses, and it does not apply the C++ 16-bit sign-extension for hex literals of four or fewer digits (the [c62] quirk).

what: Computes the chance of rescuing a body in the dungeon from the dungeon level, adding a bonus when easy-find applies and capping the chance at 100 on level 1 areas 18 and lower.
ev: It repeats the C++ chance formula (16 - level, doubled when easy-to-find, floored at 0.1) and the level-1 area-18 ceiling, but it uses the ceiling to scale a per-day roll and returns a day count, not a capped chance value as `rescueChance` does.

what: Computes the rescue threshold in days for a given level as ln(level)^2 × 100 + 21, clamping levels below 1 to 1.
ev: It computes the same threshold, `Math.Log(level) * Math.Log(level) * 100 + 21`, but only inline as part of the day-by-day loop that picks the ceiling, and it returns 0 for levels below 1 instead of clamping them to 1.

what: Maps a random roll against two box-chance thresholds, each shifted by a bonus, to pick the treasure class for a chest (class 2 or 3, or none if the roll misses both).
ev: Both walk the two box thresholds in order, with a later match overwriting an earlier one, and return 2 or 3 or none; the candidate derives the bonus from the lair flag rather than taking it as a parameter, which is a structural difference only.

what: Rolls a uniform random number of take carriers from 1 to kSeerTakeMax for the Seer's take effect, a stand-in until the real take formula from the Formulas table is available.
ev: Carriers also picks a random number of carriers for the Seer to name, but it derives that count from the size of the found list (clamped to 1..3) rather than the uniform 1..kSeerTakeMax the C++ stub assumes, and it also builds the sentence.

what: Computes the Mordor level modifier for a monster from its guild level as the truncated value of level × ln(level + 1), a formula used in breath/acid/electrocution damage.
ev: GroupAttacks computes the same expression inline for breath (`VbInt(monLvl * Math.Log(monLvl + 1))`) but as part of a larger method rather than as a standalone level-modifier function, and no candidate implements the function on its own.

what: Decides whether a monster can appear in an encounter by checking that its kind is allowed by the area's spawn mask and that its level-found does not exceed the encounter floor for the viewer's level and stud-square status.
ev: DrawOne keeps only monsters with LevelFound <= floor, which matches the level check, but it has no area spawn-mask test, no index bounds check, no stud-adjusted floor, and it picks a monster by chance rather than returning a yes/no eligibility answer.

what: Ethereal Portal (R20) moves the caster two squares forward through the wall in front, by calling the shared displacement routine with a 0 offset and a distance of 2, and stops rather than hanging if rock lies behind the wall.
ev: StepThrough is Ethereal Portal's step in the facing direction, ignoring walls and leaving the caster on rock if it is rock, but it moves one square with map-edge wrapping, while the C++ `etherealPortal` moves two squares via `displaceWithin(0, 2)`, and no candidate does the two-square displacement.

what: Changes the party's dungeon level by one floor up or down when they stand on a matching staircase square, handling the exit to town, the level-limit check, arrival placement, exploration marking, and time cost.
ev: UseStairs takes the stairs the party stands on, handles level 1 going to town, and calls ChangeLevel, but it takes no delta, its level-limit and arrival-square logic is outside the snippet, and the visible text does not show the time cost or exploration marking.

what: Applies resting-time aging by computing the days a character ages from their current and maximum hit points, adding them to the character's age, and announcing the passage of time to the player.
ev: RestInCity uses the same rest-aging formula (days proportional to missing hits, with Hits set to MaxHits and Age increased), but it also clears spells, poison, and disease and handles the city arrival, and no candidate returns the same days value or emits the "Time passes while resting." message.

what: Charges a Seer's locate fee to the payer through CharPay (with the bank covering any shortfall), but only if the payer can afford it, returning false without charging otherwise.
where: Mordor.App/CityWindow.axaml.cs CityWindow.LocatePerson (its affordability test is CityWindow.CanPay, candidate 7)
ev: LocatePerson does the same check-then-CharPay sequence for the Seer's locate fee, but it also asks for confirmation, refreshes the UI, saves, and shows the Seer's reply, and it returns nothing instead of a bool; no candidate is a plain helper that only checks affordability, charges through CharPay, and returns success or failure.

what: Scales a spell's base magnitude by the caster's sheet factors (C × Q × R × kSheetFactor divided by SL, minus a small epsilon, floored), never letting the result drop below the base value, and returns the base unchanged if SL is zero or negative.
ev: No candidate computes a spell's scaled magnitude from C×Q×R×kSheetFactor/SL with the floor, epsilon, and base-value floor; the nearest, Mordor.Core/Spells.cs Spells.Cost, computes a spell's price through Rules.Fn1485Price, which is a different quantity.

what: Looks up the map square at 1-based coordinates (x, y) on a dungeon floor, returning nullptr when the coordinates fall outside the 30-wide grid or past the stored squares.
ev: That local function looks up a square by 1-based linear index with a range check and returns its wall flags (or 0 out of range), which matches the core of `viewSquare`, but it takes a single index instead of (x, y), has no 30-column check on x, and returns 0 rather than nullptr.

what: When a mod hook throws, marks that mod as disabled and posts a player-facing message saying the hook failed and was turned off.
ev: Guard disables the mod when its hook throws (via `Fault`, whose body isn't shown), but none of the candidates posts a player-facing "hook failed and has been disabled" message with the load order; they only log.

what: Rolls a percentile check against the companion's chance to leave (never true for ForLife companions), returning whether the companion departs.
where: Mordor.Core/CompanionMood.cs Step.Round (with Mordor.Core/Character.cs Binding.ChanceToLeave supplying the chance)
ev: Step.Round skips bound-for-life companions and rolls against Binding.ChanceToLeave, but it also drifts the binding level, forces a leave at zero binding, and compares a 0-200 roll (`NextDouble() * 200`) instead of the C++ 0-100 roll, so it does not return the same bool.

what: Computes the highest item level a quest can award for a guild, by taking the quest monster level cap, dividing by 1.5, adding 1, flooring the result, and clamping it to the game's maximum quest item level (kQuestItemLevelCap).
ev: QuestItemBand computes `(int)(tier / 1.5) + 1`, the same floor(x/1.5)+1 as the C++ function, but it takes the tier directly and has no explicit clamp to kQuestItemLevelCap, which only matters for tiers above 10 that its caller (QuestTier) never produces.

what: Returns the character's chance to leave the party, taken from the stored raw value and clamped to the allowed range the rules specify.
ev: The candidate also clamps a leave chance, but it computes the raw value from binding level, guild levels, Charisma, and hits rather than reading a stored value, and its 0–90 clamp is not confirmed to match the C++ clamp range.

what: Computes the opening spell-charge cost for a charm by multiplying the spell's cost ratio by the charm's opening spell level and by 1.9, then truncating to an integer (rule R35).
ev: Fn1485Price is the general spell-point price formula (rate × level × 1.9-style multiplier, floored), which is the same underlying arithmetic as the C++ R35 charm-opening cost, but it takes level, u4, rate and sl rather than the C++ inputs (slInit, scRatio), and it floors exactly instead of using the C++ "- 0.0001" epsilon.

what: Returns true when a drag swap between two companions must be refused because either one is dead or in a non-normal death state, per the SRD rule notes [c8] and [c55].
ev: Rearrange refuses the drag swap when either companion is dead, matching the C++ check, but it tests only `IsDead` (not the non-normal `deathState`) and is a larger function that also performs the swap and returns a message string rather than a bool.

what: Decides whether a character's wear-class limit blocks equipping another item of that class: no limit (-1) never blocks, a limit of 0 always blocks, and a positive limit blocks once the number already worn reaches it.
ev: The cap check `max > 0 && WornOfClass(cls, item) >= max` matches the positive-limit branch of `wearClassFull`, but it is embedded in a larger function that also checks hands, guilds, level and stats, and it returns "Using too Many!" instead of a bool. It also never returns true for a limit of 0, which the C++ function does.

what: When the owner's order is refused after an empty item, it flips the companion's combat order between Defend and Fight (anything not Defend becomes Defend), clears the order target, and tells the player the companion refuses the order.
ev: It makes the same None/Fight-to-Defend and Defend-to-Fight flip, but it sends a queued spell order to Fight where the C++ sends it to Defend, it leaves the order target in place instead of setting it to -1, and it does not emit the "refuses the order" message.

what: Handles the player's typed "char" command in the options screen, parsing a party member number and a character option name, then either reporting that option's current on/off state or setting it and returning a confirmation message.
ev: The C++ charCommand parses a party member and character option name to report or set a per-member on/off feature flag in featureState, but no candidate does this: the closest, CombatOrder.ApplyDefault, reads a character's combat setting, and the rest are item, drag, key, and tab handlers.

what: Computes the breath-weapon damage modifier for a monster from its guild level relative to the character's guild level, using a logarithmic level-modifier formula from the game's rules (R39).
ev: No candidate computes the R39 LN(LevelMod)/LN(1.08) breath modifier; the closest, CombatEngine.GroupAttacks in Mordor.Core/MonsterAttack.cs, has a breath branch but its visible part uses a level-based chance and `VbInt(monLvl * Math.Log(monLvl + 1))`, and the rest is truncated.

what: Recomputes the character's protection value from the level of their active guild by calling protectionRecompute, storing the result in the character's combat protection stat.
ev: It derives protection from the guild level (`c.Guild.Level / 2 + 1`), but only when the Protect bit is set, and it writes `c.Protection` rather than the C++ `combat.protection` from an unconditional `protectionRecompute(activeLevel)`.

what: Decides whether a monster group encounter loop ends, returning true only when the party is solo (size 1), matching the original game's rule rather than the port's alternative check.
ev: The C++ function is a loop-exit predicate that ends the monster group loop only when the party is solo (size 1), and no candidate implements that exit condition; CombatEngine.MonsterAttacks shares the same party-size/UBound(Chars) context from MULTIMOD.BAS but targets a group's attack selection, not whether the loop exits, so it is only a related piece of the same loop.

what: Computes the seer's fee for a given character level as a base fee multiplied by the level, rounded half-to-even.
ev: It uses the same base constant (132567.52) and a deterministic per-level fee, but multiplies by `Log(level + 1) * level` instead of the C++ linear `base * level`, and truncates with a cast rather than rounding half-to-even.

what: Decides whether an item of the given type must be equipped before its spell can be used, returning true for types 1–22 and 29, 32, 33, and 34.
ev: It tests the same condition, `(Type >= 1 && Type <= 22) || Type == 29 || Type == 32 || Type == 33 || Type == 34`, and likewise leaves out type 0, so it returns the same result for every item type.

what: Checks whether a typed word is a valid companion slot number from 1 to kCompanionSlots, and the slots are fixed in place (never compacted) per rule R67.
ev: The C++ function parses a typed word and range-checks it to 1..kCompanionSlots, but no candidate parses user input or validates a typed slot number; they handle slot storage, acid targeting, naming, and JSON loading.

what: Reports whether an item of the given type must be equipped before it can be used, covering item types 1–22 plus 29, 32, 33 and 34 (type 0 is excluded).
ev: The candidate tests the same item-type set as the C++ function (1 to 22, plus 29, 32, 33 and 34, with type 0 excluded), differing only in taking an `Item` instead of an `i32`.

what: Computes a companion's blow damage modifier by adding the companion's critical-hit bonus, derived from its special property flags, to the base damage modifier (SRD rule R28).
ev: CompanionStrikes derives a companion's crit bonus from its special-attack flag bit 10 (+4) and builds the blow modifier from the companion's damage mod, which is the same idea as the C++ function, but it is a full blow routine rather than a pure "damMod + crit bonus" helper, and no candidate exposes that exact two-input computation.

what: When a joiner arrives from a fight, it takes on the front monster's current and maximum hits instead of its own.
ev: Each companion that joins is built from the front monster's `Hits` and `MaxHits` (the doc comment says "they all arrive with the front one's hits and its rolled maximum"), which matches the C++ helper's outcome, though the candidate sets this inline and falls back to `Hits` when `MaxHits` is zero, and the companion initializer is truncated in the excerpt.

what: Ends an action run by closing the current context and marking the run as no longer active.
ev: The C++ `finishActionRun` only sets `run.active = false` after closing a context, and none of the eight candidates ends a run by clearing an active flag; the closest, `ModHost.RunActions`/`Run`, run mod hooks and close each context in a `finally`, but they never mark a run as inactive.

what: Carries a character home by setting their dungeon level to 0 and their area to -1, leaving their X and Y position unchanged, as the game's rescue rules define.
ev: It sets `DungeonLevel = 0` and `Area = -1` and leaves X and Y alone, exactly as the C++ function does, but it also takes a `days` argument and adds it to `Age`, which the C++ function does not do.

what: Returns the value a character contributes to one of the Hall of Records categories (maxHits for Constitution, total experience for Most Experience, gold on hand plus in bank for Wealthiest, otherwise the matching ability score).
ev: No candidate maps a record kind to a character's value: the callers (CityWindow's OfferRecords, CheckWealthiest, and OfferSkillRecords) consume such values but don't compute them, StatRecord goes from index to Kind, and the Wealthiest caller passes bank gold alone rather than gold on hand plus in bank.

what: Registers the town-screen "seer" player command, which lets the player search for a creature, item, or person for a fee, with "seer yes" and "seer no" to answer the Seer's pending offer.
where: Mordor.App/CityWindow.axaml.cs CityWindow.ShowSeer (with CityWindow.Locate as the inner command handler)
ev: The C++ function only registers the "seer" town command and its dispatch (search for creature/item/person, plus yes/no), while the candidates implement the Seer's behaviour itself: ShowSeer and its inner Locate handle monster and item searches with fees, Seer.Fee and LocateCharacterFee compute the charges, and LocatePerson covers the person search, so the registration and "seer yes/no" command parsing have no direct counterpart and none of the candidates is an exact match.

what: Returns the percent chance of a breath fire attack, at 80 if the lead foe's guild level is more than a quarter above the companion's, 20 if it is well below, and the base 50 otherwise.
where: Mordor.Core/Combat.cs CompanionRound / CompanionCombat.CompanionBreathes (the class containing `CompanionBreathes`; the exact enclosing class name isn't shown in the excerpt)
ev: `CompanionBreathes` picks the same 50/80/20 chance from the lead foe's guild level against the companion's, but its "much weaker" test is `lead < comp - comp/4` (a difference), while the C++ uses `lead * 1.25 < comp` (a ratio), so the 20% outcome can differ for some level pairs, and it also embeds a dice roll and attack that the C++ function doesn't.

what: Computes the percent chance that a paralysis effect lands on a character by adding the resistance percentage to the character's CON, then clamping the result between a floor and a cap (the floor and cap constants are defined elsewhere).
ev: It is in the same paralysis domain and also combines resistance and CON, but it is a per-tick wear-off roll using log-scaled hold and fight terms, not `clamp(resist + con, 5, 95)`, and no candidate computes that clamp.

what: Moves a creature or party one square in the given compass direction (north decreases y, east increases x, south increases y, west decreases x), wrapping around at the map edge.
ev: Both move the position one square in the facing direction and wrap at each map edge, but StepThrough also returns whether the destination is rock, and it wraps with explicit bounds checks rather than `wrapMapCoord`.

what: Returns the defence value unchanged when the defender is not defending, and otherwise scales it by a defend factor (engine comment says x1.5) to produce the defending defence in combat.
ev: It computes the same base defence but has no defending flag and deliberately omits the x1.5 defend bonus (calling it dead code in the original), whereas the C++ function applies x1.5 when defending.

what: Rolls the number of monster groups in an encounter from the lead monster's NumGroups, with a chance (per R16) to subtract a random cut, then clamps the result to the allowed 1–4 range.
ev: No candidate rolls a group count from NumGroups, applies the chance-based cut, or clamps to 1–4; the closest (CombatEngine.AliveGroups, CombatMonster.Runs, and RefreshCombat) only split an existing monster list into runs of the same kind, and the rest cover unrelated mechanics.

what: Decides whether a companion is still able to act in combat, which is true only while its hit points are above zero (rule R22.1).
ev: The hit-point test `c.CurHits > 0` appears here, but only inside a loop that selects the next member, and it is combined with `!c.IsDead` and `!c.Stoned`, so it is not a standalone "can act" check like `companionCanAct`.

what: Steps one square ahead in the facing direction and kills the ethereal character if the square they land on is rock, using the preferred engine's rule R25.
ev: StepThrough steps one square the way you face and returns whether that square is rock, as the C++ does, but it wraps at the map edge instead of returning no kill off-map and ignores walls, whereas the C++ uses squareAhead, which stops at walls (candidate 3 has that function but never tests for rock).

what: Applies the Teleport spell's displacement move: it computes the target square from the party's facing and offsets, runs the arrival test, and either moves the party there (changing level or settling the area) or applies the failed-teleport consequences.
ev: TeleportTo matches only the target computation (facing-relative right/forwards offsets, wrap, and the clamped down-level), while the arrival test is in Outcome.ForSpell, the failed-teleport handling in DungeonWindow.TeleportedIntoRock, and the move-and-settle step in ChangeLevel and SettleArea, so no single candidate does the whole function.

what: Rolls d100 against a character's resistance to poison or disease and, if the roll beats it while the affliction level is still zero, sets the affliction level and announces the affliction to the player.
ev: The chest-trap poison and disease branch sets the poison or disease level from a resistance check, but it uses a different roll (half the resistance, reversed), skips the level-is-zero test, and announces nothing, so it is a related variant rather than the shared afflict routine.

what: Decides who receives town income from a sale: the party member named by the TownIncomeBank mod answer if it is a valid party index, otherwise the selling character.
ev: Both return the first mod's TownIncomeBank answer when it names a party member, and otherwise fall back to the seller's hand, though the C# returns null for that fallback where the C++ returns sellerIndex.

what: Returns whether the limited-release splash should be shown, which is true only if the build variant supports the limited prefix and the MORDOR.INI [Loading Information] Limited flag is set.
where: Mordor.Core/GameOptions.cs PortSettings.Load (closest, but it reads the port's own settings file, not MORDOR.INI, and does not gate a splash)
ev: No candidate decides whether to show the limited splash from the MORDOR.INI [Loading Information] Limited flag. PortSettings.Load reads a "Limited" key from a different INI, and LimitedVersion.Apply sets the limited mode from the folder check rather than from an INI flag.

what: Morgue Grab Body (R30.3) lets the party's selected member take up a dead character as their carry, recording the dead character's name on that member and marking the party's carrying slot as holding a dead character, with no Hide test required.
ev: Like morgueGrabBody, it is the morgue's Grab Body with no Hide test and nothing already carried put down, and it sets the selected character's carried-character name to the chosen body; it differs in taking the name through a picker instead of a parameter and in clearing the companion slot rather than setting a carry-slot enum.

what: Forfeits a player character's membership in a guild by clearing its experience and quest progress, marking it unjoined, reverting the active guild to Nomad if it was the one left, and posting a "You have left the guild" message.
ev: ForfeitQuest resets the active guild's quest fields and recomputes equipment, but it demotes the character by a cost instead of clearing experience and unjoining the guild, and it has no fallback of the active guild to Nomad.

what: On arrival at a square, if the leader is lost, it ends the lost state when the square is already mapped, and otherwise lets the party try to work out where they are, then syncs the party's lost flags.
ev: It covers the same arrival logic (work out where you are when lost, end the lost state on mapped ground, then sync the party's lost flags), but it runs the rolls before the mapped-ground check rather than after, so a lost leader on mapped ground can get the "figured out" messages where the C++ would only say "found yourself".

what: Removes one randomly drawn item from a shop's stock as a buy-out, making up to maxDraws random picks (unbounded if negative) and accepting the first draw, since the acceptance test is not yet specified.
ev: No candidate draws a random stock item, removes it, and gives up after a draw cap; the closest, `DrawOne`, makes a weighted monster pick without removing anything, and `DepletedByBuying` only decides whether a purchase takes an item off the shelf.

what: Returns true unless the companion joined freely, so that bind spells only take effect on companions who did not join of their own will (rule R49).
ev: No candidate tests `joinedFreely`, but BindEnter refuses binding when `c.BindingLevel < 0` with "FreeWillCannotBind", a related R49 check that uses a different field and sits inside a UI handler rather than a predicate.

what: Checks whether a character meets every stat requirement for an item, returning false if any current stat falls below the item's required value for that stat.
ev: EquipProblem's final loop returns a stat refusal when any current `Stats[i]` is below `it.StatsRequired[i]`, which is the same check as the C++ function, but EquipProblem also tests hands, guild, and guild level and returns a message rather than a bool.

what: Computes what the store charges the player to buy one copy of an item, in whole gold, using the store's shelf count and the reference price formula (list price at floor 0, otherwise shelf-count dependent).
ev: The shelf-count and floor-0 buy-price formula matches the C++ `storeBuyPrice`, but PriceOf returns the raw value with no division by 10000 to get whole gold, and it takes an alignment argument that the C++ signature does not have.

what: Computes the attack and defence bonuses a character gains on reaching a given level for a guild, using a placeholder linear interpolation from zero up to the guild's maximum at the maximum level, rather than the real SRD per-level rule.
ev: Both take a guild and level and return the attack and defence granted, but the C++ is a linear-interpolation placeholder that its own comment says does not match the real rule, while GuildAD reads the per-level award interval and caps from the data and reproduces the published tables.

what: Rolls a save against a destruction chance for a random pack slot 1–39, and if the save fails and that slot holds an item, clears it and announces "Item destroyed."
ev: Both pick a random pack slot from 1 to 39 and destroy the item there, but the candidate triggers only on quicksand after its own roll, with no save against a destruction chance, and it requires `ChestTraps.Destructible`, which the C++ function does not check.

what: Returns the complication percentage for a failed non-rock rescue raise, which is currently stubbed to always be 0 pending a race lifespan field, so failed raises never complicate.
ev: It implements the same reference formula the C++ comment cites, (ageDays / 365) / (lifespan / 2) * 100, but the C++ stub always returns 0 until a race lifespan field exists, so the outcomes differ.

what: Opens or closes a quest for a party member and guild by setting or clearing that quest's flag in the session's feature state.
ev: No candidate sets or clears a per-member, per-guild quest-open flag in session feature state; the nearest, `OpenWindow.SetWanted`, toggles a mod window's open flag, and the quest candidates either mark completion or only read quest state.

what: Blocks an Elf character from using an item that requires great strength, returning false in that case and true otherwise.
ev: No candidate checks the character's race or an Elf restriction; the nearest, Character.EquipProblem, applies guild and stat-minimum refusals to every character regardless of race, so it does not match the C++ Elf-only great-strength block.

what: Returns the larger of two numbers, which callers use to take the greater of two stone-related chance or value figures when resolving petrification in the game.
ev: Candidate 6 is the only one that deals with taking the larger of two figures in the petrification-related context, but it actually concerns hit-point gains on level-up rather than a max-of-two-values helper, so the match is only partial at best and the C++ `maxD` (a plain `a > b ? a : b`) has no direct counterpart among the candidates.

what: Returns the monster group that is currently in play for the companion's round: the combat monsters when a fight is underway, otherwise the waiting group (per rule R41.1).
ev: No candidate is a standalone equivalent, but LetCompanionGo (and CompanionsDrift) inline the same selection, `var live = _combat?.Monsters ?? _waiting;`, which picks the combat monsters when a fight exists and the waiting group otherwise, just embedded in a larger method rather than returning the group itself.

what: When a player's character kills a monster, it offers that monster to the Hall of Records as a candidate for the "Deadliest Creature" record, comparing its power against the current holder and noting whether the party was solo.
ev: Check runs the same Deadliest Creature comparison by monster power, stores the monster id, and handles the holder's own record, but it omits the member lookup, the explicit day serial, and the `alone` announce path that hallRecordKill delegates to hallCheck, and it always returns silently for this kind, which may not match the C++ announce behavior.

what: Rolls a random number and returns true when it falls below half the character's poison resistance (scaled to a percentage), deciding whether poison takes the character's chest-trap gold or item.
ev: Spring's poison-gas case makes the same roll (`rng.NextDouble() * 100 < ResistancePercent / 2.0`) and keeps the same backwards "<" comparison, but it sits inside a larger trap dispatcher and sets the Poisoned flag on each character instead of returning a bool that decides whether poison takes gold or an item.

what: Simulates searching for a body that has been killed in the dungeon, returning the number of days it takes for the body to be found (capped at the rescue day limit), by repeatedly rolling a daily chance of discovery.
ev: Both loop day by day, return the first day the body is found, and stop at the 2,000,000-day cap, though the C++ returns exactly the cap while the C# can return one past it and returns 0 for levels below 1, and the C# inlines the daily roll rather than calling a separate `rollBodyFoundToday`, which I could not check.

what: Decides whether a slime attack has any effect by comparing a slime roll against a threshold of 50 plus twice the dungeon level, so deeper levels make slime strikes more likely to hit.
ev: No candidate computes a slime roll against a 50 + 2×level threshold; Candidate 2 only mentions "the same roll the Slime" in a comment about picking a pack slot, and Candidate 3 only maps the slime monster kind to a sound name.

what: Computes the race experience multiplier f = ((ln r / ln(r+1)) + 1) − 0.7 + r/25 from the race's experience factor plus one, which scales experience awards for a character's race in the Mordor rules (SRD c05p1).
ev: Fn12A1 contains the same race multiplier expression, ((Log(l038C)/Log(l038C+1))+1) - .7 + l038C/25 with l038C = raceExp+1, but only as a step inside a larger guild experience-for-level calculation, and no candidate computes the multiplier on its own.

what: Computes the guild level equivalent of a spell level as spell level × 2 − 1, a game formula from the SRD casting rules (c106), though whether the result is a cost or a level is still marked unknown.
ev: Rules.SpellLevel is the inverse direction, computing Int(guildLevel / 2 + 0.5) to get a spell level from a guild level, while the C++ function computes spellLevel * 2 - 1 to get a guild level from a spell level, and no candidate implements that forward formula.

what: Computes how well an item's alignment fits a character's alignment, returning Full for unaligned items or matching alignments, Half for one step apart, and Subtract for two steps apart (Good versus Evil).
ev: FitFor returns Fine for unaligned items or matching alignments, Adjacent for one step apart, and Opposed when Party.Opposed (Good against Evil), which map to the C++ Full, Half and Subtract classes.

what: Computes the experience points required to reach a given level, combining the guild's experience penalty and the race's experience modifier with the 1995 Mordor level-curve formula (R21).
ev: Both compute the experience needed for the next level from the guild and race experience factors, but Fn12A1 is a loop-based port of the original VB routine rather than the closed-form R21 formula, and its docstring says the closed form disagrees with it in 12 of 16,800 guild/race/level cases.

what: Returns the Nomad guild's value for a given level, which is 10 at level 1, 10 + 1.5×level for even levels 2 through 30, and 0 for all other levels.
ev: No candidate returns the fixed sheet value (10 at level 1, 10 + 1.5×level for even levels 2–30, else 0); the closest, Rules.GuildAD, computes attack/defence awarded by level from the guild-level formula, which is a different quantity.

what: Parses the typed "pen buy <row> <member>" command, validating its arguments and producing the player's error messages before handing the purchase to the confinement-buy routine.
ev: No candidate parses a "pen buy <row> <member>" argument list or produces its usage and row/member error messages; Confinement.Take only decrements one pen count (a piece of what confinementBuyRow does after validation), and the ClickRow and IdEnter handlers are GUI paths.

what: Decides whether the owner may choose a body for the carried item, which is allowed only when the carry slot is empty or holds a companion (carry index below the companion slot count).
ev: Run opens with the same gate, `who.CarryingCompanion < four` (with an extra `CarryingCharacter == ""` check), but it then goes on to pick and carry a companion, so no candidate is a standalone predicate that answers whether the carry choice is open.

what: Rolls a 40% chance, using the context's RNG, for whether a character gets the quest class head start.
ev: The C++ function is a single 40% RNG percent roll for the quest class head start, and no candidate draws a 40% chance for a head start; the closest, Rules.cs table.QuestMonster, uses a 40% roll (`Math.Floor(rng.NextDouble() * 100) < 40`) but only to choose between the class's first monster and -1 inside a loop that picks a quest monster, so it does not do the same thing.

what: Decides whether a party member falls down a chute, which happens unless the character is levitating and the rules say they hover over the pit at this dungeon level.
ev: Floats returns the negation of the C++ fall test (levitating && hovers, where the C++ returns !(levitating && hovers)), but its C# `&&` short-circuits and skips the Rules.HoversOverPit roll for non-levitating members, whereas the C++ comment says VB's `And` draws the roll for every member, so the RNG state diverges.

what: Returns a race's normalized racial penalty factor r (Human = 1.0), looked up from the SRD penalty table, which feeds into the experience required for advancement.
ev: Candidate 7 is the experience-for-next-level routine, which is a different function from `racialPenalty`, which only looks up the race's penalty factor r in table T5; it is the closest related code because it consumes the race's Exp field, but no candidate returns the normalized racial penalty value itself.

what: Resolves which guild membership a quest, claim, or titles command acts on by preferring the character's active joined guild, otherwise the first joined guild, and reports that guild back to the caller.
ev: No candidate resolves a membership by preferring the active joined guild and falling back to the first joined guild, and returns both the membership and the guild; the closest, Character.QuestSatisfied, only reads the active `Guild` property and never picks or returns a membership.

what: Finds the next loaded, enabled mod hook at or after the given index, in load order, so that hooks run in the order the mods were loaded; returns -1 if none remain.
ev: RunActions walks the hooked live mods in load order and runs each one's hook, skipping any that are no longer running, which covers the iteration that nextHookedMod supports, but it never returns a next index and does not use afterIndex.

what: Applies the rock death outcome to a party member by killing the character with the Rock death state and cause, flagged as a rule-driven death.
ev: Candidate 8 sets `CauseOfDeath = Rules.DeathRock` and calls `Kill` on each victim, which is the rock-death kill step, but it is embedded in a walk-into-rock flow with map and automap writes and no direct equivalent of `killCharacter`'s Rock state and rule-driven flag.

what: Computes the award-level step for Mordor's experience progression by dividing half the experience cap plus an accuracy term by the adjusted award-level interval, rounding the result to an integer (returning 0 if the divisor is zero).
ev: AdInterval contains the same per-step formula, `Round(((HitsCapLevel/2.0) + acc/18) / (AdEvery + bonus))` with half-even rounding, but embeds it in a loop over levels and has no zero-divisor guard, so it does not compute the single step the C++ function returns.

what: Builds a game context view for const callers by casting away const on the session and returning its non-const context, so the read-only rule helpers (createBase, creationPool, statCeiling) used during character creation can run against game state without mutating it.
ev: No candidate builds a read-only context view from a session by casting away const to return its non-const context; the closest, CharacterCreationWindow.Roll, only resets character stats during creation and does not touch session context access.

what: Given a hook's status, it decides whether the original game answer is used: only an Ok status lets the mod's decision stand, while a null decision or a throw falls back to the original's answer (rule R12.3).
ev: The C++ function maps a hook status to a boolean (use the original answer unless status is Ok), but no candidate maps a status to a fallback decision; the closest, ModHost.Guard-based methods like AskShortfall and ArrivedInTown, handle null or throw fallback inline with no separate status-to-bool check, so they are related but not equivalent.

what: Draws the chance for a companion to successfully cast a spell: level-1 casters succeed 40% of the time, other levels 100%, and a companion with no cast level never casts.
ev: No candidate gates a companion's cast on its cast level with a 40% chance at level 1 and 100% otherwise; Candidate 2 (Combat.cs CompanionCasts) is the closest companion-casting path but uses only the mishap roll, and Candidate 3's CastSpellDraw is an unconditional draw for a character's own cast.

what: Clamps a floating-point value to the inclusive range [lo, hi], returning the nearest bound when the value falls outside it; used here to keep a monster's proc chance within its allowed limits.
ev: No candidate is a standalone clamp, but ChanceToLeave ends with `Math.Clamp(x, 0, 90)`, which clamps a percent chance to a fixed range as clampF does, though the surrounding companion-abandonment computation and the monster-proc context differ.

what: Decides whether a creature is the lair monster of an area by checking that the area has a nonzero lair id and the creature's id matches it.
ev: Locate contains the same lair test (`area.LairId > 0 && area.LairId == def.Id`) but only as one step in a placement search that adds a 75% roll and then picks a random area, so no candidate is a standalone equivalent of `isLairMonster`.

what: Returns the item-use factor for a guild, with Nomad at 0.8 and Healer at 1.5 and 1.0 as a placeholder default for the other guilds whose values are unknown.
ev: No candidate maps a guild to its item-use factor. UseLevel only reads the factor from `GuildDef.ItemUseFactor` and turns it into a level requirement, while the C++ function hardcodes Nomad 0.8, Healer 1.5, and a 1.0 default, and the OpenDejenol factor comes from loaded game data.

what: Applies the R8 morgue fee step for a dead character's payer: if the guild covers the raise fee it is waived, otherwise the payer is refused with "Not Enough Gold!" when short, or the fee is charged from their purse.
ev: Visit contains the same fee step (a guild-paid raise is free, a short purse gets "Not Enough Gold!" in a SORRY! box and nothing is taken, otherwise the cost is charged), but it is embedded in a larger routine that also shows the Yes/No offer and runs the raise, and it does not return a MorgueFeeOutcome.

what: Disables a mod for the rest of the session after it faults, marking it faulted with a reason, deactivating it, and emitting events so the host removes its Harmony patches and the original rule answer is used instead.
ev: Both mark the mod faulted with a reason, remove its Harmony patches, log the fault, and notify the game, with the same session-only disabling; the C++ takes the reason as input and sets `active = false` explicitly, while Fault builds the reason from the call site and exception and does not visibly clear an Active flag.

what: On a player attack, it builds the hit-check arguments with the monster's Defense set to 0 and the character's Defense set to the given value (rule R19).
ev: SwingOnce's comment says the original passes the monster's defence as an unassigned local, which is 0 on a player blow (MODULE4.BAS:433), matching the monsterDefense = 0 part of R19, but no candidate builds the hit-check args or sets the character's Defense to the given value.

what: Returns a monster's floor by reading its levelFound field, standing in for a floor value that the game data does not define on MonsterDef.
ev: Locate reads `mon!.LevelFound` as the monster's floor (`int level = monster ? mon!.LevelFound : item!.Floor`), which is the same field read the C++ does, but only as one step inside a larger Seer lookup, and no candidate is a standalone accessor that returns LevelFound as the floor.

what: Applies fog to a square by clearing its wall and door flags, so the square stays but its walls and doors are no longer shown (per rule c27).
ev: In fog, `Square` keeps the square's feature bits and skips its wall and door edges, which mirrors `applyFog`'s intent, but it only withholds those edges from the recorded map rather than clearing bits on a square state as the C++ function does.

what: Implements the R27.7 rule for a lone monster group: it takes a snapshot of per-party-member target weights and draws a single target for that group using those weights.
ev: The candidate makes the same weighted party-member draw (a snapshot of halving weights, one roll per group, and the target clamped to the party), but it runs for every alive group rather than as a lone-group rule, and it does not cover the unimplemented DeathState leave step.

what: Computes a character's attack and defence caps in Mordor by taking the per-field maximum of the attack and defence limits of every guild the character has joined.
ev: BestGuildAD also takes the per-field maximum of attack and defence over a character's guild memberships, but it uses each membership's level-dependent awarded values (via GuildAD) instead of the fixed per-guild caps (kMaxAttack/kMaxDefence) that CharacterAdCap uses, so the outputs differ.

what: Maps a party-wide spell effect id (200 and up) down to its underlying real effect id by subtracting 200, leaving other ids unchanged.
ev: `Of` returns `s.Effect - PartyOffset` when `s.Effect >= PartyOffset` and otherwise returns `s.Effect`, which matches the C++ `effectReal` if `PartyOffset` is 200 (the C++ uses `kPartyEffectBase`, presumably 200; the candidate takes a `Spell` rather than a raw `int`).

what: Returns true (refusing the action) whenever the character is held, except for taking the stairs down or the chute, which are allowed.
ev: UseStairs also exempts the stairs down and the chute from a character-status check (paralysis, not held), and only the stairs up are gated, so it shares the exemption pattern but not the held condition or the refused-action set.

what: Looks up the floor state for a given dungeon level in the game data, returning a pointer to it or null if no floor exists at that level.
ev: FloorFor returns the floor whose LevelNum equals the requested level, or null when none matches, which is the same lookup as floorAt, but it searches the window's own `_floors` list rather than the game's floor state, so the source collection and data it reads differ.

what: Rolls a percentile check against the character's disease resistance (resistance 4 for the Disease Spores chest trap) and, on failure, sets the character's disease level to the dungeon level, returning whether they were afflicted.
ev: Spring applies the same resistance-halved roll and sets the disease level to the dungeon level on affliction, but it runs over the whole party, has no `DiseaseLevel == 0` guard against re-afflicting someone already diseased (the C++ leaves that case unchanged), and does not return a per-character result.

what: Reports whether a companion slot is a living participant in combat, meaning it is occupied, has Hits above zero, and is not dead.
ev: No candidate is a slot-level predicate that tests occupancy, `Hits > 0`, and not-dead together; the nearest, `CompanionSlots.Remains` (which checks `_slots[slot] != null`) and `Walk` (which splits living from dead by `IsDead`), each test only part of that and return something different.

what: Reports whether a change of alignment, going from one alignment index to another, crosses more than one step on the alignment spectrum, using the raw index difference.
ev: It uses the same test, `Math.Abs((int)from - (int)to) > 1`, but only to pick a fee multiplier of 2 or 1 rather than returning the boolean the C++ function returns.

what: Returns the treasure-class bonus granted to a lair chest, but only when the encounter is a lair and the chest's box-chance roll (BoxChance[2]) is positive.
where: Mordor.Core/Rules.cs Rules.ChestClass (the method is `ChestClass` in Mordor.Core/Rules.cs, per Candidate 1)
ev: ChestClass applies the same lair-and-BoxChance[2]>0 condition to add a 25 bonus, but it then uses that bonus to pick a chest class rather than returning the bonus value itself as `lairBonusFor` does.

what: Records one rejected subtype draw for the companion's subtype selection, resetting the subtype to 0 after more than 150 tries and marking the pick as failed after more than 300.
ev: No candidate keeps a rejected-draw counter that resets a subtype to 0 after 150 tries and sets a failed flag after 300. The nearest, Combat.cs KnownAsIndex, has a retry loop with a try limit, but it redraws a misidentified monster name and has no subtype reset or failed flag.

what: Computes the threshold experience points needed to reach level x for a given guild and race, using a quadratic-plus-linear formula scaled by guild and race multipliers and rounded to a whole number (returning 0 for x <= 0).
ev: Both compute the threshold XP for a level from a guild factor and a race factor, and the candidate is a line-for-line port of MAINMOD2.BAS fn12A1, but the C++ closed form is off by one from it in about 12 of 16,800 guild/race/level cases, which the candidate's own doc notes.

what: Returns true only for monster Id 307, the Morgul monster that the game's rules (cited as [c8], [c9], [c55]) treat as the one shared Morgul across encounters.
ev: The C++ function is a boolean predicate that is true only for Id 307, while FromId treats 307 as the one shared Id but resolves it to a specific table index (Morgul or Shadow Ninja by alignment) and returns -1 when there is no match, so it does not return a yes/no answer.

what: Drawing the owner cancels that character's misdirection by clearing its misdirected flag, per rule R45 of the Mordor SRD.
ev: No candidate clears a misdirection flag or cancels misdirection on a character; the closest, KaizenView.cs RowDrag.Retarget, only reassigns a buff row's target through a dialog, and the rest are dialog, box, or companion-victim helpers.

what: Stores the player's preload character name in the port's own settings file under the Character key (empty section name, as the source notes it is unstated), so the game remembers which character to load.
ev: It writes the preload leader's name under the Character key in the port's own settings.ini via PortSettings.Write, but it is part of the unload flow, it blanks the entry when the leader is not marked, and it uses the port's section rather than the empty section name the C++ uses.

what: Computes a monster's overall power rating from its attack, strength, hit points, dexterity, and guild level, plus bonuses for each special attack and spell flag it has.
ev: The candidate computes the same rounded `Att*2 + STR*10 + Hits/10` term, adds `DEX*2` and `GuildLevel`, then adds 75 per special-attack bit over 14 and 100 per spell bit over 18, matching the C++ `powerFromFields`.

what: Converts a library roll or identification level into a monster grade for the Mordor library, where a result of 0 or less gives grade 4, 1 gives grade 3, 2 gives grade 2, and anything higher gives grade 1 (per rules R54 and R52).
where: Mordor.Core/Librarian.cs bumps.FileCompanion (also Librarian.cs bumps.FileSighting, which has the same mapping inline)
ev: Both candidates contain the same idLevel-to-grade mapping (<=0 gives 4, <=1 gives 3, <=2 gives 2, else 1), but only inline inside functions that also write a store record, so neither does the C++ function's pure conversion alone.

what: Rolls a d100 and reports whether the roll is at or below 50 plus twice the dungeon level, which decides whether a slime attack reaches the player.
ev: No candidate rolls a d100 against a threshold of 50 plus 2 times the dungeon level to decide a slime attack, so the closest, Rules.HitThreshold (a d100 to-hit check), uses a different threshold and serves a different purpose.

what: When the party falls out of the sky, it kills every member with an ordinary death (with a tell box shown for each) and then displays the message "You fall out of the sky!" to the player.
ev: It kills every party member with an ordinary death and shows a tell box, matching the C++ core, but it shows one box with a different message ("The party has teleported... fallen to their deaths!") instead of the C++ "You fall out of the sky!", and it calls Kill directly rather than killPartyMember.

what: Computes the old-age contribution to a character's death-related chance as 5 + ln(pct − 98) for ages above the threshold, and returns 0 otherwise.
ev: It uses the same 5 + ln(pct − 98) term but inside a random death roll that returns a bool, and it clamps ln(0) at 98% instead of keeping the literal value, so it is a related version rather than the same function.

what: Applies the Asmodeus strip by reducing a monster group count by one, never letting it fall below one.
ev: ShowPortraits applies the same Asmodeus rule, `count = Math.Max(1, count - 1)`, but to a count of visible slots computed from runs in the encounter rather than to a bare group count, so it is a related version with different inputs.

what: Builds the "You were accidently hit for" or "You were accidently electrocuted for" caption naming the victim (plus "and his companions" when applicable) and sends it to the player, showing the hit caption only if the watched character was struck.
ev: Candidate 1 shows the same rule that only the watched character's hit caption is displayed, but it receives the text as a parameter and never builds the "You were accidently hit for / electrocuted for" wording, the victim name, or the "and his companions" suffix (Candidate 3 has the suffix idea, but with different text and no electrocution path).

what: Decides whether a wall word marks a legal teleporter destination by checking that the square has neither the Rock bit nor the Teleporter bit set.
ev: No candidate tests the Rock or Teleporter bits to validate a teleport destination; Candidate 3 (DungeonWindow.axaml.cs, if.TeleporterSquare) explicitly says the square routine's teleporter "tests neither rock nor level 0," and Candidate 6 (DungeonNav.cs, DungeonNav.SetPosition) places the player on rock without any check.

what: Maps the companion's idLevel (how much the player knows about them, with 0 meaning fully known) to the display text shown in the Companion Information screen, such as "You know All" or "You know Nothing".
ev: The candidate maps the same idLevel values to the same four strings ("You know All", "More to learn", "Lots more to learn", and a default of "You know Nothing"), with the same switch structure, assuming the named constants equal 0, 1 and 2.

what: Rolls a random percentage and returns true (the chest ailment takes effect) when the roll falls below half the given resistance value.
ev: Spring inlines the same test for poison and disease, `rng.NextDouble() * 100 < ResistancePercent(c, kind, item) / 2.0`, but it is one step inside a larger trap dispatcher and does not exist as a standalone roll-and-compare function.

what: Computes the trap disarm stat as a weighted sum of Wisdom divided by 4 plus Dexterity divided by 2, per game rule R34.
ev: The case 0 (thieving/disarm) branch computes the same `wis / 4.0 + dex / 2.0` stat, but only as one term inside a larger disarm-chance formula that also adds guild rating and subtracts a dungeon-level opposition term, so the standalone WIS/4 + DEX/2 function is not reproduced by any candidate.

what: Returns the SP cost of casting a spell, which is zero when the cast comes from an item (itemLevel != 0) and otherwise the caster's spellbook cost from the spell-cost engine.
ev: The line `int cost = itemLevel != 0 ? 0 : Spellbook.Cost(spell, who);` matches the C++ zero-for-item-level rule and the engine call, but it sits inside a larger refusal gate that also checks known spells, stats, and anti-magic squares, and the same expression also appears in Combat.cs at.RoundCheckCast.

what: Runs one companion's per-tick check in the dungeon: a companion with binding below 100 may drift one point toward zero and, if it drifts, may then leave the party, a binding of zero always makes it leave, and a companion whose alignment opposes its owner's may defect to the hostile side, with the result reported back to the caller.
ev: Step.Round covers the drift roll, the leave roll after a successful drift, and the always-leave at binding zero, but no candidate implements the opposed-alignment defection roll (75% Evil, 15% Neutral).

what: Returns true only when the target character is dead, which is the condition under which the R113 cmdWait command acts on that character.
ev: OnWait opens with the same dead-only guard (`if (!_ch.IsDead && !_awaitingRescue) return;`) that the C++ predicate encodes, but it is an event handler that also runs the wait action, and its extra `_awaitingRescue` clause means it does not return exactly `who.isDead()`.

what: Marks a floor square as explored on the automap, but only when the party has the Mapping effect active and the square is within the floor's valid range.
ev: Both return early when mapping is off and otherwise mark the current square explored, though the C++ takes explicit x,y and bounds-checks them while the candidate uses the nav's own X,Y, which are always on the floor.

what: Projects a character's level from the ratio of desired to current experience points, scaled by the current level via a square root, returning 0 when current XP is non-positive.
ev: No candidate computes a projected level as sqrt(desiredXp / currentXp) * currentLevel with a non-positive-XP guard; the closest, Binding.NextLevel and Character.ExpForNextLevel, are different level or XP-threshold rules and do not take a desired XP as input.

what: Applies the stat modifiers from an item definition to a character's stats, one stat at a time, optionally in reverse (for example, when the item is removed), as a special effect of the item.
