ev: It loops over the six stats and applies each item modifier with a reversed flag, as the C++ wrapper does, but it adds a race-based ceiling, a minimum clamp, messages, and Hall checks, and its reversed case only subtracts positive modifiers, which may not match the C++ `applyStatMod` helper (whose body isn't shown).

what: Implements the R18 group hostility check: a Good lead facing a Good viewer is never engaged, a Neutral lead is engaged with a 60% chance by rolling against a peace threshold, and any other lead alignment (Evil, per the unresolved note) defaults to engaged.
ev: It uses the same alignment pairing, with Good facing Good never starting a fight, but it returns a charisma-adjusted per-tick chance instead of the C++ fixed 40% neutral-peace roll and always-engaged Evil default.

what: Withdraws gold from the party's bank account into hand, failing with a Beep result if the requested amount exceeds the bank balance or the bank balance is negative.
ev: The withdrawal branch applies the same Beep check (amount > GoldInBank or GoldInBank < 0), then moves the amount from bank to hand, but BankTyped takes typed text rather than an amount, rejects zero, returns Moved instead of Ok, and adds overflow guards the C++ lacks.

what: Returns the morgue rescuer's fee for a rescue, which is currently a placeholder constant (kRescueFeeUnpriced) because the real price is not yet known from the game's source.
ev: No candidate returns a morgue rescuer fee: the fee-returning candidates (Seer.Fee, Seer.LocateCharacterFee, StoreStock.IdentifyFee) price searches or identification, and the rescue-related ones (Rescue.CloseEnough, CityWindow.ShowDead) check coordinates or show the dead screen without pricing a rescue.

what: Serializes one guild membership record to or from the save file, covering the member's guild level, experience, attack and defense, guild gold, and the state of their guild quest (kind, progress, target, level, count, and whether it is done or pinned), with range limits on the quest kind and state.
ev: No candidate reads or writes the guild membership fields (level, experience, att, def, guild gold, quest kind/state/target/level/count/pinned) to a save file; the closest, Character.RollQuestForLevel and Progress.QuestStateOf, only set or read quest state in memory.

what: Applies a disease cure attempt by charging a fixed hit-point cost to the character, then clears the disease if the roll result passes and otherwise reports that it remains.
ev: AilmentStep makes a disease cure roll and costs hits on failure, but it charges 1 hit only on failure, uses a different threshold (195) and the poison level in the roll, and has no result-based clear/remain outcome, whereas the C++ charges a fixed cost on every attempt.

what: Computes the gold needed to advance to the next level in research, as the player's gold-gain factor P (1 + GGF/10) times floor(30.1·x² + x/10), rounded half up.
ev: Both return the gold needed to advance a level from the current level and a gold factor, but Fn12B2 is the guildmaster's loop-based formula (MAINMOD2.BAS:2140-2155, using 60.2) rather than the C++ research formula P * floor(30.1·x² + x/10) rounded half up.

what: Builds the help text shown to the player for a given game screen by collecting the help lines of every feature command registered to that screen.
ev: No candidate filters a registry of feature commands by screen and concatenates their help strings; the closest, HelpBundle's TextOf and HelpWindow's Topic.Load, build help from extracted WinHelp topics, not from per-screen command registrations.

what: Returns the fixed resistance value of 90 when the gear grants resistance, since worn items replace rather than stack with the race's base resistance, otherwise it returns the race base.
ev: It applies the same rule, replacing the race base with a flat 90 when any equipped item resists the kind, but it also takes the higher of a spell's resistance, which the C++ helper does not do.

what: Computes a combatant's total swings per weapon for melee combat by adding the actor's Swings value to the weapon's Swings value (SRD c07p1, R7).
ev: The candidate computes the same per-weapon `actor.Swings + w.Swings` sum, but only as one step inside a larger routine that also loops over the swings and handles targets and weapon failures, while the C++ function is just the sum.

what: Checks whether a spell cast in a mod's dungeon can go ahead for a given caster, returning a refusal (blocked by monsters on the square, an invalid or dead caster, a missing required target, or a map/raise/bind spell) or None when the cast is allowed.
ev: ModCast applies the same gates (monsters present, caster not in party or dead, map/raise/bind excluded via SpellThrown.Handles, target required via PresetFor), but it then performs the cast and returns a bool instead of the C++ function's pure CastRefusal check, and it does not report which refusal applied.

what: Computes the weight a perception value contributes to working something out in the game, returning zero for non-positive perception and otherwise the square of its natural logarithm (per SRD rule R28).
ev: The candidate computes the identical weight inline (`perception <= 0 ? 0 : Math.Log(perception) * Math.Log(perception)`), but only as one step inside a larger method that also applies the floor, facing, and location rolls, so it does not match the C++ function's standalone purpose.

what: Computes the percent chance that an archive paralysis effect takes hold on a target, as 100 minus the sum of their resistance and Constitution, never dropping below a fixed floor of 5.
ev: It is a related paralysis check that also takes resistance and CON with a floor of 5, but it decides whether paralysis wears off each tick using a log-based formula and a cap of 90, not the R37 onset chance of 100 - (resistance + CON) with a floor of 5.

what: After a chute fall, it either runs the level-change routine when the party leader has moved to another floor, or else settles the area, skipping that settle when the caster was standing over a chute.
where: Mordor.App/DungeonWindow.axaml.cs DungeonWindow.ChuteFall (candidate 2; ArriveBySpell in the same file is the other close match)
ev: ChuteFall computes the leader's landing floor after a fall, which is the leaderChangedLevel test, but its settle/ChangeLevel decision is cut off in the excerpt; ArriveBySpell skips SettleArea when a chute is under the caster, matching the chuteUnderCaster half, but neither candidate has the full branch that calls ChangeLevel when the leader changed floor and otherwise settles the area.

what: After a chute fall is resolved, it shows the "There is a chute here. Select TAKE to use." message once if any party member who did not fall is visible on screen.
ev: It supplies the chute announcement for a square with a chute, but it has no fall or visibility check, and the candidate that handles the fall (Mordor.App/DungeonWindow.axaml.cs ChuteFall) is truncated before any such check appears.

what: Maps a 1-based dungeon square coordinate (x, y) to its slot in the floor's flat square array, returning a pointer to that square or null when the coordinate falls outside the map.
ev: No candidate converts a 1-based (x, y) to a flat-array index and returns null when it is out of range; the nearest, PerceiveAhead.SquareAhead, uses 0-based coordinates and only bounds-checks neighbours, and OriginalSaves.ReadAutomap computes an index from file record numbers rather than from (x, y) inputs.

what: Applies the mod's hook reply to the game: if the hook threw, the mod is faulted for the session and the original answer is used, and if the decision was null the original's answer is kept, otherwise the mod's answer stands.
ev: Guard matches the throw branch (it faults the mod via Fault and returns the original's fallback answer), but it has no null-decision branch and returns a generic T rather than the C++ bool.

what: Returns the spit attack's chance percentage for a victim, picked from high, mid, or low bands by comparing the victim's level against the monster guild's level (Table D).
ev: It takes the character's guild level and the monster's guild level and returns 90, 50, or 10 for above 1.25x, between, or below 0.75x the monster's level, which matches Table D's bands; the C++ branch-to-band mapping is flagged as inferred (CONFLICT 17), so I could not confirm that part against the source.

what: Computes the hit points a character gains when reaching a new guild level, using the guild's average hits, a 2/3 chance of a random bonus, a Constitution bonus above 16, and a cap of 999 maximum hits.
ev: Both return no hits when another guild already reached the level and both roll AH plus a 2/3 chance of an AH/5 slice plus a CON-16 bonus below the cap, but the C++ grants AvgHits past the cap and treats level equal to the cap as past it, whereas LevelUp grants LateHits past the cap and still rolls at level equal to the cap.

what: Moves the party out of the dungeon and into town when they climb the stairs, placing the leader at the party's square on town level 0 and printing the "You climb the stairs to town." message.
ev: The stairs-up branch at level 1 sends the party to town (leader's DungeonLevel set to 0, exit to the city, with the climb routed through BeforeStairsToTown), but the excerpt never shows the leader's X/Y being written to the party square, the facing being set, or the "You climb the stairs to town." line, which the C++ does.

what: Computes the per-guild spell price for a given spell level, rate, and cost ratio, scaled by the guild's spell level and rounded with the game's price rule (with a one-off reduction when the exact product is a whole number).
ev: It rounds `level * rate` half-to-even, floors `rated * u4 * rate * 1.9 / SL`, and subtracts one when the exact product is whole, matching the C++ R28/R29 rule; the differences are that it takes the already-clamped SL directly instead of `guildLevel`, and it computes the product exactly rather than in f64.

what: Returns a character to sanctuary: if no sanctuary point was ever set it reports that and does nothing, otherwise it ages the caster by kSanctuaryDays and reports the return.
ev: It performs the same ageing by a given number of days and returns the "X older" line, and its doc names the original's Sanctuary call (MAINMOD2.BAS:1352) as a caller, but it has no never-cast check and no sanctuary return logic, which lives in a caller not among the candidates.

what: Realigns an unequipped item to a new alignment for a fee: equipped items are refused, the player is asked to confirm, and the fee is charged from the payer's purse before the item's alignment is changed.
where: Mordor.App/CityWindow.Store.cs, Realign (method; the candidate header is garbled as "with.Realign")
ev: It refuses equipped items with a message, asks the player to confirm the fee, charges it (failing with "Not enough gold!" if unaffordable), and then sets the new alignment, but unlike the C++ it never sets the `aligned` flag.

what: Maps a character's library identification level (all or mostly identified) to the corresponding library grade value (4, 3, or 0 otherwise).
ev: FileItem computes the same grade inline (All gives 4, Mostly gives 3, otherwise 0) but also writes the record's name, grade, and Id, so it covers more than the C++ mapping function.

what: When a companion is asked to attack by right-click, this checks whether the companion's alignment permits it, prints a refusal message if it won't, and otherwise sends the companion into combat as a forced action.
ev: It mirrors rightClickAttack's flow: it ignores the click when no companion is selected or the companion has fallen, refuses with a message when both the character and companion are Good, and otherwise calls LetCompanionGo with forced: true. The refusal text is the port's own NoAttackingGoodCompanions string, not the C++ "Your companion will not attack.", and the C++ alignment check is folded into the Good/Good test.

what: In the kicked-out companion case, it rolls the creature's turn check against its alignment and the master's alignment, and returns true only when the companion does not turn, so it leaves silently with no message printed.
ev: On a Kick Out where the companion does not turn, it clears the slot with no message of its own, which matches the C++ silent leave, but this is embedded in a larger method that also handles the turn outcome, redraws, and saves, and it does not isolate the not-turned predicate or take the alignment inputs directly.

what: Rolls d100 against the lead character's LockedChance and reports whether a treasure chest is locked, but only when its treasure class is above 1.
ev: The C++ function is only a lock check (d100 roll ≤ LockedChance and treasure class > 1), while DropsItem rolls a d100 against the monster's ItemChance with class modifiers and a cap, so it is a different test; the closest match for the lock logic itself is Mordor.Core/Rules.cs EncounterGold, which only mentions the lock as a gold multiplier and does not perform the roll, so neither candidate does what rollChestLock does.

what: When the encounter is cleared, it empties the count of every monster group that has no living monsters left, but only if the party has more than one member.
ev: RefreshCombat hides groups with no living monsters from the display, which matches the dead-group part of the rule, but it never sets a count to 0, has no party-size check, and does not run on encounter clear.

what: Decides whether a teleport destination level is rock (non-existent), returning true when the level exceeds either the maximum dungeon level or the number of dungeon levels available.
ev: Its line `if (level > SpellEffect.MaxDungeonLevel || level > dungeon.Count) return Outcome.IntoRock;` is the same level-range test as `teleportLevelIsRock`, but ForSpell also handles the fall at level 0 and tests x/y and the rock square, so it does more than the C++ predicate.

what: Decides how a character's eligibility for a guild is shown during creation: hidden if the race is not allowed, italic if the alignment is not allowed, bold if the stats qualify, and plain otherwise.
ev: RefreshGuilds skips guilds the race disallows, italicises those the alignment disallows, bolds those whose stats qualify, and leaves the rest plain, which is the same decision order as eligibilityStyle, though it draws the row directly instead of returning an enum.

what: Returns true only if the character's level in the given guild is strictly higher than the level in every other guild, which implements the game's "highest guild" condition.
ev: LevelUp computes the same strict "greater than the highest other guild" test (`Guild.Level > highestOther`), but only as an inline step inside level-up, not as a standalone predicate, and it compares only joined guilds rather than all guilds at stored level.

what: Adds the item's spell-point bonus to the user's current spell points on use (e.g. Scroll of Spells +50, Tome of Spells +200) and announces the restored amount to the player, with no cap applied.
ev: No candidate adds an item's spell-point bonus to a character's current SP on use and announces it; Combat.CastSpell handles item-sourced casts but spends SP rather than restoring it, and Character.RecalcSpellPoints only clamps or refills SP after creation or level-up.

what: Converts a companion's binding level into its bound value by taking the absolute value, multiplying by 4.5, and rounding half-to-even to an integer.
ev: ChanceToLeave computes the identical bound, `Math.Round(Math.Abs(bindingLevel) * 4.5, MidpointRounding.ToEven)`, as an internal step, but it then goes on to return a leave chance rather than the bound itself.

what: Lets a party member buy a store item in town by checking the shelf row, charging the stock-dependent gold price, moving one copy into a free pack slot, and removing it from the shelf.
ev: This candidate only decides whether buying removes a copy from the shelf, which is one step of doBuy, and it does not check the row, charge gold, or place the item in a pack slot; the other candidates are store display, pen pricing, or pack rendering.

what: Checks whether an item can be equipped under its wear-class limit: unwearable items are refused, and an item is refused when the player already has that class's maximum number of items equipped.
where: Mordor.Core/Character.cs Character.EquipProblem (with Character.IsWearable covering the cap-0 refusal)
ev: EquipProblem refuses when the count of equipped items in the class is at or above a positive max, matching classCapPasses' count check, but it also checks hands and guilds, and it does not refuse a max of 0 (IsWearable does that, as a separate method).

what: Uncurses an item in a party member's pack slot by checking the curse flag and equipped status, then, if funds cover the fee, clearing the slot's curse flag and charging the member the gold uncurse price.
ev: Refusal reproduces only the C++ refusal check (not cursed, then not equipped, returning the message), while the argument parsing, slot lookup, price and fee computation, funds check, clearing of the slot curse flag, and fee charge are not in any candidate.

what: Decides whether the player may exit the dungeon, refusing with a "Cannot exit while monsters are in the area!" message if monsters are nearby while the character is alive and below ground, otherwise prompting "Exit Mordor?" and returning a confirm outcome.
ev: Its doc comment describes the same rule (monsters present, character alive, not in town gives a Beep and "Cannot exit while monsters are in the area!" with the close cancelled; otherwise "Exit Mordor?"), though it is a window Closing handler with a callback rather than a returned outcome enum, and the visible code is truncated so the check itself isn't shown.

what: Computes the landing dungeon level for a chute ride by adding the chute's depth to the level the player falls from (depth 0 means no level change).
ev: ChuteFall computes the landing as `from + Math.Max(0, (int)rec.Depth)`, which matches the C++ addition with depth 0 meaning no change, but it then clamps the result to the limited-version maximum and the dungeon's level count and handles party movement, which the C++ helper does not do.

what: Rolls the monster no-cast chance for a spell attempt, giving mages a 10% chance and non-mages a 50% chance of failing to cast.
ev: ChooseSpell uses the same 10% and 50% figures for monster spell casting, but it applies them as two separate rolls (a flat 10% no-cast, then a further 50% for non-Mage classes, about 55% total) rather than the single 10%-or-50% roll in the C++ function.

what: Computes the gold fee for uncursing an item as a fixed fraction (0.8 times the divisor, per the given factors) of its list price, rounded half to even.
ev: No candidate computes the uncurse fee of list price × 0.8 / 0.5 rounded half to even; Uncursing.Refusal only decides whether the clerk refuses, and StoreStock.RealignCost is a similar price-times-factor store fee but for realignment at 0.72.

what: Returns true when a character's age in days has reached 98% of their race's natural lifespan, marking the onset of old age.
ev: It repeats the C++ 98%-of-lifespan threshold test (`pct < 98` returns false) but then adds a random death roll, so it answers "may this character die of old age" rather than returning the boolean onset check.

what: Sets the character's standing combat order to the chosen spell id, so that spell becomes the combat-setting spell before the cast check runs.
ev: CastInCombat sets the spell as the pending order (`pending.Kind = OrderKind.Spell; pending.SpellId = c.Spell.Id`) before `CheckCast` runs, matching the C++ ordering, but it is a whole cast flow rather than the single `order.spellId` assignment, and SetOrder (Candidate 5) also writes `o.SpellId` but adds kind, engagement, and UI side effects.

what: Checks that a save file's race and guild names match entries in the loaded game data, reports each unknown name to the player, and returns whether both are valid so the load can be refused.
ev: CheckNames also refuses a save whose race or guild name is missing from the game data, but it throws on the first failure instead of reporting each unknown name to the player and returning a bool, so the outcome differs.

what: Decides whether a character's guild level is high enough to join a monster's guild, returning true when the character's level is equal to or greater than the monster's.
ev: No candidate returns whether the character's guild level is at least the monster's; the nearest, Rules.LevelGapChance, compares levels against a quarter-level margin and returns a percentage chance, and the rest either check membership, return one level, or compute other values.

what: Converts an experience point total into an actual EP value for the Mordor rules by dividing it by 8 (R24).
ev: No candidate divides an experience total by 8 to get actual EP; the closest experience-related methods (ExpForNextLevel, ExperienceCap, ChestExp) compute level thresholds or chest awards, not this conversion.

what: Decides whether a new purse total strictly exceeds the current Wealthiest record, so the record is replaced only on a strictly greater amount (game rule R31).
where: Mordor.Core/HallRecords.cs HallRecords.Fresh (seeded record board; Kind.Wealthiest is seeded at 5466453 under "Nimblefingers")
ev: The C++ function is a one-line strict-greater comparison (`purse > recordPurse`) deciding whether a new Wealthiest value replaces the record, and none of the candidates contains that comparison, so the nearest match is the closely related record-board code, which only seeds the Wealthiest record and does not implement the replace-on-strictly-greater rule.

what: Computes the Mordor ECV score (per SRD rule R73) as a weighted sum of attack, defense, hits, and the Strength stat, weighting attack 1x, defense 4x, hits 2x, and Strength 2x.
ev: No candidate computes the weighted sum 1*att + 4*def + 2*hits + 2*Strength; CharacterPanel.AttackDefence (Mordor.App) only gathers a character's attack and defence totals, and the other candidates compute unrelated values (damage, base worth, item worth, drift).

what: Ticks the ailment timer for the player's game state, skipping the tick if one is already running, and emits an "Ailment tick" event carrying the ailment interval; the actual ailment effects are resolved elsewhere.
ev: AilmentTick has the same `_inAilment` re-entrancy guard and is the dungeon's ailment timer tick, but it also runs the full per-member effects (water, poison, disease, paralysis) that the C++ function leaves to another module, and it does not emit an "Ailment tick" event carrying the interval.

what: Computes how many character creation points remain for a new character, using the 30-point pool plus the race's bonus points minus the amount each stat exceeds the race's minimum.
ev: Roll computes `_pool = 30 + _race.BonusPoints - spent` with `spent = sum(stat - race.Min)`, the same formula as the C++ function, but it derives the stats itself from the race minimums plus five rather than taking a `stats` argument, so it is a related version with different inputs.

what: On a chest drop, it sets the slot's curse flag whenever the item carries any curse, per rule R44.
ev: AwardCrest sets `SlotCursed = crest.Cursed != 0` on the new slot, the same flag rule as the C++ function but on a guild crest award rather than a chest drop, and Candidate 5 (DungeonWindow TreasureFrom, the chest path) is truncated before its `Loot.NewSlot` call, so I can't confirm it sets the flag there.

what: Charges a party member the identify fee from their purse to identify one pack item, after validating the member and slot numbers and reporting whether the item was identified, already known, unaffordable, or empty.
ev: The candidate computes a per-step identify fee for a store item, which resembles the C++ `identifyFee` quote, but it does not validate member or slot, deduct gold, change the item, or report an outcome as `doIdentifyItem` does.

what: Draws the percentile cast roll (0–99) once for each cast that passes the gate, before any spell effect is applied, following the game's rule R12.
ev: Both draw one value from the RNG per passing cast, before any effect, and discard it because nothing reads it (the C++ returns it and the C# uses `NextDouble()` rather than `below(100)`); Mordor.App/DungeonWindow.axaml.cs box.CastSpellHere also performs this draw at the same point in the cast path, but it also contains the gate and effect logic.

what: Handles the typed `disarm <member>` command by checking for a chest on the current square and trapped status, then replies with a message, and does not perform the disarm roll or change the chest because it lacks the rng context needed.
ev: OpenChest covers the same "not trapped" check and the disarm roll that cmdDisarm defers, but it runs from the in-combat chest UI rather than a typed `disarm <member>` command, and it does roll and change the chest where cmdDisarm only replies with a message.

what: Returns false when a chute lies under the caster, so the normal area settle is skipped because the chute fall settles the area it ends in (rule c47).
ev: ArriveBySpell calls SettleArea only when `!_nav.Floor.Has(_nav.X, _nav.Y, Floor.CHUTE)`, skipping it under a chute because the chute fall settles the area it ends in, which matches c47's `return !chuteUnderCaster`, though the candidate also runs RerunSquare and inlines the check rather than returning a bool.

what: Maps a pen alignment index (0, 1, or 2) to its display name, Good, Neutral, or Evil, for the confinement pens in Mordor's rules.
ev: It maps pen index 0, 1, 2 to Good, Neutral, Evil, but returns an `ItemAlignment` enum value (`i + 1`) rather than a display name string, and it has no fallback that maps other values to Evil.

what: Returns true when a companion's binding level is already at or above the requested level, meaning the binding attempt has no effect (the caller still spends the points).
ev: The line `if (comp.BindingLevel >= level) return "... had no effect!"` is the same comparison as `bindHasNoEffect`, but it is embedded in a function that also computes the level from the spell, sets the binding, and returns message text, while the C++ function takes the level directly and returns only a bool.

what: Computes the gold cost of the morgue's own-body raise offer as 2912.32 times the character's max hits divided by 1.5, floored to whole gold and converted to currency units.
ev: It computes the same 2912.32 * (maxHits / 1.5) expression but rounds half-to-even into a long instead of flooring it as the own-body offer does, and it omits the final conversion by kGoldToCurrency.

what: Recruits the front group's surviving members as companions, one per free companion slot, copying their template (hits and rolled max) and decrementing the group count, and says "No room" when all slots are full.
ev: Both take joiners only from the front group, copy the front's hits and rolled maximum, never reload the front, print "Join - No room for more Companions!" when no slot is free, and stay silent on success; the candidate bounds the loop by the offer count and returns a string rather than a count, which are structural differences only.

what: Returns the archive route target level for a guild, which is 28 for Warrior, 30 for Nomad, and 41 for Wizard, and 0 for any other guild since no target is defined.
ev: No candidate maps a guild to a fixed archive route target level (28/30/41, else 0); the closest, Rules.GuildAD, computes per-level attack and defence grants, and Kind.Range only takes a target level as an input to a roll formula.

what: Converts a value to fixed-point form by scaling it by 10000 and rounding half-even to an integer, per SRD rule R12.
ev: Rules.Cur computes `(long)Math.Round(x * 10000.0, MidpointRounding.ToEven)`, which is the same scale-by-10000 and round-half-even to a 64-bit integer as the C++ `curFixed`.

what: Blocks spellcasting in a square when either an antimagic or extinguisher effect is present, per the SRD rule that no spells can be cast there.
ev: It sets `_combat.NoSpellsHere = Floor.Has(ANTIMAGIC) || Floor.Has(EXTINGUISHER)` for the current square, which is the same OR of the two flags that `castBlockedBySquare` returns, though it reads the flags from the floor instead of taking them as parameters.

what: Converts a gold amount entered by the player into the game's internal currency units (1/10000 gold), treating negative input as 0 and rounding half-to-even.
where: Mordor.Core/Combat.cs, if.SetGold (private static method; the candidate's class is shown as "if" in the candidate header)
ev: SetGold does the same double-to-Currency conversion (scale by 10,000, round half to even via VbCurrency.TryFromDouble), but it has no negative-input clamp to 0 and it sets monster fight gold, not player-entered input, and on overflow it logs a message instead of returning a value.

what: Computes a guild's half-level for spell purposes by halving the guild level and rounding up at the half (floor(level / 2 + 0.5)), per SRD c09p2.
ev: It computes the same `(int)(guildLevel / 2.0 + 0.5)`, but it clamps the result to 1..255, so a guild level of 0 gives 1 where the C++ gives 0.

what: Scans level 1 of the dungeon for the square flagged as stairs-up and reports its 1-based x and y coordinates, which the descend code uses to place the party.
ev: FindStart also scans dungeon level 1 for the STAIRS_UP square and returns its coordinates, but it is a resume-or-start routine that uses 0-based x/y and falls back to (1,0,0), whereas the C++ function returns only the 1-based first match and reports failure via a bool.

what: Enforces the alignment rule for spells cast from an aligned item: the item only works for a character of its own alignment, and any other use fails with "Nothing Happens."
ev: Problem contains the same rule, returning "Nothing Happens." when an aligned item's alignment differs from the character's, but only as one branch of a larger function that also checks charges, equipment, and spell index, and it reads the slot's alignment rather than the item's.

what: Attempts to remove a curse from an equipped item, reporting "not cursed" or "not equipped" to the player when the uncurse is refused, and otherwise clearing the item's curse flag.
ev: Refusal makes the same two checks in the same order (not cursed, then not equipped) and returns the matching clerk messages, but it does not clear `SlotCursed` on success, so the clearing step of uncurseSlot is missing.

what: Lets the player kick out a companion, refusing if it is dead (drop it first) or in the city, warning if it is bound, and only releasing it when the player has confirmed the Yes answer.
ev: It runs the same sequence as the C++ function: it returns on the dead-companion and in-city refusals (via CompanionTurn.KickOutProblem), asks for confirmation with the bound-companion warning in the question text, and calls LetCompanionGo only on Yes; the wording of the messages differs from the C++ strings.

what: Sets the player's Sanctuary location in the store by copying the given position and dungeon level, then announces that the location is set.
ev: The doc comment says it applies Set Sanctuary to the character, but the excerpt is truncated before that branch, so I could not confirm it copies the position and dungeon level or announces the message; no candidate visibly does the copy.

what: Computes an item's protection (Defense) value from its SL as 3 × (LN SL)², per R15 of the Mordor rules.
ev: It uses the same formula, 3 × (ln p)², but takes its input from the character's Protection value (a spell effect, returned as an int) rather than from an item's SL, and no candidate computes item protection from SL.

what: Checks whether a square's bit flags allow a magic lock to be applied, returning false if the square has the ANTIMAGIC or EXTINGUISHER flag set.
ev: It tests the same two flags (Floor.ANTIMAGIC and Floor.EXTINGUISHER) on the current square, but it stores the result in `_combat.NoSpellsHere` and `AntiMagicHere` rather than returning a bool, and it does not run the C++ function's bit-mask check.

what: When the party leader is at zero hits, this checks whether a chest's trap has killed the party: if the leader is still standing nothing happens, otherwise the opener is killed if they are in the leader slot and not already dead, and the chest's gold is left untouched.
ev: It performs the same leader-at-zero-hits check and kills the pre-prune opener slot without setting the chest untrapped, but it has no slot-0 restriction (the C++ only kills when `openerSlot == kFirstMemberIndex`), it prunes the party first, and it does not return an outcome enum.

what: Returns the realignment cost multiplier for changing an item's alignment in the game: 0 for the same alignment, 1 for a neighbouring step, and 2 for anything further across the spectrum.
ev: It applies the same Abs-on-raw-index rule to pick a 1x or 2x multiplier, but it charges 1x for identical alignments where the C++ returns 0.

what: Checks whether a party can continue an in-progress stair climb, which is allowed only while the party is still on the stairs and still inside the dungeon (rule R124).
ev: Its doc comment says a deferred climb proceeds only if the party is still on those stairs and the dungeon is still up, which is the R124 condition, but the shown code never tests that predicate and the check would have to be in the unshown `LeaveAfter`.

what: Returns true when a spell's level exceeds the caster's ceiling, marking the spell as unreachable under the SRD c09p2 casting rules [c62].
ev: CanCast contains the same ceiling test (`spellLevel > SpellMax[category]`) but only as one clause alongside category-bounds, rate, and guild-level checks, and no candidate exposes the bare `spellLevel > ceiling` predicate.

what: Rolls the breath chance for a companion by comparing the lead foe's guild level to the companion's, returning 80 if the foe is more than a quarter stronger, 20 if it is more than a quarter weaker, and the base chance otherwise.
ev: The candidate computes the same 80/50/20 chance from the same quarter-level thresholds, but it takes the lead foe from the live monster list instead of as an input, and it also rolls the chance and applies the breath, so it covers more than this percent-only function.

what: Identifies an item for a Character payer by charging an identify fee from their purse (refusing if they can't afford it or the item is empty or already identified) and then raising the item's identification level to full.
ev: The candidate computes the same identify fee the C++ `identifyFee` call uses, but it does not charge the payer's purse, check affordability, reject empty or already-identified items, or set the item's ID level to All, so the full identify action has no candidate.

what: Rolls a uniform random d100 (1 to 100) from the game's RNG, used for percentile checks in the status-effect rules such as poison, disease, paralysis, petrification, and aging.
ev: It draws the same `rng.Next(100) + 1` as the C++ d100, but only inside a comparison (`<= perception`, with a teleporter exception), so it returns a bool rather than the roll itself; no candidate returns a bare 1..100 roll.

what: Unequips a worn item from an inventory slot, refusing if the slot is empty, not an item slot, or flagged as cursed, otherwise clearing the item's equipped state and releasing its hand width back to the free hands.
where: Mordor.App/CityWindow.Mdi.cs, EquipSelected (the "on.EquipSelected" header in the candidate list)
ev: This method unequips a worn slot after a cursed check, clears the slot curse, and recomputes effects, but it is a toggle that also equips, it logs "Cannot unequip! Item is cursed!" where the C++ is silent, and it does not explicitly release hand width.

what: Builds the one-line gear summary shown to the player in the town menu, giving the combat attack/defence value and the total attack and defence for the character's equipment and pack, recomputed on each gear command.
ev: It computes a character's total attack and defence from stats, guild and equipped gear, the same totals `totalAD` gives, but it omits the separate combat A/D value, counts only equipped items rather than the pack, and does not build the gear summary string.

what: Reports whether a character is incapacitated, which in this implementation means dead or paralysed, so they cannot use items; the SRD does not define the condition, so this is a chosen behaviour.
ev: ModUseItem refuses item use silently when the caster is dead or paralysed (`caster.IsDead || caster.Paralysed`), which is the same condition as `isIncapacitated`, but it is part of a larger use routine rather than a standalone check, and no candidate is a standalone equivalent.

what: Handles the player's typed "release <member> <slot>" command by validating its arguments and either returning a usage message or releasing the chosen companion slot in the session.
ev: The candidates cover only the release step (emptying one slot, with DropCompanion adding the carry clearing), while none parses a typed "release <member> <slot>" command, validates its arguments, or returns the usage message.

what: Classifies a victim's level against a reference level using 1.25x and 0.75x ratio bands (Table D), returning the high, mid, or low outcome used by breath, spit, and electrocution effects.
ev: No candidate classifies a victim level against a reference level with 1.25x and 0.75x ratio bands to pick high, mid, or low; the closest, Loot.cs RollDrop and Asmodeus.DropBand, compute item drop level ranges, and CompanionMishap.Chance computes a mishap percentage.

what: Lists the identify fee for each unidentified item in the party's packs (or reports nothing to identify) as a town service, without actually identifying anything.
ev: The candidate computes the same identify fee for a single item (the `identifyFee` at FRMCTYS.BAS:568), but nothing in the candidates loops over the party's pack slots, skips fully identified items, or reports "Nothing to identify."

what: Rolls a percentile die against the companion's breath chance (derived from the leading character's guild level and the companion's level) and returns whether the breath attack fires that round, per SRD rule R35.
ev: The candidate rolls `Floor(_rng.NextDouble() * 100) < chance` with the same 50/80/20 guild-level chance, matching the C++ roll, but it also goes on to pick a mishap victim and apply damage, so it covers more than the single roll-and-return that `rollCompanionBreath` does.

what: Rolls a d200 with a cure bonus based on Constitution and poison level, and the poison is cured if the roll exceeds 185.
ev: Its poison branch rolls `rng.Next(200) + (effectiveCon - 10) * 2 - poisonLevel * 2` and cures when the roll exceeds 185, matching the C++ roll and threshold, but it is embedded in a larger step that also handles disease and hit loss, and the C++ `cureRollBonus` body was not shown, so I could not confirm the bonus formula is identical.

what: Spends a caster's spell points for a cast by subtracting the cost from their current spell points, with no clamp at zero per the SRD.
ev: CastSpell contains the same bare `actor.CurSpellPoints -= cost;` step with no clamp, but it is the whole cast routine with refusal checks, logging, and effects around that one subtraction, not a standalone payment function.

what: Returns the index of the first living party member who is in the city (dungeon level 0), or -1 if no one qualifies, which determines the town gold leader per the rule c36.
ev: It returns the first member who is not dead and has DungeonLevel == 0 in party order, or null when none qualifies, which matches the C++ loop that returns the index or -1; it returns the Character rather than an index.

what: Decides whether a library item is listed for sale, returning true only when its grade is at least Mostly (rule R56 of the Mordor rules).
ev: No candidate applies a grade-at-least-Mostly threshold to decide whether an item is listed: Candidate 1 (`Librarian.KnowsMonster`) only checks whether a creature record exists, Candidate 6 (`CityWindow.axaml.cs` `ShowLibrary`) builds the list but is cut off before any item filter, and the rest either write grades or draw item pages.

what: Rerolls the trap opener's current hit points to a random value from 1 to max HP and current spell points to a random value from 0 to max SP, as the T3 chest-trap fate effect.
ev: No candidate rerolls the opener's current HP to 1..max and SP to 0..max; ChestTraps.Spring (cut off after case 4) handles poison, disease, and fire damage, SpellEffect.ApplyToCharacter's "Fate" is the spell rather than a trap effect, and RecalcSpellPoints only clamps or refills SP.

what: When a character's body is rocked, unloading it from the party clears any pending raise from that body, per the rules for raising the dead.
ev: Forget clears the raise (RaiseChance = 0, RaisedBy = " ") as the C++ function does for a rocked body, but it is not gated on the rocked ailment and is called from the sub0930 decline path, not from an unload, so it does not match the C++ function's rocked-unload condition.

what: Computes the healing magnitude of a spell from its base value, power, and spell level, using the scaled-magnitude formula with the heal base constant.
ev: SpellHeal builds the same heal magnitude (mod1 from base, Log(SL)/Log(10), and power) but then subtracts a random roll and truncates to an integer, while healMod returns the deterministic scaled magnitude as a double, and no candidate returns that magnitude alone.

what: Decides whether an item's alignment lets its effect bit count for a character, so an unaligned item always counts and an aligned item counts only when its alignment matches the character's.
ev: The candidate's doc comment says "Unaligned, or of their alignment," which matches the C++ rule, but it also requires `slot.Equipped`, which the C++ predicate does not check, and it delegates the alignment test to `ItemHelps`, whose body was not shown.

what: Returns the index of the party member currently carrying a dead character's body, or -1 if the party is not carrying a dead body or no member is carrying one.
ev: No candidate returns the index of the member carrying a body; the closest, Mordor.App/DungeonWindow.axaml.cs DungeonWindow.DeliverCarried, loops over carriers but acts on them instead of returning an index, and none checks the C++ `carryingSlot == DeadCharacter` gate.

what: Heals a companion party member by a rolled amount (via spellHealRoll) and caps the result at the companion's maximum Hits.
ev: Its doc comment says a heal rolls each target on its own and caps it at the maximum, which matches healCompanion's roll-then-cap, but it is a whole-spell dispatcher covering party, person, and companion targets, and the companion branch is truncated in the candidate, so the single-companion heal is not isolated.

what: Decides whether a companion monster spawns, either always, by rolling a percentage chance, or only when there is space available, according to the selected spawn mode.
ev: No candidate decides whether a companion spawns; MdrLoader.cs LoadMonsters only reads the raw CompanionSpawnMode word into the Monster record, and the other candidates cover DPS display, backups, and companion attack or raise mechanics.

what: Decides whether a spell effect applies to a given monster, so effects 75–99 only hit monsters of the matching class (effect 75 targets class 0), and otherwise lets the effect through.
ev: The class gate (effect 75-99 zeroes the damage unless the target's class index equals effect minus 75) appears inline in SpellHitsOn, but it is one step in a damage calculation rather than the standalone pass/fail predicate that the C++ function is, and no candidate exposes that predicate on its own.

what: Returns the chest-trap chance percentage (0, 25, 75, or 90) for a given chest class, looked up from that class's mod data.
where: Mordor.Core/Rules.cs Rules.ChestClass (candidate 2; closest match, but it returns the chest class from the monster's BoxChance roll rather than looking up the trap chance for a given class)
ev: None of the candidates returns the trap chance percentage (0/25/75/90) for a chest class; Rules.ChestTrap (candidate 1) hardcodes that same 25/75/90 mapping by class but also rolls the trap index and takes the monster's TrapFlags into account, so it is only a related piece rather than the same lookup.

what: Under R3, further swings keep aiming at the currently targeted group while it still stands, and otherwise shift aim to the first standing group.
ev: Retarget keeps the order's target while its group still has a living member and otherwise moves it to the first living monster (the fn0DCD(-1) fallback), but it works on monster indices rather than returning a group index, and it runs after the character's turn rather than choosing the swing's aim.

what: Computes a character's melee damage modifier from guild level, fighting and weapon factors, and the crit, backstab, invisibility and size-difference adjustments defined by the game's rules (R23/R24).
ev: The modifier body matches line for line (fighting base term, weapon multiplier, +5 crit, +2 backstab, half when unseen, tenth-of-size-difference), but the candidate then passes the result to Fn0DEE and returns a rolled damage int, whereas the C++ function returns the double modifier itself.

what: Removes the spell-granted effects (protection, levitation, invisibility, and see-invisible) from the character who opened the chest when the blackout trap triggers.
ev: Both are the blackout trap's effect on the opener and both target protection, levitation, invisibility, and see-invisible, but ClearSpellEffects also zeroes spell-granted resistances (which the C++ leaves alone) and recomputes from gear, so gear-granted states survive, whereas the C++ clears the four flags directly.

what: Handles the player's typed options command in the game, either reporting the current value of a named option or setting it on or off, or to a number from 0 to 100, and returns the message to show.
where: Mordor.Core/GameOptions.cs GameOptions.Load (closest, but it only reads stored option values and does not handle the typed command)
ev: No candidate parses a named option with an on/off or 0-100 value, sets it, or reports its current value, so the C++ `gameCommand` behavior is absent; GameOptions.Load only reads the same kinds of settings from INI and port files.

what: Computes the gold fee for reviving a character in Mordor, taken as 2912.32 times the character's max hits divided by 1.5 and truncated to whole gold.
ev: It uses the same 2912.32 × (MaxHits / 1.5) formula, but rounds half to even where the C++ truncates with vbInt, and its own comment says the Int() truncation applies to the separate own-body offer.

what: Returns true when a non-ForLife companion still has hits above zero, so that the Fear trap (trap 9) releases that companion.
ev: Step.Round skips companions with `c.Hits <= 0` (a fallen companion is passed over), which is the hits half of the C++ check, but it does not test ForLife as a release condition in the same way: it returns early for `BindingLevel >= Binding.ForLife` and only releases based on a random roll against `Binding.ChanceToLeave`, so it does not implement the C++ predicate `hits > 0 && !forLife` as a direct boolean.

what: Computes the acid damage modifier for a monster attack from the monster's and character's guild levels, using a logarithmic formula from the game's R39 rules and truncating the result to an integer.
ev: No candidate contains the `LN(MonGuildLvl+1) + (MonGuildLvl+1)/15) / LN(1.08) - CharGuildLvl/10 + 1` acid modifier; the nearest, `Combat.cs` `CompanionSpits`, delegates its acid damage to `SpecialHits.Raw` without showing this formula.

what: Computes the age threshold for the old-age roll, 5 plus the natural log of how far the character's age percent exceeds the onset value (98), with a tiny floor so the log stays defined.
ev: The candidate computes the same threshold, `5 + Math.Log(Math.Max(pct - 98, 1e-9))`, with an equivalent 1e-9 floor, but embeds it in a bool-returning death roll that also derives the percentage from age days and lifespan, rather than returning the threshold alone.

what: Computes a character's total attack and defence values by combining guild-derived A/D, stat-derived A/D, the stored A/D shift (subtracted), and the fitted worn-item attack or defence sums.
ev: It returns both att and def from guild AD, stat AD plus the stored shift, and worn items, but it adds `Rules.BaseAD`, clamps at zero, and sums raw equipped Att/Def without the alignment fit that `fittedWornSum` applies.

what: Seeds a floor's room-count tally and room total from the header's area count, so that the shortfall used later in markAreaEmptied is defined.
ev: No candidate assigns a tally or room total from the header area count; the nearest, `DungeonWindow.axaml.cs` `HeaderAreasOf`, only reads the count, and `DungeonState.cs` `TallyOf` (which may lazily initialise the tally) is not among the candidates.

what: Returns true when a monster with the needs-good-weapon bit (R13/R15) is hit by a weapon whose floor is below half the monster's level found, meaning the weapon is too weak to affect it.
where: Mordor.Core/Combat.cs PlayerSwings (the `NeedsGoodWeapon` check at the top of its swing loop)
ev: The check `MonsterProperty.Has(target.Def, NeedsGoodWeapon) && w.Floor < (int)(LevelFound / 2)` is the same predicate as the C++ function, but it is inlined in a larger method that also sets the actor to Defend, clears item orders and skips that hand's swing, so no candidate implements the standalone predicate.

what: Registers the typed "inspect" and "disarm <member>" commands for the dungeon screen, so the player can check a chest's trap or attempt to disarm it.
ev: No candidate registers typed "inspect" or "disarm <member>" commands; the closest matches are TrapReadout (what inspect reports about the trap) and DungeonWindow.axaml.cs OpenChest (the single thieving roll that disarms the chest), but neither is a command registration.

what: Decides whether a character may join a guild by checking that no entry in the guild's unmet requirements list remains, so the join is refused if any requirement is unmet.
ev: JoinGuild refuses the join when `g.Unmet(this).Count > 0`, which is the same eligibility test as `unmet(...).empty()`, but it also performs the join and its side effects, and no candidate is a standalone eligibility predicate (GuildDefs.Unmet in Mordor.Core/GuildData.cs only builds the list).

what: Enforces the spell-point rule for standing spell orders: if the caster lacks enough SP for the spell's cost (cost-0 spells are always affordable), the order switches to Fight while keeping its target.
ev: RoundCheckCast turns a standing spell order into Fight when the cast is refused, and the refusal includes the spell-point check, but it reacts to any refusal (not only insufficient SP), also clears SpellId and removes the item order, and never explicitly keeps the target as the C++ does.

what: Marks a square as explored (mapped) in the game's automap, and does so regardless of whether the square is currently fogged, per the c27/c28 rules.
ev: The C++ function unconditionally sets the explored flag with no other condition, while SetPosition only calls MarkExplored when the target is not rock, and no candidate shows a plain mark-explored step that ignores fog as the C++ does.

what: Computes a companion's new binding level after a step, capping it at the maximum binding level (kBindingMax).
ev: It applies the same cap-at-Max rule with the same Step and Max constants, but it uses Math.Abs(current) where the C++ uses the raw level, so the two differ for negative (free-will) levels, though they match for non-negative ones.

what: Counts how many of a character's four companion slots hold a living companion, meaning occupied, not dead, and with hits above zero (R22, R25.3).
ev: Its first loop counts occupied slots with `Hits > 0`, the same living-companion predicate as the C++ function, but the method is a random slot picker that returns an index or -1 and never returns the count.

what: Returns the wand's strength as the item's level, so a wand's power depends on the item itself rather than on the user casting it (rule R78).
ev: CastSpell takes the spell level from the item (`itemLevel`) when it is above zero, so a wand's power comes from the item rather than the caster, but it also falls back to the caster's guild or spell level when the item level is zero or negative, which `wandStrength` never does.

what: Checks whether two inventory slots can be swapped, returning OutOfRange for invalid indices, then SourceGuildIssued, DestGuildIssued, SourceEquippedOrBanked, DestEquippedOrBanked in that order, or Ok if the swap is allowed.
ev: It performs the same slot-range and guild-issued refusals for a swap, but it only refuses equipped items when the two slots belong to different characters, while checkSwap refuses equipped items on either side unconditionally, and it also acts on the swap rather than only returning a status.

what: Rolls a 1-in-3000 die against a charm-based threshold to decide whether a monster found at a given level joins the party as a friendly companion.
where: Mordor.Core/Combat.cs FillGroup (the join-offer block at 1948-1967, which is cut off before the roll itself)
ev: The candidate's join-offer section is the code that would call the friendly-join roll, but its body is truncated before any 1-in-3000 roll against a charm threshold appears, and no other candidate performs that roll.

what: Computes the gold needed to reach the next level for a character, using the wiki formula for Mordor's level-up gold requirement scaled by a gold factor, rounding the result half up.
ev: Both compute the gold needed for the next level from the level and the guild gold factor, but Fn12B2 is a loop-based sum with a 60.2 rate and no (level-1)^2*30.1 term, so it does not reproduce the wiki formula or its (goldFactor/10 + 1) multiplier.

what: Computes the gold a character needs to advance from a given level, summing a per-level cost that grows with level and scaling the total by the guild's gold parameter, using the 1995 game's rounding rules.
ev: Fn12B2 takes the guild level and guild Gold and runs the same loop (60.2 rate, half-level times term `(l/2)*2 + (l-1)`, rounding to even at each store, then `acc + acc*(Gold/10)`), differing only in its 80-bit x87 arithmetic emulation; the candidate's text is cut off before its final rounding line, so that last step is inferred.

what: Decides whether a companion's spell fails because it is a heal with no affect group, and if so tells the player "Comp. #N failed in casting."
ev: CompanionCasts reproduces the same outcome for a companion's heal (routed through the damage path, M5B1D of 0 reaches no monster, caption "Comp. #1 failed in casting"), but it does this implicitly as part of a larger routine rather than through a standalone check that decides the failure from route and affect group.

what: Computes the spell level used for a level-0 item heal from the guild level via the SRD rule, clamping the result to a minimum of 1.
ev: It applies the same level-0 fallback to the caster's guild spell level via `Rules.SpellLevel`, but it has no explicit minimum-1 clamp and also handles a nonzero item level, which the C++ helper does not; `Mordor.App/DungeonWindow.axaml.cs box.CastAndThrow` states the never-below-1 rule but only inline and inside a much larger method.

what: Maps a player's facing (N, E, S, or W) at a grid square to the edge it faces, returning the wall, door, and secret-door bit flags for that edge, with south and west stepping back one square so both refer to the shared edge.
ev: EdgeAt uses the same facing-to-edge mapping, with south and west stepping back one square and the same wall, door, and secret-door bits, but it returns a classified Edge enum (Wall/Door/SecretDoor/Open) read from the flags rather than the raw bit-index triple the C++ function returns.

what: Returns the Table T-2 wear class cap for an item, which is meant to limit which classes may wear it (0 means unwearable, a positive number is the maximum, -1 means no cap), but it currently always returns the no-cap value because the data field is not yet wired.
where: Mordor.Core/Character.cs Character.MaxWornOfClass (used with Character.WearClassOf to go from item to class)
ev: MaxWornOfClass returns the per-class wear cap from MDATA1 (1, 0, or -1), which is the Table T-2 value the C++ stub is meant to return, but it takes a wear class rather than an item, and the C++ function always returns the no-cap value.

what: Resolves a damage spell cast against the foe groups in an encounter, walking the groups from the start group onward, applying damage to each living group (with a companion-immunity check that cancels the spell), and reporting which groups were reached, whether anything was hit, and the resulting target mark.
ev: CastDamage walks the monster groups from the aimed group (via BySlot and the Alive check), applies damage per victim, sets the all-or-nothing and "Failed" outcome that turns the order to Fight, and emits per-group captions including the companion-failed wording, matching castDamageSpellOnFoes; the candidate is truncated, so the target-mark and immunity-cancel details are inferred from its doc comment rather than seen in the code.

what: Attempts to raise a dead, stoned, or rock-bound character: it refuses invalid raise types, applies the 1-CON stone penalty, rolls against the raise chance (zeroed for rock), and on failure checks whether the attempt complicates based on age, restoring hit points on success.
ev: Resolve covers the C++ roll-against-chance, the rock chance zeroing, the complication branch, and the stone Constitution loss, but it differs in details: it uses `rng.Next(100) > roll` with a quiet-failure aging path, does not handle the Refused checks or kind validation (those are in Rules.RaiseRefusal), and does not set the hit restoration or clear pending-raise fields on success as the C++ does.

what: Computes the price of a penned (identified-for-sale) item from its base value, the number of copies in stock (capped at 9), and the identify level, floored at zero.
ev: The candidate has the same idLevel <= 0 guard, the same stock cap at ShelfCap (9 in the C++), the same `(0.13 * value) / ((stock/2 + 1) * 0.9) / idLevel + 1` formula, and the same zero floor, with the rounding done by `Lng`, which I'm assuming is round-half-even like `roundHalfEven`.

what: Computes the gold fee charged to realign an item's alignment, at 72% of its base price (doubled when more than one alignment step is requested), rounded half-even and returned in currency units.
ev: Both compute round-half-even(0.72 × price × (2 if the alignment step is more than 1, else 1)), with the C++ version returning currency units via kPerGold where the C# returns gold, and the C++ returning 0 for a missing item definition where the C# has no such guard.

what: Decides whether a purchase depletes a shop's stock, returning true when the item is a dungeon item or when the shelf would be left at zero copies of an aligned item.
ev: Both return `dungeon || aligned` (candidate: `it.Floor > 0 || bought != Unaligned`), but the C++ takes precomputed flags while the candidate derives them from the item and alignment, and the candidate's aligned clause has no floor-zero or zero-copies condition that the C++ flag name implies.

what: Checks that the deepest level reached is within the allowed rescue range for the town replenish step of the death rules (R7 step 7), logging an error and returning false if it is not, otherwise logging that the town is replenished and returning true.
ev: Both are the town replenish step of the rescue, but TurnOverTown has no deepest-level range check, no error log, and no bool result; it replenishes the store and pens directly with the deepest level passed through.

what: Reports whether a teleporter record stands on the given square of a dungeon level, per rule R75 of the Mordor rules.
ev: No candidate reports whether a teleporter record stands on a square; `Teleporting.ForSquare` only uses `fl.Has(x, y, Floor.TELEPORTER)` as a rejection test while picking a random destination, and the other candidates handle teleporter messages, lethality, or destinations.

what: Decides whether a command-switch slot number is valid for the current screen: in the dungeon it must be 1 to the party size (and party size above one), while in the city any slot from 0 upward is accepted.
ev: The dungeon half of the C++ check (party size above one and the slot must exist) appears as `_party.Members.Count > 1 && slot < _party.Members.Count` in HandlePartyKey, but that method is an Alt-key handler that silently ignores invalid slots rather than returning a validity bool, and no candidate contains the city branch (`slot >= 0`).

what: Returns the age change in days that a special item type applies to a character: the Potion of Youth makes them 365 days younger, Dragon's Blood makes them 3650 days younger, and special type 25 gives +28 days (sign and magnitude marked unknown in the source), with 0 for any other type.
ev: ApplySpecial maps special type 13 to one year younger (365 days) and type 14 to ten years younger (3650 days) through Younger, matching the C++ lookup, but it has no type 25 (+28 days) case, it is embedded in alignment, spell-point and stat logic, and Younger adds a 16-year floor the C++ function does not have.

what: Builds a list of the names of every member in the player's current party, for use in the seer's person-search feature.
ev: LocatePerson builds the list of other characters' names (every saved character except yourself) for the Seer's LOCATE CHARACTER picker, which is related to the C++ party-name list but is not the same thing: it covers saved characters rather than the current party's members, and it excludes the player rather than returning all party members.

what: Decides whether a character who has joined a guild may be re-offered the sitting guildmaster position, which happens only when the character's level is strictly above the level recorded for the current master and the character's name matches the holder.
ev: Claim applies the same strict level-above-recorded-holder test and re-offers to a sitting master, but it does not require the character's name to match the holder (it lets any higher-level character take the seat), and it has no joined-guild check, so it is a claim operation rather than the C++ holder-only re-offer predicate.

what: Runs one player round by letting each living party member act, then their companions, and stops early if the round guard says to end the round.
ev: RoundPaced walks each living character in party order, runs their own action and then their companions, and stops when no monsters remain, which matches playerRound's shape, but it also checks for an empty monster list before the companions act, whereas playerRound runs the companions first and then checks the guard, so a character who kills the last monster would prevent that owner's companions from acting in the candidate.

what: Applies the sanctuary spell's effect by adding 365 days (the original's aging amount, or the port's constant) to the target character's age and emitting a message saying the spell aged them.
ev: AgeBy adds a caller-supplied number of days to Age and returns a generic "You are now X older." line, and its doc names Sanctuary (1352) as a caller, but the sanctuary-specific call with its own amount and message wording is not among the candidates.

what: Rolls a race's base value for one stat by drawing uniformly at random between that race's minimum and maximum for that stat.
ev: No candidate draws a random value between a race's min and max for a stat; the closest, CharacterCreationWindow.Roll, deterministically sets each stat to min+5 (capped at max) and spends the remaining points, and the other candidates are point-spending UI, stat-change, or complication logic.

what: Rolls a random number of aging days for a monster, capped at 365 times a scale factor derived from the monster's guild level (clamped between 1 and 5).
ev: No candidate rolls a 1d1825 aging value or caps it at 365 times a guild-level scale; the closest, Character.cs keeps.AgeBy, only applies a day count that the caller supplies (it is a downstream consumer, which its own doc comment notes for monster aging), so it is not even a partial match.

what: Decides whether a companion's breath attack is blocked, returning true when a fire breath bit is set or when a cold breath bit is set and the cold breath has not already been blocked by an earlier breath.
ev: CompanionTurn inlines the same guard, `Bit(def.SpecialAttackFlags, 3) || (Bit(def.SpecialAttackFlags, 4) && !round.Breathed)`, with the same precedence note, but it is part of a larger loop that also handles the mishap draw, spit, and blow, so it is not a standalone equivalent.

what: Computes the spell damage modifier for a Mordor spell at a given spell level, adding the base damage, a logarithmic level-scaled term (LN(SL+1)/LN(5)), and a truncated power term, with spell levels below 1 treated as 1.
ev: SpellDamage computes the same mod1 expression as the C++ function (base + base·Log(sl+1)/Log(5) + (int)((sl/10)·(power−1)), with sl floored to 1), but it then subtracts a random cut and applies resistance, while the C++ function returns only the modifier.

what: Maps a stored companion alignment value (0 to 2) to the companion's alignment scheme by shifting it up by one, and otherwise falls back to the monster definition's alignment, per the SRD c12p1 companion rules.
ev: Candidate 1 converts a monster's character-scheme alignment (0/1/2) to the item scheme, which matches only the C++ fallback `alignmentOfDefinition(monsterAlignmentValue)`, but none of the candidates has the stored-value branch that shifts 0..2 up by one, and candidates 2 and 3 map in the opposite direction.

what: Handles the town-menu "cast" command by parsing the typed member, spell name, and optional group, checking the caster is alive, reachable, and has enough spell points, then spending the SP and reporting that the non-combat spell effect is not yet applied.
where: Mordor.App/DungeonWindow.axaml.cs box.CastSpellHere (with box.CastAndThrow and DungeonContext.Cast in Mordor.Modding/ModApi.cs as related paths)
ev: The C++ townCast is a town-menu command that checks reachability, combat-only status, and SP, then spends SP without applying the effect; the candidates are dungeon-side cast paths (CastSpellHere, CheckCast, Refuse) that run the gate and effect in a dungeon, and none of them matches the town-only, no-effect, parse-and-report behavior exactly.

what: Rolls each active poison and disease against a 0-199 draw adjusted by Constitution and poison level to see whether it clears or costs hit points, and rolls an old-age check for characters at or past the onset age, then returns the hit points lost this tick.
ev: The poison and disease rolls, thresholds (185/195), HP costs (2/1), and the poisonLevel quirk match the C++, but AilmentStep omits the old-age roll and returns the HP loss rather than applying it to curHits (candidate 2's AilmentTick may cover old age, but its text is truncated).

what: Returns a character's age in whole years by dividing their age in days by the days-per-year constant (the SRD starts characters at 5840 days, or 16 years).
ev: It computes `ageDays / 365.0` as a step toward a percentage rather than returning whole years, and no candidate returns an integer age in years (Rules.DiesOfOldAge uses the same division inside a death-chance check).

what: Decides whether a charm spell kills its target by checking if the charm's damage is at least the target's remaining hit points.
where: Mordor.Core/Combat.cs Combat.Charmed (its doc comment states the same rule: the original charms whatever the spell's damage would have killed)
ev: No candidate code compares damage against remaining hits to decide a charm kill; Charmed only builds the companion from the hits the creature had before the spell, and the "would have killed" rule appears only in its comment, though the truncated bodies of CastSpell and CastDamage may contain the check.

what: Builds the text listing of a member's buffer slots for the player, showing the member's name and a numbered description of each exposed slot.
ev: BuffersPage builds the same numbered 1-to-10 slot list, each line using SpellBuffers.Describe, but it creates UI buttons instead of returning text, adds a cost column, and has no "Buffers for member N (name):" header.

what: Reports whether a seer's person offer is still pending in the session, by checking that the seer's feature-state entry exists and is non-empty.
ev: No candidate checks a seer's pending-offer entry in a feature-state dictionary; the closest, DungeonWindow.RunPendingTreasure and the PendingRaise offer methods, track different pending features and never test whether a seer offer is outstanding.

what: Serializes or deserializes one dungeon floor's state (level, tallies, per-square explored/identified/seen bits, and area respawn data such as emptied time, respawn timer, lair and spawn mask) to or from the save file.
where: Mordor.App or Mordor.Core Import/OriginalSaves.cs, OriginalSaves.ReadRooms (the ReadRooms method in that file)
ev: ReadRooms reads each level's respawn tally and per-area Foes and Fight data from the original MDATA10 file, which overlaps with visitFloor's tally and area-respawn fields, but it is an import of the original game's files rather than a save-file serializer, and no candidate handles the square explored/identified/seen bit rows or the save-file read/write symmetry.

what: Rolls the stud spread for a stud draw by comparing a random number against a limit, returning the "on" spread value when the roll passes and 0 otherwise.
ev: Its stud branch makes the same draw (`NextDouble() * 75 < 50`) and sets spread to 1 on a pass, but it has no else, so on a miss it keeps the depth-based spread instead of returning 0 as `rollStudSpread` does, and it adds depth and caps the result.

what: Applies the pit-fall rules (R52–R54) to each party member: levitating members may hover unharmed, others take rolled pit damage that can push their hits below zero, and a lone character's death halts the step.
ev: Rules.PitDamage and Rules.HoversOverPit cover the damage and levitation rolls (R53), and SquareInfo.FellIntoPit covers the on-screen message, but no candidate loops over the party, applies damage per member, emits the per-member messages, or stops the step on a lone death (R54).

what: Returns true when a spell effect code falls in the 50–60 range reserved for the game's "Resists" effects, so the caller can apply resistance handling.
ev: ResistKind tests the same resistance effect range as isResistEffect (ResistFirst through ResistFirst + Effects.ResistanceKinds, which should be 50–60 if ResistanceKinds is 11, though I did not verify that constant) but returns the resistance index or -1 rather than a bool, so the caller tests `>= 0` instead of a true/false result.

what: Settles where a spell's caster ends up after a teleport or displacement: rock arrival kills the caster, a fall from the sky does nothing, and otherwise the caster's spell points are reduced by the spell's cost (floored at zero) and the party is marked as having arrived by spell.
ev: Outcome.ForSpell computes the fall, rock, or arrives outcome that settleArrival receives as input, but no candidate applies the rock death, deducts and floors spell points, sets the arrived-by-spell flag, or emits the arrival message.

what: Reports whether an item is part-used, meaning its current charges are below the item's maximum charges (rule R61), which requires maxCharges to be positive.
ev: The candidate contains the same charges-below-maximum test (`sl.Charges < it.Charges`) but only as an inline gate for guild-issued items that it then refills, and it has no standalone part-used predicate or the `maxCharges > 0` guard.

what: Decides whether a candidate Deadliest Hall of Records entry beats the stored record by comparing the monsters' powers (a stored value of -1 forces the change), and otherwise compares the raw values, so a record only changes when the new value is higher.
ev: For Deadliest it returns no change when the candidate monster's power is not greater than the stored one, and otherwise resets the stored value to -1 so the plain `value <= r.Value` test passes, which matches the C++ decision; it additionally writes the new record and builds an announcement, which the C++ predicate does not do.

what: Reports whether a companion's body is magic-immune by returning the body's magicImmune flag, which stands in for the R27.7 test that the header says is not present in this part of the code.
ev: The C++ function only returns the body's magic-immune flag, while SpellHitsOn embeds the same bit-2 test on the companion's definition (`MonsterProperty.Has(compDef, 2)`, the line-2556 test) inside a full spell-damage calculation, so it is a closely related version rather than an equivalent predicate.

what: Stores a mod setting flag as the text "True" or "False" in the mod settings store, following the chapter 21 formula F4 for saving toggle values.
ev: `WriteFlag(modId, key, value)` writes `"True"` or `"False"` through the store's text write, which is what the C++ `writeStoredFlag` does via `writeStoredText`.

what: Checks whether a character's membership in guild g is active, meaning joined with a level above zero, and for class-restricted items that guild must also be the character's primary (active) guild.
ev: CanUse uses the same two rules (joined with level above 0, and class-restricted items look only at the primary guild), but it answers an item-level question using the item's guild bitmask instead of testing one guild index g.

what: Converts a raw spell effect code into its real effect by subtracting the whole-party offset (200) when the code is in the whole-party variant, otherwise returning the code unchanged.
ev: Both subtract the party offset from the raw effect when it is at or above that offset and otherwise return it unchanged; the only difference is that `Of` takes a `Spell` and reads `s.Effect` rather than receiving the integer directly.

what: Applies the monster group special-attack effects (breath, acid spit, electrocution, and melee side effects like poison) against one party member, rolling chances and damage per the game's rules.
ev: GroupAttacks runs the same group turn against one character (breath with the same 50/80/20 gate and level-0 log guard, then acid, then melee specials like poison), but it also covers companions, the melee swings, and extra specials (ageing, drain, stoning, paralysis, destruction, theft) that the C++ function explicitly omits.

what: Picks one monster from a class range by weighted random draw (chance values), considering only monsters whose levelFound falls within the eligibility window around the target floor, and reports found=false when no eligible monster has weight.
ev: It makes the same cumulative-weight draw over a class's monsters and returns null when none qualifies, but it draws the class itself, filters only on `LevelFound <= floor` rather than the spread-based eligibility window, and rejects town-level monsters.

what: Checks whether a given guild is allowed to use an item by testing the bit for that guild in the item's guilds mask.
ev: The bit test `(it.Guilds & (1 << i)) != 0` for a guild index matches the C++ check, but CanUse takes a whole character and applies class-restricted and joined-guild logic instead of testing one given guild index.

what: Computes the monster's breath range from its level and the character's level, using a seeded logarithmic formula that differs from the companion breath calculation.
ev: Its monster breath section starts the same seed computation (`VbInt(monLvl * Math.Log(monLvl + 1))`), but the candidate is truncated before the range formula, and the method covers the whole group turn rather than just the range.

what: Rolls a d100 percentile die and returns true when the result is 1, implementing the any-class check from the Mordor SRD (a 1% chance).
ev: No candidate performs a plain 1% d100 check that returns true on a roll of 1; the closest, Rules.cs RollQuest's 5% let-off test, uses a different threshold and purpose, and Loot.cs DropsItem and Seer.cs LocateCharacter use different rolls and outcomes.

what: Applies electrocution damage from a monster's electrical breath attack to the targeted party member, but only when the attacker's breath type is Electrical, and reports the hit to the player.
ev: No candidate applies electrocution damage from a monster's Electrical breath gate to a party member; the only electrocution mentions are as a companion blow rider in CompanionTurn/CompanionStrikes, and Kind.ResistedBy merely maps Electrical resistance.

what: Displaces the party by a given number of squares to the right and ahead of its facing inside the dungeon, while outside the dungeon it instead destroys the whole party as the spell's rule (R20) requires.
ev: It computes a new position from right and forward offsets relative to facing, as displaceWithin does, but it wraps at the grid edge, adds a level change, returns coordinates instead of moving the party, and has no outside-the-dungeon party death.

what: Returns the lowest item-drop band for a given drop level, using a lookup table for levels 1 to 16 and a halved, rounded value (minimum 1) for higher levels.
ev: RollDrop computes the same base band, `(int)Math.Round(level / 2.0, MidpointRounding.ToEven)` clamped to at least 1, but it is only one step inside a larger drop routine that also applies box chance, chest class, and Asmodeus overrides, and it has no lookup table for levels 1 to 16.

what: For each monster struck in melee, it records the damage dealt (unless the monster is charmed) and, on a killing blow, logs a kill credited to the owning character.
where: Mordor.Core/Combat.cs Blow.Credit (kill side is closer in Mordor.Core/Combat.cs KilledBy)
ev: Blow.Credit reports inflicted damage to the owner's damage event unless the blow is a charm (`removes` false), and KilledBy records the owner's kill, but neither does the C++ pair of a damage record and a kill record per strike, and the C++ `damageRecorded` tally and `monsterKills` list have no counterpart in either method.

what: Places a companion into the live encounter set as a non-hostile monster, copying its monster id, alignment, hit points, and guild level, and marking it alive only if it has hit points left.
ev: It removes a companion and calls `JoinTheFight(outcome.Became)` to put the resulting monster into the fight, which is the same step as the C++ push into the live set, but the field copying and `hostile = false` happen in `CompanionTurn.Check` or `JoinTheFight`, which are not among the candidates.

what: Removes the party member in the given position (refusing the leader, the last remaining member, or a full roster) and sends that record to the end of the roster, leaving the party's remaining members in order.
ev: The C++ function unloads a party member at a given position (refusing the leader and last member) and rotates that record to the end of the roster, whereas no candidate removes or reorders party members.
