The closest, Party.cs is.LoadFor, handles loading members back into a party, and Party.cs is.SaveParty only writes the roster file, so neither matches.

what: Ethereal Portal (Passwall) moves the party one square forward through a wall, killing the caster and not spending the spell if the target is rock, otherwise shifting the party's position and marking it as arrived by spell.
ev: StepThrough does the one-square step in the facing direction with edge wrap and reports whether the new square is rock, but it does not kill the caster on rock, does not set the arrived-by-spell flag, and does not handle the spell's spend, all of which movePassThrough does.

what: Reports whether an item kind is one of the combinable kinds (23–28, 30, 31) that the original game's combine/swap logic allows, so a typed swap can only proceed for those item types.
ev: Both return true exactly for types 23 through 28, 30 and 31; the only difference is that the candidate takes an `Item` and reads its `Type`, while the C++ takes the kind integer directly.

what: Takes a thief's share of the party's gold, rounding the amount to whole gold pieces (half to even) and capping it at the lesser of the rolled amount and the purse, then removes it from the purse and returns the amount taken.
ev: It takes the lesser of the roll and the purse and rounds a purse with a fraction half to even (10.5 gives 10, 11.5 gives 12), matching the C++ amount rule, but it does not deduct the amount from the purse, does not clamp a negative remainder itself, and returns null on overflow instead of returning 0.

what: Clamps a chest disarm chance percentage to the allowed range of 5 to 98 percent, as the game's trap-disarming rule requires.
ev: TrapReadout clamps the disarm chance up to a minimum of 5 and down to a maximum of 98, which matches the C++ range, but it does so inline within a larger function that also computes trap-name confidence, rather than as a standalone clamp.

what: Leaving an area (R94) unloads the current floor's room by setting its roomStamp to -1, so the old room is no longer loaded when the party moves on.
ev: The C++ function only clears the current floor's roomStamp to -1 (unloading the room with no write-back or monster round), while LeaveArea writes the room back, gives an engaged group its leave round, and then clears the loaded state, so it is a related but more detailed version.

what: Computes the respawn delay in seconds for a given monster level, using the engine's formula of 5 × (level/2) × 60 (which yields 150 × level seconds, not the 150-seconds-per-level-pair the rules text states), with the result rounded through VB-style CInt rounding.
ev: It uses the same `5 * (level / 2.0) * 60` term, but adds a 1200 base, subtracts a per-tally adjustment, and floors at 120, so it does not return the C++ function's bare 150 × level rounded value.

what: Fills a companion slot from a monster, copying its identity, alignment, hits, and guild level, and setting its binding state (bound if the binding level is positive, ForLife at the maximum binding value) with all death, pending-raise, and release flags reset.
ev: AcceptJoin builds a new Companion from the front monster's Ref, Id, and hits/max hits, as fillFromCreature does, but it is a join-offer path that binds at -10 and its body is truncated, so it does not show the full field copy, binding flags, or reset of death/pending-raise/release state.

what: Converts the character's best guild rating (attack and defence values) into an attack/defence pair used by the combat and attribute calculations.
ev: It returns the highest guild attack and the highest guild defence across the character's memberships as an (att, def) pair, which is what `bestGuildPair` takes from `bestGuildAD(c)` and repackages as `AdPair{best.att, best.def}`.

what: When an item's level is zero, the character's current spell points are reduced by the spell's cost, per the game's casting rule for level-0 item casts.
ev: CastHere sets the cost to zero unless itemLevel is 0 and then deducts it in Spend(), which matches the C++ charge, but it covers only the non-SpellThrown effects, runs the charge only after the case completes, and has no clamp at zero, while CastSpell (Mordor.Core/Combat.cs) deducts the cost for every cast regardless of item level.

what: Computes the old-age death chance threshold for a character at a given percent of max age, which is 5 plus the natural log of how far past 98% the character is, returning 0 at or below 98%.
ev: The C++ `oldAgeThreshold` returns the threshold `5 + ln(pct - 98)` (0 at or below 98%), and `DiesOfOldAge` computes the same `5 + Math.Log(pct - 98)` threshold from the same percent-of-lifespan, with the same 98% gate and a guard against log(0), though it also folds in the roll and returns a bool rather than returning the threshold alone.

what: Decides whether a creature is hidden from the reader: an invisible creature is skipped only when the reader is in the dungeon (level above 0) and lacks See Invisible.
ev: Its early return uses the same condition (invisible monster, reader lacks See Invisible, DungeonLevel > 0), but that is one step inside a larger method that also files the sighting record, so it is not a standalone equivalent.

what: Counts how many of a guild's extra-swing level thresholds a character of the given level has reached, returning the number of additional swings for Multiple Swings guilds and 0 for all others.
ev: Given a guild membership (guild and level), it counts the doubling-threshold levels the character has reached and returns that count, with 0 for guilds that have no Multiple Swings threshold, which matches the C++ table lookup; it computes the thresholds by formula rather than from a table, a structural difference only.

what: Decides whether a companion is dead, which is true when its Hits are at or below zero or its dead flag is set.
where: Mordor.Core/Character.cs (no matching method name; the nearest is the death-state logic in Candidate 2's `Companion.IsDead` usage) — best candidate: Mordor.Core/CompanionSlots.cs stays.Rearrange
ev: Candidate 2's remark says a companion's hits are floored at zero so `Companion.IsDead` stands in for the original's `Hits = 0` check, but no candidate defines `isDeadCompanion` itself as "Hits <= 0 or dead flag," so this is only a related use of the same test, not an equivalent function.

what: Announces a character's gained level (via a say message) when their level has risen above the level they had before the experience award, which is the game rule that experience only signals a level-up when it crosses a threshold.
where: Mordor.Core/Combat.cs Combat.GiveExperience (the Mordor.Core file that defines it; the candidate's class name was not shown)
ev: GiveExperience announces only when experience crosses a threshold ("now has enough experience to make a level"), which matches R47's crossing-only rule, but it never announces a gained level and compares experience totals rather than levels before and after, so it does not do the same thing as announceExperienceIfLevelUp.

what: Picks which monster group a spell hits: the group the caster aimed at if it still has living members, otherwise the first group that still has living members, or -1 if none do.
ev: RefreshCombat applies the same rule (keep the aimed group if it has living members, else take the first group standing, else -1), but embedded in UI refresh code that also writes back the order target and builds display rows, and Retarget (Mordor.Core/Combat.cs) is a void, monster-index version of the same fallback.

what: Computes the bonus added to a poison or disease cure roll from the character's effective Constitution (above or below 10, doubled) minus twice the ailment's level, per Table F.
ev: The bonus expression `(effectiveCon - 10) * 2 - poisonLevel * 2` matches the C++ formula exactly, but it is computed inline inside a d200 cure roll with a threshold check, and the disease branch uses the poison level, so no candidate is a standalone equivalent of `cureRollBonus`.

what: Computes the minimum heal amount for an archive (healing) spell from its base value, power, and spell level, using the R13 formula with a fixed divisor.
ev: The candidate uses the same heal base (`baseHeal + baseHeal*log(sl)/log(10) + int(sl/10*(power-1))`) and its random roll lies in the lower half of that value, but it returns a random heal rather than the R13 minimum divided by a fixed divisor.

what: Picks one of the 11 false chest-trap names at random for the game's chest-trap bluff, using the context's RNG, with the 12th bit never selected.
ev: When the trap-name roll fails, TrapReadout shows a random name via `rng.Next(ChestTraps.Names.Length)`, which matches the false-name draw, but it is only one branch of a larger function and it is not a standalone pick over the 11 names with bit 11 excluded.

what: Adds experience earned from a melee blow to the actor and announces to the player when that gain pushes them past the threshold needed to level up.
ev: It adds the award to the character's experience and says "now has enough experience to make a level" only when the total crosses the level threshold, judged by the totals before and after, as the C++ does; it also clamps at the pin cap and announces the pin, which the C++ leaves unimplemented, so the outcome differs only when experience reaches the cap.

what: Loads a dungeon area when the party changes levels by finding the floor matching the party's current dungeon level and recording the party's current area on it as the room stamp.
ev: It records the party's current level and area as the loaded area (`_loadedArea = (_level, fl.AreaIdAt(x, y))`), which is the C++ room-stamp step, but it also generates the room's monsters, writes the room file, and logs messages, none of which the C++ function does, and it does not look up a floor by dungeon level.

what: Rolls a turn-related chance check for a companion creature against its master, returning true or false based on a percentage derived from their alignments, with certain 0% and 100% outcomes short-circuiting the random draw.
ev: Outcome.Check makes the same kind of alignment-based turn decision, but it uses fixed per-alignment thresholds (always turns two steps apart, 75% for Evil, 15% for Neutral) and always draws two random numbers, instead of computing one percentage and returning early at 0 or 100.

what: Clamps the engagement-modifier input Log(CHA) to a floor of kLogChaFloor (engine rule R22, from c18), so a Log(CHA) below the floor is raised to it and anything else passes through unchanged.
ev: The C++ function floors the Log(CHA) value itself at 1, but EngageChance is the same engagement formula and clamps charisma to at least 1 before taking the log (`Math.Log(Math.Max(1, charisma))`), which yields a floor of 0 on the log and gives different results for CHA values between 1 and e.

what: Maps a character's alignment (Good, Neutral, or Evil) to its corresponding guild-mask bit, which is used when checking guild membership eligibility by alignment.
ev: The C++ function returns the guild-mask bit for an alignment, and AllowsAlignment computes the same kind of per-alignment bit (`1 << (int)a`) but only tests it against AlignMask, so it does not return the bit and I could not confirm it matches kAlignBitGood/Neutral/Evil.

what: Decides whether a breath attack's sweep through party groups keeps going, stopping when a survivor halts it or when the kill count reaches the give-up limit of five.
ev: CompanionBreathes runs the breath sweep across groups and stops at a survivor, as the C++ does, but it caps kills at four per group rather than a running total of five, and no candidate contains the five-kill give-up predicate itself.

what: Returns true only if the party has at least one member and the first member (party index 0, the leader) is alive, which gates whether the ask-to-join rule (R122) can proceed.
ev: The C++ function checks only that the party has members and that the leader (index 0) is alive, while WhyCannotJoin gates on the joiner's own state and the party-size, name, alignment, and location rules, and the leader-alive check appears only in candidate 2 and 5's `_party.Members[0].IsDead` early return (candidate 2's AskToJoin also checks that first, so it is the closest match to the leader-alive gate, though it does more).

what: Returns whether the character's Defend order is active, which in game terms makes that character harder to rob.
ev: No candidate returns whether the Defend order is active; the closest, Mordor.Core/Combat.cs DefenseOf, only mentions in a comment that Defend makes you harder to rob (MONSMOD.BAS:3323) while its code computes defence value, and the other candidates handle Defend's display, setting, or clearing.

what: Refuses a dead character's attempt to join the party while monsters are present, per the SRD c12p1 join rule.
ev: Its doc comment states the same rule (a dead joiner is refused with "Cannot raise character in Combat!" while monsters are present), but the visible code is cut off before that check, and Mordor.Core/Party.cs Party.WhyCannotJoin refuses dead characters unconditionally rather than only when monsters are present.

what: Refuses a user-initiated window close by showing the player a message telling them to use the Mordor EXIT buttons to leave the game.
ev: RefuseCloseBox also cancels a user-initiated window close (`e.Cancel = true`), but instead of showing the fixed "Please use the Mordor EXIT buttons" message it runs the port's "Exit Mordor?" query or a "Cannot exit while monsters are in the area!" notice, so the message text and outcome differ.

what: Prints the general store's stock list in the town menu, numbering each distinct item as a row the player can buy from and showing each item's name, gold price, and copy count.
ev: ShowStore builds the General Store screen, and its visible code is cut off before the Buy grid, so it is unclear whether it numbers distinct items or shows counts. Mordor.Modding/ModHost.cs ModHost.StoreRowOrder and Mordor.Core/StoreStock.cs StoreStock.PriceOf cover related pieces (row order and per-item price), but none does the numbered distinct-item listing with name, price and copy count.

what: At fight end, checks whether the lead group's first creature is Asmodeus and, if so, applies the defeat-of-Asmodeus outcome to the game state.
ev: EndCombat takes slot 0 of the lead group (from Foes[0].Ref, or Monsters[0] as a fallback), checks whether it is Asmodeus, and calls BeatAsmodeus() before the room is stored and the spoils are awarded, which matches the C++ check's position at the start of fight-end processing, though EndCombat runs this only inside the `_combat.Won` branch and derives slot 0 itself instead of receiving it as a parameter.

what: Computes spit and electrocution damage for a companion by taking half the special hit range between attacker and target levels, then applying the target's resistance percentage.
where: Mordor.Core/SpecialHits.cs Kind.Raw (resistance comes from Mordor.Core/SpecialHits.cs Kind.AfterResistance, used in Mordor.Core/Combat.cs left.CompanionSpits)
ev: Kind.Raw uses the same half-range share for non-breath kinds and AfterResistance applies the resistance, so together with the CompanionSpits call site they reproduce the C++ function, but no single candidate does both steps and Raw does not separate spit from electrocution.

what: Builds the list of item IDs eligible to appear for a given level range and item category, taking one contiguous run of matching items starting at the first match, per SRD rule R7.
ev: None of the eight candidates builds a list of item IDs filtered by a level range and category (the C++ contiguous-run scan); they all concern spells, guild rates, or monster damage, and CastGate.Unfit touches an item's spell level only as a gate on casting refusals.

what: Rolls a percent chance, based on the identify skill and whether the item is in fog, to decide whether an unidentified item gets renamed.
ev: RenameChance computes the same percent chance (skill +20, times 0.75 in fog, clamped 10 to 90) that rollRename passes to rng.percent, but no candidate performs the percent roll itself.

what: When a character's standing combat order is forced to Fight because they have run out of spell points, it resets the order and emits a message telling the player the order was dropped.
ev: ItemCharge also forces the order to Fight via `Sub102FMinusOne` and emits a message when a resource runs out, but the resource is item charges rather than spell points, and it removes the item order instead of only resetting the standing order.

what: Checks whether a given member number refers to an existing character in the party roster, returning true if the roster lookup finds one.
ev: Buffs.Member returns the party member or null, which is the same null-check pattern as the C++ accMember lookup, but it finds the member by name rather than by 1-based slot number, so the number-to-roster check is absent.

what: Computes the chance to identify an item from the player's skill, adding 20, clamping to 10–90, and then quartering it when the player is in darkness (R72).
ev: It takes the same inputs and clamps to 10..90, but it applies darkness as a 0.75 multiplier on skill before adding 20 and clamping, whereas the C++ adds 20, clamps, and then divides the chance by 4 in darkness, so the outcomes differ.

what: Raises the known level of a sighting to whichever is higher, the current known value or the new grade, so Known never goes down (engine rule R23/c12).
ev: No candidate is just the max-raise, but FileSighting contains the same rule inline (`if (rec.Known < grade) rec.Known = grade`), and it also covers the grade derivation, name, place, and counts that the C++ helper does not.

what: Packs an item's seven status flags (guild-issued, aligned, chest teleporter, destructible, equipped, lost, slot-cursed) into a single bit-field integer so they can be saved to the game's text save file.
where: Mordor.Core/Character.cs Character.SyncSlotCurses (or none for a flag-packing match; no candidate packs the item flags into a bit-field)
ev: None of the candidates builds the seven-flag bit-field integer (guildIssued 1, aligned 2, chestTeleporter 4, destructible 8, equipped 16, lost 32, slotCursed 64) that the C++ `itemFlagBits` returns, so the closest is only a loose relation: SyncSlotCurses touches the slot-curse flag for equipped gear, not the packing.

what: Turns the result of a combine/swap check into the message shown to the player, such as "Item #N combined to Item #M." or the reason a combine was refused.
ev: Combine emits the same "is not compatible class", "is not of the same type", and "STORE: Item #N" wording for the same conditions, but it does the whole combine rather than mapping a check result to text, and its not-identified message ("is not completely identified.") differs from the C++ "Not Completely Identified!" text, while the Ok and Overflow messages are not produced as strings there.

what: Rolls a d100 against the chest's lock chance and the chest class to decide whether the chest is unlocked or magically locked, with magic locks suppressed in squares where magic doesn't work (ANTIMAGIC or EXTINGUISHER).
ev: No candidate rolls the d100 against LockedChance, checks ChestClass > 1, or suppresses the lock in no-magic squares; Loot.DropsItem rolls a d100 for an item, Rules.MagicallyLocked only tests an existing lock state, and EncounterGold's comment says the lock roll happens in the caller.

what: Decides whether the damage-spell group loop keeps going, returning true while fewer groups have been hit than the spell's Damage1 count and the loop is still within the four fixed damage slots.
where: Mordor.Core/Combat.cs CastDamage (candidate 1, a private method that holds the group loop)
ev: CastDamage walks the damage spell's groups over the four slots via `CombatMonster.BySlot` and `Alive(g)`, so it contains the group-loop logic that the C++ `damageLoopContinues` predicate controls, but no candidate expresses the continue condition itself (groupCount < Damage1 and step < 4) as a standalone check, and the visible portion of the candidate does not show that exact condition.

what: Find Direction (reference effect 13) reports the party's current facing as a compass code in a spell-cast message for dcast.
ev: No candidate reports the party's facing code in a spell-cast message; the nearest, DungeonWindow.axaml.cs SavePos, writes the facing code (+1) onto party members' records but never reports it, and the other facing-based candidates (RelativeDirection, TeleportTo, MazeSelect.Select) use facing to compute movement or visibility rather than reporting it.

what: Clamps a computed raise chance to the allowed band of 10 to 98 (using kRaiseChanceMin and kRaiseChanceMax), so a raise-the-dead success chance never falls outside the rule's limits.
ev: The C++ function only clamps an arbitrary input to 10..98, and SpellRaiseChance applies the same 10..98 clamp, but only after computing the chance from CON and effect and overriding it for rock deaths.

what: Computes the total gold a character needs to advance from level 1 to level n+1 using the archive closed-form formula, scaled by a gold factor (ggf) and rounded half up.
ev: Fn12B2 uses the same 30.1 step and the same (1 + Gold/10) multiplier, but it sums odd multiples (2i-1) to get a per-level cost of about level² × 30.1, not the C++'s sum of squares n(n+1)(2n+1)/6 for the total from level 1 to n+1, and no candidate computes that closed form.

what: Reports whether a companion slot is in use, meaning it is marked occupied and refers to an actual creature.
ev: Show sets `_filled[i] = c != null`, which covers the "occupied" half of the C++ predicate, but no candidate tests `Ref >= 0`, and Show is a page-rendering method rather than a standalone check.

what: Confinement buy takes one penned companion of a monster for the payer, charging a price based on the creature's base worth and how many are penned, then releasing one pen slot.
where: Mordor.Core/Confinement.cs Confinement.PriceToBuy (with Confinement.Take as the closest match for the pen release)
ev: PriceToBuy covers only the pricing step, based on the monster's base value and the number already penned, and Take covers only the one-slot release without the pen-allowed check, while no candidate charges the payer or validates the inputs as confinementBuy does.

what: Computes a paralysed character's attack and defence values from base, best guild and equipped gear bonuses, with the stat term taken as zero and results floored at zero.
ev: The candidate's docstring describes the paralysed outcome (base, guild and gear with the stat part removed), but it gets there through the stored AD shift rather than a separate function that zeroes the stat term, so its output depends on shift state and it is not the same computation.

what: Rolls which quest, if any, a guild member is offered: a 6% chance of no quest, otherwise a 25% chance of an item (Fetch) quest when the guild level is high enough, falling back to a monster (Defeat) quest when eligible.
ev: Both roll a no-quest chance, then a 25% item (Fetch) quest when eligible, else a monster (Defeat) quest, but RollQuest uses a guild-specific QuestPercent gate, a 5% let-off, a level-under-5 cutoff, and a level-above-15 item condition, and it never returns no-quest for a guild level that is too low for monster quests, unlike the C++ function.

what: Returns whether the first group in the encounter has a join offer, which is a game rule about whether monsters in that group will offer to join the party.
ev: JoinLine reads the same field, `group[0].JoinOffer`, but uses it only to build the "N goblins offer to 'j'oin" text rather than returning the flag itself, and AcceptJoin and Finish touch that field only as a guard or as part of other logic.

what: Computes the hit points a character gains on reaching a new level, using the guild's average hits, a Nomad-only bonus for levels in a given range, a constitution bonus below the max level, and a fixed past-max amount when the level exceeds the cap.
ev: LevelUp computes the same kind of per-level hit gain (past-cap LateHits, AvgHits plus a constitution bonus only below the cap), but it adds a random roll, uses a hard-coded CON>16 threshold, and has no Nomad-only extra-hits bonus for a level range, which the C++ function has.

what: Reads one 7-word stats-required run, a 7-word stat-mod run, and four 32-bit values (ability, alignment, resistance, charge) from a byte buffer at an offset into an item record, returning false if any read runs past the buffer.
ev: LoadItems reads item records including StatsRequired and StatsMod as 7-word runs, but it reads them after many other fields rather than as the first two runs, and it never reads the four dword fields ability/alignment/resistance/charge at the same position. The C++ function is a single fixed-offset reader for those six fields only, while no candidate does exactly that.

what: In town, when the player presses ALT-p with a party of two or more, it decides whether the party pools gold on hand or also deposits it, refusing outright in the dungeon or for a party of one.
ev: It returns the original's PoolOnHand by default and defers to a mod's answer, which covers the pooling choice, but it has no in-town or party-of-one refusal, and the truncated DungeonWindow.HandlePartyKey P case looks like the refusal path but can't be confirmed from the snippet.

what: Validates a typed gold amount for a give-gold command, refusing it if it exceeds the gold held and otherwise converting it into the internal gold units to hand over.
ev: GoldAnswer matches the C++ validation (empty is 0, Val below 1 is 0, Val above gold held is refused, otherwise the text is returned), and GoldFromTag covers the CLng conversion, but no single candidate combines them or does the C++ gold-unit scaling and the post-CLng check against held gold, which uses VbCurrency rather than units.

what: Caps a spell level to the range 1 to 255 so that the effective spell level used for spell damage and healing stays within the game's limits (a spell level of 0 counts as 1).
ev: That method clamps the level it is given to 1..255 with the same bounds as the C++ function, but only as one step inside a larger damage calculation, and no candidate is a standalone clamp of a spell level; Rules.SpellLevel also uses 1..255 but transforms a guild level (Int(level/2 + 0.5)) rather than clamping its input.

what: Computes the experience a single blow earns for the attacker or their owner, using the game's per-blow formula scaled by damage inflicted, monster and attacker guild levels, companion status, and party size.
ev: It returns 0 for non-positive hits, applies the same per-blow formula with the 0.25 companion factor and the 1/(1+guildLevel/333) factor, then applies the party factor and half-even rounding in the same order as the C++ function.

what: Checks whether a character has learned a given spell by scanning their list of known spell IDs, returning true if the spell is present.
ev: The C++ function is a boolean membership test over a stored list of spell IDs, while Spellbook.Known derives the known spells from the guild spell table and returns a list, so a caller could check membership on its result, but no candidate tests by ID directly.

what: Runs the pre-attack special effects for a monster in game terms, first its breath attack and then its acid attack, against the chosen party member.
ev: The candidates have no monster pre-attack that runs breath then acid against a chosen party member; CompanionTurn runs breath then spit, but for a companion's turn, and it also draws friendly fire and adds a blow.

what: On arrival at a dungeon level, it finds that level's floor state and, if found, triggers the look-around report from rule R102.
ev: The C++ `arrived` triggers the R102 look-around report on arrival at a level, and WalkHere/RefreshAreaLook build that same look-around listing (mdrmazLookAround), but they run on the F2 key, not on arrival, and no candidate performs an arrival-triggered look-around report.

what: In the Mordor rules, a neutral lead character gets a 40% chance to be friendly, rolled only when the lead's alignment is Neutral.
ev: No candidate rolls a 40% friendly chance gated on the lead character being Neutral; Rules.EngageChance computes a monster's chance to attack from alignment pairing and charisma, which is a different mechanic.

what: Handles a character who is rescued after being lost in the dungeon: adds the days spent waiting to their age, cures any poison, moves them to town, and announces they were carried home.
where: Mordor.App/DungeonWindow.axaml.cs DungeonWindow.WaitForRescue (the closest-flow match; Mordor.Core/Rescue.cs Rescue.CarryHome is the closest pure-logic match)
ev: The candidates roll the days, add them to age, move the character to town (DungeonLevel = 0, Area = -1), and announce the find, but none clears poison, and CarryHome explicitly leaves it alone, so the poison cure from the C++ function is missing.

what: Computes the roll increase granted by a magic lock as the natural log of (level + 10) times 5, returning 0 if that argument is non-positive.
ev: The candidate applies the same `Math.Log(dungeonLevel + 10) * 5` increase, but only as one addend inside the larger drop roll, and it has no guard returning 0 when the log argument is non-positive as the C++ function does.

what: Returns true only when an item's fit to a character is a full match (FitClass::Full), which is the condition for the item's effect bits to count, while opposed-fit curses are handled separately by applyEquipCurse.
ev: `ItemHelps` returns `FitFor(...) == ItemFit.Fine`, which matches `fitCountsEffects` returning `fit == FitClass::Full`, assuming `Fine` corresponds to C++ `Full` (the candidates' `Adjacent` half-strength case indicates it does not count fully).

what: Rolls the seer's frequency-line check by drawing a random number and returning true when it falls below kSeerFrequencyPercent (75) out of 100, per rule R64 step 4 of the Seer locate-monster service.
ev: No candidate draws a random number and tests it against 75 for the frequency line; Candidate 2 (Seer.Frequency) only maps a Chance value to a text label, and Candidate 7 (Seer.LocateCharacter) rolls a different check against three times the level.

what: For each surviving party member (skipping the dead), it writes a guild-log entry recording their Asmodeus defeat, with the wording depending on whether the character was in a party.
ev: The C++ writes a guild-log line per survivor and skips the dead, while BeatAsmodeus appends a guild-log line for every party member, choosing the party or lone wording via `inAParty = _party.Size > 1`; the candidate does not skip dead members, but its loop is over `_party.Members`, so the dead-skip difference is the only gap, and the vanished-body no-rule-effect point also matches its "Nothing else changes" comment.

what: Rolls a percent chance, based on how many days the store's stock has aged, to decide whether the store replenishes its items.
ev: It opens its loop with the same percent-chance gate (`rng.NextDouble() * 100 > chance`, with chance taken from days and clamped 1..50), but that gate is one step inside a full restock routine, not a standalone roll, and there is no separate chance function like `storeReplenishChance`.

what: Reports to the player, via a message, that levels were regained below the character's maximum level, without applying the bonus hit points since their amount is not modelled.
ev: No candidate reports regained levels below the maximum: Character.LevelUp (candidate 4) awards hits for a newly made level and ForfeitQuest (candidate 5) takes hits back on demotion, but neither handles the regain notification.

what: Returns true when a breath or acid attack has reduced a companion's hit points below zero, so that companion is carried away, while a companion at exactly zero is left for the next sweep.
ev: Run is the next-sweep carry that the C++ comment says picks up companions at exactly zero, but it treats `Hits <= 0` as carry-worthy (`c.Hits > 0` is skipped) rather than the `hits < 0` test in `breathAcidCarryTest`, and no candidate contains that breath/acid predicate.

what: Rolls a placeholder 50 percent chance, when a monster hits the player, to destroy a destructible item in the given pack slot if its level qualifies, and removes it if the roll succeeds.
ev: The quicksand branch rolls `Rules.QuicksandTakesSomething` and then removes a random pack slot's item if it is destructible, which is close to the C++ slot-destroy step. It differs in trigger (quicksand, not a monster hit), has no floor-minus-2 level gate, and picks a random slot rather than taking one as input.

what: Checks whether the hands the player is already using, plus the item's hand width, stay within the two-hand limit (R6), so an item can be equipped only if enough hands are free.
where: Mordor.Core/Character.cs Character.EquipProblem (with Character.HandsUsed as the running hand count)
ev: EquipProblem performs the same R6 test, `HandsUsed(item) + it.NHands > 2`, returning "No Free Hands!", but it is one step inside a larger function that also checks worn-count, guild, level and stats, so it is not a standalone predicate like the C++ `handsCheckPasses`.

what: When a charm fills the last companion slot, the charmed creature leaves the fight, the next creature in its group is felled, and the third creature in the group is set to nought hits and not unrolled, per the game's charm fallout rules.
ev: No candidate sets the charmed creature's fight flags, felles the next group member, or zeroes the third member's hits; Combat.cs `Charmed` only builds the companion record, and the visible part of `CastDamage` is truncated, so its unseen body is the only place the fallout could still be.

what: Moves an item from a bank slot into the first free pack slot, re-reads its identification level against the character's knowledge (raising it if higher and logging "Item identified."), and clears the bank slot, or refuses with "Pack is full" if no pack slot is free.
ev: It moves a vault item into the receiver's first free pack slot, re-reads its identification and clears the vault slot, but it adds a guild-issued refusal, takes a separate receiver character, and returns a message string instead of a withdraw outcome, and it does not log "Item identified." itself.

what: Cures poison on a character when they rest in town, but only if they currently have a poison level above zero.
ev: RestInCity clears poison on each member as part of the town rest (via EndAilmentsAndSpellResists), but it also does much more, and the poison-only cure, Mordor.Core/Character.cs CurePoison, lacks the town-rest trigger and the level guard.

what: Reads an option's text value from the player's settings.ini file, falling back to the legacy MORDOR.INI file and then to a supplied default when the key is absent.
ev: It applies the same settings-then-MORDOR.INI precedence per key, but it loads every option into typed fields with per-field defaults instead of returning one text value with a caller-supplied default.

what: Renders the party roster as text for the player, listing each member's number, name, race, active guild and level, HP and SP, status, experience and gold.
ev: RefreshParty rebuilds the party roster rows (name, hits, spells, status, combat order) but builds UI controls rather than text and omits race, guild, level, XP and gold, while SaveImport.cs order.Summary lists characters with race, guild, level, hits and gold as text but describes imported save files rather than the live party.

what: Re-runs the square the party has just moved onto by settling and describing the area again (per R65/R81), without re-firing any chute or teleporter.
ev: The C++ function only re-settles and describes the area, while this candidate also re-works out position, records arrival and runs AfterMove, which applies square effects, so it differs in scope (ArriveBySpell is a closer match in its settle step but also runs the full square routine).

what: Applies the R42 water/quicksand hazard to a non-levitating character by subtracting the hazard level from their current hits, and on quicksand may roll (R43) to pick a random pack slot whose item the caller should destroy.
ev: It does the same R42/R43 steps as the C++: it returns early when levitating, subtracts the level from hits, rolls `QuicksandTakesSomething`, and picks a slot with `_rng.Next(PackSlots - 1) + 1`, though it destroys the item directly and adds logging and a death check instead of returning a result for the caller to apply.

what: Decides that a complication is guaranteed for a character whose age is at least half the race's maximum age, per the game's chapter 18 rules.
ev: The C++ function is a boolean threshold (age >= raceMaxAge / 2), and ComplicationChance expresses the same rule as a percentage that reaches 100% at half the race's lifespan, with Complicates then always true; no candidate returns the bool itself.

what: Returns the combined effect bits of all equipped items that apply under the fit rules (Table T-5), delegating the actual calculation to gearEffects, with Critical Hit and Backstab excluded from having any effect.
ev: The C++ wrapper only delegates to gearEffects, and Candidate 1 is the same OR of ability bits over equipped slots that pass the fit check (`Counts`), but it does not explicitly drop Critical Hit and Backstab bits, which the C++ comment says have no effect.

what: Charges a Seer's fee to a character by spending hand gold first and then bank gold, returning false if the payer cannot afford it.
ev: Pay takes gold on hand first, then the bank, and returns false without moving anything when the purse is short, which matches seerCharge's charPay logic; the only difference is that Pay does not short-circuit on a fee of zero or less.

what: Decides whether a piece of equipment can be worn or toggled on, refusing when the class's max-worn limit is zero and capping at the limit when it is positive, with negative values treated as uncapped per the port's R70 rule.
ev: The C++ function is a pure predicate that refuses when maxWorn is 0 and when maxWorn is positive and wornInClass has reached it, and EquipProblem performs the cap check (`max > 0 && WornOfClass >= max`) but adds hands, guild, level and stat checks and does not refuse on max == 0 itself; Character.IsWearable covers only the zero-refusal step, so no single candidate matches.

what: Classifies a monster-versus-character level comparison into High, Low, or Even bands using 0.75× and 1.25× thresholds, which feeds game mechanics such as breath and spit attack chances.
ev: No candidate compares a character level against a monster level with 0.75× and 1.25× thresholds; the closest, Loot.cs of.RollDrop, bands item drop levels by halving them, and Asmodeus.DropBand just returns a fixed range of three floors.

what: Maps a library item's identification state to its grade for the Library, returning 4 for fully identified, 3 for mostly identified, and 0 for partial (which hides the item from the listing).
ev: FileItem maps IdLevel.All to grade 4, Mostly to 3, and anything else to 0, sets the name only on a new record, raises the grade only upward, and writes the record either way, which matches libraryItemGrade's mapping (the C++ function itself only returns the grade, while the candidate also applies it to the store).

what: Computes the base melee factor F from the guild level and fighting modifier using the SRD R23 formula, a game mechanic that feeds into combat damage.
ev: Its fighting case (case 4) computes the same expression, FightingBase + ((Log(100 + lvl) / 1.75 - 2.3) * rating^2) / 2, but clamps the level with Math.Max(1, guildLevel), so a level-0 input gives a different result than the C++ function.

what: Computes a companion's stone value from its Constitution score via a logarithmic formula (CON × ln(max(1, CON)) / ln 2.5), minus a floor amount, per the R30 rule.
ev: No candidate computes a companion stone value from CON with a logarithmic formula minus a floor; the closest, Morgue.CompanionChance and SpellEffect.CompanionRaiseChance, return raise-success percentages, and SpellRaiseChance uses a linear CON term.

what: Returns the gold a character can spend for an exchange: only on-hand gold while in the dungeon, but on-hand plus banked gold when in town (rule R23.2).
ev: The same rule appears inline as `available = from.DungeonLevel != 0 ? from.GoldOnHand : purse` (on-hand in the dungeon, on-hand plus bank in town), but only as the spending limit inside a transfer, not as a standalone function, and it adds an overflow check that the C++ lacks; ExchangeWindow.ShowGold computes the same quantity for display.

what: Applies the Potion of Youth / Dragon's Blood effect by subtracting the given number of years (converted to days) from the character's age, with the age clamped so it never goes below zero.
where: Mordor.Core/ItemUse.cs ItemUse.Younger (the `Younger` method in the `box` class)
ev: It subtracts `years * 365` from age like `duseYounger`, but it floors age at 16 years instead of zero, and it also returns a message, so the clamping outcome differs.

what: Applies the stone-raise cost to the character's Constitution, reducing the CON stat by a fixed amount (kStoneConLoss) after any raise attempt regardless of outcome, with no floor.
ev: Resolve applies the same unfloored `c.Stats[(int)Stat.Con] -= 1` for stone deaths, but it sits inside a larger routine and returns early on a quiet failure, so the stone loss is skipped in that case, unlike the C++ "regardless of outcome" behavior.

what: Reads the x, y, x2, y2, and z2 coordinate fields from a JSON object into a FloorTeleporter record, as part of the generated game-data loader.
where: Mordor.Core/MdrLoader.cs MdrLoader.LoadFloor (the private `LoadFloor` method, inside the per-teleporter loop)
ev: The loop reads X, Y, X2, Y2 and Z2 with the same word reads into a `Floor.Teleporter`, but it is only one part of a full-floor loader and adds a filter (`X > 0 && Y > 0`) that the C++ reader doesn't have.

what: Resolves which mod folders the game should search, using the semicolon-separated paths in the MORDOR_MODS setting when it is set, and otherwise falling back to the mods folder beside the game folder and the one beside the program.
ev: It matches the C++ logic (';'-split, trimmed, empties dropped, otherwise the game-folder and program-folder mods dirs), but it treats a set-but-blank MORDOR_MODS as unset and returns the default roots, whereas the C++ returns no roots.

what: Returns the highest spell ceiling among all guilds that have a spell table, computed as the best guildCeiling value over those guilds (0 if none qualify), which determines the strongest spell level a party can reach through the guilds.
ev: No candidate takes the maximum spell ceiling over all guilds with a spell table; the nearest, `it.ReachingGuilds`, filters per spell and yields per-guild levels, and `Rules.BestGuildAD` takes the best attack and defense, not a spell ceiling.

what: Decides whether casting a spell with a given effect code requires the caster to choose a target, returning true only for effect codes 0 and 18.
ev: It decides the "Cast on Who?" prompt for the Damage/Cure cases from the same `Damage2 > 0` (M5B33) test as the C++ rule, but it also asks for many other effects, and it returns "no ask" for party-wide spells, so it is not the same predicate as `castAsksWho`, which returns true only for effect codes 0 and 18.

what: Returns the index of the first empty companion slot (one whose ref is -1) for a new companion joining the party, or -1 if all four slots are occupied.
ev: Add returns the same first-hole index (or -1 when full), but it also writes the companion into that slot and takes an extra `keepSlotName` argument, whereas the C++ function is a side-effect-free search over the slot array; the bare search is presumably `FirstFree`, which isn't shown.

what: Computes the ailment roll offset for a character from their effective Constitution (relative to a base of 10, weighted) minus a penalty scaled by level, which feeds into the chance of resisting poison, disease, and similar status effects.
ev: AilmentStep inlines the same `(effectiveCon - 10) * 2 - poisonLevel * 2` offset inside its cure rolls, but it does not return the offset on its own, and it adds the roll, the thresholds, and the hit losses.

what: Handles the typed "quest <member>" command by checking that the named character belongs to the Nomad guild, refusing if a quest is already open, and otherwise assigning a new guild quest and replying to the player.
ev: It rolls and writes a new guild quest onto the character's guild, as `cmdQuest` does via `assignGuildQuest`, but it runs after a level is made rather than from a typed "quest <member>" command, and it has no member lookup, Nomad-guild check, open-quest refusal, or reply text.

what: Finishes a teleport for the party leader by optionally pruning dead members, moving the leader to the destination square and level, then applying the after-a-fall, square re-run, and area-settling steps defined in rules R80 and R81.
where: Mordor.App/DungeonWindow.axaml.cs DungeonWindow.TeleporterSquare (also Mordor.Core/Party.cs Party.RemoveTheDead covers only the prune step)
ev: TeleporterSquare moves the party to teleporter destinations, splits off members not on the leader's square, and forces a settle, but it is the square-routine teleporter rather than the leader's teleport finish, and it has no level-change call, afterAFall, or rerunSquare step, while RemoveTheDead matches only the initial prune.

what: Checks whether a character's class allows wearing another item, refusing with a non-None WearRefusal when the number of worn items has already reached the class's maximum (a negative maximum means no limit).
ev: EquipProblem contains the same test (`max > 0 && WornOfClass(cls, item) >= max` returns a refusal), but it is buried among guild, level, and stat checks, and it treats a maximum of 0 as no limit where the C++ function refuses whenever the maximum is 0 or higher.

what: Shows the player a caption for each group the damage spell reached, plus a "Failed!" message if the cast did nothing.
ev: CastDamage emits one caption per group the spell reaches and a "Failed" caption when nothing happens, matching the C++ structure, but its caption wording ("You Fried Two", "Failed" without the "!") differs from the C++ placeholder text ("The spell reaches a group.", "Failed!").

what: Returns true only when an item's level is 0, so that the level-0 item gates apply to buffers and level-0 items in the Mordor spell-casting rules.
ev: No candidate returns whether level-0 item gates apply to a buffer or item. The closest, Candidate 6 (DungeonWindow.axaml.cs box.CastAndThrow), only branches on `itemLevel > 0` to choose a heal level, and Candidate 7 (ItemUse.CastLevel) substitutes the caster's level for level 0 rather than gating on it.

what: Rolls a percentage die and walks the spawn table's cumulative percentages to pick which item, if any, spawns for the player.
ev: No candidate walks a running sum of percentages to pick an entry; the closest, Loot.cs Loot.DropsItem, makes a single chance roll with no table walk, and Loot.cs Loot.RollDrop picks from a band of item records rather than cumulative percentages.

what: Computes the percentage chance of losing CON on a raise, as 50 minus twice the character's natural CON, floored at zero.
ev: The candidate computes `Math.Max(0, 50 - con * 2)` on natural CON, which is the same formula and zero floor as the C++ `max(0, 50 - CON*2)`.

what: Gates lock eligibility by chest class, allowing locks only on BOX, CHEST, and ASMODEUS chests (any class above 1).
ev: No candidate gates lock eligibility on chest class; Mordor.Core/Rules.cs EncounterGold only mentions in its doc comment that a chest can be locked only above class 1 and takes `chestLocked` as a plain input, while ChestTrap's `chestClass <= 0` gate applies to traps with a different threshold.

what: Advances the spawn-try counter by one for each attempt at placing a monster group, a bookkeeping step in the game's spawn procedure that the caller resets per group.
ev: The C++ function is a bare per-attempt increment (`tries + 1`) for a spawn-placement counter, and no candidate has that standalone bookkeeping step. The closest, `Combat.cs whatever.Generate`, is an encounter generator with no shared try counter, and `WaveMix.cs Fn19F4` and `Confinement.cs per.Replenish` use retry counters in unrelated procedures.

what: Returns true when the target creature has the immunity-to-weapons bit set (bit 5), which nullifies any weapon attack against it per rules R14 and R15.
where: Mordor.Core/Combat.cs struct.PlayerSwings (closest weapon-vs-target gate, but it checks the NeedsGoodWeapon property, not the weapon-immunity bit)
ev: No candidate tests the target's immunity-to-weapons bit (bit 5) to nullify a weapon attack; the magic-immunity checks in SpellHitsOn use bits 2 and 3 for spells, and PlayerSwings only skips a weapon when the monster needs a good weapon and the weapon's floor is too low.

what: Parses a typed gold amount as VB's CLng would, accepting optional sign and blanks, rejecting anything else (including thousands separators), and rounding half to even to a whole gold value.
ev: It matches the C++ on whole-string CLng with blanks, a sign, half-to-even rounding, and a null/Type-mismatch failure, but it accepts thousands separators (AllowThousands), &H/&O radix literals, and E/D exponents, which giveCLng rejects.

what: Checks whether at least kAilmentTickMs milliseconds have passed since the last ailment tick, so that the game's ailment effects advance every 4 seconds of real time (rule R21).
ev: No candidate compares elapsed time against a 4-second threshold; Candidate 1 (DungeonWindow.AilmentTick) is the tick body that a design-time timer fires every four seconds, not the due check, and Candidate 3 (PlayClock.Tick) tracks play time rather than ailment timing.

what: When a party member dies, this clears all of that member's ailments (status effects) by calling endEveryAilment on them.
ev: The C++ `deathHeadRoutine` does nothing but call `endEveryAilment` on the victim, and `EndEveryAilment` does that same sub048C work (unparalyse, clear poison, disease and spell resists, then recompute), differing only in that the victim is passed in directly rather than looked up by index. Candidate 1 (`Sub0930Head`) also calls `EndEveryAilment` but adds `ReleaseFollowers`, which the C++ function does not do.

what: Rolls a quest for a joined guild member at their current level, either letting them off with no task or assigning them a Defeat or Fetch quest at a level tier, and announces the result to the player.
ev: The candidate matches the C++ roll structure (rounded 0-100 draw, let-off at 5 or below, tier from level), but it adds a QuestPercent gate and a fetch chance of 25% only above level 15, where the C++ uses a 50/50 split, and it does not do the joined check, quest state setting, or announcement.

what: Computes the initial cost of a spell for a given guild by calling the general spell-cost formula with the character's spell level set to 0, so the spell's base cost and guild modifier are applied.
ev: Spellbook.Cost is the general spell-cost formula (via Rules.Fn1485Price) that wikiInitialCost delegates to, but it takes the character's actual guilds and level rather than a guild with spell level 0, so no candidate computes the initial cost itself.

what: Computes the published spell cost for a spell, scaling its rated spell level and cost ratio by the caster's rate and guild level using the R29 test-page formula, then truncates the result to an integer.
ev: It computes the same quantity (rated level × cost ratio × rate × 1.9 over spell level, floored) but uses exact integer arithmetic instead of the page's `- 0.0001` epsilon, so results differ on edge cases, and a cost ratio of 0 gives 0 here versus -1 in the C++.

what: Rolls a percent chance, computed by identifyChance from the character and the darkness and fog conditions, to decide whether the identification check (R72, per group, per character, per tick) succeeds.
ev: Rules.IdentifyChance computes the same clamped per-tick percentage (skill, reduced by darkness, plus 20), but it takes a skill and a dark flag instead of a character and fog, and it does not perform the RNG percent roll that rollIdentify returns; the per-tick caller DungeonWindow.IdentifyMonsters is only partly visible.

what: Computes the gold depth term used in Mordor's treasure calculation from a found level, reproducing the original formula Log((LevelFound+1) / Log(2)) with the division placed inside the log as written.
where: Mordor.Core/Rules.cs Rules.GroupGold (the candidate named "1.GroupGold"; the method is GroupGold in Rules.cs)
ev: GroupGold contains the same depth term, `Math.Log((m.LevelFound + 1) / Math.Log(2))`, but it is one step inside a larger group-gold calculation, not a standalone function, and it does not isolate that term as the C++ function does.

what: Decides whether a party death in the party window offers the player rescue, returning true only when the party has more than one member (a port quirk noted as possibly differing from the original game).
ev: The same `_party.Size > 1` test decides whether a death in company goes to the party-list update instead of the dead screen with its rescue offer (candidate 1 `Kill` uses it the same way), but the candidate's outcome is the reverse of the C++ return value: it offers rescue when the party is alone, while `deathOffersRescue` returns true when the party has more than one member.

what: Deposits gold from the player's carried purse into their bank balance, refusing amounts that are zero, negative, or more than the gold on hand.
ev: The deposit branch refuses amounts that are zero or negative or above gold on hand, and otherwise moves the amount from on-hand to bank, matching the C++ rule; it differs only in taking text input, returning a BankAnswer enum, and skipping overflowing updates.

what: Attempts to poison a character: a resistance roll against the Poison resistance decides whether the character becomes poisoned at the found level, with the poisoned status and message applied if the roll fails.
ev: Spring also rolls against the Poison resistance and sets Poisoned and PoisonLevel at the dungeon level, but it compares against half the resistance with the test reversed, has no PoisonLevel == 0 guard, and prints no message, so it is not the same as tryPoison.

what: Computes the damage a companion takes after resistance, reducing it by half the resist percentage (integer-truncated) of the incoming damage.
ev: It applies the same "half the resistance" reduction to the damage, but it keeps the fractional half (`resistancePercent / 2.0`) and rounds with `VbInt` instead of the C++ integer division and truncation, so results differ for odd resist values and at rounding boundaries.

what: Computes a character's age as a percentage of their race's lifespan (age in years divided by lifespan, times 100), returning 0 if the lifespan is non-positive, which feeds the old-age death check.
ev: It computes the same percentage `(ageDays / 365.0) / raceLifespanYears * 100.0` with the same non-positive-lifespan guard, but it then applies the old-age death roll instead of returning the percentage itself.

what: Checks whether a given chest trap (such as Not Trapped through Withering) is set in a bitmask of trap flags for a chest in the game.
ev: The C++ function is a pure predicate that tests whether bit `trap` is set in `trapFlags`, while `is.ChestTrap` only uses the same `(TrapFlags & (1 << t)) != 0` test inside a loop that randomly generates a trap for a chest, so the bit test matches but the purpose does not.

what: Applies Mordor's R11 swing rule, where a guild's award replaces the current swing figure only when the award is higher, so swings never go down.
ev: After computing each guild's extra swings, RecalcSwings runs `if (extra > Swings) Swings = extra;`, which is the same keep-the-higher rule as `raiseSwingsIfHigher(currentSwings, award)`, though it is inlined into a loop over guilds and mutates a field.

what: Implements R25 by stopping the combat clock, letting the monsters make their free attacks during a free round, and then restarting the clock.
where: Mordor.App/DungeonWindow.axaml.cs CombatTick (candidate 1), with the free-attack step in Mordor.Core/MonsterAttack.cs CombatEngine.MonsterAttacks (candidate 7) as the closest rules-side match.
ev: The C++ function is a short wrapper that stops the combat clock, runs one monsters' free attack round (sub0A64), and restarts the clock, while the candidates cover related pieces (the timer guard and clock-off flag in CombatTick, the monster attack routine in MonsterAttacks, and the arrival/leave rounds in ArrivalRound and SameAreaReload) but none of them stops the clock, runs the free round, and restarts it as one unit.

what: Rounds an extended-precision intermediate result to a 64-bit mantissa using round-half-to-even, as each X87 floating-point operation does in the game's emulated arithmetic.
ev: It does the same half-to-even rounding of m·2^e to a 64-bit mantissa, but it takes no sticky input, so an exact-half tie with a nonzero sticky remainder rounds down where normalizeRound rounds up, and a carry out of 64 bits leaves a 65-bit mantissa instead of being renormalized.

what: Computes a monster caster's spell level as a quarter of the monster's guild level, rounded down, with a minimum of 1 and a maximum of 255.
where: Mordor.Core/MonsterAttack.cs MonsterAttack (class containing `MonsterSpellHits`; the method is private, so the class name is not confirmed here)
ev: `MonsterSpellHits` computes the same caster level (floor of guild level / 4, minimum 1, maximum 255) inline, but then goes on to compute spell damage, so it does only part of what the C++ function does.

what: Checks whether one item can be combined with another, returning the first refusal reason (same item, different type, different id, or different alignment) or no refusal if they are compatible.
where: Mordor.Core/Combining.cs struct.Combine (with cannot.Refusal in the same file covering the whole-list refusals)
ev: The C++ combineCheck tests same-item, type, id, and alignment in order and returns the first refusal; Combine and Refusal together cover the same type/id/identification checks, but Combine's alignment check is truncated in the candidate and the "same item" check is handled by a silent skip rather than a returned refusal, and the message wording (swapped type/id text) differs from what the C++ returns.

what: Checks whether a given file number is in the list of regenerated mdata files, returning true if it is and false otherwise.
ev: The C++ function is a plain membership test over the kRegeneratedMdataFiles list, and no candidate checks whether a file number is in a list of regenerated MDATA files; the closest, OriginalSaves.cs ReadGuildLog and Backups.IsCharacterFile, only touch individual MDATA files and do not perform that lookup.

what: Computes the damage modifier for a damage spell at a given spell level, scaling the base and power values with a log term LN(SL+1) to produce the damage figure the engine applies.
ev: The C++ `damageMod` returns the log-scaled base-plus-power damage figure (the `mod1` term), which matches the first part of `Rules.SpellDamage`, but `SpellDamage` then applies a random reduction and resistance that the C++ function does not.

what: Computes the damage from a chest trap blast by taking a random fraction scaled by the trap's difficulty and strength, multiplied by ln(d+2), and adding 1 so the damage is always at least 1.
ev: The case-3 branch computes the same blast formula, `(int)(rng.NextDouble() * (dungeonLevel * 4 * Math.Log(dungeonLevel + 2))) + 1`, with no resistance, but it is inline in a larger trap dispatcher rather than a standalone function taking `d` and `k`.

what: After a successful stat raise, rolls a percentage chance (derived from the current Constitution) and, if it succeeds, permanently lowers the character's natural Constitution by 1 and announces the loss.
ev: It computes a natural-CON-based percentage for losing a CON point, but only on a morgue raise (not after a successful stat raise), and no candidate rolls that loss or decrements CON after a stat raise.

what: Copies one item definition's fields from a parsed JSON object into an ItemDef record, reading each named integer, double, string, or array value, as generated code for the game's data files.
ev: The C++ readItemDef copies every ItemDef field from a parsed JSON object by name, but Candidate 1 (MdrLoader.cs is.LoadItems) is the nearest match and reads the same item fields from a binary record file by position rather than from JSON, while the other candidates are UI, combat, or monster-related and do not populate an item record at all.

what: Returns false only while a dead character's body is being carried in the morgue, which skips the carry choice in the game's rules.
ev: No candidate gates a carry choice on whether a dead character's body is being carried; the closest, Candidate 6 (DungeonWindow.axaml.cs PickUpBody), handles picking up a body and putting down the current one but never skips a choice, and Candidate 1 (DropBody) is the put-down command.

what: Reports whether a group index is valid and the group still has living members in the encounter, which the game uses to decide if a spell or breath attack can target that group.
ev: It returns only the groups that still have living monsters, so "group g is alive" is equivalent to g being a valid index into that list, but it builds the whole list rather than answering a bool for one index, and it has no index-range check like the C++ `g >= 0 && g < kMaxGroups`.

what: When a store's highlighted row is sold out or hidden, it disables the BUY and INFO options, withdraws any pending alignment choice, and cancels choosing.
where: Mordor.App/CityWindow.axaml.cs CityWindow.ClickRow (closest, but it only enables the BUY and INFO buttons and sets the alignment; it never disables them or clears the choice for a sold-out or hidden row)
ev: No candidate disables BUY and INFO, clears `choosing`, and resets `alignment` to -1 when the highlighted row is sold out or hidden; ClickRow handles the same buttons and alignment choice, but it enables them, and StoreRowVisible only decides whether a row is drawn.

what: Clears every party member's protection masks and all eleven protection values to zero, then announces that the party's protections are extinguished.
ev: No candidate clears a party member's protection masks or resets the resistance/protection values to zero and then announces "Your protections are extinguished!"; Effects.Recompute only zeroes `c.Protection` as the first step of a full recompute from gear and spells, and ApplyToCharacter only raises SpellResist values to 95.

what: Draws a random occupied slot in the victim's party list for a companion spit attack, using the attacker's companion count as the range (a known original-game quirk), and returns -1 as a miss if no occupied slot is hit within 1000 tries.
ev: Slot also draws a random slot, retries up to 1000 times until it finds an occupied one, and returns -1 on a miss, but it draws from the attacker's own companions over the fixed range of 4 and never checks the victim's list, so it lacks the C++ function's attacker-count-range and victim-index quirk.

what: Returns true when a companion's carry-slot index equals the given slot0 value, which tests whether that companion is occupying the specified carried-item slot.
ev: The C++ function is a pure predicate (`carryIndex == slot0`), and DropCompanion contains that same equality test (`who.CarryingCompanion == i`) but only as a step before clearing the carry, alongside releasing the slot.

what: Decides whether the Mordor library item page shows the damage modifier, which it does only for weapons at grade 4 (a display quirk of the game).
ev: DescribeItem makes the same decision inline, showing the damage modifier only for a weapon (class 0) at full knowledge, but it also requires DamageMod != 0, which the C++ predicate does not check.

what: Computes a sheet base value for a character attribute by multiplying Q and R by the sheet factor (1.9), subtracting a small epsilon, and truncating to an integer, per SRD rule R6.
ev: None of the eight candidates computes a value from Q and R or applies the 1.9 sheet factor and epsilon truncation; they are all UI and display methods (sheet visibility, tabs, spell lists, monster portraits), so none matches `sheetBaseValue`.

what: Marks a party member as dead in the given death state and queues a "has died" message for the player, with the original's cleanup step left unimplemented.
ev: Kill marks the character dead, zeroes CurHits, counts the death, and logs a message, which matches the C++ core, but it always runs the original's sub0930 cleanup (companions, ailments, states), which the C++ leaves unimplemented, and it logs the caller's reason string rather than the C++ "has died." line.

what: Returns the guild membership record for a given guild from the character's guild list, indexing the character's guild array by the guild's numeric value.
ev: The C++ `memberOf` returns a character's membership record for a guild by numeric index, and no candidate does that, but DrawGuild's line `_ch.Guilds.FirstOrDefault(m => m.Guild == def.Name)` finds the same membership record by name inside a larger UI method, returning null when absent.

what: Announces to the player, via localized messages, where each other saved character is located relative to the caster (too far away, in the city, or in a compass direction) when the Locate spell is cast.
ev: Its Locate branch lists every other saved character (excluding the caster) for the player to pick from, but it does not classify each one's location or announce direction, city, or too-far for all of them, and the truncated body may do more; Mordor.App/CityWindow.axaml.cs CityWindow.LocatePerson is a different Seer service that charges a fee and reports one chosen character.

what: Teleport-in-combat spell: sends up to a capped number of monsters away from an encounter, one group at a time, rolling a per-monster chance to impale each one into rock.
ev: No candidate removes monsters from a group, decrements count/livingCount, rolls an impale chance, or applies a teleport cap; the closest, CombatEngine.AliveGroups and CombatMonster.Runs, only partition monsters into same-kind groups, and the rest handle display, identification, or setup.

what: Deactivates a loaded mod by marking it inactive and emitting the messages telling the host to call OnDisable (for lifecycle mods) and to remove the mod's Harmony patches.
ev: Its doc comment describes the off branch (stop calling the mod, run OnDisable, remove Harmony patches) in the same order as deactivateMod, but the code is truncated before that branch and Switch also handles switching a mod on, so it is a broader version rather than the same function.

what: Rolls a percentile check against the character's poison resistance and, if it fails, sets the character's poison level to the dungeon level, which is the Poison Gas trap's effect in the Mordor rules.
ev: The per-character Poison Gas check is the same (resistance halved against a 0-100 roll, then poison level set to the dungeon level), but Spring applies it to the whole party, does not skip characters who are already poisoned as the C++ `poisonLevel == 0` guard does, and returns a TrapResult instead of a bool.

what: Determines a loaded companion's alignment, keeping a valid saved alignment and otherwise falling back to the creature's own alignment (Good/Neutral/Evil mapped to 1/2/3).
ev: Settle gives an Unaligned companion its creature's own alignment on load, as alignOnLoad does, but it does not reproduce alignOnLoad's rule of keeping any valid saved alignment (1 to 3) and falling back to the creature's alignment for other values, and it leaves the companion Unaligned if the creature cannot be found.

what: Arrival rest in town: moves the party to the leader's dungeon level and square, clears each member's area, rests every member (living or dead) via restInCity, reports any days passed, and returns the leader's rest days.
ev: It places the party on the leader's level and square, sets every member's Area to -1, rests each member in turn with the per-member rest and report (silent when no time passes), and differs only in returning a message list instead of the leader's day count, and its body is truncated so the rest loop is not fully visible.

what: Computes the grid location a spell effect lands on by offsetting the caster's or target's position by a number of squares to the right, forward, and down relative to the facing direction, wrapping the x and y coordinates around the grid edges.
ev: It does the same job, offsetting a position by right/forwards relative to facing, wrapping x and y at the grid edges, and changing the level by "down", but its axis mapping differs from the C++ (for example, North adds +y to forward where the C++ uses -y) and it clamps the depth change to ±3 and floors the level at 0, which the C++ does not do.

what: Applies a chute fall to a party member, moving them to the floor below by the chute's depth, dealing landing damage (reduced by race size) that cannot take their hit points below zero, then announcing the fall and recording it in the result.
where: Mordor.App/DungeonWindow.axaml.cs DungeonWindow.ChuteFall (the landing damage is in Mordor.Core/Chute.cs Chute.Land)
ev: DungeonWindow.ChuteFall moves each member down by the chute depth and announces the fall, and Chute.Land applies the race-scaled landing damage and its message, but no candidate both applies the damage and floors hit points at zero (Land subtracts without clamping), and the truncated ChuteFall may call Land.

what: Checks whether a given race may take a given alignment by looking up that race's alignment mask, so creating a character can reject alignments the race is not allowed to have.
ev: LoadRaces stores each race's alignment mask as `AlignMask`, the same data the C++ looks up, but no candidate tests a race's alignment mask against an alignment (GuildDefs.AllowsAlignment does the same test against a guild's mask instead).

what: Checks whether the player may use a pack item in the dungeon, returning NotInDungeon, NoEffect, MustBeEquipped, OutOfCharges, or Ok based on the item's special type, spell, equip state, and charges.
ev: Problem covers the equip and charge refusals in a related order, but it has no dungeon check, tests "no effect" by charges rather than by special type and spell, and returns strings instead of the UseCheck enum.

what: Computes archive-form player damage as the base damage plus a random bonus of 1 to Atk/8 (rounded down), returning the total.
ev: Fn0DEE's comment discusses the same "+ Rnd[1 to Atk/8]" term but reads it as a subtracted adjustment that applies to 999 of 1000 blows, alongside a full level/strength/dice damage calculation, while the C++ function simply returns the truncated base plus a random 1 to Atk/8 bonus.

what: Reports whether a given forced-flag setter (the teleporter square, the Teleport spell, or a lone chest trap) is one of the three sources allowed to set the forced flag, per rule R14.
where: Mordor.App/DungeonWindow.axaml.cs DungeonWindow.SettleArea (also DungeonWindow.ChestTeleport for the lone-chest setter)
ev: Neither candidate checks which setter raised the forced flag. SettleArea's comment names the same three sources and consumes `_forceSettle`, and ChestTeleport sets it for the lone opener, but no candidate reproduces the C++ membership test over the `ForcedFlagSetter` enum.

what: Rolls the chance for a monster to breathe, ends the turn or group turn in the level-0 and out-of-range cases, and otherwise rolls breath damage from the monster's level and the caster's guild level.
ev: GroupAttacks runs the same breath chance roll (50/80/20 from the guild-level comparison) and level-0 handling, but as one step of a larger group turn and the visible text is cut off before the range and damage steps, while SpecialHits.Kind.Raw has the same damage shape but omits the final divide-by-2.

what: Returns the ordered list of town sections (Store, Confinement, Morgue, Guild, Bank) that the leader visits when the party is in town and the leader is alive, or an empty list otherwise.
ev: SwitchedTo fires the Store, Confinement, Morgue, Guild and Bank UPDATE calls in the C++ order, gated on the leader being in town and alive, but it also does unrelated UI work and omits the early return for an empty party, and it never returns the ordered list the C++ function produces, so it does the same action in a different form rather than the same function.

what: Determines whether a single blow counts as "Severed" in the game's combat rules, which happens when the blow has both a critical-hit proc and a backstab proc.
where: Combat.cs sub0D08.SwingOnce (closest; it rolls the crit and backstab booleans but never combines them into a severed outcome)
ev: No candidate returns or tests a "Severed" result from crit && backstab; SwingOnce rolls both procs independently and its comment says they stack +5 and +2 damage rather than producing a combined classification.

what: Advances an item's identification level by one step per Identify click, with the General Store allowed to reach the full level and other locations capped at the level just below it.
ev: NextIdLevel steps Barely to Partial to Mostly to All and holds at All, which matches the C++ General Store branch, but it takes no location argument, so it does not cover the non-store branch that caps at Mostly.

what: Returns the wall/feature flags for a given dungeon square (numbered from 1), or 0 if the square is out of range, following the game's rule that a square's walls come from its field entry.
ev: The nested `Walls(int square)` returns `fields[square - 1].Flags` when `square` is in `1..fields.Length` and 0 otherwise, which is the same 1-based lookup and out-of-range rule as `fieldFlagsAt`, though it sits inside a larger method rather than being a standalone helper.

what: Runs one combat round per tick when the party is underground and the clock is not minimised, letting the party act, retargeting, reporting dead members, and then having monsters attack.
ev: Both are the per-tick combat timer that skips when minimised or already in a round, then runs one round with the party acting before the monsters, but the candidate's body is cut off before the retarget and dead-member steps, so those are unverified, and it has no explicit underground check.

what: Registers the town-screen "realign" player command, which takes a member, item slot, and alignment and changes that item's alignment for a fee.
ev: The C++ function only registers a town-screen command entry (name, screen, handler, usage text) and none of the candidates does that, but candidate 1 performs the same alignment change for a fee, though through the ID-box UI with a Yes/No confirm rather than typed member/slot/alignment arguments.

what: Handles the player's request to remove the selected member from the party, refusing if they are the leader or monsters are nearby, asking for confirmation otherwise, and then removing them and pruning the dead.
ev: It refuses the leader with "Leader cannot leave Party!", refuses when monsters are present with the same named message, asks for confirmation, removes the member, and prunes the dead, though it checks monsters before the leader (the C++ checks the leader first, and its comment marks that order as unknown) and also saves the departing character in the dungeon.

what: Pays a rescue hire's cost from the gold leader's wallet, refusing the hire if no valid gold leader exists or the wallet cannot cover the cost.
ev: CharPay pays a rescue-style charge from the town's current character (`_ch`), falling back to the bank and returning false when short, which matches the refusal behavior, but it has no gold-leader index and no invalid-index check, and the rescue hire flow in RescuersButton is the caller that uses it.

what: Decides whether a monster of a given alignment may join a character of a given alignment: Good monsters join only Good characters, Neutral monsters join anyone, and Evil monsters never join.
ev: No candidate returns whether a monster of a given alignment may join a character; the closest, Rules.EngageChance, uses the same alignment pairing to compute a per-tick chance that monsters attack, and CompanionTurn.Outcome.Check computes a turning roll, so neither makes the join decision.

what: Reports whether an inventory item slot is empty, using the placeholder rule that an item with id 0 counts as empty, since the SRD Formulas section defining slot emptiness was not supplied.
ev: It applies the same rule that an item id of 0 means an empty slot, but it takes a pack slot index instead of an item, adds a null check and range bounds, and treats slot 0 (the Hands) as never empty, so the outcome differs for slot 0.

what: Decides whether an item is destructible by a monster or slime, returning true unless its special type falls in the guild-marker range (below 500 or above the destructible maximum of 511).
ev: It returns true unless `SpecialType` is below 500 or above `500 + GuildData.All.Count - 1`, which is the same range test as the C++ `specialType < kGuildMarkerBase || specialType > kDestructibleSpecialMax` (511), differing only in taking an `Item` rather than a bare integer.

what: Fire ball trap from chest opening: every living party member takes a rolled fire trap damage amount, reduced by their Fire resistance.
ev: Spring applies a rolled fire trap damage to each party member, reduced by Fire resistance, which matches the C++ intent, but it uses a level-based damage formula with a different resistance calculation, and it has no dead-member skip.

what: Applies the fear effect from the T3 trap: every living companion whose binding level is below 100 is driven off (marked unoccupied and not present), and the "Your companions were scared away!" message is shown.
ev: No candidate applies the T3 fear trap's mass removal of every living companion with binding below kBindingMax or emits "Your companions were scared away!"; the closest, DungeonWindow.CompanionsDrift, removes companions gradually through per-round mood rolls and different messages.

what: Builds the list of spell ids (indices into the spell table) that the caster can currently reach, by testing each spell against the reach check spellWithinReach.
ev: It tests every spell record against the same guild reach gate (rate above zero, ceiling reaching the spell's level, and Level × rate ≤ guildLevel/2 + 0.5) and returns a per-index bool array, which is the same outcome as the C++ id list, though the C++ `spellWithinReach` body itself was not provided to confirm the match line by line.

what: Builds the display title for a mod from its manifest, using the mod's id and appending a space and its version when a version is present (per the R21/F2 title formula, with the name branch unavailable).
