ev: Describe builds "name version" (falling back to the id when no name is found) and omits the version when it is empty, which mirrors the C++ title formula, but it takes a parsed "id@version" string rather than a manifest and prefers the name over the id, so it does not do the same thing.

what: Reports whether an item is cursed for the purposes of a slot, returning true when the item's curse value is anything other than none (kind 1 and kind 2 curses are not distinguished).
ev: Its first line tests `it.Cursed != 0` to set the slot's curse flag from the item, the same check as the C++ function, but it also sets the flag for alignment opposition and mutates the slot rather than returning a bool; PackRow.Italic (Mordor.Core/PackRow.cs) uses the same `it.Cursed != 0` predicate but adds an identification requirement.

what: Decides whether a dead character is eligible to be pruned (removed) by checking that they are dead and their current hit points are zero or below, a condition the source notes as unresolved in which rule governs.
where: Mordor.Core/Party.cs Party.RemoveTheDead (candidate 8; the class name is inferred from the file, since the candidate label is ambiguous)
ev: The C++ function is a standalone predicate (dead and CurHits <= 0), while RemoveTheDead embeds a related test inside a loop (removes when CurHits <= 0 or IsDead or Stoned, and keeps only living, unstoned characters with hits above zero), so it adds a Stoned condition and differs in the dead-with-hits case.

what: Computes the chance that a teleport spell cast in combat sends an enemy into rock, as 100 minus the creature's magic resistance clamped to 0–100 (a guessed formula, since the SRD gives none).
ev: No candidate computes a teleport-into-rock chance as 100 minus magic resistance; the closest, Effects.ResistancePercent, only looks up a character's resistance, and SpellEffect.TeleportTo handles teleport destination coordinates, not an impale chance.

what: Switches a mod on or off at runtime: it saves the setting, and if the mod is a lifecycle mod that is not faulted it loads or reactivates it (or deactivates it when switched off), otherwise deferring the change to the next start or refusing a switch-on with a bad manifest.
ev: Switch matches the C++ logic of loading or reactivating a lifecycle mod on, deactivating it off, and deferring faulted or non-lifecycle mods, but it returns NextStart instead of Failed for a switch-on with a manifest problem, and it does not visibly save the setting to settings.ini as the C++ does.

what: Decides whether an item definition matches a requested category, where a category value of -1 acts as a wildcard that matches every category.
ev: No candidate matches an item definition against a category with a -1 wildcard; the closest, GuildDefs.CanCast and ReachingGuilds, reject negative categories rather than matching all of them, and they concern spells and guilds, not items.

what: Marks every party member as saved (R94 SaveChar), with the storage representation left unimplemented and the context, floors, and game data arguments unused.
ev: The C++ function only sets `saved = true` on each party member, while SaveChar persists the whole party to disk via `_party.SaveAll` along with window layout, map, and dungeon state, so it is a related save-the-characters routine rather than the same flag-setting operation.

what: Picks a monster's spell school by drawing random schools up to a fixed number of attempts and returning the first one allowed by the monster's spell-flag mask, or no school if none is found.
ev: ChooseSpell opens with the same school-sampling loop (random pick from 18 schools, accepted if the monster's SpellFlags bit is set, capped at 1000 tries), but it then goes on to pick a spell and applies several extra gates, and it never returns the school on its own.

what: Maps a companion spawn mode number to the rules for choosing a monster: a floor-offset range (-3..-1, -3..0, or 0), repeating the previous monster, a fixed monster table index, or keeping the previous window, with unknown negative modes selecting nothing.
ev: No candidate maps a companion spawn mode to floor offsets, repeat, table index, or keep-previous; MdrLoader.LoadMonsters only stores the raw CompanionSpawnMode value, and CompanionRef.IndexOf/At only resolve a table index to a monster.

what: Decides whether a companion is eligible to be offered a realignment, which is allowed only when the companion's owner ID level is Completely (rule R72).
ev: IdEnter enables the realign buttons only in the `c.IdLevel <= 0` branch, which gates realignment on the same level-0 rule as canOfferRealign, but it is embedded in a larger UI routine that also handles selling, identifying, and value display, and it compares the raw int rather than checking an OwnerIdLevel.Completely enum.

what: Returns true when a monster's spawn weight is at or below the quest-rare threshold, marking it as a rare quest monster under rule R34.
ev: No candidate compares a spawn weight against a threshold of 9; the closest, Rules.cs table.QuestMonster, applies a random roll against a Rarity field when rejecting rare monsters, which is a different rule.

what: When the player steps onto a square, unless that square is fogged, every orthogonally adjacent square in the floor is marked as mapped on the automap.
ev: OnEntry also gates its neighbour writes on the fog of the square stepped onto, but it writes only the west and south neighbours' walls (east and north sides), also writes the own square, and returns early when lost, whereas markNeighbours marks all four orthogonal neighbours as mapped with no lost check.

what: Computes the item drop-level band for a treasure chest in Mordor, using the drop level, a box-chance roll that can lower the band's floor by one, and treasure-class modifiers, then clamps the result to valid levels.
ev: Its opening band computation (half-even floor, box-chance roll setting low to top-1, class 1 and class 3 shifts, and the clamps) matches the C++ line for line, but RollDrop also overrides the band for Asmodeus and goes on to pick an item, so it is a larger function rather than the same one.

what: Picks the guild with the lowest positive rate from a list of candidate teaching guilds, using rate as a stand-in for cost, and returns its index or -1 if none qualify.
ev: It also picks the cheapest accepted guild by keeping the lowest cost among guilds that reach the spell, but it compares computed spell costs instead of raw rates, returns a price rather than a guild index, and has no -1 "none qualify" return.

what: Appends a new guild log entry, recording the guild, the game day, and the text, to the stored guild log.
ev: Entry.Append loads the whole log, appends one entry with the guild and text, and rewrites the file, which matches guildlogAppend, but it always stamps `Today()` instead of taking the explicit `day` parameter the C++ function accepts.

what: Resets a guild member's quest by clearing its kind and target and marking the quest as not done, as step 1 of the R42 quest-forfeit or reassignment procedure.
ev: Its first line clears QuestType, QuestTarget and QuestDone exactly as clearQuest does, but it then rolls and assigns a new quest, so it does more than the C++ function.

what: Decides whether a character can pick up a carried monster, allowing the pickup only when the monster is no more than one size category larger than the character's race.
ev: Run contains the same test, `def.Size - (int)RaceData.ByName(who.Race).Size <= 1`, which gates whether the carry is set, but it is inline within a larger routine that also picks the best companion slot and builds the message lines, whereas the C++ function is only the predicate.

what: Reads one of a square's three flags by index for save purposes: explored and identified as stored, and automap as true when nonzero (the code's own comment marks the automap flag as simplified to a seen flag).
ev: No candidate reads the explored, identified, and automap fields of a per-square save state by index; the closest, SharedMap.Recorded, only tests a bit in a flag word and has no explored or identified equivalent.

what: Decides whether a monster group may offer to join the character by checking that the group's leader's alignment is Neutral or matches the viewer's alignment, via the engine's join rule.
ev: No candidate checks the leader's alignment against the viewer's, but FillGroup's "1948-1967: the offer to join" section appears to set JoinOffer for each group, and its text is truncated before the alignment test, so it may contain the rule.

what: Registers the "guildlog" town command, which lets the player view a guild's log or clean it down to the newest 50 entries.
ev: Entry.Clean keeps the newest fifty log entries, which matches the "guildlog clean" half of the C++ command, but no candidate registers a town command or handles the per-guild view (candidates 2, 3 and 5 cover viewing the log, not registration).

what: Computes one melee swing's damage in Mordor from attacker and defender values, strength, level, and damage modifier, applies the random adjustment draws, and returns 0 on a miss per the final hit gate (R18), otherwise the damage dealt.
ev: Fn0DEE takes the same inputs (attack, defence, level, strength, damage modifier), makes the same threshold, strength, damage-modifier taper, roll, attack/defence adjustment, 999-in-1000 check and hit gate in the same order, and returns 0 on a miss or a blow that comes to nothing, otherwise the damage dealt.

what: On a party's arrival in town, offers each living-or-dead party member to the Hall of Records and returns the announcement lines for any records they set, using a per-record offer value and a check that records the new best.
ev: RestOnArrival runs on arrival in town and checks each party member against the records, but it only checks the MostExperience record and discards the announcement lines, whereas the C++ offers every member against the full kArrivalRecords set and returns the lines (OfferRecordLines does the line-collecting, but has no per-member loop).

what: Maps the Shadow Ninja monster index to the Morgul index so the two share one Id 307 entry, per rule R63 in the monster-key settlement.
ev: FromId resolves the shared Id 307 to the Morgul (first table index with the Id) when the alignment does not settle it, but it looks up an index from an Id rather than mapping index 389 to 278 directly, and the C++ function is a plain index-to-index canonicalization.

what: Rolls a percentage check against kLairDrawPercent (75%) to decide whether a lair's named monster is drawn.
where: Mordor.Core/Seer.cs Seer.Locate (the class name is inferred from the file name; the candidate header is garbled)
ev: Locate performs the same 75% lair-named-monster check (`rng.NextDouble() * 100 < 75`) as rollLairDraw, but only as one step inside a larger function that searches the floor for a square to place the monster.

what: Computes the acid spit damage a monster inflicts on a character, derived from the monster's and character's guild levels with a random roll, and scaled by 0.7.
ev: Kind.Raw with the AcidSpit kind uses the same range, the same roll-plus-half-range formula, and the same 0.7 scale as the C++ function, but it takes the roll and range through Floor instead of vbInt, so the results can differ at half-way values.

what: Computes a companion's stoning chance from their Constitution and the level at which they were found, capping the result at 95%.
ev: No candidate computes a stoning chance from CON and found level with the log formula and 95% cap; the closest, Raising.Resolve and the raise-chance methods, handle resurrection success and CON loss, not stoning.

what: Decides whether a record left by a stone that is no longer a fight monster counts as damage credited to the player, returning true only when the monster is still a fight monster.
ev: Credit gates the damage event on `Monsters.Contains(target)`, so a stale record outside the fight is credited with no damage, which matches the C++ predicate, but that check is one condition inside a larger method and Credit still awards experience to the stale record, which the C++ function does not address.

what: Finds the first of the character's four companion slots that is still empty (not occupied by a Companion), returning its index or -1 if all are filled, which the game uses when a companion joins the party.
ev: Add calls `FirstFree` and returns that first empty slot index or -1 when full, which matches the C++ search, but it also writes the companion into the slot, and the `FirstFree` property the logic lives in is not among the candidates.

what: Computes the natural logarithm of a value, returning 0 for non-positive inputs (the sheet leaves that case undefined), which feeds into the game's spell-magnitude and scaling formulas.
ev: BaseValue takes a log of strength plus dexterity clamped with Math.Max(1, ...), which gives 0 for non-positive integers like lnOf, but it has no standalone helper, no return-0 guard, and a different guard on the guild-level log.

what: Casts the Cure Paralysis spell on the caster, which fails during combat and otherwise removes the paralysis from them.
ev: Companion.Apply frees the caster when they are held, which matches the C++ unparalyse step, but nothing in the candidates reproduces the fail-in-fight branch, and Combat.cs NonCombatInFight explicitly exempts Cure Paralysis from in-fight refusal, which contradicts it.

what: Maps a typed companion slot number (Rule R68) to a zero-based slot index, returning that index only if it is in range and occupied by a companion, otherwise -1.
ev: It returns the slot index if it is non-negative and occupied and otherwise -1, which matches the final occupancy check, but it has no VB-value parsing, the minus-one offset, Integer-range or half-even rounding, or upper-bound check against the slot count, and its input is a UI control index rather than a typed value.

what: Returns true when the given creature is the lead character named "Asmodeus" (matched by its knownAs text), which the rules use to identify Asmodeus as the party leader, and false if there is no lead.
ev: The C++ check (lead non-null and `knownAs == "Asmodeus"`) is not implemented in any candidate; RenderView, RollDrop, and ShowChest call an `Asmodeus.Is(lead)` helper, but that helper's definition is not among the candidates.

what: Computes a companion's join bar as Charisma times 10, reduced by 10 for each level above the first the monster was found at, floored at zero (per SRD c12p1).
ev: No candidate computes a join bar of Cha×10 minus 10 per level above the first, floored at zero; the closest, Combat.cs FillGroup, has a join-offer section that is truncated before any bar calculation, and KnownAsIndex's bar is an identification-skill formula.

what: Checks whether any equipped item the wearer counts for carries a resistance flag matching the given damage kind, and returns true if so, which grants the character resistance to that damage type.
ev: It runs the same loop (equipped slots that count for the wearer, then a resistance-flag bit test for the kind), but it returns a percentage that also includes the race base and spell resistance, rather than the bare bool the C++ returns.

what: Computes the chance that a monster's critical hit or backstab procs, from the attacker's guild level, the attacker's floor, and the defender's level, clamped to the set floor and cap.
ev: It uses the same expression (guild level over 650 for critical or 500 for backstab, times Log(floor+1), minus the defender's Log(level/999+1)*100) with the same clamps of 2..50 for critical and 4..75 for backstab.

what: Returns the breath-weapon threshold percentage (80, 50, or 20) for a monster, chosen by comparing the highest guild level against the monster's level through a ratio band lookup.
ev: The breath block in GroupAttacks computes the same 80/50/20 chance from the highest guild level (`MaxGuildLevel(c)`) against the monster level with the same quarter-band comparisons, but it is inline inside a larger routine rather than a standalone function that returns the percentage, and CompanionBreathes in Combat.cs does the same inline.

what: Finds the first unoccupied companion slot in the party's roster (the "hole" a new companion fills), returning its index or -1 if the roster is full.
ev: Add takes the first free index (`FirstFree`), returns -1 when none is free, and otherwise returns that same index after placing the companion there; it also writes the slot, which the C++ finder does not, and `FirstFree` itself is not shown, so I could not confirm it treats slots holding leftover records the same way as the C++ `occupied` flag.

what: Rolls the damage dealt by a monster's spit attack, scaled by the monster's guild level and the victim's active level, with a random factor and a final rounding step.
ev: Raw uses the same spit-branch formula, `(floor((u*range+1)/2) + range/2) * 0.7`, but `Range` is not shown, so it is unverified that it equals the C++ `q`, and Raw takes the victim's `TopGuildLevel` where the C++ uses the victim's active level.

what: Decides whether a spell on an item fires when used by a character, succeeding if the item is unaligned or its alignment exactly matches the user's alignment (Good, Neutral, or Evil), with no partial-strength case.
ev: It maps an item alignment to the matching character alignment and returns null for unaligned, which is the comparison step inside spellFiresOnUse, but no candidate decides whether the spell fires on use, so the unaligned-always-fires rule and the match check are missing.

what: Lowers one of a character's ability stats by 1 (if it is above the race's minimum) and returns that point to the character's unspent points pool, per rule R4.2.
ev: That handler does what lowerStat does for one stat: if `_stats[idx] > _race.Min[idx]` it decrements the stat and increments `_pool`, but it is an inline lambda inside RefreshStats, which also rebuilds the UI, so the match is partial in scope rather than in logic.

what: Handles the player's typed "carry <member> <slot>" command, validating the member and slot, refusing when the target can't be picked up, and otherwise setting the carried companion and producing the player-facing message.
ev: Run produces the same "You are now carrying X." line for the typed command and drops the previous carry with the same "dropped ... to carry ..." message, but it auto-selects the strongest fallen companion rather than validating a member and slot the player typed, so the parsing, "no such member", "is empty", and "already being carried" refusals have no counterpart.

what: Returns true when the viewer is a newbie under the game's R10 rule, meaning their character level is 1 and the area they are in has an id below the newbie cutoff.
ev: No candidate implements the R10 test (viewer level == 1 and area id < 18); the closest, Combat.cs whatever.Generate, reads the viewer's level but its visible text does not show a newbie predicate, and the rest are area-lookup or save-loading helpers.

what: Tests whether an item's resistance bitmask covers a given damage kind, returning true when the item resists that kind of damage and false if the kind is out of range.
ev: It performs the same item bitmask test (`ResistanceFlags & (1 << kind)`), but only as one step inside a function that also adds race baseline and spell resistance and returns a percentage, and it has no `resistIndex` mapping or out-of-range-to-false check, while the C++ function only returns a bool for a single item's flags.

what: Implements R18 of the Mordor rules: the first guild joined after Nomad costs nothing, so it returns true only when the character has not yet joined any guild besides Nomad.
ev: JoinVisitedGuild makes the join free (cost 0) when no guild other than the current one has level > 0, which is a related first-join-is-free check, but it tests against the current guild rather than Nomad and is inlined in a larger join flow rather than returning a standalone predicate.

what: After an explosion, if the party leader is at zero hits, it marks the chest opener as dead and records a death count, skipping the case where the opener is not in slot 0 and only one character is still alive.
ev: After the chest trap, OpenChestBy checks whether the leader is below 1 hit and then kills the opener's pre-prune slot, which matches the C++ trigger and target, but the candidate is truncated and I can't confirm it has the C++'s Q14 guard (opener not in slot 0 with one survivor) or the Q13 already-dead check.

what: Dominate Demon binds the demon to the player by setting its bound flag and raising its binding level to at least the Domination base level, then announces that the demon is bound.
ev: It is a closely related spell-driven bind that raises the companion's BindingLevel toward a computed level and announces the result, but it never sets a separate bound flag, computes the level from the spell and caster rather than a fixed Domination base, and uses a different message.

what: Marks the party as lost and, if the square index is valid, sets the lost bit on that square's automap entry, then tells the player they have realised they are lost.
ev: LoseDirection also marks the party as lost (LostPosition and LostFacing) when a square spins the walker round, but it doesn't write a lost bit to the automap or print "You realise you are lost.", and it's triggered by a spinning square rather than the lost-realisation step.

what: After a targeted party member is knocked to 0 hits, drops their companions, prunes the dead from the party, and reports whether the monster's turn ends (lone character died), the group stops (only one member left), or the turn continues.
ev: RoundPaced prunes the dead after the characters' turns (the UPDATE that unloads everyone at nought while more than one is left), which resembles the C++ prune step, but it does not drop companions per knocked-out target or return the MonsterTurnEnds/GroupStops/Continue outcome.

what: Advances the chest countdown by one step before the opener acts, and announces "The guards are alerted!" when the countdown reaches zero.
ev: No candidate decrements a chest countdown or announces "The guards are alerted!" when it reaches zero; the closest, Candidate 2 (DungeonWindow.axaml.cs OpenChestBy), handles the chest opening itself, not a countdown step before the opener acts.

what: Returns true when a companion's hit points are below zero, meaning breath or acid attacks remove that companion from the party (a companion at exactly 0 survives), per rule R36.
ev: The breath sweep that removes companions is in this candidate, but the visible text (cut off mid-method) never shows the `hits < 0` threshold, and no candidate contains the one-line predicate itself or mentions R36's "exactly 0 survives" rule.

what: Handles the player's chute-take action: refuses it on a dead-end level, otherwise drops every party member and the party itself down by the chute depth and prints the "You drop down the chute" message.
ev: ChuteFall(taken: true) drops each party member to the chute's landing floor for the TAKE action, but it also breaks up the party as sub0908 does, which the C++ explicitly skips, and no candidate reproduces the C++ dead-end refusal message together with the drop.

what: Computes the chance, in clamped 25 to 90 range, that a character's item is destroyed by a slime attack, using the character's level found, dexterity, the monster's dexterity, and whether the character is paralysed.
ev: No candidate computes the slime item-destruction chance from level found, dexterity, monster dexterity, and paralysis; the closest, CombatEngine.AttackChance, uses a different formula (50 + (monDex - charDex) * 5) for whether a group gets a free attack.

what: Rolls a d100 against the character's age-based natural death chance, once old age has set in, and emits an "Old age claims the character" message if the roll succeeds.
ev: Both take age and racial lifespan, return false before old age sets in (under 98% of lifespan), and die when a d100 roll is below a chance that rises with age; the candidate omits the "Old age claims the character" message and its chance formula can't be checked against the C++ `naturalDeathChancePercent`, which isn't shown.

what: Converts a raise-dead spell's effect value into a tier by subtracting 19 and clamping the result to a minimum of 1 (so effects 20, 21, 22 map to tiers 1, 2, 3).
ev: The candidate computes the same `Math.Max(1, effect - 19)` tier, but only as an intermediate step in a larger chance calculation and never returns the tier itself, whereas the C++ function returns just the tier.

what: When a thief's aimed group is empty, the function makes the thief retarget to another group, applying the game's rule for thieves whose target has disappeared.
ev: Retarget applies the same rule (if the aimed group is gone, move the order to the first group standing), but it has no check that the character is a thief, which the C++ function requires before it acts.

what: Converts a character's Known (identification) value, clamped to the valid scale, into an IdLevel, where values at or below zero mean the item is fully identified.
ev: SlotFrom makes the same countdown-to-IdLevel conversion (`3 - known`) with range handling, but it reads a saved 0-3 field, treats out-of-range values as fully known with a warning instead of clamping to the scale, and has no separate branch for zero or below, while IdCountdown is the inverse direction.

what: Registers the "use" dungeon command and the "useitem" town command, which let a player use an item from a party member's pack slot (potions heal, scrolls cast) and route to the handlers that do the work.
ev: No candidate registers the "use" or "useitem" commands, but UseSelectedItem carries out the dungeon Use of a pack slot (potions heal, scrolls cast, other items charged and applied), which is what the registered "use" command routes to; the candidate's town-side OnPackUse only refuses with "Must be in Dungeon to Use items.", so it does not match the town "useitem" handler.

what: Computes a store's replenish chance from the number of days the stock has aged, by rounding days down to a multiple of kStoreReplenishStep.
ev: The candidate computes the same `(days / 100) * 100` expression, but as a float literal division clamped to 1..50 inside the larger restock loop, whereas the C++ function is a pure integer-division round-down helper.

what: When a character is a member of a guild, this checks whether they can claim the guildmaster seat, and if the claim succeeds, places the guild crest in their pack and tells the player whether it was placed, there was no room, or they already hold it.
ev: It runs the same claim-then-award sequence and posts the placed and no-room messages, but it never shows the "already hold" message (AwardCrest returns null text for AlreadyHeld) and it has no explicit joined check.

what: Computes the minimum spell-casting cost (in silver/SC) for a sheet by taking the larger of the initial cost plus one and a floor value derived from the input c, using a placeholder formula whose true rule is not yet known.
ev: Both compute a spell-casting cost and clamp it up to a floor, but Spellbook.Cost derives its base from the spell's level and guild rate rather than the C++ sheet inputs c, q, r, and the C++ formula is an unverified placeholder, so it is not the same computation.

what: Decides whether a crafted item can go on the shelf of a town store, failing it if the item is cursed, if it is unaligned with a zero floor, or if its alignment's row count has reached the shelf cap of 9.
ev: It tests the same three conditions as storeShelvesItem (not cursed, not unaligned with floor 0 via ShelvedBySelling, and the alignment's count below the shelf cap), differing only in that it reads the store from the instance rather than taking it as a parameter.

what: Decides whether a Seer carrier's item is hit by a given effect: named items always hit, and other items hit only if their type code is valid and their drop level falls within the floor up to floor plus a random band of 0 to kSeerBandSides-1.
ev: Carriers applies the same rule (one band roll, named entries certain regardless of band, otherwise drop level within floor to floor+band), but it matches each treasure entry against the specific item's type, while the C++ function takes no target type and only checks that the type code is valid (>= 0).

what: Builds the full set of six character attributes (STR, INT, WIS, CON, CHA, DEX) by taking each stat's value with all modifiers applied, such as race bonuses and equipment effects.
ev: That method computes one stat with equipped modifiers added, which is the per-element step of `statsWithModsOf`, but no candidate builds and returns all six attributes.

what: Applies the Gear A/D fit rule (R9) to a raw attack or defence value, returning it unchanged for a full fit, halved with round-half-to-even for a half fit, or negated for a subtract fit.
ev: It matches all three branches of adWithFit: Fine returns raw, Adjacent (the half case) uses Math.Round(raw / 2.0, MidpointRounding.ToEven) for round-half-to-even, and the default branch (Opposed, the subtract case) returns -raw.

what: Maps a monster spawn mode number to the spawn window (how far above or below the party's level a creature may come from) and to a fixed monster table entry, or to "lead itself," with modes 7 and negatives leaving the previous window unchanged.
ev: No candidate maps a monster spawn mode to a spawn window or table entry: Candidate 1 (Loot.cs RollDrop) picks chest loot, and the other seven cover help files, PNG decoding, UI, maze walls and automap drawing, so none does what spawnPickForMode does.

what: Shows the public-beta limitation notice (stating how many dungeon levels the limited build allows) in the limited build only, and writes the Limited=True flag to MORDOR.INI when the build calls for it.
ev: Apply switches the limited-build mode on or off from the folder's verdict and reads the About date and order price for it, but it does not show the limitation notice, write Limited=True to MORDOR.INI, or count dungeon levels, so it covers only the mode-switching part of showLimitationNotice.

what: Computes the cumulative gold needed to reach the next character level, summing a per-level cost step (rounded half-up) for levels 1 through glvl and then scaling the total by a multiplier derived from GGF/10.
ev: Fn12B2 reduces to the C++ sum of round((2g-1)×30.1) over g = 1..level, then multiplied by (1 + Gold/10), and its x87 rounding makes the half cases round up as the C++ does.

what: Computes the Disarm stat for a character as WIS/4 + DEX/2, using real (non-integer) division.
ev: The thieving case computes the same `wis / 4.0 + dex / 2.0` term, but only as an intermediate inside a larger disarm/pick chance formula that adds guild rating, level, and dungeon-level opposition, and no candidate returns this stat on its own (Rules.BestAbilityValue case 0 repeats the same term inside another larger expression).

what: Returns true when a character is at level 1 and the dungeon level is above the newbie depth limit, which switches on the newbie guard protection for low-level characters in shallow areas.
ev: No candidate checks for character level 1 combined with a dungeon depth below a limit to enable a newbie guard; the closest, Mordor.Core/DungeonState.cs DungeonState.NoteDepth, only tracks the deepest level reached.

what: Rolls how many monsters from a group join the player as friendly companions, picking a random count from 1 up to the smaller of the group size and the join cap (4).
ev: FillGroup sets the group's `JoinOffer` in the "offer to join" section (MONSMOD.BAS:1948-1967), which is where the R43 count would be rolled, but the snippet is cut off before that roll, and no candidate visibly computes `Int(Rnd * min(groupSize, 4)) + 1`.

what: Decides whether an item should be re-identified when retrieved, returning true when the probe roll exceeds the threshold (the port's chosen reading of the SRD rule, which says re-identify when the probe is below the threshold).
ev: No candidate decides re-identification on retrieval by comparing a probe roll to a threshold; the closest, Combat.cs `CharmIdLevel`, computes a monster's identification difficulty level, not a probe-versus-threshold check.

what: Returns the crit rule or the backstab rule, whichever matches the requested combat proc, so the combat code can apply that proc's game mechanics.
ev: No candidate returns a crit or backstab rule chosen by proc; MonsterCritChance only picks its divisors, floor, and cap by a backstab flag and computes a chance, while SwingOnce rolls crit and backstab separately rather than selecting one.

what: When the player holds Shift and presses a buffer key during combat, it decides whether that buffer slot fires a spell, uses an item, or becomes a standing order, and records the standing order in featureState.
ev: FireBuffer does what buffersFireSlot does: an empty buffer does nothing, an item buffer uses its pack slot, and a spell buffer goes through CastKnownSpell, which makes it the standing order during a fight and casts it otherwise. The differences are structural: the C++ returns a BufferFire enum and records the order itself, while the port delegates that decision to CastKnownSpell.

what: Charges the companion's identify fee from the purse and, if the party can pay, sets the companion's owner ID level to Completely; otherwise it returns a not-enough-gold result.
ev: That candidate computes the companion identify fee, the part corresponding to `penPriceToIdentify`, but no candidate charges the purse and sets the companion's ID level to Completely as `identifyCompanion` does; the App's `IdEnter` only displays that fee.

what: Records that a group of monsters has used its one allowed spell attack, which marks the spell as used and ends that group's attacks for the round.
ev: Its per-round `round.Breathed` flag and `round.Over` exit mirror the C++ spell-used and attack-ended flags, but it handles companion breath rather than a group's monster spell attack, and no candidate records a group's spell use.

what: Rolls a random check against the companion's chance to leave and reports leaving if the roll succeeds or the companion's binding level is zero.
ev: Step.Round contains the same leave test (`rng.NextDouble() * 200 < ChanceToLeave(...) || BindingLevel == 0`), but it also applies binding drift first, computes the chance itself, and returns early for fallen or bound companions, so it is not a standalone equivalent of the C++ function that takes the chance as input.

what: Sums the attack or defence contribution of every worn item for a character, with each item's raw value adjusted by how well its alignment fits the character's alignment (R13).
where: Mordor.Core/Combat.cs, WornSum (the enclosing class name is not shown in the candidate header)
ev: WornSum sums each equipped slot's item value, passed through `ItemAlignments.AttDefWorth` with `ItemAlignments.FitFor(slot.Alignment, c.Alignment)`, which matches the C++ loop of `adWithFit(raw, fitFor(it.alignment, charAlign))` over worn items, with the A/D kind selected by the `f` delegate.

what: Computes the hall date field for the game's date display as days since 1900-01-01 plus a fixed offset (R22).
ev: The C++ `daysSince1900 + 2` equals the VB serial because 1899-12-30 is two days before 1900-01-01, so DaySerial (days since 1899-12-30, returned as long) gives the same value, though it takes a DateTime rather than a day count.

what: Returns the total XP needed to reach a given character level, scaled by the guild's experience factor and the race's experience multiplier, and rounded to a whole number.
ev: It calls `Rules.Fn12A1(Guild.Level - 1, ...)`, which gives 0 at level 1 and otherwise the same half-even-rounded threshold as the C++ `levelXpAtTarget`, but it takes the level from the character rather than as a parameter.

what: Decides whether a newer item name replaces the existing name in the game's record, which happens only when the existing Known value is 0.
ev: Merge contains the same rule (`if (there.Known == 0) there.Name = newer.Name;`), but it also merges Known, NSeen, NDeaths, Location, LastSeen and Id, while the C++ function only returns the yes/no decision.

what: Handles the player's typed "load <name>" command by showing usage text if no name is given, otherwise asking the roster to load the named member into the session reply.
ev: It loads a saved character after a name pick and password check, but it takes no typed name argument and has no "load <name>" usage reply, and no candidate handles a typed command or a roster member by name.

what: Resolves a player-typed guild argument, trimmed and case-insensitive, to a valid guild index either by number or by guild name, returning false if neither matches.
ev: ByName does only the name-matching half of glParseGuild, and it differs by using an exact case-sensitive match with no trim, no numeric index path, and a throw instead of returning false.

what: When the party is split across dungeon levels by a chute, it removes everyone not on the leader's level from the party, marks any of them at zero or fewer hits as dead, and moves the rest to the landing square on the floor below.
ev: ChuteFall handles the same chute event and its doc comment says it "breaks the party up as sub0908 does," but the excerpt is cut off before that step, and the only visible break-up logic is in TeleporterSquare, which removes off-square members for teleporters rather than saving them to the floor below or marking hits<=0 members dead.

what: Decides whether a limited-version message applies when a player takes a Chute at the last level, walks onto a Chute there, or uses a Teleporter to a destination beyond the last level, and sends the matching "doesn't work in the Limited Version" message.
where: Mordor.Core/LimitedVersion.cs LimitedVersion.ChuteIsDeadToTake (the other two branches are LimitedVersion.ChuteIsDeadUnderfoot and LimitedVersion.TeleporterIsDead)
ev: The three candidate predicates cover the same three decisions (take chute at last level, walk onto chute at last level, teleporter destination above last level), but none of them emits the "doesn't work in the Limited Version" message or returns the matching kind as the C++ does, and no single candidate covers all three cases.

what: Handles the player's typed "spells <member>" town command by validating the member number, then replies with the spells that member can reach along with each spell's SP cost and whether it's usable in combat or town.
where: Mordor.App/DungeonWindow.axaml.cs DungeonWindow.RefreshSheetSpells (or Mordor.Core/SpellBuffers.cs SpellBuffers.CostText for the per-spell cost)
ev: No candidate lists a member's reachable spells with their SP costs and combat/town tags as a town command; RefreshSheetSpells lists a character's spell-book rows and CostText shows one buffer's spell cost, which are only related pieces, while the Refuse/CastGate and ApplyDefault candidates cover the cast rules rather than the listing.

what: Works out the identification level a recipient achieves when exchanging an item, applying the R13 quirk where the item's levelScale names another item whose difficulty values set the result, and never returning a level below the item's current idLevel.
ev: It implements the same levelScale-as-item-reference quirk, but it reads the stray item's Floor rather than the dungeon level, takes no "never below the current level" clamp on the recalculated value, and only runs when the test fails, so it is not the same function.

what: Computes the percentage chance of charming a monster into joining the party, from the player's Charisma minus the monster's level plus one, divided by three, floored at zero.
ev: No candidate computes the charm join percentage `(CHA - mLvl + 1) / 3` floored at zero; the closest, `Binding.ChanceToLeave`, uses Charisma and monster level but computes a companion's chance to leave, not a join chance.

what: Rolls a d6 on the drain table (Table E) and returns the drain result that the roll maps to.
ev: No candidate rolls a d6 or maps a roll to a drain result; the closest, GearCheck.Run, only mentions drains as a cause of equipment failing, and RollDrop is item drops from a monster chest.

what: Decides whether a companion held in confinement can be sold, which under the current simplified rule is any companion that is not dead.
ev: IdEnter refuses a companion with `Hits == 0` ("NoDeadOnes") and enables the Sell button only for living ones, which matches the dead-cannot-be-sold part of `!c.isDead`, but it is a UI handler that gates the Sell button rather than a sell-eligibility predicate, and it checks Hits rather than an IsDead flag.

what: Removes a party member who chooses to leave (R10), refusing if monsters are present in the dungeon or if the leader tries to leave, otherwise saving the leaver at the party's current level and square and pruning any dead members.
ev: It makes the same checks in the same order (monsters in the area in the dungeon, then the leader refusal, then confirmation), removes the member, saves them at the party's current level and square, and prunes the dead, but it works on the selected character instead of a slot argument and drives a dialog and file save rather than returning a result.

what: Rolls the player's critical-hit and backstab procs for a blow, each as an independent chance check against the supplied percentages, with crit resolved before backstab and both before the hit gate.
ev: SwingOnce makes the same two independent rolls in the same order (crit, then backstab) against computed percentages, but it also derives those percentages from guild levels and weapon bits and goes on to the damage roll, whereas the C++ function only rolls the two procs against supplied percentages.

what: Given the party's position, it looks up the square the party stands on and reports whether a Take press would use stairs (up or down), a chute, or nothing.
ev: UseStairs checks the same square flags (stairs down, then stairs up, then chute) on a Take press, but it performs the level change or fall and returns a message instead of returning a Stairs/Chute/None classification, and it adds paralysis and last-level rules.

what: Adds spell points restored by a Scroll of Spells (50) or Tome of Spells (200) to the character's current spell points, capped at their maximum, and reports the restoration to the player.
ev: It caps current spell points at the maximum (`Math.Min(CurSpellPoints, MaxSpellPoints)`), but it never adds an item's amount and does not report the restoration, so the Scroll/Tome restore is not implemented in any candidate.

what: Decides whether a disease clear attempt succeeds, returning true when the roll result is above the kDiseaseClearAbove threshold (195).
ev: The disease branch applies the same `roll > 195` cure test as the C++ function, but it is embedded in a larger method that also rolls the die, handles poison, and counts hits lost, while the C++ function is only the threshold predicate.

what: Computes the chute-fall landing damage, returning 0 if the character is Levitating and otherwise the standard chute damage for the landing level and race size.
ev: Land returns no damage for a Levitating member and otherwise calls Rules.ChuteDamage for the landed level and race size, which matches the C++ logic, though Land also subtracts the damage from CurHits and builds a message string that the C++ function does not.

what: Refills an emptied room's population once its last-emptied stamp is more than one respawn period old (or if it was never stamped), by resetting the room's stamp and emptiedAt fields.
ev: RefillDue applies the same "stamp more than one respawn time old, or never set" test to an empty room, but it is a predicate that only returns a bool, and it also adds a standing-group check that the C++ lacks; it does not reset the stamp or emptiedAt fields, which is the C++ function's actual effect.

what: Computes the base melee damage a monster deals to a character from its strength, guild level, and a damage modifier, then reduces it by a random amount tied to the character's defence minus the monster's attack, floored at zero.
ev: Fn0DEE computes the same strength term, level term, roll and damage-modifier product, but its defence reduction is a different formula (`(def-atk)/8` with a random adjustment) and it adds a hit-chance roll that the C++ function does not have.

what: Checks whether a vault/pack slot index is valid for the bank, accepting only slots 1 through 39 and refusing slot 0 and anything at or above kBankSlots (40).
ev: Its first line applies the same rule, refusing pack slot 0 and anything at or above a size limit, but it checks `PackSize` rather than the bank-slot limit, is embedded in a deposit operation rather than being a standalone predicate, and no candidate checks the vault index against `kBankSlots` (40) by itself.

what: Decides whether a chest gets a magic lock by checking whether the square allows one, then rolls the lock against the chest's locked chance and treasure class.
ev: No candidate rolls a chest lock from a square-allowed check and a locked chance; `Loot.DropsItem` and `Rules.is.MagicallyLocked` read the lock state but never roll it, and `Rules.is.EncounterGold` explicitly leaves the lock and class decision to its caller, so the function that makes that roll is not among the candidates.

what: Returns whether an item can be realigned, which is refused while the item is currently equipped (rule T-11, citing SRD c22).
ev: Realign refuses when `slot.Equipped` is true, which is the same test as `canRealign`, but it is an inline guard inside a larger action (cost, confirm, payment, refresh) rather than a standalone predicate that returns whether realigning is allowed.

what: When a companion turns on its owner, the companion's slot is vacated and marked as released, and the game announces that it has joined the fight against the owner.
ev: Its turn branch vacates the slot (DropCompanion) and joins the fight (JoinTheFight) when CompanionTurn.Check says the companion turns, which covers the C++ slot-vacating and join steps, but it has no "released" flag, its announcement comes from the Check outcome rather than being emitted by the function, and it also handles the Kick Out and refusal paths.

what: Reads the guildlog entry count from session state and unpacks each stored entry in order, skipping any damaged records, to return the guild log rows oldest first.
ev: Both read a stored count, then load guild-log records oldest first from the file, skipping or stopping at damaged records (the C++ skips a bad record, while Entry.All breaks at a truncated tail and catches read errors), so the outcome matches for a healthy log and differs only in how corruption is handled.

what: Returns the companion's breath-attack chance (50 by default, 80 if the lead's strength is more than a quarter above the companion's, 20 if more than a quarter below).
where: Mordor.Core/Combat.cs CompanionBreathes (private method in the combat class)
ev: The method computes the same 50/80/20 breath chance from the lead foe's guild level against the companion's, with the same quarter-band thresholds, but then goes on to roll the chance and handle the mishap and sweep, which the C++ function does not.

what: Returns the game's ratio of one monster's price to another's (R74), giving 0.0 when the denominator price is zero.
ev: No candidate divides one monster's price by another's or returns 0.0 for a zero denominator; each candidate computes a single item's buy, sell, identify, realign, or order price.

what: For one party member after a chest trap, it applies fire or explosion trap damage (R3/R4) when the trap is one of those types, then clamps the member's current hit points to zero if they have dropped below 1 (R5).
ev: Spring applies the same explosion (trap 3) and fire (trap 4) damage to each party member, with fire reduced by resistance, but it never clamps CurHits to zero when it drops below 1, which is the R5 step that resolveMemberTrap performs, and no other candidate performs that clamp for a single member.

what: Reports whether a monster's home area (its lair, per rule R28) matches the given area id.
where: Mordor.Core/Seer.cs Seer.Locate (the LairId check on `area.LairId == def.Id`)
ev: The C++ `isLairOf` only compares a monster's home area to an area id, while Candidate 1 treats a monster's lair as an area with `LairId == def.Id` and then rolls a 75% chance, which is a related but different lair concept and not a direct equality check on a home area.

what: Returns a character's required XP scaled by their race's penalty multiplier, rounded half-even, per the game's racial XP rule (R9/R11).
ev: Fn12A1 computes the experience needed for the next guild level from the level and the guild and race Exp fields, but it does not take the character's stored xpRequired and scale it by the racial penalty with half-even rounding as the C++ function does.

what: Handles the player's typed "titles <member>" command by looking up the named party member's Nomad guild membership and replying with their guild title and level, such as "Vagrant (1)", or an error message if the name is unknown or they aren't in the guild.
ev: The C++ function builds the reply from a guild title plus the level in brackets, and GuildTitles.Of supplies the title for a level in a guild (the title half), but no candidate looks up the named member, checks guild membership, or formats the "Vagrant (1)" string, and the error replies are absent.

what: Returns whether a given race may take a given guild, barring Elves, Osiri, and Gnomes from Warriors and Giants, Morlochs, and Gnomes from Wizards, with every other combination allowed.
ev: Both answer whether a race may join a guild, but AllowsRace reads the guild's RaceMask from data (and returns true for an unknown race) where the C++ hard-codes the Elf/Osiri/Gnome and Giant/Morloch/Gnome exclusions, so they match only if the mask data encodes those same rules.

what: Denies a teleporter or chute destination when its dungeon level is past the build level limit for the current release, per rule R131.
ev: Clamp applies the same last-level limit to every level change and returns a clamped level plus a denial line, using a global `On` flag rather than a release parameter, so it is a related check and not a boolean predicate for teleporter and chute destinations only.

what: Returns true once a companion subtype's count of attempts reaches the retry limit, at which point it gives up.
ev: No candidate checks a companion subtype's attempt count against a retry limit; Candidate 2 (Combat.cs KnownAsIndex) has a similar retry cap of 100 draws for monster misidentification, but it is a different rule with a different purpose.

what: Applies the R14 band-penalty term: returns w times the amount v lies above hi (positive) or below lo (negative), or 0 if v is within the band [lo, hi].
ev: The candidate's expression `v > hi ? w * (v - hi) : v < lo ? w * (v - lo) : 0` matches the C++ branches exactly, including the negative contribution below the band, while Rules.StatsAD only calls this helper.

what: Computes a character's experience points needed at a given level, using the wiki's level-XP formula scaled by the guild and race factors and rounded half-to-even.
ev: Fn12A1 computes the same wiki formula (i = L²·G·250/3, j = (2L−1)·344, k + l + 0.3) for the same inputs, but it uses float and Currency intermediates, and its own doc says it differs from the closed-form wiki version by one in 12 of 16,800 guild/race/level cases. The candidate's return line is also truncated, so I could not confirm its final rounding.

what: Computes the number of extra swings a character earns from the Multiple Swings ladder, based on their Multiple Swings value and guild level, using the SRD's logarithmic threshold progression (R10).
ev: SwingsFor runs the same ln(10 - mod + 1) threshold ladder with half-to-even rounding and the same doubling step, returning the extra swings for one guild level; it differs only in reading the modifier from GuildData rather than taking it as a parameter, and in omitting the explicit m >= 11 guard, which yields the same zero result via NaN comparisons.

what: Reports whether a companion is fallen, meaning it occupies a filled slot and has zero or fewer hit points.
ev: Step.Round skips a companion when `who.Companions[index]` is filled and `c.Hits <= 0`, the same test as companionsFallen, but only inline as an early return within a larger routine, not as a standalone predicate.

what: Rolls a percentile die (1–100) and returns whether it is at or below the given monster proc chance, so a monster's special effect (crit or backstab) triggers.
ev: DropsItem makes the same 1..100 roll and `roll <= chance` comparison, but adds chest-class and lock modifiers and a cap at 90, and it is not a generic proc check; MonstersEngage uses a strict `<` and tests engagement, not a proc.

what: Lists the dead party members in the town Morgue, and reports that raising them is not yet available, so no gold is taken and nobody is revived.
ev: The candidate is the same morgue counter, but it implements raising (Raise Character takes the fee and writes the raise to the body) instead of refusing, and it does not list every dead party member with their death state as doMorgue does.

what: Applies the acid breath attack from a monster's pre-attack step: if the attacker has a special attack of acid type, it computes acid damage from the monster's guild level and the victim's active level, then deals that damage to the victim and announces the hit.
ev: GroupAttacks runs one group's whole turn, with its doc comment listing "Breath first, then acid" as one step among many, so it covers the acid stage of monsterAcid but not as a standalone routine, and the candidate code shown is cut off before that acid step.

what: Checks whether a character who has joined a guild outranks the current guildmaster, and if so installs the character as the new guildmaster (taking the master's level and name, and recording the roster index when the character is in the roster) and announces the claim to the player.
ev: Claim makes the same level-outranks-holder takeover decision and sets the new master's name and level, but it has no roster-index (holder) field, no joined check, and no announcement, and ClaimMastership in CityWindow.axaml.cs only wraps it.

what: Rolls a random number against half the poison resistance value to decide whether the poison gas trap catches the character, with higher resistance meaning a higher chance of being caught.
ev: The poison branch applies the same test, `rng.NextDouble() * 100 < ResistancePercent(c, kind, item) / 2.0`, and poisons the character only when it passes, though the check is embedded in the larger trap-spring function and applies the result rather than returning a bool.

what: Applies a cure spell to a character by removing poison and disease, and for the Cure spell also restoring missing hits (halved while diseased, with the amount left unresolved per Table H).
ev: Apply handles the Cure and cure-poison/disease effects by clearing ailments and capping the heal at maximum, but it is a whole-spell dispatcher that does not halve the heal while diseased or apply the C++ heal-before-clear order, and Character.CurePoison and Character.CureDisease cover only the clearing halves.

what: Applies the chest poison-gas trap: each party member rolls against their poison resistance, and on failure becomes poisoned at the party's dungeon level.
ev: For each party member it rolls `NextDouble() * 100 < ResistancePercent(c, ResistPoison) / 2` and on success sets `Poisoned = true` and `PoisonLevel = dungeonLevel` silently, matching the C++; the one difference is that it uses `Effects.ResistancePercent`, which may include gear, where the C++ reads the raw `resistances.resist[]` value.

what: Checks whether a rescue location is valid under the game's rules by confirming the coordinate part count, that x and y are at least 1, and that the level falls within 1 to 15.
ev: The button handler inlines the same checks (three coordinate parts, x and y at least 1, level 1 to 15) but runs them inside a UI click handler that shows messages and charges gold, not as a standalone bool validator.

what: Applies a poison cure attempt that costs the character 2 hit points each try and, if the cure roll succeeds, clears the character's poison level and announces the poison is purged, otherwise announces that the poison remains.
ev: AilmentStep rolls the poison cure and clears poison on success, as the C++ does, but it charges the 2 HP only when the cure fails (the C++ charges on every attempt), it also handles disease, and it emits no "purged"/"remains" messages.

what: Reports whether any loaded mod in the host is currently active, returning true as soon as one is found and false otherwise.
ev: It gates on `ModHost.Active.Live.Any()`, the same "is any mod running" test as `anyModActive`, but it uses that test to decide whether to subscribe a redraw rather than returning a bool, and no candidate returns a bool or checks an `active` flag across all loaded mods.

what: Computes a character's effective Constitution for status-effect checks by adding the gear-granted CON bonus to base CON, following the SRD legend rather than the port's gear-less tick.
ev: No candidate computes base CON plus gear CON; Rules.AilmentStep (candidate 1) only consumes a precomputed `effectiveCon` parameter, and its doc comment cites the VB formula `CON + gearCON - 10`, but that is not the same function.

what: Returns true when a breathing monster's guild level is 0, meaning its breath attack does nothing more that turn, following the original game's behavior.
ev: Its breath branch mentions a level-0 monster case, but the excerpt is cut off before the code, so it is unclear whether that case makes the group do nothing, and no candidate is a standalone guild-level-0 predicate like `breathGroupInert`.

what: Converts a game value (such as a currency or stat amount) into an x87 80-bit extended-precision form by splitting it into a 64-bit mantissa and exponent plus a sign, with NaN, infinity, and zero all mapped to zero.
ev: X87.Of also converts a double exactly into a mantissa and exponent, but it keeps the stored 53-bit mantissa rather than normalizing to 64 bits, and it does not map NaN or infinity to zero, so those inputs give different results.

what: Registers the party-management town commands "roster", "unload", and "load" (the latter capped at 4 party members) so the player can list the party, remove a member while keeping their record, or bring a left-out member back.
ev: The C++ function only registers the three town commands "roster", "unload", and "load" with their handlers, while no candidate registers commands (Roster, AreaLook, WalkHere, LoadFor, LoadAllFrom, Strangers, OnLoad, and RosterPath are about listing, placement, loading, or file paths), so the unload/load party-management behavior is absent from the candidates.

what: Applies a race's resistance percentage to an amount by reducing it by that percent, rounding the reduction half-even, and returns the remaining value.
ev: SpellDamage applies `resistPct` as a multiplier and rounds the result half-to-even, which is close to the C++ reduction, but it is embedded in a spell-damage roll and clamps the percent and result, so it does not match `amount - round(amount * pct / 100)` exactly.

what: Dropping a dragged item slot onto a spell buffer clears that buffer on the character's order (if the index is valid) and reports that the buffer was emptied.
ev: The candidates handle the same drop-on-buffer event, but they store the dragged item or spell in the buffer (only an empty item slot clears it), whereas the C++ function always empties the buffer and returns BufferEmptied.

what: Computes the guild spell protection Defense value for a given spell level as 3 × ln(⌊SL/2⌋ + 1)², reproducing the source's known-buggy formula as written.
ev: It applies the same 3 × ln(p)² formula, but it takes the character's Protection value (Level/2 + 1) rather than a spell level, and it truncates the result to an int with VbInt where the C++ returns a double.

what: Cure Paralysis, when the caster is paralysed, clears the caster's paralysis level and paralysed status and says "Paralysis cured," regardless of which character the player picked as the target.
ev: Its doc comment says Cure Paralysis frees the caster if the caster is held, whatever target was picked, which matches the C++ quirk; it differs only in that the closing message names the picked character rather than being a fixed "Paralysis cured." string, and the Cure Paralysis branch body is cut off in the candidate, so this rests on the doc comment.

what: Handles the town "rescue" command: with one argument it resolves a pending raise on a fallen party member, and with four arguments it charges a fee and, if the guessed location is close enough, either restores a living member's hit points or carries a dead body home to the morgue, returning the resulting message to the player.
where: Mordor.Core/Rescue.cs Rescue.CarryHome (with Mordor.App/DungeonWindow.axaml.cs pick.WaitForRescue and CityWindow.axaml.cs looked.WaitForRescue as the callers that use it)
ev: The C++ town "rescue <member> <x> <y> <level>" path (charge a fee, check the guessed location with a closeness test, then either restore a living member's HP or carry a dead body home) has no direct match in the candidates, since the closest one, looked.RescuersButton, is the morgue's Hire Rescuers counter that only collects the coordinates and cost and never shows the closeness check or the outcome, and CarryHome only covers the carry-home step for a body the player waited to have found, not a fee-based search or the living-member heal.

what: Checks whether a buffer slot index refers to an item in the player's pack (slots 0 through kPackSlots-1), as opposed to some other kind of buffer slot.
ev: The C++ `bufferIsItem` returns `b >= 0 && b < kPackSlots`, and `SpellBuffers.IsItem` is the same expression with `PackSlots` in place of `kPackSlots`.

what: Rolls a percent chance (75%, per the lair-named constant) to decide whether a lair spawns a named monster.
ev: Seer.Locate contains the same lair-named check (`area.LairId == def.Id && rng.NextDouble() * 100 < 75`), but it is embedded in a search over floor areas rather than being a standalone 75% roll, and it uses `<` where the C++ comparison is unstated.

what: Rolls a percent chance against the companion stone chance (computed from the companion's Constitution and the level at which the stone was found) to decide whether the stone succeeds.
ev: No candidate rolls a companion-stone success against a Constitution- and level-based chance; the closest, Raising.Resolve, uses a similar percent-threshold roll but for a character's raise failure, and the companion-raise candidates (SpellEffect.CompanionRaiseChance, Morgue.CompanionChance) only compute raise chances.

what: Takes the party up or down a level via stairs in the dungeon, refusing the climb if the leading member is paralysed or dead, and otherwise moving the party one level within the build's bounds.
ev: It matches the C++ on the core behaviour, moving one level down or up via ChangeLevel and refusing the climb when the leader is paralysed while letting stairs down through, but it differs in that level 1 exits to town instead of clamping, it checks only paralysis (not death) for the climb, and it returns a message string rather than a StairsOutcome.

what: Decides whether a stone (petrification) attack from a stoner creature lands on a target, using the stoner's CON against the target's stone resistance and level, per the referenced rule notes.
ev: No candidate implements the stone-landing CON check directly, but CompanionStrikes' doc comment describes the stone's constitution test, reading the companion's own CON when the target is a monster, and the visible text does not include the test itself, so this is only a related method.

what: Swaps the contents of two pack slots (empty slots included) after checking both indices are valid, and optionally remaps the character's spell buffer references to follow the moved items.
ev: Both swap two pack slots (empty included) after range-checking, return success, and remap spell buffers only when a `buffersFollow` flag is set; the candidate uses one-based slots and refuses slot 1 and anything past 40, whereas the C++ uses zero-based slots checked by `validStorage`.

what: Returns the damage modifier for a player blow, adding the critical-hit increment when the blow crits and the backstab increment when it is a backstab, so both stack on a "Severed" blow.
ev: It adds the same +5 for a critical and +2 for a backstab, but it also builds the fighting term, weapon modifier, invisibility halving and size difference, then rolls damage, so it is a larger function rather than a standalone modifier.

what: Computes a character's guild-based attack and defense awards as the highest att and highest def across all guilds the character has joined, taking each stat's maximum independently.
ev: It takes the max attack and max defence independently across the character's guild memberships, as the C++ does, but it derives each value from `GuildAD(m.Guild, m.Level)` rather than reading the stored `m.att`/`m.def` fields, and it has no explicit joined check.

what: Caps an identification level earned by an exchange-form item at MOSTLY unless it was obtained at the General Store, which is the only source allowed to reach full (ALL) identification under the game's T6 table.
ev: No candidate caps an ALL identification level to MOSTLY based on whether the item came from the General Store; the closest, Rules.NextIdLevel, can raise a level to ALL with no source check and no cap.

what: On arrival at a dungeon square, it places the square on the automap, and the rest of the square effects (water, anti-magic, pits, stairs, teleporters) are left unimplemented in this part of the rules.
ev: AfterMove runs the square's effects on arrival in sub0835 order, and the candidate's notes say the square routine also includes the automap write, but it goes well beyond the C++ stub, which only records the square on the automap, and the excerpt doesn't show that automap write as a separate step.

what: Decides whether a creature with alignment `creatureAlign` turns against its owner, returning true when the two alignments are more than one step apart (R36).
ev: No candidate compares a creature's alignment with its owner's and returns whether the gap exceeds one step (R36); the candidates handle pen counts, pen keys, item alignment flags, store display, and guild eligibility.

what: When a room is cleared of its foes, it records the time of clearing (the stamp) and marks the room's foe slot as emptied, unless the room was already emptied.
ev: MarkCleared has the same "already emptied" guard (`Foes[0].Ref == -1`), stamps the time, and sets the emptied marker, but it also zeroes the group counts, lowers the level tally, and stores the room, which stampRoomEmptied does not do; its stamp is seconds since midnight rather than the C++ `nowMs`.

what: Looks up a toggle's index in a mod's declared settings by matching its key case-insensitively, returning -1 if no toggle matches (the F5 DefaultFor lookup).
ev: DefaultFor does the same case-insensitive search over the declared toggles, but it returns that toggle's default value (or false), not its index, and it has no -1 path, so it is a related lookup rather than the same function.

what: Returns the age cost a character takes when raised from the dead, depending on how they died: 54 years for a quiet failure, 84 for being stoned, and 124 for being turned to rock.
ev: Both map Stoned to its age constant, Rock to its age constant, and every other cause (including causes 3-7) to the ordinary/quiet-failure constant, though the candidate's constant values (AgeDaysStoned, AgeDaysRock, AgeDaysOrdinary) are not shown, so the 84/124/54 figures are unverified.

what: Writes a guild log line announcing that the character was resurrected, using the game's death-message text key.
ev: This method appends the same guild-log "resurrected" line (sub0578, `GuildLog.Wrote.Resurrected(who.Name, by)`) on a successful raise, but only as one step inside a larger offer-and-roll flow, while the C++ function does nothing but write that line.

what: Checks whether a character's Intelligence, Wisdom, Constitution, and Charisma all meet the minimum stat requirements for a given binding spell (Control, Bind, or Domination).
ev: Unmet checks each stat against a per-stat minimum (`Stats[i] < ReqStats[i]`), the same mechanism as the C++ check, but it covers six stats for guild membership rather than INT/WIS/CON/CHA for a bind spell, and it returns a list of unmet requirements instead of a bool.

what: Computes the difficulty of a charm spell from the caster's level and the guild level using a logarithmic formula, applying an extra 1.5x multiplier unless the p036E flag is set.
ev: IdLevelRoll computes the same rounded `(30 + LevelFound) * Log((GuildLevel+5)/10 + 1)` difficulty and the same `p036E` 1.5x halving, but then goes on to compare it against identify skill and returns an ID level rather than the difficulty, and it omits the C++ `arg > 0` guard.

what: Rolls the CON-loss check for the morgue path (kind 23) using the character's natural Constitution score against a threshold derived from that score, which can cost the character Constitution.
ev: The candidate computes the same natural-CON-based morgue threshold (`max(0, 50 - con*2)`) and its doc describes the `Rnd * 100 <` roll, but the roll itself (`rollConLoss`) is not shown in any candidate, and Raising.Resolve's CON-loss handling is truncated in the excerpt.

what: Decides whether a monster is hostile to a character based on the monster's alignment: Good monsters attack anyone not Good, Neutral monsters attack on a rolled 60% chance, and Evil monsters always attack.
ev: It also keys on monster alignment versus character alignment and gives Good monsters no chance against Good characters, but it returns a charisma-scaled per-tick engagement chance rather than the C++ boolean rule (Good hostile to non-Good, Neutral 60% roll, Evil always hostile), and its Evil-monster numbers (25/35) don't match "always hostile."

what: Prunes the party member at the given index, removing a dead member from the party under the game's R11/R12 rules, and reports whether the removal happened.
ev: It removes dead party members under the same unload-and-save rules, but it works on the whole party through `_party.RemoveTheDead` rather than one member at a given index, and it returns nothing instead of a bool.

what: Decides whether a poison-clearing attempt succeeds by checking that the roll result is above the kPoisonClearAbove threshold (185).
ev: AilmentStep contains the same poison-cure test (`roll > 185` means cured), but it also rolls the value, applies the disease check, and deducts hits, so it does more than the C++ function's single comparison.

what: Returns the race's experience multiplier by looking up the race's raw experience value in a table, which sets how much a character of that race's experience gains are scaled.
ev: LoadRaces reads each race's raw `ExpFactor` float from the MDATA1 record, which is the input the C++ uses, but no candidate maps that raw value through a multiplier table the way `kRaceMultByRawExp[kRaceRawExp[race]]` does.

what: Applies damage to a trap's hit count, leaving the remaining hits after the damage with a floor of zero.
ev: TakeDamage performs the same subtract-then-floor-at-zero on hits, but it mutates a Character and emits "Ouch"/"Aigh" lines, whereas the C++ is a pure integer function with no messaging.

what: Rolls a healing amount for a spell by adding a random value from 1 to the minimum to the minimum itself, per the SRD's healing formula (R13).
ev: Both compute a random healing amount from a base value, but SpellHeal uses a log-scaled formula with a subtracted random term, not the C++ rule of minimum plus a random value from 1 to minimum.

what: Decides whether a given weapon is resisted at the current dungeon level by checking it against the weapon list for that level band, returning false for level 1 and for any level above 16.
ev: No candidate checks whether a weapon is resisted by dungeon-level band (the `kWeaponBand*` lists or level 1 and above-16 handling); the closest, Combat.cs `WeaponsOf`/`WeaponOf`, only selects equipped weapons, and the crit/backstab and swing methods don't involve resistance.

what: Registers the town-screen "uncurse" command, which lets a player pay a fee to remove a curse from an equipped item for a named party member and slot.
ev: The C++ function only registers the town "uncurse" command, while Refusal covers just part of the uncurse rule by returning the clerk's refusal for an uncursed or unequipped slot, and no candidate registers the command or charges the fee.

what: Sets the combat order for a party member so that their next action is cleared of any item or spell and instead assigns the given slot, ignoring out-of-range member indices.
ev: KeepItemSlot only clears the cast flag (`ItemCast = false`) on an existing item order, or removes the order, and never sets the slot or item to -1 as setItemOrder does; CombatSettingItem may set the order when it runs the Use command, but its body is truncated so I can't confirm that.

what: Rolls a d3000 check against a Charisma-and-level-based join bar, and if the roll passes, picks which of up to four groups makes the join offer (group 0 is the only one shown).
ev: FillGroup's comment covers the same join-offer logic (lines 1948-1967, where JoinOffer is set per group), but the candidate is truncated before the d3000 roll against the Charisma/level bar and the pick among up to four groups, so the match can't be confirmed.

what: Item (fetch) quests can only be started by the player once their guild level exceeds kItemQuestMinGuildLevel (15), a gate the engine enforces in place of the wiki's "begins at level 15" rule.
ev: RollQuest applies the same gate (`guildLevel > 15`) to pick an item quest, but only as one inline condition inside a larger quest roll, not as a standalone predicate like `ItemQuestStarts`.

what: Computes the constant penalty factor used in the thieving formula (F6), returning ln(2) × 4 × ln(2) × 1.25 × 1.25 × 1.5 as a double.
ev: No candidate is a standalone constant, but AbilityFloor (and also AbilityCeiling and BestAbilityValue) computes the same value inline as `against * 1.5` with `against = (Math.Log(2)*4)*(Math.Log(2)*1.25)*1.25`, which equals the C++ F6 product, as a sub-expression of a larger ability-floor formula.

what: Returns the character's resistance value for the given index (the resistance slot indexed by idx), which status-effect checks such as poison, disease, paralysis and petrification use to decide whether an effect takes hold.
ev: It returns a character's resistance to one kind, but it recomputes the value from race baseline, gear flags and spell resistance rather than reading a stored slot, and it takes extra inputs (an item lookup) that resistAt does not.

what: Attempts to add a candidate character to the player's party automatically, refusing with a player-facing message if the candidate is absent, dead, the party is full, the leader is dead, or the candidate is opposite-aligned to a member, and otherwise joining them to the party.
ev: LoadFor applies the same not-here, dead, and opposite-alignment refusals and announces "is now a member of your party" on joining, but it loads the whole saved roster rather than adding one candidate, and the visible code has no full-party or dead-leader check in the C++ order.

what: Drops an item from the player's pack, refusing if the character is paralysed, the slot is invalid or empty, or the item is guild-issued; it asks for confirmation first, refuses to drop an equipped cursed item, and otherwise destroys the item outright.
where: Mordor.App/DungeonWindow.axaml.cs DungeonWindow.OnSheetDrop (CityWindow.Mdi.cs CityWindow.OnPackDrop is an equivalent city version)
ev: Both check paralysis, the selected pack slot, and guild-issued items, ask for confirmation before refusing a cursed equipped item, then remove the item outright, matching the C++ order, though the port also refuses slot 0 (the Hands) which the C++ does not.

what: Withdraws the selected vault (bank) items into the first free pack slots, stopping when the pack is full, and clears any party item-buffer orders that pointed at the slot each item moved into.
ev: For each selected vault row it takes the first free pack slot, stops with the "no free slots" message when the pack is full, and moves the item via TakeFromVault, which also clears buffers naming that slot; it differs only in sorting rows, showing a message, and returning no count.

what: Charges the raise cost from the party's gold (on hand first, then bank), rolls a percent chance to restore a dead companion to life with 1 hit, and permanently loses the companion (marks it unoccupied and says so) if the roll fails.
ev: It charges through CharPay (hand, then bank, refusing when short) and then runs a raise roll, which matches the C++ flow, but it uses Raising.Resolve with complications rather than a single percent roll, and the candidate is truncated before any failure path that would mark the companion unoccupied.

what: Converts an unsigned magnitude into a signed 64-bit game value, clamping it to the i64 range so that out-of-range results saturate at the limits instead of overflowing.
ev: The C++ function clamps an unsigned magnitude into the signed i64 range with sign handling, and no candidate does that: Saturate in VbCurrency.cs clamps a signed long to a Currency range, GetInt64 and GetCurrency read raw values with no clamping, and the rest are unrelated parsers or rounding helpers.

what: Decides whether a join offer is accepted for a group by admitting groups with alignment 1 (read as Neutral) or groups whose alignment matches the viewing character's alignment.
ev: FillGroup's join-offer block (the `if (s.Engaged == 0)` branch that sets `JoinOffer`) is the only candidate that decides whether a group is offered to join, but its text is cut off before any alignment test, so I can't confirm it implements the `g == 1 || g == v` rule.

what: Decides whether a right-click attack on a companion is ignored (no HP left), refused (a Good companion checked against a Good comparison alignment), or lets the companion go.
ev: It matches the Hits > 0 check and the Good-companion refusal, but it also requires the player's own alignment to be Good, whereas the C++ compares the companion against a constant Good, so a non-Good player with a Good companion is refused in C++ and let through in the candidate.

what: Each engagement tick, it counts down the encounter timer, then either has a hostile group attack or rolls a Charisma-based check to turn a peaced group hostile when the selected character is near it.
ev: CombatTick is the once-a-second timer where waiting monsters decide whether to start on you, which is the role of engagementTick, but the visible text (truncated) shows no countdown, no Charisma-based hostileRoll, and no join-offer check, so the details differ or are unverified.
