what: Returns true when a single step in the given facing from square (x, y) would move the party off the edge of the dungeon level's map.
ev: SquareAhead returns null when a step would leave the map, which is the same bounds test, but it also returns null for walls, doors and secret doors, which the C++ function ignores, and no candidate is a pure off-map check.

what: Decides whether the chest trap panel is shown by comparing the viewer's base DEX against group 0's monster DEX (the viewer's DEX must be strictly higher), and keeps the previous panel state with an error log if either DEX is zero.
ev: ShowChest uses the viewer's own DEX against Foes(0)'s DEX to decide whether the trap panel shows, but its log-based formula (MONSMOD.BAS:4118-4128) differs from the C++ strict comparison, and it has no zero-DEX error log or keep-previous-state branch.

what: Computes a character's starting base value for one attribute from their race, giving the race's maximum or its minimum plus the free points per stat, whichever is lower.
ev: Roll computes `_base[i] = Math.Min(_race.Max[i], _race.Min[i] + FreePerStat)` for each stat, which is the same formula as `createBase`, though Roll also sets the stat pool and refreshes the UI.

what: Returns true when the newbie guard is active, the lead character's guild level is above the newbie maximum, and the class is not the exempt class index, meaning the lead's rerolls are not protected by the newbie rule.
ev: No candidate contains a newbie-guard check, a guild-level-above-maximum comparison, or an exempt-class-index exclusion; the closest, Rules.AbilityLead, iterates guilds to pick the best ability chance and does not gate anything on a newbie rule.

what: Decides whether a dead character must sit out the rescue wait, which applies when they are dead below ground (dungeon level above 0) unless their body was pulled up by rock.
ev: It hides the wait button for rock deaths (`WaitBtn.IsVisible = !inRock`) as the C++ predicate does, but it also shows the button at level 0 where the C++ returns false, and no candidate returns the same boolean (`dead && level > 0 && not rock`).

what: Applies the "nought" rule at dungeon level 0: every party member is moved to area -1, and any dead member found inside rock on a deeper level is blanked and removed from the party with a message to the player.
ev: It matches the level-0 rule of setting every member's area to -1 and leaves dead-in-rock members alone, but it does not blank or remove those bodies from the party or show the "body is lost in the rock" message, and it also copies the leader's area on deeper levels, which the C++ does not do.

what: Picks the index of a gold-share receiver among the party members by drawing a random number and weighting the two end indices at half weight, reproducing the original game's distribution (not a uniform draw).
ev: It is the same half-even rounded draw `roundHalfEven(Rnd * n)`, but it takes n directly with no `memberCount <= 1` guard and no `memberCount - 1` mapping, so the receiver pick would need a caller passing `memberCount - 1`, and no candidate performs the gold-share receiver selection.

what: Reports whether the HP note should be shown for a spell, which requires both that a damage range exists and that the spell row's HP flag is "Y".
ev: No candidate checks a damage range's presence together with a spell row's HP flag to decide whether an HP note shows; the closest, Buffs.cs DropVerdict.AsksTarget, asks whether a spell prompts "Cast on Who?", which is unrelated.

what: Looks up the spell attached to an item by its 1-based spell index, returning the zero-based index into the spell list, or -1 if the item has no valid spell.
ev: It applies the same guard (`SpellIndex > 0` and `SpellIndex - 1` within the spell list) and returns the spell at that zero-based position, but it returns the `Spell` object or null instead of the index or -1.

what: Computes the Protect value a cast spell grants, as half the spell level rounded down plus one, per SRD c09p2 [c27].
ev: For the Protect case, this method writes the cast's Protection as `Int(casterSpellLevel(...) / 2) + 1` (MAINMOD2.BAS:1046), the same formula as `protectionFromCast`, though the candidate is truncated and the expression appears only in its comment, and it is embedded in a larger method rather than a standalone function.

what: Returns true when an item's type number falls in the consumable range 23–28 or is 30 or 31, meaning the item is used up when its charges or uses run out.
ev: The method returns `(it.Type >= 23 && it.Type <= 28) || it.Type == 30 || it.Type == 31`, which is the same type-number test as the C++ `isConsumedType`, differing only in taking an `Item` instead of a raw `i32`.

what: Builds the encounter-square traits for a dungeon square, where a ROCK flag suppresses random encounters, a STUD flag raises the encounter spawn floor by one, and a FOG flag leaves the encounter group unidentified.
ev: It matches only the STUD part (`onStud ? level + 1 : level`), but it omits the ROCK suppression and FOG unidentified flags and returns an int rather than the traits struct.

what: Widens an encounter's LevelFound spread by kSpreadStep when no monster is found, and reports the new spread to the player.
where: Mordor.Core/Rules.cs Rules.EncounterSpread (closest concept only; it rolls a spread from level and does not widen one when nothing is found)
ev: No candidate increments an encounter's spread by a fixed step after a failed search or reports the new value, since Rules.EncounterSpread computes a fresh random spread from level and stud status, and the other candidates use spread for position blur or misidentification.

what: Computes the minimum damage of an archive-style damage spell from its base value, power, and spell level, using the R10 formula (averaging base and a level-scaled term).
ev: SpellDamage builds the same base-plus-level-log-plus-`Int(SL*(Power-1)/10)` term as the C++ R10 formula, but it uses `Log(SL+1)/Log(5)` where R10 uses `LN(SL)/1.61`, and it applies a random roll and resistance instead of returning the half-average minimum.

what: Rolls a percent chance, based on the relation value, to decide whether a breath attack fires.
where: Mordor.Core/Combat.cs as.CompanionBreathes (`CompanionBreathes` in the `Combat.cs` candidate; the `as.` prefix in the candidate header is a typo for the enclosing class)
ev: It performs the same relation-based percent roll (50, 80, or 20 from the guild-level comparison) that decides whether a companion breath fires, but it also goes on to resolve the mishap and damage, which the C++ function does not do.

what: Implements the R8 no-weapon rule: if the actor has no weapon or total swings are below 1, it announces "Using no weapon!" and sets the actor's combat order to Defend, returning true.
ev: When there is no weapon or the total swings are below 1, PlayerSwings prints "Using no weapon!", sets the actor's order to Defend, and stops, which matches the C++ rule; it also clears ItemOrders for the actor, a side effect the C++ function does not have.

what: Reports whether a mod id is already taken in the host's mod list, so a later mod with the same id is skipped and the first one found is kept (rule R5).
ev: Discover does the same duplicate-id check (case-insensitive match against already-discovered mods, skipping the later one and keeping the first), but it is inline within discovery rather than a standalone query that returns whether an id is taken.

what: Decides whether a companion can be a candidate for binding, which is true only when it is still alive (Hits > 0) and has a nonzero BindingLevel.
ev: Round opens with the same living-companion guard (`c.Hits <= 0` returns early), but its second check skips bound-for-life companions rather than requiring a nonzero BindingLevel, and it returns a Step instead of a bool, so it is not the same predicate.

what: Under rule R28, Alt+1 through Alt+4 switch the active command when the party has more than one member and the chosen slot is occupied.
ev: For Alt+1..4 it calls `SwitchCommandsTo(slot)` only when `_party.Members.Count > 1 && slot < _party.Members.Count`, which is the same condition as the C++ `party.size > 1 && digit <= party.size` with the 0-based slot, and it otherwise does nothing, though it returns a handled flag rather than a bool.

what: Classifies where a target stands relative to the locator, returning "too far" if the dungeon levels differ by more than the locate range, "in the city" if the target is in the city area, and otherwise a relative compass direction.
ev: No candidate classifies a locate target as too far, in the city, or by relative direction; the closest, Mordor.Core/Seer.cs Seer.LocateCharacter, only rolls for success and formats the "at x,y,level" message, and Seer.Locate picks a monster spawn square rather than classifying a target.

what: Pools all party members' on-hand gold, splits it evenly among them, and gives any leftover coins to the chosen remainder member (or the first member if the index is invalid).
ev: PayGold also splits a pot evenly across the party, but the pot is encounter and stolen gold added to each member's purse, with the remainder discarded rather than given to one member, whereas the C++ pools every member's existing on-hand gold and gives the remainder to a chosen member.

what: Reads a party member's buffer value for a given slot from the session's feature state, returning -1 (kBufferEmpty) when the buffer is unset or its stored text can't be parsed as an integer.
ev: No candidate looks up a buffer by member and slot in feature state or parses its text to an integer; IsEmpty only tests the -1 sentinel (`buffer < 0`), which is one part of what buffersRead does, while SpellBuffers.Describe reads the slot and returns "(Nothing)" when empty but produces a display string rather than a value.

what: Decides whether a caster can reach a given spell through any joined guild they belong to, by checking the guild's spell rate and ceiling for the spell's school against the caster's guild level.
ev: For each spell it applies the same test as the C++ loop: a joined guild with level above zero, a rate above zero for the spell's school, a ceiling that reaches the spell level, and the level-versus-guild-level gate (`Level * rate <= guildLevel / 2 + 0.5`), returning true if any guild passes; it differs only in running over all spells at once and checking `Level > 0` instead of a separate `joined` flag.

what: Blackout trap: when a chest trap triggers, every party member loses their active spell effects, levitation, invisibility, and protection, and the player is told the lights went out.
ev: It strips a character's spell mask and spell-granted resistances and then recomputes, which matches the per-character core of the blackout trap, but it also clears `SpellResist` (which the C++ does not), omits the party loop and the "lights go out" message, and is a per-character helper rather than the trap handler itself.

what: Rolls a d100-style check against the companion's morgue chance (derived from natural Constitution) to decide whether a companion's raise from the morgue succeeds, returning true on success.
ev: It computes the same companion morgue chance (`Math.Min(98, 75 + con)`) and the same fail-on-`Int(Rnd*100) > chance` rule, but it stops at the threshold and does not perform the roll or return a success boolean as the C++ function does, and `Raising.Resolve` rolls against a caller-supplied chance inside the broader raise routine.

what: Given a chest trap number, it returns the trap's scope: none for trap 0 or out-of-range values, whole party for traps 1–4, and opener-only for traps 5–10.
ev: Spring applies traps 1-4 to every party member and takes the opener as a separate parameter, which implicitly encodes the scope split, but no candidate returns a scope value or handles the none/out-of-range cases the way chestTrapScope does.

what: Swaps two player inventory slots (numbered 2 to 40) and, when requested, retargets the character's spell buffers so they keep following the moved items.
ev: It rejects slots at or below 1 and above PackSize (the 2..40 range), swaps the two pack entries, and remaps spell buffers via SpellBuffers.PackSlotsSwapped only when buffersFollow is true, matching the C++ function's behavior.

what: Returns the breath-weapon damage percentage for a monster based on the ratio of the victim's level to the monster's guild level, using Table D bands (80% above 1.25x, 50% between 0.75x and 1.25x, 20% below 0.75x).
where: Mordor.Core/Combat.cs Combat.CompanionBreathes (the inline 80/50/20 quarter-band selection, not a standalone method)
ev: It uses the same 80/50/20 bands at a quarter either way, but it compares the lead foe's guild level against the companion's (monster stronger means 80), while the C++ compares victimLevel against monsterGuildLevel (victim stronger means 80), and the percent is computed inside a larger routine rather than returned by its own function.

what: Scans the companion roster in order and returns the index of the first occupied slot whose hit points are zero, which is the candidate offered for raising at the morgue (or -1 if none qualifies).
ev: Run scans occupied companion slots and skips any with Hits > 0, so it also selects fallen companions, but it keeps the one with the greatest MaxHits (and has carry side effects) instead of returning the first slot with Hits == 0, and no candidate returns that first match.

what: When a chest trap is triggered with more than one party member present, it clears the trap so the chest is left untrapped and full, announces that, and skips loot and the trap's exit; if the party member is alone, it reveals the trap and resolves it.
where: Mordor.App/DungeonWindow.axaml.cs DungeonWindow.OpenChest (with Mordor.Core/Combat.cs Combat.TrapSprung as the trap-clearing piece)
ev: None of the candidates has the party-size > 1 branch that sets the trap to NotTrapped and announces "not trapped while others are here"; OpenChest resolves the trap roll for the opener and TrapSprung clears the trap, but neither checks party size.

what: Returns the maximum value a character of the given race may reach for a given stat, which is that race's base stat maximum plus a fixed offset of 5 (the R3 rule).
ev: The candidate computes the same rule inline (`int ceiling = race.Max[i] + 5`) as part of a larger routine that applies item stat modifiers, so no candidate returns the ceiling as a standalone value like `statCeiling` does.

what: Rolls once per day whether a body is found during a rescue wait, comparing a random draw scaled by a ceiling against a chance derived from the level, area, days waited, and whether the body is easy to find.
ev: It performs the same per-day test, `rng.NextDouble() * ceiling <= chance`, but inside a loop that returns the total days waited rather than a single-day bool, and it inlines its own ceiling and chance rather than calling equivalents of `rescueCeiling` and `rescueChance`.

what: Decides whether an item is excluded from quest-item assignment, rejecting cursed items, items of level 0, and items worth less than the minimum quest value (100 gold).
ev: No candidate has a standalone exclusion predicate, but QuestItem's loop applies the same rejections (price under 100, cursed, level 0) as part of picking an item, and QuestItemReachable repeats the same three tests only to decide whether the loop can finish.

what: Thief theft resolution: if the rolled amount exceeds the victim's purse, the stolen amount is capped at the purse's whole-gold value (rounded half-even), otherwise the rolled amount is taken as-is.
ev: When the roll exceeds the purse it returns the purse rounded half to even to whole gold, otherwise it returns the roll, and a roll equal to the purse keeps the roll, matching thiefTake; it adds a null return on overflow that the C++ version does not have.

what: When paralysis at level 0 or a city-gate clear happens, the character's current stat shift is copied into the stored stat shift so it persists, and a "Stored stat shift kept." message is shown.
ev: No candidate copies the current shift into a stored shift; the nearest, Mordor.Core/Character.cs Character.Paralyse, folds stored and current shift together on level-0 paralysis but does not perform the keep-for-good copy or emit the message.

what: Computes the gold fee for uncursing an item as 80% of its base price divided by 0.5 (rounded half-even), returned in internal currency units (gold × 10000).
ev: No candidate computes an uncurse fee; the closest, StoreStock.cs StoreStock.RealignCost, uses a different formula (0.72 × Price, doubled for cross-spectrum changes, half-even rounded) and is a realignment fee, not 0.8 × Price / 0.5.

what: Returns the spell points a player gains from using a Scroll of Spells (50) or Tome of Spells (200), and 0 for any other special item type.
ev: The switch adds 50 for special type 11 and 200 for type 12, the same mapping as the C++ function, but it is embedded in a larger method that mutates the character, adds sound and alignment handling, and skips the gain when the item is reversed, so it is not a pure lookup.

what: Decides whether combat begins on arrival, returning false if the monster group is empty, its front monster is not hostile, or no members are still alive, and true otherwise (SRD c07p1 rule R1).
ev: Its opening guard tests the same three conditions as `arrivalCombatStarts` (empty group, front not hostile, no living member), but the method is a void that goes on to start combat and run a monsters' round rather than returning a bool.

what: Builds the companion record for a creature charmed by a spell, copying the foe's identity, alignment, and special flags and setting its current and maximum hits and binding level from the cast.
ev: Both build the charmed companion from the foe with hits at cast, max hits from the roll, alignment copied from the foe, and binding level from the spell's level, but the candidate leaves Name empty instead of the foe's known name and does not copy guild level or special flags directly (it uses Ref and adds IdLevel).

what: Compares which spells a character can reach before and after a change, and announces any newly reachable spells to the player under a "New spells within reach:" header.
ev: This candidate computes the same per-spell reachability that the C++ compares before and after, but it only returns a bool array and never announces the newly reachable spells under a "New spells within reach:" header; the MakeLevel candidate is truncated and its doc comment says spells learned go to the Messages list, not that header.

what: Caps the number of hits recorded against a monster at the monster's remaining hit points, per rule R31 of the melee rules, so a monster is never recorded as taking more damage than it has left.
where: Mordor.Core/Combat.cs as.KeepRecord (nearest, but unrelated to the cap)
ev: No candidate computes min(hitsTaken, monsterHpRemaining), and KeepRecord only clamps a fallen monster's hits at zero via Math.Max(0, ...) when it passes the record to the next monster in the group.

what: Returns the current hit points a character is raised with, which is full max hits for a Resurrect or Morgue raise and 1 hit point otherwise.
ev: Resolve takes the raise `kind` and its doc comment says the hits are handled there, but the visible code is truncated before any CurHits assignment, so the Resurrect/Morgue-gets-MaxHits, otherwise-1 rule is not shown and cannot be confirmed.

what: Maps a facing-relative direction index (0 to 3) to the word the player sees for it: ahead, right, behind, or left.
ev: No candidate maps a facing-relative index to the words ahead/right/behind/left; the nearest, SpellEffect.RelativeDirection, works in right/forward/down coordinate offsets, not names.

what: Returns the lair-treasure bonus for a given lead value, but this placeholder version always returns 0 because the lair flag can't be read without GameData.
ev: ChestClass applies the same lair-treasure adjustment (+25 to BoxChance when the monster is the level's lair monster) and picks a chest class, whereas the C++ stub takes a lead value and always returns 0.

what: Decides whether an invisible creature is skipped when a sighting is checked, applying only in the dungeon (reader's DungeonLevel above 0) and not in town.
ev: The candidate's early return uses the same test (invisible and reader's DungeonLevel > 0) but adds `!reader.SeeingInvisible` and sits inside a larger filing routine, whereas the C++ function is a standalone predicate with no See Invisible term.

what: When a companion's blow reduces a victim to zero or fewer hit points, it marks the victim as dead and returns true so the caller knows this blow was the kill; otherwise it changes nothing and returns false.
ev: Both concern a companion's kill, but the candidate only reports the kill to the mods as the owner's Companion-kind damage and never checks hit points, sets the victim Dead, or returns a result, which the C++ function does.

what: Runs the R37 carry choice for a fallen companion: it picks the healthiest-or-highest-max-hits downed companion, either picks it up as the carried body (clamping negative hits to 0) if it fits the carrier's size, or releases it as too big, and then sweeps the remaining fallen companions.
ev: The candidate runs the same carry choice (downed-companion scan, "dropped" line with the slot -1 quirk that returns early, and the size test that sets the carried companion), but it clamps hits to 0 for every downed companion it scans rather than only the picked one, and the candidate is cut off before the too-big release and sweep.

what: Returns the first record index to start a Seer search from, giving monsters record 1, items record 0, and characters record 0 as a default, per the original FRMSEEK.BAS logic.
ev: Locate applies the same rule inline, searching monsters from record 1 (`_monsters.Skip(1)`) and items from record 0 (`_items`), but no candidate returns a first-record index per kind, and the Character case (default 0) is not handled separately.

what: Forces or lets a companion leave the owner's party, either as a turned-loose right-click attack or as a Kick Out, and posts the matching message to the player.
ev: The candidate has the same shape (a companion-turn check, then a join-the-fight or drop), but it leaves the companion in place when a forced attack doesn't turn or is refused, and it posts no "send your companion away" message on Kick Out, where the C++ always releases the slot and says so.

what: Computes the Protect ailment level granted by a spell cast, as half the caster's spell level (rounded down) plus one.
ev: That candidate's Protect branch sets Ailments(Protect) using the cast's number, and its comment cites MAINMOD2.BAS:1046 for `Int(casterSpellLevel / 2) + 1`, which matches the C++ formula, but the candidate is a larger effect-application method, not a standalone computation of the level, and the visible text is truncated before the formula itself appears.

what: Returns false if any worn item is cursed, so a character wearing cursed gear is refused when trying to join a guild (SRD R13.4).
ev: Both scan the worn/equipped items and refuse if any is cursed, but ForfeitRefusal gates quest forfeit rather than guild joining, returns a message string instead of a bool, and checks the slot's SlotCursed flag rather than the item definition's cursed field.

what: On finding an item, it computes how well the finder identifies it by comparing their identify skill against the item's difficulty at the current dungeon level, and returns the resulting identification level.
ev: It compares the character's identify skill with the item's difficulty and returns an IdLevel, but it uses the item's own Floor rather than the dungeon level and maps the gap to Mostly/Partial/Barely instead of the C++ level function.

what: Determines a spell's reach in combat: whole-party spells (effect 200 and up), class-filtered charm and control spells (effects 75-99), monster-targeting combat spells (effects 0 and 100), and caster-only spells otherwise, defaulting to caster-only when the spell is missing.
ev: No candidate classifies a spell's combat reach by effect id (>=200 whole party, 75-99 class-filtered, 0/100 monster-targeting, else caster-only, missing spell defaults to caster-only); the 75-99 class check in Candidates 1-3 only zeroes damage inside a monster-hit calculation, and Candidates 4-8 handle casting and target selection.

what: Each tick, if the character is poisoned and alive, it rolls to cure the poison using Constitution and poison level; on failure it takes poison damage, and if hit points drop to zero or below the character dies of poison.
ev: AilmentStep makes the same poison cure roll (CON-based, minus poison level×2, cure above 185, otherwise lose 2 hits) but also handles disease in the same call and does not kill the character or emit the poison messages, which the C++ does in poisonTick itself and the candidate's caller (DungeonWindow.axaml.cs keeps.AilmentTick) only partly covers in its truncated body.

what: Raises a sighting's Known grade to the newly read grade when that grade is higher, and otherwise keeps the existing Known grade, so Known never goes down.
ev: Each candidate applies the same raise-only rule (`if (rec.Known < grade) rec.Known = grade`), but only as one step inside a larger filing routine that also sets names, places, dates, and counts, so none isolates the plain max-merge of the two grades.

what: After a combat round, it keeps the party's commanded member index pointing at a living party member, moving to the next able member if the current one is dead or the index is out of range (per the SRD's SelectNextAble rule).
ev: It has the same forward scan for the next able member (not dead, not stoned, hits above zero) as the C++ fallback loop, but it always advances instead of keeping an able current member, and it has no empty-party or out-of-range index reset.

what: Determines which monster class a spell's class gate reads, using the group that was aimed at (falling back to a starting group) and returning that group's front monster's class, or -1 if the group index is out of range.
ev: AimedRecord returns the front monster of the order's aimed target, falling back to the first living monster, which is close to gateClassFor's aimed-group-then-start lookup, but it returns the monster object rather than its class, uses a monster index instead of a group index, and returns null instead of -1 when out of range.

what: Decides whether a theft of gold is attempted by checking if the thief's score minus a weighted monster guild level penalty falls below a threshold (rule R36).
ev: No candidate computes the gold-theft attempt check (score minus the weighted guild level compared against a threshold); the closest, CombatEngine.TheftSlot in Mordor.Core/MonsterAttack.cs, picks a pack slot to steal from and is a different decision.

what: Resolves the chest teleporter trap when a chest is opened: if the square is unmapped, all lost flags are set; a multi-member party loses the opener, while a lone opener is moved to the given position, the forced-settle flag is set, and the area is settled.
ev: It matches the lone-opener path (forced settle flag, area settled, lost flags when unmapped), but in a party it moves the opener to the new square and lets the party prune them instead of removing the opener outright, and it sets lost flags on the opener rather than the whole party.

what: Decides what happens to the party leader's saved character record when the party disbands: leave it untouched if the leader is dead, blank it if the party is solo, otherwise write or delete it depending on whether the party reloads when loaded.
where: Mordor.Mod.QoL/QolMod.cs QolMod.TownLeader (no candidate covers the disband record decision; Mordor.App/PartyUnload.cs PartyUnload.Run is the closest, since it decides what happens to the leader's record on unload)
ev: PartyUnload.Run handles the disband-time save, but it only calls SaveParty with remember true or false based on party size and the reload answer, and it never checks whether the leader is dead (R18.5) or whether the party is solo (R18.3), so it does not match resolveDisband's three-way outcome and its None/Blank/Write/Delete branches.

what: Picks the spell level used by an archive effect: a positive item level is used directly, otherwise the active guild's spell level applies.
ev: It returns the item's own spell level when it is above zero and otherwise `Rules.SpellLevel(c.Guild.Level)`, the active guild's level, which matches the C++ branch logic; it takes the `Item` rather than a bare `itemLevel`, a structural difference only.

what: Reads a named option from its config sources and returns true only when the value is "True" (case-insensitive), which is the flag-parsing rule for the game's options.
where: Mordor.Core/GameOptions.cs IniLayers.Flag (rule itself in Ini.Flag, same file)
ev: Both read a named key from the config sources and return true only when the text equals "True" case-insensitively, which matches portFlagTruthy over readOptionText; IniLayers.Flag covers the multi-source case by delegating to the layer that holds the key, while Ini.Flag applies the same rule to a single source, and the empty-versus-"False" default has no effect on the result.

what: Ages a character by the given number of years, floors the result at the minimum adult age (16 years), and tells the player "You cannot get any younger." when the floor is hit.
ev: It subtracts `years * 365` from age, clamps to `16 * 365` when the result falls below it, and returns "You cannot get any younger." at the floor, matching the C++ logic and message; it differs only in returning a string instead of calling `ctx.say`, and in also returning a "You are now ... younger." line otherwise.

what: Runs the Seer's locate-a-saved-character service: it refuses if the target is in the City, requires confirmation and enough gold, charges the fee, rolls for success, and on success reveals the target's map coordinates.
ev: It follows the same order as the C++ (city refusal, confirmation, affordability, payment, then the roll via Seer.LocateCharacter) and reports the target's coordinates on success, though it returns a message rather than a result struct and tests the city by `DungeonLevel <= 0` rather than equality with the city level constant.

what: Resolves a movement or utility spell cast by a living party member, such as Detect Rock on the wall ahead, Feather Essence levitating a target, or an Ethereal Portal or Displacement that can kill the whole party.
ev: StepThrough matches only the Ethereal Portal square step (one square ahead with edge wrap, then a rock test), while the C++ function also covers caster validation, Detect Rock, Feather Essence, Displacement, and the party-kill routine, and no candidate does those.

what: Implements the chest trap 6 (Fate) from the Mordor rules, rerolling the opener's current hit points and then current spell points to random values between 1 and their maximums.
ev: Spring is the chest-trap dispatcher, so trap 6 would most likely sit in its truncated switch, but the visible text stops after trap 4, and the Fate spell reroll in SpellThrown.Apply (and SpellEffect.ApplyToCharacter) is a related but different effect.

what: Spends one charge from a charge item (cost-free to the user, so long as charges remain) and reports the spell it casts at its fixed level, leaving the actual spell effect to the caller; if no charges remain, the cast fails.
ev: ItemCharge spends one charge when any remain and fails when none do, as the C++ does, but it does not return the spell id, the spell level, or a cast result, and its failure path also removes the order and prints a run-out message.

what: Computes the companion's melee defence bonus in the Mordor rules, adding +4 for a critical hit and +1 for a backstab.
ev: No candidate adds a critical or backstab term to a defence value; Rules.MonsterDamage adds +2/+1 to the attacker's damage modifier, and Combat.cs 3.DefenseOf computes base AD plus guild and equipment with no crit or backstab term.

what: Rolls a disease cure check, adding the character's effective Constitution bonus and subtracting twice the poison level from a d200 roll, and reports the cure as successful when the total exceeds 195.
ev: The disease branch computes the same roll (`rng.Next(200) + (effectiveCon - 10) * 2 - poisonLevel * 2`, cured above 195), but it is embedded in a combined poison-and-disease step rather than being a standalone check, and it zeroes the poison level when poison was cured earlier in the same tick.

what: Checks whether a monster kind is allowed to spawn under a spawn mask, returning true when that kind's bit (per SRD c13) is set in the mask.
ev: Both test whether bit b is set in a mask with `(mask & (1L << b)) != 0`, but Bit has no `0..kMonsterKindCount-1` range check and works on a long, so out-of-range kinds behave differently (e.g. shift counts wrap in C#).

what: Checks whether a pack slot can hold an item that an uncurse action would target, returning true only for slots 2 through kPackSlots since slot 1 is the hands and never holds an item.
ev: SwapSlots rejects one-based slots at or below 1 (the hands) and above PackSize, which is the same 2..40 bound as slotInRange, but it is an inline guard inside a swap rather than a standalone predicate, and no candidate exposes the bare range check.

what: Computes an approximate experience-point multiplier for a given race from that race's Exp value, using a logarithmic formula that the code notes does not match the reference table for Elf, Osiri and Troll.
ev: No candidate computes the logarithmic XP multiplier from a race's Exp value; the closest, MdrLoader.cs LoadRaces, only reads ExpFactor into the Race record, and the Fn12A1 and ExpForNextLevel candidates compute level XP thresholds, not a per-race multiplier.

what: Runs the identification pass over each non-empty monster group in the front encounter, calling the first and second identification passes on each group's front monster during the R42 step 2a sequence.
ev: This candidate loops over the monster groups and runs a per-group identification by the character, matching the R42 step 2a pass, but its body is truncated and never shows the two-pass (first then second) structure, so it is a related version rather than an exact match.

what: Rolls a percentile die against the best thief's chance to disarm a chest trap; on success the trap is cleared, on failure a "trap goes off" message is shown and the trap stays set for the caller to resolve.
ev: It makes the same 1..100 roll against the best thieving chance, sets the trap-disarmed result on success and the trap-goes-off path on failure, but it also awards chest XP on a disarm, which the C++ stub leaves unknown.

what: Returns true when a melee swing's damage is below 1, which the SRD rules R16 and R22 treat as a miss.
ev: SwingOnce computes the blow's damage and its comment says fn0DEE answers 0 for a miss, but the candidate is truncated before any `damage < 1` check, and no candidate visibly implements the isMissedSwing test.

what: After a fall, if the party is a lone character whose hit points are at or below zero and who is not already dead, the character is put into the dead state (rule R63).
ev: The candidate checks `_party.Size == 1 && _ch.CurHits <= 0 && !_ch.IsDead` and then calls `Kill(_ch, "")`, which is the same lone-character, zero-hits, not-dead condition that sets the dead state in the C++ function, with the same empty cause text.

what: Returns the companion price band for a given found level, clamping the level to the valid range of the price table so out-of-range levels use the first or last band.
ev: No candidate maps a found level to a companion price band with clamping; the closest, Mordor.Core/GuildTitles.cs GuildTitles.Of, does a similar clamped level-to-band lookup but returns guild titles, not prices.

what: Rolls a chest trap's damage as a random value from 1 to k (k=4 for the exploding box, k=6 for the fire ball), returning 0 when k is not positive.
ev: Spring deals the explosion (trap 3) and fire (trap 4) damage, but from a different formula (`dungeonLevel * mult * Math.Log(dungeonLevel + 2)`, with fire reduced by resistance) rather than the C++ helper's uniform `below(k) + 1` roll, and it has no `k <= 0` guard.

what: Stones a companion by marking it dead with the Stone death state, zeroing its hits, emptying its slot in the party, and announcing "Stoned one!" to the player.
ev: Its doc comment lists stoning among the specials a landed hit allows, but the visible code is cut off before that branch, so it's unverified whether it marks the companion Stone, zeroes hits, empties the slot, or announces "Stoned one!"; no other candidate handles stoning.

what: Checks whether a character has at least 10 Wisdom and at least 10 Intelligence, the prerequisite for using stat items in Mordor.
ev: None of the eight candidates checks that Wisdom and Intelligence are both at least 10; the closest, ItemInfoPage.Paint, only displays the item's stat requirements, and the others compute spell points, identify skill, stat modifiers, or item descriptions.

what: Returns the race's experience modifier (RACE_MOD, R21) used in level-up experience calculations, currently passing through the stored integer expFactor unchanged rather than the neutral 1.0 the header comment describes.
ev: LoadRaces reads the race's Exp field as a float into `ExpFactor`, which is the value `raceExpMod` returns, but no candidate returns it as the RACE_MOD modifier, and the C++ truncates it to an integer while the C# keeps the float.

what: Handles the store-side Combine action for a party member by pouring one item's charges into another after validating slot numbers, item kinds, and identification, and returns a player-facing reply message.
where: Mordor.Core/Combining.cs struct.Combine (with cannot.Refusal in the same file covering the pre-checks)
ev: The candidate covers the same combine action (pouring the charges of later slots into the first, emptying the source, rejecting unidentified items and mismatched class/id), though it differs in details: it has no equipped-item guard, no empty-slot messages, and no slot-number validation, and it models a charge-overflow crash that the C++ does not.

what: Handles the town menu's "pool gold" command by moving all other members' on-hand gold into the selected member and writing a player-facing message reporting how much was pooled or where pooling stopped on overflow.
ev: PoolGold pools every other member's on-hand gold into the selected member and stops at an overflow with earlier members still pooled, matching poolGoldToSelected, and returns the amount moved; it does not write the player-facing pooled or stopped-at-overflow message that doPool produces.

what: Returns true when the party's carrying slot holds a dead character, which blocks the companion raise (rule R16.1: a caster carrying a character cannot raise).
ev: None of the candidates returns a refusal check for a raise when the caster is carrying a dead character; the closest, `DungeonWindow.PutDownWhatIsCarried` and `CityWindow.PutDownWhatIsCarried`, only put down a carried character or companion, and `RoomRoster.Lines` only counts carried bodies for display.

what: Makes a percentile drain saving throw by rolling d100 and returning true (resisted) when the roll is at or below the character's drain resistance percentage.
ev: No candidate makes a d100 drain saving throw against drain resistance; the closest, ChestTraps.Spring, applies poison and disease resistance (halved) to trap effects, and AilmentStep handles ailment cure rolls, so neither matches.

what: Adds a damage-modifier bonus of +5 when a blow is a critical hit and +2 when it is a backstab, both stacking if both procs succeed.
ev: CharacterDamage adds the same +5 for a critical and +2 for a backstab, both stacking, but only as one step inside a full damage calculation, whereas the C++ function returns just that bonus.

what: Dispatches the player's typed `give gold ...` or `give item ...` command to the session's command handler and returns whether a reply message was produced.
ev: Both return a bool for whether the give produced output, and both run the gold-then-item give, but the C++ dispatches an already-typed `give gold/item ...` command from `words`, while GiveFlow.Run instead prompts interactively for recipient, gold, and item, and no candidate parses the typed words.

what: Reports whether a spell of the given level is reachable by any guild, by checking it against the highest spell ceiling across all guilds.
ev: It answers "is this spell reachable by any guild the character has joined" per spell, but it tests each joined guild's rate and the full level gate rather than the C++ single check of the spell level against the highest ceiling across all guilds, and no candidate computes that max-ceiling value.

what: At room entry, when a hostile group has engaged, each party member with no combat order is given their own order as their Combat Setting, per R29.
where: Mordor.Core/Party.cs moves.ApplyDefaultOrders (with the per-member call to Mordor.Core/CombatOrder.cs CombatOrder.ApplyDefault)
ev: The C++ takes each member whose order is None and sets it from their combat setting, gated on a hostile engagement; ApplyDefaultOrders does the same for every member with Kind None (its caller supplies the engagement gate, and it keeps the aimed target), and it calls ApplyDefault, which resolves the character's CombatSetting into Fight, Defend, or a spell order.

what: Charges a town cost to a party member, taking gold from hand first and then the bank, and refuses the payment if the purse is short and no shortfall cover applies.
ev: CharPay runs the optional shortfall cover, then `Character.Pay`, which takes gold on hand first, then the bank, and returns false with nothing taken when the purse is short, matching townCharge's charge and refusal; it does not return the fromHand/fromBank split or emit the "Not enough gold!" message, which the caller handles.

what: Computes one random base-damage roll for a monster's breath attack from the monster's modifier value, using the R39 breath formula (a random die-style roll scaled by the modifier, then reduced by 0.7 and halved).
ev: Kind.Raw uses the same breath structure (floor of (rnd·range+1)/2, plus range/4, times 0.7, then truncated), but it omits the final divide-by-2 from the C++ formula, and it takes guild levels and computes the range itself rather than taking the modifier directly, so the outputs differ unless Range() supplies that halving.

what: Computes the store realignment fee for a Mordor item: 0.75 × price, doubled (kRealignCrossFactor) when the item's alignment jumps more than one step (e.g. Good to Evil), rounded half-to-even.
ev: It has the same distance-based double-or-single factor and round-half-even, but it uses a 0.72 base rate where the C++ uses 0.75 (the C++ notes 0.75 matches the reference assertion of 40000 → 30000), so outputs differ for the same inputs.

what: Returns true unless the character is held (paralyzed or otherwise immobilized), so a held character takes no action on its own turn while companions still act.
ev: CharacterActs yields nothing when `ParalyzedRounds(c) > 0`, so a paralysed character takes no action while its companions still fight, which matches the C++ rule that a held character does nothing on its own turn; the candidate tests paralysis specifically, while the C++ `isHeld` predicate may also cover other immobilisation.

what: Shows the player a "mod.json could not be parsed" message and returns false to signal that the mod's manifest failed to load.
ev: Discover reports a manifest parse failure with a near-identical "mod.json could not be read" message, but it records the problem and keeps the mod in the list rather than showing one message and returning false as the C++ function does.

what: Computes an archived weapon resistance threshold from an item's level as itemLevel × 2 + 1, a formula the source marks as unverified and in conflict with R13.
ev: The C++ function returns itemLevel × 2 + 1 as a weapon resistance threshold, and no candidate computes a resistance threshold from an item level; the closest, Rules.SpecialHitChance, is a critical or backstab chance with a different formula.

what: When a companion's carry index is 4 or more (marking a carried body), it clears that index to kCarryNone so the body is put down when the game loads.
ev: The candidate also puts down a carried companion and resets the carry index to -1, but it runs on a pickup or drop action rather than on load, and it has no index-4-or-more test, so it is related rather than the same.

what: Decides whether a fatal mishap gets its own announcement, returning false when the mishap is fatal since the death message already covers it.
ev: Its doc comment says a fatal companion breath leaves before the "and his companions" line is written, so only the death announces it, which matches the C++ rule for breath mishaps; but it is embedded in a larger breath routine rather than a standalone predicate, and the code is truncated, so I could only confirm the rule from the comment.

what: Computes the chance that a character survives a destruction save, starting from a base of 45, lowered by the monster's floor value, raised by four times the character's DEX, lowered by twice the monster's DEX, and clamped between 25 and 90.
ev: No candidate computes a destruction save chance; the closest, CombatEngine.AttackChance, uses a different formula (50 + (monDex - charDex) * 5) for a free attack when the party moves, and nothing uses the 45 - floor + 4*DEX - 2*monDEX clamp to 25..90.

what: Decides whether record 0 of a given MDATA table is kept when loading the game's table data, skipping only MDATA5's record 0 because it duplicates Outcast Goblin.
ev: No candidate decides at load time whether MDATA record 0 is kept or skipped; the closest, Spells.cs `it.Known`, only filters spells by id and mentions MDATA3/MDATA5 record-0 templates in a comment, and it does not handle MDATA5 record 0 specifically.

what: Decides whether a kill spell succeeds in Mordor by comparing the rolled damage against the monster's hit points, so the spell kills only if the damage is at least the monster's HP.
ev: Its `spell.Effect == 100` branch applies the same test as `killSpellSucceeds` (damage zeroed unless `hits - dmg <= 0`, i.e. damage >= HP), but it is embedded in a monster-casting routine and returns a damage value rather than a bool.

what: Handles the player's town-menu level-up command for a chosen party member by refusing with an explanatory message when the character is dead, not a guild member, or lacks the experience or gold, and otherwise carrying out the guild level-up and reporting the new level.
ev: The candidate covers the core of doLevelUp (the max-level and canLevelUp refusals, the gold check, the level-up, and the report) but omits the dead and not-a-member checks and uses different refusal messages and a quest step, so it is a closely related version rather than an exact match.

what: Computes the item level range for an item drop, using half the drop level (floored, with a minimum of 1) as the minimum, then adjusting for chest or container sources, or returning the fixed Asmodeus chest range.
ev: RollDrop computes the same half-of-drop-level band with a minimum of 1 and a chest-class shift, but it uses round-half-to-even where the C++ uses floor, has no Container source (-1 to both bounds), maps its chest classes differently, and also picks an item rather than returning a level range.

what: Reads a mod flag setting: if the key was absent it returns the fallback, otherwise it returns true only when the trimmed stored text is "True" in any letter case.
ev: It returns the fallback when the stored value is null and otherwise returns true only when the trimmed value equals "True" under OrdinalIgnoreCase, which matches the C++ logic; it differs only in that it reads the value itself from modId and key rather than taking `present` and `text` as inputs.

what: Exposes a global-scope test entry point that forwards a roster-unload request for a party member (by index) to the game's rosterUnloadMember routine, passing back a reply string.
ev: No candidate removes or unloads a party member by index or returns a reply string; the closest, `LookAround.Roster`, only assembles the saved-character list, and `Roster.PathFor` and `RosterPath` only build file paths.

what: Projects a character's experience points forward to a desired level by scaling current XP by the square of the level ratio (returning 0 when the current level is invalid).
ev: No candidate scales a current XP value by the square of a desired-to-current level ratio with a zero guard; the closest, Character.ExpForNextLevel and ExpForThisLevel, return the XP thresholds that Fn12A1 computes for a level, not a projection from the character's current XP.

what: Switches the commanded party member to the chosen index, resetting the Spell Type box, and reports whether the town shops and buildings should refresh (leader alive and not in the dungeon, per R6).
ev: SwitchedTo does the town-refresh part (Store, Confinement, Morgue, Guild, Bank updated only when the leader is alive and at DungeonLevel <= 0, with the Spell Type box cleared), but it does not do the C++ function's index bounds check, the no-op on re-selecting the same character, or the Seer exclusion as a returned result, and it takes no targetIndex argument.

what: Buys an item from a store for a player: if the pack has a free slot and the buyer can pay the price from their gold, the item is added to the pack fully identified, otherwise the player gets a "pack is full" or "not enough gold" message.
ev: No candidate charges gold, checks for a free pack slot, and places a fully identified copy of the item into the pack; StoreStock.DepletedByBuying only covers the shelf-depletion condition that the C++ function leaves to its caller, and Confinement.PriceToBuy only computes the price that buyFromStore receives as an argument.

what: Returns the item-use multiplier for a guild, giving Nomads and Healers their own factors and 1.0 for every other guild.
ev: UseLevel reads the per-guild `g.ItemUseFactor` and turns it into a level threshold, but nothing in the candidates returns the multiplier by guild index as guildUseFactor does, with 1.0 as the fallback for other guilds.

what: Returns true when the build is the Limited version and the level is at or past the Limited build's dead-end level cap, meaning the floor is the game's final level for that build.
where: Mordor.Core/LimitedVersion.cs LimitedVersion.ChuteIsDeadUnderfoot (also ChuteIsDeadToTake and LimitedVersion.Clamp are closely related)
ev: The C++ function returns true when the build is Limited and the level is at or past the cap, while the candidates test the Limited build at the exact last level (`level == LastLevel`) or clamp levels beyond it, so they cover the same dead-end concept but with different comparison details and no single method matches the C++ signature and `>=` check.

what: Maps a facing direction to the dungeon cell holding the facing arrow by adding a fixed offset (kFacingArrowOffset), though its comment flags an unresolved clash where facing 1 lands on cell 23, the same cell as the RESCUE floor bit.
ev: No candidate maps a facing to a cell index by adding an offset; the closest, AutomapPics.Copy, only blits the arrow at a given position without taking a facing, and DungeonNav.Delta returns a direction vector rather than a cell.

what: Returns a +0.75 damage modifier while the character is counting a chest (per c65), and zero otherwise.
ev: The C++ function only returns the +0.75 chest-count bonus, while MonsterDamage applies the same `if (openingChest) damMod += 0.75;` as one step among several in a larger damage calculation (criticals, backstabs, size difference), and no candidate isolates the bonus on its own.

what: When the mod settings store changes a setting, it raises one "setting changed" event and then forwards that event to each loaded mod whose id matches the changed mod's id.
ev: No candidate raises a settings-changed event or loops over loaded mods to forward it by matching id; the closest, ModsWindow.ToggleBox, only subscribes to `Changed` and redraws its own check box when both mod id and key match, which is the receiving side rather than this raise-and-forward function.

what: Newbie protection: a character is protected in the early areas only if it is level 1 and the area id is below the newbie area limit (area 0 is assumed protected because the SRD does not say otherwise).
ev: None of the eight candidates implements level-1 newbie protection (a level check combined with an area-id threshold); they are all about area-id lookup, M59BB storage, or death-in-rock handling.

what: Finds and returns the stored floor whose dungeon level matches the party's current dungeon level, or nullptr if no such floor exists.
ev: `FloorFor(int level)` returns the first floor in `_floors` whose `LevelNum` equals the requested level, or null if none matches, which is the same lookup as `viewFloor` using the party's current level.

what: Returns true only when the character is in the dungeon and their age percentage of race lifespan exceeds the start threshold (98%), which is when the random old-age death check begins.
ev: It applies the same 98%-of-race-lifespan threshold, but it also rolls the death chance and takes no in-dungeon parameter, so the dungeon gating is left to the caller (the ailment tick in DungeonWindow).

what: Decides whether a saved option flag counts as set, returning true only when its text reads "True" in any letter case, which is the game rule for the port's flag format.
ev: Ini.Flag returns true only when the text it reads (defaulting to "False") equals "True" case-insensitively, which is the same rule as portFlagTruthy, with the difference that it looks up the text by section and key first.

what: Registers the "give" command for the Town and Dungeon screens, so a player can type "give gold" or "give item" to hand gold or a pack item to another party member.
where: Mordor.App/GiveFlow.cs GiveFlow.Run (invoked from Mordor.App/DungeonWindow.axaml.cs would.AskToGive and Mordor.App/CityWindow.axaml.cs is.AskToGive)
ev: The candidates implement the give command's behavior on both the Town and Dungeon screens, but through an interactive name/gold/item prompt flow rather than the C++ registration of typed "give gold/item <from> <to>" syntax, and no candidate performs that registration.

what: Decides where a sighting is recorded in the game: a lost reading gives Unknown, a City reading (leadLevel 0) gives the City, and otherwise the party's current square is used.
ev: FileSighting writes "?" for a lost reading and "the City" for a City reading, otherwise the live coordinates from PlaceOf, but this logic is embedded in a larger function and keys the City case on a missing place rather than on leadLevel 0 alone.

what: Computes a character's attack and defense values for the panel display by adding base AD, stat and stored shifts, the best guild bonus, and the equipped weapon and armor values, flooring each at zero.
ev: It computes both attack and defence as Math.Max(0, BaseAD + StatsADNow + StoredADShift + best guild AD + equipped Att or Def), matching panelAD's inputs and flooring at zero, though it uses the Rules.BaseAD constant where the C++ calls baseAD(local, c).

what: Returns true when the party leader (member 0) has fewer than 1 current Hits, meaning a chest trap has killed them.
ev: That method contains the same test, `_party.Members[0].CurHits < 1`, after the party prune, but it is inlined in a larger chest-opening routine that also handles the death and exits, rather than being a standalone predicate that returns the boolean.

what: Rolls a random theft slot by drawing from 2 to 40 (one draw of 39 values offset by 2) to pick which item slot a thief takes from.
ev: The candidate computes `Floor(rng.NextDouble() * 39) + 2`, which draws 39 values offset by 2 to give 2..40 exactly as the C++ `rng.below(kTheftDraw) + 2` does.

what: Decides whether a monster of a given floor is eligible for a quest, where the quest tier is capped at kQuestTierMax (10) and the monster qualifies if its floor is no deeper than that capped tier.
ev: The C++ function is a pure predicate (`floor <= min(tier, 10)`), while QuestMonster draws a monster from the class table and its doc says the run ends before the first monster deeper than the tier, so it uses the same floor-versus-tier rule inside a selection loop, and QuestTier only clamps the tier to 1..10 without any monster comparison.

what: Picks which monster class to use from a set of weights, using a roll against the weight total, and deliberately counts the first class's weight twice so the odds come out as the engine and tests expect.
ev: It makes a weighted cumulative pick over a list (by `Chance`), but it has no double-counted first weight, its kind is drawn uniformly through `RoundedIndex`, and it returns a monster rather than an index.

what: Clamps a character's stat value for a potion effect so it cannot exceed the race maximum plus a fixed allowance (kStatCeilingAboveRace) and cannot drop below the race minimum.
ev: The candidate clamps each stat to `race.Max[i] + 5` on the upper bound and to `race.Min[i]` on the lower bound, the same two limits as `clampStatForPotion`, but it does this inline inside a larger function rather than as a standalone helper, and the ceiling is only checked when a modifier is nonzero.

what: Computes a character's paralysis part as the sum of their current Str/Int/Wis/Dex-based stat value and a stored shift, where a full part of 32 counts as the paralysis threshold.
ev: The candidate computes the same sum `c.StatsADNow(_item) + c.StoredADShift(_item)` but only as an intermediate inside a larger attack/defence calculation that also adds base, guild and gear terms, while no candidate is a standalone method returning that sum.

what: Reports whether a guild definition is the Nomad guild, going by its data name "Nomad".
ev: No candidate is a standalone check that a guild's name equals "Nomad", but GuildADSingle computes `isNomad` inline as `GuildData.All[0].Name == guild`, which tests the same thing by list position rather than by name and only as a step inside a larger calculation.

what: Clamps a raw chance-to-leave value for a companion into the 0 to 90 range that the game's rules allow, so the leave chance can never go negative or exceed 90.
ev: The method ends with `Math.Clamp(x, 0, 90)`, the same 0-to-90 clamp as the C++ function, but it is embedded in a full leave-chance calculation rather than being a standalone clamp of a raw input.

what: Returns true only when the slot being visited is the last slot visited, so the mishap suffix from R32.6 applies only to that final slot, since the suffix resets on each pass.
ev: The candidate's loop sets `round.Suffix = ""` on each pass and its doc comment says the line depends only on the last slot visited, which is the R32.6 rule, but it is inlined in a larger routine rather than being a standalone slot-equality check like `mishapSuffixApplies`.

what: Builds the library page text for an item entry, listing its abilities if the entry is fully known and otherwise showing a "Not everything is known." notice.
ev: The C++ `itemPage` shows only a name plus abilities (or "Not everything is known." below full knowledge), while `DescribeItem` gives a fuller item page (type, A/D, damage modifier, curse, spell, abilities and resistances) and gates only some of those details on full knowledge, so it covers the same item-page-by-knowledge-grade behavior with different content and wording.

what: Computes the cost value from a published product by truncating (product minus 0.0001) to an integer, a rounding convention the game's casting-cost formula uses.
ev: No candidate subtracts 0.0001 and truncates a product, but Fn1485Price computes the same published spell-cost value and its doc comment explicitly contrasts its exact floor with the page's "- 0.0001" rule, so it is a closely related version with different details.

what: Rolls the first-pass chance to recognise an unidentified foe, using the character's identify skill from guild level, Int and Wis, and marks the foe as identified on success unless it is unseen.
ev: The C++ first pass gates on identified/unseen, rolls against `recogniseChance(skill, dark)`, and sets `identified`; IdentifyMonsters computes the same identify skill, the dark flag and the invisible/unseen gate, but its visible excerpt is truncated before any roll or identified flag, and the matching chance formula is only in Rules.RecogniseChance (Mordor.Core/Rules.cs), which does not roll or set the flag.

what: Decides whether a companion is released from fear, returning true when the companion is occupied, has Hits above zero, and is not ForLife; the owner is ignored.
ev: The C++ `fearReleases` tests whether an occupied companion with Hits above zero and not ForLife is released from fear, and no candidate does that; the closest, `Companion` binding in `SpellEffect.BindCompanion`, sets bind levels rather than testing fear release, and the others cover breath, spit, spells and strikes.

what: Computes the initial spell cost for an archive spell from the caster's spell-point ratio and base modifier, using the R31 formula floor(SpellPointRatio × BaseMod × 1.9 − 0.0001).
ev: The C++ function is only the R31 initial-cost formula floor(SpellPointRatio × BaseMod × 1.9 − 0.0001), and Spellbook.Cost computes the same kind of spell-point cost via Rules.Fn1485Price with a 1.9 factor and the same −0.0001 epsilon, but it takes a spell and character and goes through guild tables and level clamping rather than taking the ratio and base modifier directly.

what: Writes the named option flags into an INI document under their config keys, as "True" or "False" text, with the no-toolbar flag using a case-variant key as a kept quirk.
ev: Save writes the same named flags as True/False under the same section, but it also writes the volumes, brightness and fonts, which the C++ function does not, and it always uses the "NoToolbar" key rather than the case-variant quirk.

what: Rolls a random number against the chest's class-based trap chance percentage to decide whether the chest is trapped.
ev: Candidate 2 makes the same class-based percentage roll that decides whether a chest is trapped, but it also gates on the monster's TrapFlags, picks the trap type, and uses a different RNG form (`Next(100)+1 >= chance` rather than `NextDouble()*100 < pct`).

what: Reports whether the square at a given location on the current floor has its rock flag recorded, returning false for out-of-range coordinates, which Passwall and Teleport/Displace casting use to decide whether a destination is solid stone.
ev: It tests the rock flag on the current floor for in-bounds squares just as rockAt does, but it returns true for out-of-bounds coordinates where rockAt returns false.

what: Returns the death cry sound string ("DI-UNDEA") or the attack cry sound string ("DRAGON") depending on the flag, which are game-flavor sound names for companions.
ev: DeathSound maps a monster's kind to a death sound and returns "DI-UNDEA" only for undead, but it takes a Monster rather than a companion death/attack flag and never returns "DRAGON", so it covers only part of the C++ function.

what: Looks up a crest's spell grant in the R10 table, returning the row for that crest, or a row with no spell and zero if the crest (such as Journeyman, Warrior, or Ninja) has no entry.
ev: No candidate looks up a crest's spell grant in an R10-style table; the closest, Guildmasters.cs `changes.CrestFor`, only finds the crest item in MDATA3 by guild index and never returns or checks a spell.

what: Returns the current guild-log day counter from the session's feature state, or 0 if the value is missing or not a valid integer.
ev: Both return the guild-log day counter, but Entry.Today computes it from the system clock (DaySerial(DateTime.Today)) and never reads session feature state or falls back to 0 as glToday does.

what: Handles a party stepping onto a teleporter square under the Mordor rules (R74–R80): it works out the destination level, reports if it would pass the last level, rolls the destinations for each party member, marks unmapped destinations as lost, splits the party across those destinations, and finishes the leader's teleport.
where: Mordor.App/DungeonWindow.axaml.cs DungeonWindow.TeleporterSquare (with Mordor.Core/Teleporting.cs Teleporting.ForSquare for the per-member destination roll)
ev: The candidate rolls each member's destination, marks unmapped ones as lost, and splits the party by the leader's square, which matches most of the C++ flow, but it has no past-last-level early return (R82) and its text is truncated before the leader-teleport finish (R80).

what: Reads a pending person offer value from the session's feature-state map by key, returning an empty string if the key is absent.
ev: Both read a value by key from a store with a fallback, but ModSettings.Get returns a bool toggle with its declared default, while seerGet returns a string from the session's featureState map with an empty string when the key is absent, and no candidate handles a pending person offer.

what: Counts the bank vault slots in the player's inventory that hold an item (id > 0) and returns how many remain free.
where: Mordor.Core/Character.cs Character.DepositToVault (shown in the candidate as lands.DepositToVault)
ev: No candidate counts the free vault slots, but DepositToVault tests for a free vault slot (a hole or room to append) and returns a bool rather than the number of free slots.

what: Reports whether an item type is removed from the pack when its last charge is spent, per the original game's sub1149 rule: types 23–28, 30 and 31 are consumed when empty.
ev: The method returns `(it.Type >= 23 && it.Type <= 28) || it.Type == 30 || it.Type == 31`, the same type test as the C++ `duseConsumedWhenEmpty` and both cite sub1149 (MAINMOD2.BAS:5684-5711), differing only in taking an `Item` instead of a raw `i32` type.

what: When the party steps onto mapped ground, it calls foundYourself to end the lost state, so the player is no longer lost.
ev: It clears the lost flags (via FoundYourself) for standing on mapped ground, but it does not check whether the square is mapped; that check lives in the caller, Mordor.App/DungeonWindow.axaml.cs WorkOutWhereYouAre, which also adds lost-state rolls the C++ function does not have.

what: Moves a character who fell down a chute to the landing floor, keeping their X and Y position and setting their area to the one at that spot on the lower floor.
ev: Like `moveFallenMember`, it sets the level to the landing floor, leaves X and Y unchanged, and sets Area to `landed.AreaIdAt(x, y)`, the area at that square on the lower floor.

what: Blocks casting spells from the character window while the party is in town, per the SRD rule that spellcasting is refused there.
ev: No candidate handles spellcasting or refuses casting from the character window in town; the candidates cover town-arrival deposits, dungeon entry, the exit-to-town key, and window hosting, which are related to town but not to the casting block.

what: Caps a character's maximum hit points at 999, the game's hit-point ceiling, by returning the smaller of the given value and kHitsCap.
ev: LevelUp contains the same 999 ceiling (`if (MaxHits > 999) MaxHits = 999;`) but only as one step inside a larger level-gain routine, and no candidate is a standalone clamp that returns `min(maxHits, 999)`.

what: Computes the store fee for realigning an item in the game's R26 store by multiplying the price by 0.72 and rounding half-to-even.
ev: RealignCost computes the same 0.72 × price, rounded half-to-even, but it doubles the fee for a cross-spectrum move (Good to Evil), whereas realignStoreFee takes only the price and applies no alignment multiplier.

what: Scales a chest's gold by a 3/2 multiplier when the chest is magically locked, leaving the base amount unchanged otherwise, with the class argument ignored.
ev: EncounterGold also multiplies gold by 1.5 when the chest is locked, but it does so inside a larger encounter calculation that adds group gold, scales by monster count, and applies a chest-class multiplier, whereas the C++ function only applies the 3/2 lock multiplier to a given base amount and ignores class.

what: Checks whether a character's six stats, including any modifiers, each meet or exceed the required minimum for a spell or class, refusing if any falls short.
ev: EquipProblem runs the same six-stat loop that refuses when a stat is below its requirement, but it compares the base `Stats[i]` rather than `StatWithMods` (candidate 7 has the modded value but no check), and it is tied to item requirements rather than a generic required array.

what: Credits the caster with one kill when a charmed creature is taken, per game rule R49 (a charmed creature counts as a kill with no hits), by incrementing the caster's kill count.
ev: Candidate 3 does the same `killer.Kills++` increment, but it fires on a killing blow or spell rather than on a charm, and no candidate credits a kill when a creature is charmed (Credit with removes=false explicitly gives no kill, and CompanionKill says the game counts nothing for a companion's kill).

what: Writes the town's income, store stock and row counts, and each guildmaster's holder, level and name to the save file, or reads them back when loading.
ev: No candidate serializes town income, the guildmasters' holder/level/name, or the store row counts as a save-file block; the closest overlaps are Rescue.TurnOverTown and Import/OriginalSaves ReadStore, which load or save store stock for replenishment or import from original files, not the town record.

what: Decides whether a dead character's body is refused by the morgue, returning a refusal reason when the body is turned to rock or its active level is below or above the morgue's allowed range, and no refusal otherwise.
ev: The C++ refuses a rock body at the morgue, but its level-too-low and level-too-high checks have no counterpart in any candidate; RaiseRefusal only covers the rock refusal (effect -1, "The morgue cannot help characters pulled from Rock") and is a raise-spell check rather than a morgue range check.

what: Computes the archive minimum for a spell's damage or healing, combining a base value, a logarithmic term scaled by spell level, and a power-dependent term, then averaging the three (per the R10 and R13 formulas in the Mordor spell rules).
ev: SpellHeal builds the same three-term sum (base + base·log10(SL) + Int(SL/10·(Power−1))) but then subtracts a random roll instead of returning the halved average (g + term1 + term2)/2, and no candidate computes the archive minimum itself.

what: Rolls the old-age death check for a character past 98% of the age threshold, where the chance of dying rises with the excess percentage via a logarithmic formula (5 + Ln(pct − 98) out of 100), skipping the roll when the excess is zero.
ev: Both return false below 98%, otherwise die when `Int(Rnd*100) < 5 + Ln(pct-98)`, and both avoid the Ln(0) error at exactly 98%; the C# version still draws a random number there (the log is clamped, so the threshold is negative and no death occurs) and computes pct from age and lifespan rather than taking it as input.

what: Reports whether an item's type code is 0, which the game treats as the Hands slot type.
ev: No candidate tests whether an item type equals 0; ItemUse.MustBeEquippedToUse only documents that type 0 (Hands) is left out of its list, and the other candidates treat Hands differently (Combining, Combat) or not at all.

what: Given the signed right and forward offsets from a Soul Search origin, it returns which of the eight compass directions (relative to the searcher's facing) the target lies in, with zero offsets treated as the cardinal axes.
ev: No candidate maps signed right/forward offsets to one of eight compass directions; SpellEffect.RelativeDirection (Candidate 1) produces those offsets from coordinates and facing, which is the upstream input to this function rather than the same classification.

what: Builds the gear-screen summary line showing a character's combat attack/defence and total attack and defence, derived from the character and inventory in game terms.
ev: It computes the total attack and defence from base AD, stats, guild and equipped gear, matching two of the C++ outputs, but it does not produce the combat A/D figure or the formatted gear-screen line.

what: Fires the party-wide update when any member is dead (R14), which removes the dead from the party by calling the prune routine.
ev: Candidate 6 removes the dead from the party as the C++ prune step does, but it has no explicit any-dead gate and no bool return, and it adds captions, speech and redraws that the C++ function does not show.

what: Checks whether a character's purse holds at least the Seer's fee, which decides if the "Not enough gold!" refusal applies under rule R64.
ev: With no mod active it runs the same purse-covers-cost test as seerCanAfford and is the check LocatePerson uses for "Not enough gold!", but it also returns true when a mod's shortfall cover applies, so its outcome differs when a mod is active.

what: Computes how well an item's alignment fits the character's alignment, returning Same, Adjacent, or Opposed (Good, Neutral, Evil on a line, so one step apart is Adjacent and two steps is Opposed), which ApplySpecial uses to decide whether the item's effect applies.
ev: FitFor returns Fine for unaligned or matching alignments, Opposed only for Good against Evil (the two-step pair on the Good-Neutral-Evil line), and Adjacent for all other mismatches, which is the same mapping as duseFitOfItem's d==0, d==2, and d==1 cases.

what: Computes a character's combat attack-side adjustment for the 1995 Mordor rules (R16) as the sum of base AD, stat-derived AD, stored shift, best guild award, and fitted worn-item AD, floored at zero.
where: Mordor.Core/Combat.cs AttackOf (the method is named `AttackOf` in the candidate, with `3.` as a prefix in the listing)
ev: It has the same clamped `max(0, BaseAD + stat part + best guild att + equipped Att)` structure, but it sums all equipped items with no alignment fitting, whereas the C++ uses `fittedWornSum(..., c.alignment)`, so the item term can differ.

what: Applies a stat-boosting item to a character: if the alignment check passes, it raises the chosen stat by the item's amount (clamped to the stat's maximum), or in reversed mode lowers a positive stat modifier by that amount, never below zero.
where: Mordor.Core/ItemUse.cs ItemUse.ApplyStatMods (alignment gate is in ItemUse.ApplySpecial)
ev: Both apply a stat item's modifier with a raise-and-clamp path and a reversed path that subtracts positive values, but the C++ version targets one stat index and amount, clamps to statMax, and lowers statMods without a Hall check, while the candidate loops over all six StatsMod entries, clamps to race max + 5, subtracts from the base Stats, and runs the Hall check on raises.

what: Decides whether a guild at a given level can learn a spell of a given level, by comparing the spell's rate-scaled level against half the guild level (rounded up), and returns false for non-positive levels or rates.
ev: Its inline `levelOk` check uses the same per-guild predicate (rate > 0, Level > 0, round-half-even of Level × rate against floor(Level/2 + 0.5)), but it is only one part of a larger refusal method, while CanCast (GuildData.cs) differs by substituting rate 1 for rate ≤ 0 and comparing the unrounded half-level.

what: Returns true if any guild in the list has a positive rate and its rated spell level, after the rate is applied, is within the spell-level cap, meaning a spell of that level is castable by at least one guild.
ev: CanCast applies the same per-guild rate and rated-level test, but it compares against the caster's guild level instead of the fixed `kSpellLevelCap`, and it checks one guild rather than looping over a list.

what: Scales a chest's gold by the locked-chest factor of 1.5, converting from base currency units and back.
ev: EncounterGold applies the same 1.5 multiplier when the chest is locked, but only as one step inside a larger encounter-wide gold calculation that also sums monster groups, halves by monster count, and applies the chest class, so it does not perform the standalone gold-to-double-to-Currency scaling that scaleGoldForLock does.

what: When the whole party is wiped out, it marks the casualties as dead (leaving stoned members stoned), logs the wipe as "dead in rock" or "dead in the dungeon," counts each newly dead character's death once, prunes the bodies if more than one remains, and flags the dead screen when a single body is left.
ev: It counts and logs each newly dead character once and then prunes when more than one remains (C++ steps 4-5), but it does not mark casualties dead, log the "dead in rock"/"dead in the dungeon" wipe message, or flag the dead screen for a lone body (steps 1-3 and 6).

what: Sets the party's gold leader to whichever member has the most gold in their purse, with ties going to the lowest-indexed member, and does nothing for an empty party.
ev: No candidate picks the member with the largest purse as a gold leader; the closest, PerceiveAhead.Best, is a similar argmax loop but over best perception chance, and nothing in the set sets a gold-leader index.

what: Applies a player's use of an item from a party member's pack in Mordor: checks whether the item can be used, spends one charge (removing the item if it runs out), then casts its spell and applies its special effect such as spell points, aging, or stat modifiers.
where: Mordor.Core/ItemUse.cs ItemUse.Problem (with the Mordor.App/DungeonWindow.axaml.cs box.UseSelectedItem and Mordor.Core/ItemUse.cs ItemUse.ApplySpecial as the rest of the flow)
ev: The C++ duseUse does the whole use sequence (parse, incapacitation check, item lookup, ItemUse.Problem checks, charge spend, spell cast, then ApplySpecial), and the candidates split that same sequence across ItemUse.Problem, box.UseSelectedItem, and ItemUse.ApplySpecial, which together cover the same behavior, though no single candidate matches the whole function.

what: Returns the experience multiplier for a kill, giving companion-struck kills a reduced factor (kCompanionXpFactor, 0.25) and character-struck kills the full 1.0.
ev: It applies the same companion factor (`byCompanion ? 0.25 : 1.0`) as part of a larger XP formula, but it returns the full experience award rather than the bare factor that `xpStrikerFactor` returns.

what: Unpacks a 7-bit flag integer into the item's boolean properties (guild-issued, aligned, chest teleporter, destructible, equipped, lost, slot-cursed) during save loading.
ev: No candidate unpacks a bitmask integer into item flags; the closest, Character.ApplyEquipCurse, only sets SlotCursed from an item's cursed value and alignment, and the rest handle gives, swaps, equips, and traps.

what: Builds the list of the two alignments a companion does not currently have (Good, Neutral, Evil minus the companion's own), which is the set of options offered when realigning that companion under game rule R72.
