ev: No candidate builds the list of the two alignments other than the companion's own; the closest, CompanionInfo.AlignmentOf, only maps a companion's alignment to an int, and the rest handle turning, refs, saves, and attacks.

what: When a character equips or unequips an item, its stat modifiers are added to or removed from the character's ability stat modifiers, and a message is shown.
ev: No candidate adds or removes an equipped item's stat mods on equip or unequip and announces it; StatWithMods only computes the equipped total on read, and ItemUse.ApplyStatMods changes permanent stats for potions rather than gear.

what: When the owner is paralysed, living companions still get to act, so the function emits a "Companions act" event naming the owner and the number of living companions (or does nothing if there are none).
ev: No candidate emits a "Companions act" event gated on the owner being paralysed and the living-companion count; Candidate 4 (CompanionTurn) has companions acting in combat but does not do this dispatch, and Candidate 3 (CompanionsCleared) only un-paralyses the owner.

what: Decodes one line of a mod data file into a grid of rows and cells, using backslash escapes plus `|` as the cell separator and `;` as the row separator, so the mod's table values can be read in.
ev: It walks the line character by character with the same rules (backslash escapes the next character, `|` ends a cell, `;` ends a row, empty input gives no rows, and the final cell and row are always flushed), so the only difference is that a trailing lone backslash is appended as-is rather than kept as a literal backslash, which is the same outcome since the C++ keeps it as a literal backslash too.

what: Decides whether a new dungeon action run can start: it refuses (and logs a message to the player) if a run is already active, otherwise it starts a run only when some live, enabled mod hook exists, and reports "no hooks" so the task completes immediately.
ev: RunActions does the same no-hooks-completes-at-once and already-running-refuses checks, but it tests for hooks before the running guard (so an idle no-hook request is silently completed, not logged as refused), it logs to the host rather than showing the player a message, and it returns a Task rather than the RunHooks/NoHooks/Refused status.

what: Computes the spell-point cost of archiving a spell, using the spell's starting level, the caster's point ratio and base modifier, and the spell level divisor, with a divide-by-zero guard returning 0.
ev: It computes the same floor(StartLevel·BaseMod·rate·1.9/SL) with the same inputs, but it subtracts one when the exact result is a whole number, which archiveSpellCost does not, and it maps sl=0 to 1 where archiveSpellCost returns 0.

what: Decodes text produced by modEncodeRows back into a grid of rows and cells, where backslash escapes the next character, "|" separates cells, ";" ends a row, and an unterminated final row is kept.
ev: The candidate matches the C++ step for step: an empty line gives no rows, a backslash escapes the next character (a trailing lone backslash is kept literal), "|" ends a cell, ";" ends a cell and a row, and the end of the line always closes a final cell and row.

what: Handles the typed swap command by exchanging the contents of two pack slots (2 to 40, with the hands slot 1 excluded) for a party member, including empty slots, and returns a reply message for the player.
ev: It rejects slot 1 and anything past forty, then exchanges the two pack entries including empty ones, which matches the C++ swapApply. The C++ also checks for a missing member, which the candidate does not, and the candidate adds an optional buffer remap that the C++ does not perform (the app callers pass buffersFollow: false to match the C++).

what: Rolls a breath attack against a monster's breath chance, computed from the breather's top stat and monster level, returning whether the breath succeeds.
ev: The breath block computes the same 50/80/20 chance from the character's top guild level against the monster's level and then rolls against it, but it is embedded in the full group-attack routine and does not return a standalone breath-success bool, so it is only part of `rollBreath`.

what: Registers the town-screen player commands "pens" (lists the creatures in the Confinement pens with their buy prices) and "pen" (buys or sells a companion from those pens).
ev: The C++ function registers the text commands "pens" and "pen" on the town screen, and no candidate registers commands; ShowConfinement is the closest match because it opens the Confinement & Holding window where companions are bought from the pens with their G/N/E counts and prices, but it is a GUI window and not a command handler.

what: Matches a player's typed name against a list of names for the Seer, returning the one exact or sole partial match, or reporting none or several, with several partial matches making him refuse to guess.
ev: Candidate 1 has the same logic as seerMatch: empty input gives None, an exact case-insensitive match returns immediately, one prefix match returns One, and two or more return Several, with the only extra being an optional second name list that is ignored when null.

what: At startup, it walks the discovered mods in order and loads and switches on each one that the player has enabled, skipping any with a manifest validation problem or a fault.
ev: It loads each discovered mod in discovery order only when it is enabled and has no problem, and its Load call runs Load then OnEnable, matching the C++ loop and firstSwitchOn path; the C++ `mod.faulted` check has no direct counterpart, but it is moot at startup because nothing is loaded yet.

what: Applies a stat modifier to a character by delegating to the shared stat-modification rule (applyStatMod in items1b), with the reversed flag controlling whether positive modifiers are inverted.
ev: Its per-stat body implements the same reversed rule (positive modifiers are subtracted when reversed, others added, then clamped), but it loops over all six stats of an item and also emits messages, runs Hall checks and recalculates derived values, whereas the C++ function applies one stat/modifier pair and only delegates to applyStatMod.

what: When a newcomer joins the party, copies the leader's lost-on-floor state onto them (the lost flag from the 1995 game's dungeon exploration rules).
ev: Both copy the first member's (Chars(0)'s) lost state onto the newcomer, and ShareLostFlags copies all three flags the C++ comment describes, though the C++ body only assigns a single `lost` field.

what: Checks whether a character's alignment is compatible with a stat-raising item, passing automatically for unaligned items and otherwise requiring the item's alignment to match the character's.
where: Mordor.Core/ItemUse.cs ItemUse.ChangesStats (the enclosing class name isn't shown in the excerpt; the method is `box.ChangesStats`)
ev: It is the only candidate that gates stat-raising items on alignment, but it rejects only items one step from the character's alignment (via `FitFor`) and also requires a special type of 1, 13 or 14, whereas the C++ function passes only unaligned items or exact matches, so opposed alignments would differ.

what: Rolls a percentage check by drawing a random number below the crit-chance scale and returning whether it falls under the given chance percent, which decides whether a critical hit or backstab proc occurs.
ev: SwingOnce does the same roll-under-chance check for crits (`_rng.Next(100) < Rules.CritChance(...)`), but it computes the chance inline and is embedded in a larger blow routine, while the C++ `rollProc` is a standalone helper that takes the chance as a parameter.

what: Wraps a 1-based coordinate into the range 1..size (modular wrap-around, per SRD R19), which the game uses when moving across a dungeon grid edge.
ev: Both map a 1-based coordinate into 1..30 by the same modular shift (0 to 30, 31 to 1, and so on), but the candidate hardcodes the step of 30 instead of using the `size` argument, and it lacks the C++ `size <= 0` guard, so the two only agree when size is 30, which is the game's only grid size.

what: Computes a character's experience points required to reach a given level, scaled by a guild factor and a race experience modifier, using the SRD's closed-form XP curve (returning zero for level 1 or below).
ev: Fn12A1 computes the same kind of quantity (experience for the next level, scaled by guild and race Exp factors) but by the original VB loop with Currency rounding, not the wiki closed form, and its doc says the closed form is off by one in some guild, race and level cases.

what: When a character picks up an item, it raises the item's identification level to the level the reader can achieve, never lowering it.
ev: It applies the same "raise only, to the reader's achievable level" rule, but it runs on giving an item to a party member and also prints a message and files the item, while `Loot.OnReceived` handles pickup yet assigns the readable level of the wrong item via `LevelScale`.

what: Computes the spell cost for an opening spell sheet from the spell's cost ratio, its base level squared times 1.9 divided by the C2 divisor, floored and never less than the spell level.
ev: Both implement a floored spell-cost formula with a rate, a level-based floor, and the 1.9 factor, but they compute `level * rate * u4 * 1.9 / (10 * SL)` rather than the C++ `E4 * SL_init^2 * 1.9 / C2` with a separate C2 divisor, and the candidates add guild-table gating that the C++ does not have.

what: Charms a monster into becoming the caster's companion, placing it in a free companion slot as not freely joined, or reports that there is no room left.
ev: Charmed builds the companion record a charm produces (monster ref and id, hits, binding level, alignment), which matches the C++ function's record construction. It does not check for a free slot, place the record, set joinedFreely to false, or emit the "charmed" message, so it covers only part of the C++ function.

what: Resets a chest's trap state (trap type, trap flags, and teleporter trap) at the start of each chest generation pass, leaving the lock untouched so a lock rolled on a discarded pass persists.
ev: The candidate only sets ChestTrap to 0 when a trap goes off, whereas the C++ resets the trap type, trap flags, and teleporter trap at the start of each generation pass, and no candidate does that full reset (ChestEmptied also clears the lock and gold, which the C++ explicitly leaves alone).

what: Computes a guild's quest tier from its level by dividing by 25, rounding half-to-even, and clamping the result between 1 and the quest tier cap (kQuestTierCap).
ev: Both divide the guild level by 25, round half to even, and clamp the result to 1..10, which matches the C++ clamp to kQuestTierCap and the floor of 1 (the cap value is not shown in the snippet, but the C++ reference comment gives 1..10).

what: Releases a companion from a party slot, clearing its occupied flag and setting its creature reference to -1 while keeping its hit points and other fields, and returns a message saying it was let go (or that the member, slot, or empty slot is invalid).
ev: Release performs the same core change (empties the slot, keeps the record's name and hits, sets no carry), but it omits the C++ member and slot validation and the reply text, and DropCompanion's carry clearing is what the C++ function explicitly does not do.

what: Returns the party leader's ability-5 score (stat plus stat modifier, approximated since the real BestAbilityValue is unavailable), which is used as the value for the entry secret-door roll (R16) in the dungeon.
ev: The C++ comment says it approximates this exact function (BestAbilityValue(c, 5, gear)), but the candidate uses a guild-based formula with log terms and WIS, not the leader's raw stat plus statMod, and no candidate computes stat plus statMod directly.

what: Applies the rock-death effect that kills the entire party on a rock square: every member is marked as dead by rock with zero hit points, their bodies are left on that square of the floor, the party is flagged as wiped, and the player is told the party is crushed.
ev: It kills every party member with the rock cause and leaves them on the target square, but it is a teleport-specific handler that first records rock on the automap, relocates the party, and sets areas, and it does not explicitly push bodies onto a floor square or set `curHits` to zero as `applyRockDeath` does.

what: Returns true if a living (not dead) character's current hit points are at or below the kLivingRecoverFraction share of their maximum, which marks them as eligible for recovery at the morgue.
ev: Its living branch applies the same test as the C++ (`CurHits <= MaxHits * 0.2`), but it sits inside a larger function that also handles not-found, rock, and morgue outcomes and returns a message, not a bool.

what: When a blocked hand's weapon loop ends, the actor's item orders are cleared and the actor's combat order is switched to Defend, in both the character and the party-level order records.
ev: Its blocked-weapon branch sets `Party.OrderFor(actor).Kind = Defend` and clears `ItemOrders` for a hand that can't work, which matches the C++ core, but the candidate is truncated, never shows the `order.Kind` (character-level) write, and sits inside a per-swing loop rather than a standalone hand-finished step.

what: Decides whether a town store row is shown to the player, hiding it only when a StoreRowVisible mod has listed that row as hidden (per rules R37.2 and R38).
ev: Both return true by default and hide a store row only when a live StoreRowVisible mod answers false, though the C++ takes a precomputed row index list while the C# asks each mod live with the character and item.

what: Returns true when a spell's healing value (M5B1D) is zero, meaning the spell heals no one in Mordor's rules.
ev: No candidate tests whether a heal value is zero; `Rules.SpellHeal` (candidate 5) clamps its result to at least 1, which is the opposite behaviour, and the other candidates compute damage, costs, or effect routing.

what: Checks whether a character's current Intelligence, Wisdom, and Constitution meet the stat requirements to cast a given movement spell, where only Sanctuary has requirements and all other movement spells are always castable.
ev: Unfit covers the stat-requirement refusal (a stat below the spell's requirement) that the C++ function checks, but it is a broader check that also tests guild teaching and spell level, and the candidates contain no function that checks only the Sanctuary INT/WIS/CON requirements against current stats.

what: Returns true only when the area id is positive, which the rules (R47) use to decide whether random encounters can occur in that area.
ev: `InRoom` begins with `if (areaId <= 0) return null;`, which skips encounters for area ids of zero or below as the C++ `areaId > 0` check does, but the method also generates, refills and stores encounters, so it is a larger function than a pure gate.

what: Computes the morgue-counter chance for a character's own body in Mordor, taken as the character's natural Constitution plus a fixed bonus and clamped to the allowed raise-chance range.
ev: It is the morgue's own-body raise chance (self-raise, -1 spell term) but uses `35 * (CON / 4.5) + 40` clamped to 10..98, whereas the C++ function is `CON + 40` clamped by `clampRaiseChance`.

what: Picks which occupied companion slot at 0 or fewer Hits is carried off, taking the first such slot and replacing it only with one of strictly greater MaxHits, so ties keep the earlier slot (rule R37.2).
ev: Run contains the same selection loop (skip empty or Hits > 0 slots, take the first, replace only on strictly greater MaxHits), but it also sets each candidate's Hits to 0, emits messages, and assigns the carried companion, so it is not a standalone equivalent of pickCarryCandidate.

what: Rounds a raw fractional game value to the nearest whole number using round-half-even, implementing the B(.) rounding rule used in rest/recovery calculations (e.g. 30.77 becomes 31).
ev: `(int)Math.Round(v, MidpointRounding.ToEven)` does the same round-half-even-then-cast-to-int as `restRoundB`, and several other candidates (MazeView.CInt, SpecialHits.Kind.VbInt, Combat.cs CInt) are identical.

what: Checks whether a character is petrified by making two successive saving throws against stone resistance, with the second save's threshold derived from the target's Constitution and the monster's floor, and sets the character to Stoned on failing both.
ev: No candidate performs the two-stage stone save (resistance roll, then a CON-based second roll capped at 95 that sets DeathState.Stoned), and the nearest, Rules.ParalysisPasses, is a single paralysis roll that wears off rather than petrifies.

what: Syncs the party's dungeon area locations to the floor map, setting members to area -1 on the surface, and marks a dead member lying in recorded rock as area 0 and prunes them from the party.
ev: It matches the level-0 `-1` and the leader's-square area for living members, but it leaves a dead member in rock untouched instead of writing area 0, requires no `rockRecorded` check, and does not prune that body from the party.

what: Computes the facing direction of a dead party member's body in the dungeon by offsetting the lead character's facing by a constant and wrapping it to four directions, though the base of the result is unresolved.
ev: No candidate computes a dead body's facing from the leader's facing plus a constant offset and a mask; the closest, DungeonWindow.axaml.cs DungeonWindow.SavePos, only copies the leader's facing (+1) onto living party members' records, and the other candidates are turn, opposite, relative-direction, readout, or map-selection helpers.

what: Builds the line of companion-drift text shown to the player when a companion's binding to its owner weakens by one level but stays at or above zero.
ev: The `drifted` string on the `BindingLevel >= 0` branch is `"\"{owner}\" - {companion} has broken a level of binding!"` with both names trimmed, the same text as the C++ function, though Round also performs the drift roll and takes a character and slot rather than names.

what: Charges the payer a fee for identifying a companion and, if the companion is not already fully identified, improves its identification level by one step toward Completely.
ev: This candidate computes the identify fee for a companion, which is only the first half of the C++ function; no candidate charges the payer and also lowers the companion's IdLevel by one toward Completely.

what: Adds one creature to a pen if it is below the shelf capacity of 9, returning true when a creature was added and false when the pen is already full.
ev: PenOne applies the same ShelfCap-of-9 test and increments the pen only when below it, but it returns true even when the pen is full, whereas penAddOne returns false in that case, and PenOne also keys the increment to the creature's own alignment rather than a single pen counter.

what: Rolls a percentage chance, using the acid spit chance derived from the monster's and character's guild levels, to decide whether an acid spit attack succeeds.
ev: No candidate computes an acid spit percentage from the monster's and character's guild levels: CompanionMishap.Kind.Chance (candidate 3) is a friendly-fire mishap chance from one companion's level and body count, and Rules.LevelGapChance (candidate 5) takes both levels but returns a fixed 10/50/90 gate for other specials, not an acid spit chance.

what: Offers a score to one of the twelve Hall of Records slots and, if the score beats the current record, stores the new holder, key, value and day, returning an announcement flag so the game can show the "just set the record" message (silent for self-improvement and for the deadliest-creature record).
ev: Candidate 1 does the same steps in the same order: it returns nothing unless the offer beats the record (with creature records compared by monster power), stores holder, value and day, stays silent for same-holder improvements and the creature record, and otherwise returns the "You have just set" or "just set" line depending on `alone`. The one structural difference is that the C++ keeps a separate `key` field while the C# uses `value` for both roles.

what: When a slot is unequipped, its curse flag is cleared, so the curse comes back the next time the item is equipped.
ev: This method clears `slot.SlotCursed = false` on unequip, as one step inside the equip/unequip toggle, but in the candidate that step is a no-op because `CanUnequip` already refuses cursed slots, whereas the C++ function clears a flagged slot directly.

what: Checks whether a slot number falls within the range of valid item equipment slots, which is a gate on whether an item can be equipped to or removed from a slot.
where: Mordor.Core/Character.cs is.CanUnequip (the candidate's name is garbled in the list, so this is the closest match I can see)
ev: The C++ function only range-checks a slot number, while CanUnequip checks whether a slot is cursed, which is a different question; no candidate performs a bounds check like `slot >= kFirstItemSlot && slot <= kLastItemSlot`, so this is at most a related gate and not an equivalent.

what: Computes a player's theft outcome against a monster by subtracting twice the monster's level from the theft score, then reports whether gold can be stolen (value under 50) and whether an item can be stolen (value at most 10).
ev: No candidate computes `score - monLvl*2` or applies the gold (<50) and item (<=10) thresholds; the nearest, CombatEngine.TheftSlot, only picks which pack slot a thief reaches, and GroupAttacks merely lists theft among the specials that follow a landed hit.

what: Looks up a toggle in a mod's manifest by its key, ignoring case, and returns that toggle's default value, or false if no toggle has that key.
ev: DefaultFor finds the toggle whose key matches case-insensitively, returns its Default, and returns false when no toggle matches, which is the same behavior as declaredToggleDefault.

what: Returns a +25 bonus to the chest-chance threshold when the monster is a lair monster and its BoxChance[2] value is above zero, otherwise 0.
ev: ChestClass computes the identical bonus (25 when isLairMonster and BoxChance[2] > 0, else 0) as a local variable, but it then uses that bonus to pick the chest class instead of returning it, so the method as a whole does something different.

what: Handles a typed "swap" command that moves a party member's item between two inventory slots, refusing invalid member numbers and slots outside 2 to 40 (slot 1, the hands, cannot be moved), then applying the swap.
ev: The candidate swaps two one-based pack slots after rejecting slot 1 and anything past 40, matching the C++ slot check and swap, but none of the candidates parses the typed member number or validates it against the party, and none has the "swap <member> <slot1> <slot2>" argument handling or usage message.

what: Handles the typed "forfeit <member> <guild>" command by looking up the member and guild, asking the rules whether the member may leave that guild, and replying with the result while marking the membership closed.
ev: The candidates have no typed "forfeit <member> <guild>" command handler, so nothing parses the arguments, looks up the member or guild, or sends the "has left" / "cannot forfeit" replies. ForfeitQuest does the core effect (demoting the guild level and reducing max hits), which matches the part of the C++ that the comment defers to `Forfeit`, but it returns an item list rather than a success bool and doesn't mark the membership closed.

what: Returns whether a store row change is permitted, as answered by the town mod hooks (the "R40" rule, where a mod that throws counts as false).
ev: It returns true only if some live mod's StoreAllowsRowChangeWhileChoosing answer is true, with a throwing mod guarded to false and the base answer false, which matches the C++ "refused unless some mod answered true; a throwing mod counts as false" rule.

what: Computes the monster swing bound for a given hit total (rule R46): scales the monster's hits by 0.5/2, rounds with VB-style Int, and adds 1 to get the maximum number of swings.
ev: It uses the same expression (`Hits * .5 / 2`, plus 1) but only as the range of a random roll, `Int(Rnd * ...) + 1`, and returns no deterministic swing bound, so it is a related version rather than the same function.

what: Picks a monster class by weighted random chance (R11), using the class list and per-entry weights, with a fallback draw when all weights are zero and a final leftover rule that assigns the remainder to the last class.
where: Mordor.Core/Combat.cs whatever.Generate (the closest is Mordor.Core/Confinement.cs per.DrawOne, which uses the same cumulative-weight threshold test)
ev: No candidate is a standalone weighted-class pick with the all-zero-weight fallback and the leftover-to-last rule; Generate appears to inline the class pick (it builds the `list` and `v` arrays), but the visible excerpt is truncated before that code, and Confinement's DrawOne uses the same weighted threshold but returns null on zero total and has no leftover rule.

what: Computes the cost of one step of a binding, scaling the current cost by a factor that falls as the bound-to level rises past the top of the scale (with negative binding levels giving a negative factor).
ev: The step factor `f` uses the same formula as the C++ (`a + 4`, or `12 - a` past 12), but Binding.Cost takes the monster guild level, multiplies by 1237 and divides by 4, and takes the absolute value of the level, whereas the C++ returns only `current * f` and has an unresolved scale.

what: Turns off the row-order mod setting for the rest of the session when a mismatch is detected under rules R39 and R44, by clearing the match flag and setting the disabled flag.
ev: On a mismatch, StoreRowOrder calls Fault, which disables the whole mod for the session, as the C++ does for the row-order setting, but it does not set match or disabled flags on a row-order setting and it also unpatches Harmony and logs.

what: Computes a character's Adventure Difficulty (A/D) gain interval at a given level for a guild, using the hits-cap level, the guild's AdEvery and AdMaxLevel values, and a +3 bonus for Nomad characters, following the SRD rules R38 and R69.
ev: The candidate has the same loop, Integer-rounded step with half-even rounding, early break, `acc == hitsCap` to `level + 1` fix-up, 1.1 scaling above AdMaxLevel, and final rounding, with only a minor difference in zero-denominator handling (C++ forces step 0, the C# divides by zero).

what: Registers the "buffer" player command on both the Town and Combat screens, so a player can set or list spell buffers for a party member with the usage line shown in help.
ev: The C++ function registers a typed "buffer" command for the Town and Combat screens, and no candidate registers or dispatches a player command; the closest candidates (CharacterPanel.BuffersPage, SpellBuffers.Describe) only render or fire buffers from the UI and do not parse "buffer <member> [<slot> <spell>]" or register it per screen.

what: When a body that was saved on a rock square is loaded, it is placed back onto that rock square's body list and a message announces that a body lies on the rock, provided the square exists and is rock.
ev: No candidate pushes a loaded body onto a rock square's body list or emits the "A body lies on the rock." message; the closest, DungeonNav.SetPosition, only moves the player and skips marking rock squares explored, and its doc comment mentions a saved body loading there.

what: Handles the in-game `options` command: with no arguments it lists all options, with a numeric first argument it runs a character-specific option command, and otherwise it passes the words to the game-wide option command.
ev: The candidate opens the game-wide options window, which matches only the `gameCommand` branch, while none of the candidates lists all options when given no arguments or dispatches on a numeric first argument as `cmdOptions` does, and the candidates are GUI button handlers rather than a text-command dispatcher.

what: Blocks equipping and dropping pack items for any character whose paralysed ailment is set, per the game's paralysis rule.
where: Mordor.App/CityWindow.Mdi.cs on.OnPackEquip (the same `_ch.Paralysed` gate also appears in on.OnPackDrop)
ev: Several handlers repeat the C++ check that a paralysed character cannot equip or drop, but each embeds it in a larger click handler rather than providing a standalone predicate, and no single candidate covers both equip and drop.

what: Applies the complication effect to a character by adding 15 years to their age, multiplying their maximum hit points by 0.8333 (rounded down), and capping current hit points at the new maximum.
ev: The candidate matches the C++ age +15 years and MaxHits × 1/1.2 (≈0.8333), but it also fills CurHits to the new maximum where the C++ only clamps it when it exceeds the maximum, and it adds the stat loss and unequip logic that the C++ leaves to raiseCharacter.

what: Rolls the damage dealt by a monster's breath attack, derived from the monster's guild level and the victim's active level, with a random factor, returning 0 if the attack's base value is not positive.
where: Mordor.Core/MonsterAttack.cs CombatEngine.GroupAttacks (breath section; the damage roll is cut off in the candidate)
ev: The candidate has the same first step, `VbInt(monLvl * Math.Log(monLvl + 1))`, and the same breath-chance gating, but the excerpt stops before the q and damage computation, and the separate `SpecialHits.Raw` (Candidate 4) lacks the C++'s final `/ 2`.

what: When an inventory slot is emptied, this resets every spell buffer that points to that slot back to the empty marker (-1), so the character no longer casts from a slot that has been cleared.
ev: It loops over the buffers and resets each one that holds an item whose pack slot equals the emptied slot to Empty, which is what resetEmptiedBuffers does; it differs only in also checking that the buffer holds an item and bounding the loop by the buffer array length.

what: Adds the given number of days to a character's age in days, which is the ageing mechanic (R63) of the game.
ev: AgeBy does the same core update as addAgeDays (`Age += days` with no other state change), but it also returns a "You are now X older." message string, which the C++ void function does not.

what: Checks whether a charm spell effect (codes 75 through 99) applies to a monster, returning true only when the effect's offset from the first charm code equals the monster's class.
ev: The candidate embeds the same test (`s.Effect` in 75..99 and `Mdata1.MonsterClasses[target.Type].Index == s.Effect - 75`) but only as a step that zeroes damage in a larger monster-spell-hit calculation, not as a standalone bool predicate.

what: Gives the free round to monsters already engaged in combat (rule R25 of the Mordor SRD) by delegating to freeRoundAs with the "Moved" caller.
ev: ArrivalRound gives an engaged group its free round with `AttackKind.Moved` when the party walks into an area, which matches freeRound's Moved caller, but it also starts the combat from the waiting group and is tied to arrival, while freeRound is only a generic delegate to freeRoundAs.

what: Handles the player's bank command in town by depositing or withdrawing gold from member 1's purse, with range checks and messages reporting the result.
ev: BankTyped performs the same deposit and withdraw moves between on-hand and bank gold with the same refusal checks, but it takes typed text instead of an integer, returns an enum with no messages, and skips overflowing statements rather than refusing the whole transaction. The C++ `depositGold` call has no candidate counterpart.

what: Handles the typed `pen sell <slot> <member>` command by validating its argument count and parsing the companion slot and party position, then asks the confinement logic to sell that slot's companion, or replies with a usage or range error.
ev: No candidate parses a `pen sell <slot> <member>` command or calls a sell-slot routine; the nearest, CityWindow `IdEnter`, only looks up a typed companion slot and prepares the sell price display, and `PriceToSell` only computes the price.

what: Rolls a 1–3000 die and returns whether the roll is at or under the character's join chance, which is CHA×10 minus 10 per level below the level the monster was found at, clamped at zero.
where: Mordor.Core/Combat.cs FillGroup (the join-offer block at lines 1948-1967)
ev: No candidate computes the 1-3000 roll against a CHA-based threshold; FillGroup's join-offer block is the likely caller of this check, but its code is cut off before any join roll, so the overlap is only the offer-to-join context.

what: Computes the effective deepest level for the dungeon, taking the larger of the dungeon-wide deepest level reached and the current map's deepest level visited, and treating zero as level 1.
ev: It computes `Math.Max(DungeonState.Load(SavesDir).DeepestReached, map.DeepestVisited)` as the C++ does, and the zero-to-1 fallback appears in its comment and in the clamp to at least 1 in AutomapWindow.SetDeepest, though the candidate does not set 1 directly.

what: Computes a theft score for a thief by adding a random roll (0–99) to a level-and-coefficient-based bonus, then adds half that score again when the victim is defending.
ev: The C++ theftScore computes a random roll plus a level-and-coefficient bonus and adds half again when defending, while GoldToSteal only caps a gold theft at the roll and handles rounding, so it shares the theft context but not the scoring formula; none of the candidates computes the theft score itself.

what: Records an ordinary death for a character by zeroing their hit points, clearing paralysis, poison, disease, and resistances, releasing any carried-character link, marking them Dead unless they are Stoned, and incrementing their death count and logging it.
where: Mordor.App/DungeonWindow.axaml.cs DungeonWindow.SetDead (the pick class's SetDead method)
ev: SetDead zeroes hits, marks the character dead with the ordinary cause, increments the death count, and logs it, but it does not clear paralysis, poison, disease, resistances, or the carried-character link, which are split across Character.EndEveryAilment, Character.EndAilmentsAndSpellResists, and Sub0930.

what: Computes the melee damage modifier adjustment from the size difference between the target and the monster, giving a bonus when the target is smaller and a penalty when it is larger (per SRD R35).
ev: The size term (`sizeDiff / 10.0` added when positive, subtracted when negative, with the sign convention matching the C++ "smaller target gets a bonus") is inlined in a larger blow function rather than standing alone, and the divisor of 10 is not confirmed against `kSizeStepDivisor`.

what: Decides whether a sighting of a monster replaces its recorded name, returning true only when the existing Known value is 0 (the newer name takes over in that case).
ev: Merge applies the same rule (`if (there.Known == 0) there.Name = newer.Name;`), but inline within a larger merge of several record fields rather than as a standalone predicate returning a bool, and FileSighting, FileItem, and FileCompanion use the same inline check.

what: Rolls the hit points a character gains on reaching the next level in a guild, using the guild's average hits, a 2/3 chance of a random bonus, and a CON-based bonus below the hit-cap level, or a flat late-hits amount past that cap.
ev: It mirrors HitsGain step for step: the zero return when another guild already reached the new level, the flat LateHits past the cap, the gated 2/3 random bonus, the AvgHits base, and the CON bonus only when CON is above 16 and below the cap, with the same roll order. It differs only in that it mutates the character and clamps MaxHits at 999.

what: Returns the lock type (ChestLock) stored on a chest's square record, which the original game uses as the chest's lock state.
ev: No candidate simply returns the chest's stored lock value; the closest, Rules.cs `is.MagicallyLocked`, only turns a lock state into a bool, and Combat.cs `RoomRecord.Copy` and `pick.Take` copy `ChestLock` without returning it.

what: Computes a shop or library price for an item as a linear fit over its attack, defense, hit points, resistance sum and guild level, then rounds it and clamps it to a minimum price floor.
where: none (nearest is Mordor.Core/Confinement.cs per.PriceToBuy, a shop buy price, but it uses a log-scaled stock formula rather than a linear fit over att/def/hits/resSum/guildLevel)
ev: No candidate computes a linear combination of attack, defense, hit points, resistance sum and guild level with an intercept and a 1000 floor; the closest shop-price methods (PriceToBuy, PriceToSell, PriceToIdentify) use different inputs and formulas.

what: Reads one font's face and point size from the options INI file, falling back to the default face when the face is empty or missing and to the default size when the size is absent or not a number (SRD R4.1 and R4.2).
ev: For each font it reads the face, falls back to the default face when the value is empty or missing, and reads the size with the default size as fallback, which is the C++ per-font logic, though ReadFonts does it for both fonts in one method and relies on `ini.Number` for the not-a-number fallback, which I did not see.

what: Maps a walked-into-the-dungeon arrival outcome (falls from the sky, lands in rock, or arrives normally) onto the matching displacement outcome for the party, as used when the party is displaced by a teleporter or similar effect.
ev: No candidate maps an arrival outcome onto a displacement outcome; Teleporting.cs Outcome.ForSpell (the closest) classifies where a teleport lands but never converts to a DisplaceOutcome value.

what: Rolls the ambient sound check for a dungeon tick, which succeeds with a flat percent chance only when nothing is in front of the party.
ev: Candidate 1 makes the same flat 10% roll (`_rng.NextDouble() * 100 >= 10`) and only when nothing is in front (no combat or waiting state), while also adding a leader-alive gate and playing a random ambient sound, which the C++ function leaves to its caller.

what: Applies the T3 poison gas chest trap to each living party member, who must pass a Resist(5) check or be afflicted with poison at the dungeon level's strength.
ev: Spring applies poison at the dungeon level to each party member through a resistance roll, matching the trap's purpose, but it uses ResistancePercent/2 with an inverted comparison rather than the C++'s Resist(5), and it does not address whether dead members are skipped.

what: Looks up a mod setting by mod ID and key in the settings store and returns its text, or the supplied default if no matching entry exists.
ev: It looks up the text for a mod ID and key in the settings store, the same lookup as the C++ function, but it returns null when the key is absent instead of taking and returning a caller-supplied default.

what: At item generation, it marks the item's slot as cursed when the item is a Cursed==2 type or the item came from chest treasure landing in a pack slot.
ev: Loot.AttachesItself matches only the `item.cursed == CurseKind2` half of the C++ condition and doesn't set a slot flag, while Mordor.App/DungeonWindow.axaml.cs DungeonWindow.TreasureFrom describes the chest-landing and attach-on-arrival behavior but its code is truncated before showing where `SlotCursed` is set.

what: Teleports or displaces the party by a spell's offset from its facing, first deciding whether the arrival lands safely, is blocked by rock, or falls from the sky, and then moving the party and applying the arrival consequences and the spell's point cost.
ev: ForSpell makes the same fall/rock/arrives decision from the target level and square, but it does not compute the offset from facing, move the party, apply the arrival consequences, or charge the spell's point cost.

what: Formats a gold amount for display as a whole number rounded half up, keeping a minus sign on negative amounts that round to zero so they show as "-".
ev: It matches the C++ rounding and sign rules (half away from zero, "-" for a negative amount that rounds to nothing, "0" for a positive one), but it groups thousands with "###,###" under the current culture, so 1000 prints as "1,000" where the C++ prints "1000".

what: Records a teleporter on the player's automap whenever the square is resolved, so teleporters are always noticed.
ev: For a teleporter, PerceiveSquare always identifies the bit and writes it to the automap, but only when the leader is not lost (`mapIt = got && !lost`), whereas the C++ `noticeTeleporter` writes the bit unconditionally.

what: Rolls a d100 against the chest's disarm value (clamped) to decide whether the player successfully disarms a chest trap.
ev: OpenChest performs the same check inline (`_rng.Next(100) + 1 <= thieving`, disarmed on success) but embeds it in a larger method that also sets captions and awards XP, and the visible code shows no clamp of the disarm value like `clampChestDisarm`.

what: Rolls a single random number to decide whether a treasure chest is generated for an encounter, and if so whether it is a plain box or a full chest, with the thresholds shifted by a bonus for lair monsters.
ev: Both roll once, add a lair-monster bonus to the BoxChance[1] and BoxChance[2] thresholds, and let the second match overwrite the first to give class 2 or 3 (class 0 otherwise); the candidate scales the roll as 0-99 where the C++ uses Rnd*100, which is a minor difference.

what: When a party takes a chute, every member lands from the fall automatically, with no roll, by calling the per-member chute-fall logic in turn.
ev: With taken=true the method skips the per-member float roll (`!taken && Chute.Floats(...)`) and lands every party member on the chute's floor in turn, which matches takeChuteLanding's no-roll, all-members behavior, though the candidate also carries the walk-on branch and is truncated before the damage step.

what: Returns whether an item can be deposited in the vault, which it cannot if it is currently equipped (rule T-10).
ev: Deposit contains the same T-10 refusal (an equipped, non-empty pack slot is refused with "Cannot put equipped items in the bank!") but embedded in the full deposit flow rather than as a standalone predicate like canBankItem.

what: Decides whether a character counts as a body (a dead character that rescue can recover) by treating any death state other than Alive or Stoned as a body.
where: Mordor.Core/Party.cs moves.RemoveTheDead (closest, but it is party-pruning logic, not a body predicate)
ev: No candidate returns whether a character is a body by excluding only Alive and Stoned; RemoveTheDead tests `!c.IsDead && !c.Stoned` to decide who stays in the party, which treats stoned characters as gone, the opposite of the C++ rule.

what: Decides whether the join offer should be displayed for a given encounter group, showing it only for group 0 when exactly one group has creatures present and that group has its join offer enabled.
ev: JoinLine returns the offer text only when group[0].JoinOffer is positive, which matches the final check, but it omits the group-index-0 test and the exactly-one-group-present test, and it renders a string rather than returning a visibility bool.

what: Computes the spell cost for Mordor's casting rules as (spell level / character's spell level) × spell cost × guild modifier × 1.9, returning 0 when the character's spell level is zero.
ev: Both compute a spell's point cost for a character, but Spellbook.Cost uses the source's fn1485 price with per-guild rates and a floor, not the C++ formula (spellLevel / characterSpellLevel) × spellCost × guildMod × 1.9 with a zero-divisor guard.

what: Totals the Def values of all currently equipped worn items in the player's inventory to give the character's overall defence bonus from armour.
ev: Its `id` term sums `Def` over equipped slots with a null-item fallback of 0, the same as `equippedDef`, but it is embedded in a larger function that adds base, stats, and guild values and does not return the gear sum alone. The other candidates (`WornSum`/`EquippedSum`/`DefenseOf`) apply alignment fit weighting, so they differ from the plain sum.

what: Dungeon-mode command entry point that hands a typed `use <member> <slot>` command to the shared item-use handler, which applies the item's effect and produces the reply for the player.
ev: UseSelectedItem applies the same item-use logic (refusals, spell cast or charge spend, ApplySpecial, messages) that the shared handler does, but it works on the currently selected pack slot with no typed `use <member> <slot>` argument parsing and returns nothing, so it is not the command entry point itself.

what: A rotator loss sets the party's lost flags for position and facing (leaving the floor flag alone) and tells the player they have lost their bearings.
ev: On the loss branch it sets LostPosition and LostFacing and leaves the floor flag alone, as the C++ does, but it adds a perception roll the C++ doesn't have, never sets a general lost flag, and omits the "You have lost your bearings." message.

what: Equips a pack item for a character if the equip check passes, marking it equipped, reducing free hands by the item's hand width, and applying any equip curse tied to the character's alignment.
ev: This method performs the equip flow (wearable and refusal checks, setting `Equipped`, applying the equip curse), but it also toggles unequip, never reduces free hands by the item's hand width (R6), and has no hands/out-of-range slot guard, so it covers only part of `equipSlot`.

what: Picks a companion slot to act for the party by sampling random draws until it lands on the character (slot 0), the phantom fifth slot, or an occupied companion, returning 0 when no companion is present or after 1000 failed draws.
ev: It has the same logic as the C++ function: return 0 when no slot is occupied, draw `floor(rng.NextDouble() * 5)`, return on slot 0 or 4 or an occupied slot, redraw on an empty slot, and return 0 after 1000 draws.

what: Returns the level used as the base for the guild level in the pen listing, taking the first party member's level or 1 when the party is empty.
ev: No candidate returns the first party member's character level (or 1 when the party is empty) as a base level; the nearest, Rules.ChestExp, only takes a first-character guild level as a parameter inside a chest-disarm XP formula.

what: Rolls the new hit points for a character on load, picking a random sign and then a random swing of up to a quarter of the base hits, and returns the base hits adjusted up or down by that amount.
ev: It draws the sign first, then the swing (`floor(rng*(Hits*.5)/2)+1`), and returns hits minus or plus that swing, which matches rollLoadHits; it also sets MaxHits, a small extra the C++ function does not do.

what: Applies a stat or maximum-hits drain from a status effect to the character, lowering max hits (capping current hits to match) or reducing an ability stat by the drained amount, and announces the result to the player.
ev: No candidate applies a status-effect drain to ability stats or max hits; the closest, Raising.ApplyComplications, lowers stats and max hits but as the price of a raise, with no drain amount, no hitsDrain branch, and no status-effect announcement.

what: Computes the number of days a character must rest to recover from missing hit points, scaling 100 × the missing fraction of max hits by a divisor of 3.25 and rounding half-to-even, with zero days returned when the character is at full health or has no max hits.
ev: Its comment gives the same formula, `(100 - Hits/MaxHits*100) / 3.25`, but the shown body only clears effects and never computes or rounds the days, so the half-even rounding and the maxHits ≤ 0 case are not shown.

what: Rolls a per-member chance that a character floats over a chute at the given dungeon level, returning true when a random percentage falls at or below the chute float percentage for that level.
ev: Both roll a per-member chance to float over a chute, but Floats requires the member to be Levitating and uses Rules.HoversOverPit (a pit formula, `5 + level/4 < Rnd*100`) instead of the C++ `Rnd*100 <= chuteFloatPercent(level)` threshold, so the outcome differs.

what: Computes the sale price of an item from a product value under the R10 engine's rounding rule, reducing a whole-number result by 1 and returning 0 for zero or negative products.
ev: It applies the same floor-then-subtract-one-if-whole rule, but it computes the product internally from level, rate, and SL instead of taking a product argument, and the visible code has no explicit zero or negative guard (the R10 guard is unconfirmed, as the C++ comment's U10 notes).

what: Re-reads each pack item's identification knowledge on a character level gain and raises the item's ID level when the reread shows it has become better known, announcing each upgrade to the player.
ev: It loops pack slots 1 to PackSize-1, skips empty slots, re-reads each item's known level via Loot.OnReceived, and announces "Item #N" for each slot whose level rose, matching the C++ loop; its extra Librarian.FileItem call is the library filing the C++ leaves out because that module lacks library state.

what: Applies the effects of the square the party stands on after a move in the Mordor dungeon, including rolling a random facing for rotators, resolving pit falls, and announcing stairs, while leaving water/quicksand costs and teleporter/chute handling to other modules.
ev: AfterMove runs the same square effects in the same order (perception, extinguisher, facing bits, rotator, pit, stairs captions), but it also handles water, quicksand, teleporters and chutes, which the C++ unit explicitly leaves to other modules, and it is the whole routine rather than this one unit.

what: Computes the damage a blow deals to a target by first working out the blow's damage modifier (taking into account whether the target is unseen and its level) and then rolling the final damage against the target's defense.
ev: It builds the same modifier (fighting term, weapon, crit, backstab, half against an unseen target, size difference) and then calls Fn0DEE, but it takes no target-level input, which the C++ blowDamage passes to blowDamageMod.

what: Computes the minimum cost for the R8 archive spell as the starting spell level multiplied by the base modifier.
where: Mordor.Core/Spells.cs Spellbook.Cost (the candidate's header is labelled "it.Cost"; the class name is inferred from the `Spellbook.Cost` call in candidate 8)
ev: The candidate computes a general spell cost through `Rules.Fn1485Price` with rounding and a floor, and its doc comment mentions the `StartSpellLevel * BaseMod^2` formula, but it does not compute the R8 archive minimum `startSpellLevel * baseMod` as a standalone result.

what: Computes a monster's free-attack threshold from the difference between its Dexterity and the character's, with a floor of 5 and an optional cap of 98 that applies only when the level-change rule is in effect.
ev: The candidate computes 50 + (monDex - charDex) * 5, floors it at 5, and caps it at 98 only for the ChangedLevel kind, which matches the C++ formula and its cap-only-when-flagged behaviour (the C++ `cap` bool maps to `kind == ChangedLevel`).

what: Determines whether a given race may join a given guild in Mordor, returning false for Elves, Osiri and Gnomes as Warriors and for Giants, Morlochs and Gnomes as Wizards, and true for all other combinations.
ev: It answers the same question for a given guild and race by testing the race's bit in the guild's RaceMask, the data-driven equivalent of the C++ hardcoded exclusion lists, though whether the mask values exclude exactly the listed races cannot be confirmed from this candidate alone.

what: Decides whether a dungeon level appears on the automap, returning true only if at least one of its cells has been explored (the original game deliberately hides levels the player has never reached).
ev: ReadAutomap records a level's explored cells only when there is at least one (`if (cells.Count > 0) map.Explored[level] = cells;`), which is the emptiness test behind the C++ check, but it is a save loader and never returns a show/hide decision for the automap.

what: Counts how many of the given thresholds a character's level has reached (level is at or above each threshold), which determines how many swings the character gets, per the Mordor guild tables.
ev: It counts the levels that reach a guild's swing thresholds, but it generates the thresholds internally from the guild's mod and uses a strict `level > threshold` comparison, where the C++ counts a supplied array with `level >= thresholds[i]`.

what: Returns the level a teleporter sends the player to: the square's Z2 destination level when it is positive and different from the current level, otherwise the current level (rule R76).
ev: ForSquare contains the same level rule inline (`t.Z2 > 0 && t.Z2 != fromLevel ? t.Z2 : fromLevel`), but it is embedded in a larger method that also draws destination coordinates and loops over the party, so no candidate is a standalone equivalent of teleporterLevel.

what: When the party leaves the dungeon, a carried dead companion's body is moved to the morgue list and the carrier is freed to carry nothing, with the game's delivery message shown to the player.
ev: This candidate also delivers a carried body to where the carrier is, but it saves the body's position to its file instead of moving it to the party's morgue list, and it does not clear the carrier's carried name, reset the carrying slot, or show the "Your companion is delivered." message.

what: Builds the one-line readout for the Look page showing the party's x,y coordinates, dungeon level, facing letter, and living count with an optional "+dead" suffix.
ev: For a party with no lost flags and a living character, Readout builds the same "x,y,level facing [ living+dead ]" string, but it adds lost-position, lost-level, lost-facing, and dead-viewer branches that the C++ function does not have.

what: Domination charm reduces the number of creatures a charm can affect in one group to the lower of the group count and the cap of four, returning zero for empty groups.
ev: No candidate computes the clamp min(groupCount, 4) with a zero result for empty groups; CastDamage (Combat.cs) is the nearest, since it defines the same four-slot constant (mc02A6) for group spells, but its visible text is truncated and it does not show that count logic.

what: Runs the Morgue raise attempt for a dead companion: charges the gold cost, rolls a chance based on the companion's Constitution to succeed, clears the owner's carried-character state, and either restores the companion to full Hits and Normal state or releases the slot empty.
ev: The candidate computes the same companion raise chance (`Math.Min(98, 75 + con)`, failing on `roll > chance`), but none of the candidates charges the gold, clears the carry, releases an empty slot on failure, or restores Hits and Normal state on success.

what: Returns the percentage resistance a character has against a given resist kind, or 0 if the index is out of range.
ev: It returns a character's percentage resistance to one kind, matching the C++ purpose, but it recomputes the value from race base, gear, and spell resistance instead of reading a stored array, and it has no 0 return for out-of-range indices (a negative kind would throw on array access).

what: Checks whether a cursed item can be uncursed by returning NotCursed if the item isn't cursed, NotEquipped if it isn't equipped, otherwise Ok, following the game's uncurse ordering.
ev: Refusal returns NotCursed when `!slot.SlotCursed`, then NotEquipped when `!slot.Equipped`, otherwise null (the uncurse goes ahead), which is the same check order and outcomes as checkUncurse's NotCursed, NotEquipped, Ok, with the result expressed as a message string rather than an enum.

what: After a companion is kept in the carry choice, every other companion slot whose hit points have dropped to zero or below is cleared and marked released, per rule R37.4.
ev: No candidate clears the occupied flag and sets the released flag on every other companion with hits at or below zero; CompanionFalls and CompanionCarry.Run choose the carried companion and set hits to zero, but never release the other slots, and CompanionFalls's comment only refers to the sweep as something that happens elsewhere.

what: Produces the text shown to the player for a spell-book pack buffer slot, showing the buffered item's name or spell's name with its cost, and clearing the slot when its item is gone.
ev: Candidate 1 matches the C++ empty-slot reset and the spell-past-end "(Nothing)" without clearing, but it formats item text as "Item #n. Name" instead of the quoted item name, and it omits the spell cost that the C++ appends, which is split out into CostText (Candidate 3).

what: Computes which alignments can be chosen in the General Store or Confinement from the stock counts, deciding whether the player must pick one (several stocked), the only stocked alignment is auto-selected, or the previous choice is kept.
where: Mordor.Core/AlignmentChoice.cs AlignmentChoice.Offer (built by `For`, with the three-way rule in `Chosen`)
ev: `For` derives enabled flags, stocked count and last-stocked index from the counts, `Asks` is `Stocked > 1`, and `Chosen(before)` returns -1, the single stocked alignment, or the prior choice, matching the C++ logic, though the C# covers only the three pen alignments rather than all four.

what: Decides where a creature or party lands after a teleport or displacement: a destination at level 0 or above results in falling from the sky, a level beyond the dungeon's maximum or a rock square results in being driven into rock, and anything else arrives safely.
ev: It applies the same ordered tests (level <= 0 falls, level above the maximum is rock, rock square is rock, otherwise arrives), with extra checks that the level exists in the loaded dungeon and that the coordinates are on the map, which the C++ takes as a precomputed `destIsRock` flag.

what: Returns the cost to join a guild, which the engine sets to 0 whether or not the character already holds another guild, since the priced amount for an extra guild is not given in the source.
ev: Candidate 3 has the same name and purpose, but it computes a nonzero formula price for an extra guild, while the C++ function always returns 0 because the priced amount is unknown; Candidate 2 gets the zero-when-no-other-guild branch right but also calls that formula.

what: Returns true when the aimed foe group is gone, meaning its index is out of range or its record shows zero remaining members, which the thief retarget logic uses to decide whether the thief must pick a new target.
ev: Retarget tests the same gone-group condition (index out of range, or `NextInGroup` finding no member) and then reassigns the target, but it is a void method that changes the order rather than a bool predicate like `aimedGroupGone`.

what: Handles the typed "unload <member>" command by resolving a party member from a number or name and then unloading that member's equipment or state through the roster, returning a message to the player.
ev: The C++ command resolves a member by number or name and then unloads them via rosterUnloadMember, while PruneTheDead only shares the unload step (saving a party member and removing them from the party) but runs automatically on members at nought hits rather than from a typed command, and no candidate parses a member number or name the way cmdUnload does.

what: Computes the low-level monster value for a found monster's level as its level minus a third of that level, rounded down via the engine's vbInt helper, and returns it as an integer.
where: Mordor.Core/Loot.cs of.RollDrop (also Mordor.Core/MonsterAttack.cs gives.ChooseSpell has the same VbInt(level - level/3.0) expression)
ev: The C++ function computes vbInt(level - level/3.0), and ChooseSpell computes the identical expression as a spell-level floor, but no candidate computes that value as a standalone function returning it; RollDrop uses a different formula (level/2 rounded to even) and ChooseSpell uses it only as one bound inside a larger spell-selection routine.

what: Computes the stoning chance for a target as its Constitution times a log-based factor, minus the attacker's level, capped at a maximum value.
ev: No candidate computes a stoning chance from CON, a log factor, and attacker level with a cap; the closest ones (Morgue.CompanionChance, SpellEffect.CompanionRaiseChance, Rules.SpellRaiseChance, Rules.ParalysisPasses) compute raise or paralysis chances from different inputs and formulas.

what: Returns true when the rounded draw is at most kLetOffMaxRoll, which is the let-off check in AssignQuest that grants the quest let-off chance (about 5.5% per the engine's stated value).
ev: RollQuest performs the same let-off test (`Roll() <= 5`, returning -1) but only as one step of the full quest roll, whereas the C++ QuestLetOff is a standalone predicate that takes an already-rounded roll and compares it to kLetOffMaxRoll.

what: Computes the fixed fee the seer charges for a person search at a given dungeon depth, using a logarithmic-times-linear formula with no randomness.
ev: It implements the same formula, `132567.52 * Log(level + 1) * level` with no random element, cast to long, matching the C++ `seerPersonFee`.

what: Checks whether a candidate character name would collide with an existing character's name once both are reduced to sanitised file names, so that two characters cannot end up sharing a save file.
ev: Plan decides a new character "exists" when `Character.SafeFileName(ic.Name) + ".json"` is already on disk or the name matches an existing one, which captures the sanitised-collision idea, but it builds an import plan rather than returning a bool, and it never sanitises the existing names themselves.

what: Decides whether an encounter can offer the player a join option, which is refused when more than one monster group is still alive and otherwise follows group 0's join-offer flag.
ev: FillGroup's comment says an encounter of more than one group never offers because only Foes(0).JoinOffer is read, but it gets there by wiping the flag on each pass, not by counting groups with livingCount > 0 and returning false, so the occupancy check is missing.

what: Looks up a guild's critical-hit or backstab coefficient (CritMod or BSMod) for a given ability, returning 0 when the character has no guild or the guild has no entry in the table.
ev: No candidate looks up a guild's coefficient by guild index and returns 0 when the guild is absent; the closest, Combat.cs `WinningGuild`, instead picks the best-scoring guild the character belongs to for an ability.

what: Clamps a monster's tick save chance (per Table K) to the range 5 to 90, so the value can never fall below 5% or rise above 90%.
ev: It applies the same 5-to-90 clamp to a per-tick save chance, but that chance is paralysis wearing off rather than the monster tick save from Table K, and it is computed inside a larger function rather than being a standalone clamp.

what: Computes the spell cost product for the Mordor engine as rated × u4 × rate × kCostFactor ÷ spell level, returning 0 when the spell level is zero.
ev: Fn1485Price computes the same `rated × u4 × rate × 19 / (10 × SL)` product, but it derives `rated` from level × rate internally instead of taking it as input, returns a floored int instead of a double, and clamps SL to at least 1 where the C++ returns 0 for spellLevel 0.

what: Rolls a disease-resistance check against the victim's disease resistance and, if the victim fails and is not already diseased, sets their disease level to the attacker's level and notes that they have been diseased.
ev: It sets `Diseased` and `DiseaseLevel` on each party member who fails a resistance roll, but it rolls against half the resistance, has no "not already diseased" guard, and takes the level from the dungeon level rather than the attacker level.

what: Decides whether an item may be shelved at a given floor and alignment row, refusing cursed or unaligned items, items below the deepest stocked floor, and rows already at the shelf cap.
ev: ShelvesSale checks the cursed flag and the per-alignment shelf cap, as the C++ does, but it refuses only floor-0 unaligned goods (via ShelvedBySelling) rather than all unaligned items, and it has no check against the deepest stocked floor (kDeepestStocked).

what: Computes the item level range for treasure drawn from a chest, container, box, or the Asmodeus chest, widening or shifting the base min/max levels per the SRD table T3 (Chest: min +1, Container: min and max -1, Asmodeus chest: fixed 14 to 16).
ev: RollDrop applies a similar chest-class shift (class 1 lowers both bounds by 1, class 3 raises the low bound by 1) to a monster-derived drop band, but it does not take a base min/max and return an adjusted range, and it has no fixed 14-16 Asmodeus-chest case (that is handled separately by Asmodeus.DropBand).

what: Compares a guild's stored attack and defence values against the recomputed ones and, if they differ, emits a "guild.stats_differ" warning event to the player/game context listing the guild index and both sets of values.
ev: No candidate compares stored guild attack and defence against recomputed values or emits a "guild.stats_differ"-style warning; the closest, Rules.GuildAD (candidate 7), only recomputes a guild's Att/Def for a given level without any comparison or event.

what: Checks whether a player-typed pack slot is a real item slot, refusing slot 1 because it is the character's hands rather than an item, and sets the refusal message the player sees.
ev: ItemAnswer refuses the Hands slot the same way and cites the same FRMINTER.BAS reference, but it also refuses equipped items, returns a different refusal string, and does not write the "Slot 1 is your hands" message, so it is a related check rather than an identical one.

what: When the player fires a buffer with Shift during combat, it decides whether an item is used, a spell is cast immediately, a spell becomes a standing order, or nothing happens, based on whether monsters are present, whether the fight continues, and the spell-use disposition.
ev: FireBuffer does what buffersFireFromShift decides: an item buffer uses its pack slot, a spell buffer becomes a standing order during a fight and is cast otherwise, and empty or out-of-range buffers do nothing. It performs the action rather than returning a BufferFire value, and delegates the order-versus-cast choice to CastKnownSpell/CastInCombat rather than testing monstersPresent and fightOn inline.

what: Implements the R13 rule that after a teleporter or chute the party is pruned of its dead only when the party size has dropped, returning true if the size decreased.
where: Mordor.App/DungeonWindow.axaml.cs, DungeonWindow.PruneTheDead (labelled `pick.PruneTheDead` in the candidate list)
ev: No candidate returns a size-drop boolean, but PruneTheDead records the size before pruning and returns early without announcing or refreshing when `_party.Size == before`, which is the same "only act if the size dropped" gate applied to the general prune rather than specifically after a teleporter or chute.

what: For the confinement (pen) alignment choice, it copies the pen counts unchanged and passes them to the shared alignment-choice logic, offering only the Good, Neutral, and Evil buttons.
ev: ClickRow builds the Good/Neutral/Evil offer from the pen counts and passes it to AlignmentChoice.For, as confinementRowClick does, but it adds UI handling (frame, await, button enabling) that the C++ wrapper does not have, and Candidate 8 (AlignmentChoice.Offer) is only the shared logic the C++ function calls, not the G/N/E wrapper itself.

what: Computes the morgue Constitution-loss roll threshold for a character, which is 50 minus twice their CON, so high-CON characters effectively never lose CON there.
ev: It computes the same `50 - CON * 2` threshold, but clamps it at 0 with `Math.Max(0, ...)`, whereas the C++ returns negative values above CON 25; the loss decision is identical either way because the roll can never fall below a non-positive threshold.

what: Rolls a disease-resistance check against the character's Resistance (stat 4) and, if the character fails while not already diseased, sets their disease level to the level where it was found and shows the "You have caught a disease!" message.
ev: Its trap 2 (Disease Spores) branch makes a disease-resistance roll per party member and sets `Diseased` and `DiseaseLevel = dungeonLevel` on failure, but it is a chest-trap effect with a halved-resistance threshold, no "already diseased" check, and no "You have caught a disease!" message, unlike `tryDisease`.

what: Returns true when a character's current hit points are zero or below, which marks them as a casualty of the update step in the game's death rules (R6).
ev: No candidate is a standalone "curHits <= 0" predicate, but AfterRoundSounds uses the same `CurHits <= 0` test on party members, combined with a not-yet-counted-dead filter and a sound-playing action, so it only covers part of the C++ function.

what: Records the mod's "Enabled" flag (true or false) into the mod settings store for the given mod ID.
ev: SetEnabled(modId, on) calls WriteFlag(modId, "Enabled", on), which writes the "Enabled" key as "True" or "False" (via candidate 5), matching the C++ writeStoredFlag call and the F4 comment.

what: Looks up a guild's HP-per-level parameters (average hits per level, the level cap at which the rate changes, and the late-level rate) from a table, falling back to placeholder values for guilds not in the table.
ev: LoadGuilds reads each guild's AH (hits per level), ML (level cap) and MH (late hits) from the data file, the same three fields hitsParamsFor returns, but it loads every guild at once instead of looking up one guild, and it has no placeholder fallback for unlisted guilds.

what: Decides whether casting a level-0 item spell costs spell points, which it does unless the p01AA flag is set, and treats any higher-level cast as free.
ev: The candidate charges SP only when the item's level is 0 (`free: lvl != 0`, citing MAINMOD2.BAS:1355), which matches the C++ rule for the case where p01AA is zero, but the C++ predicate takes two inputs (castLevel and p01AA) while the candidate folds both into one item-level input.

what: Converts a raw item alignment value from the item data into the game's alignment category (Unaligned, Good, Neutral, or Evil), treating values 0 and 1 as Unaligned and falling back to Unaligned for out-of-range values.
where: Mordor.Core/Import/OriginalSaves.cs SlotFrom (containing class not shown in the candidate)
ev: SlotFrom maps alignment values 0 to 3 directly and falls back to Unaligned for out-of-range values, but it has no rule that makes raw value 1 Unaligned (it casts 1 straight to Good) and it also emits a warning note.

what: Picks a companion monster for a spawn window by weighted random selection among monsters whose native level falls in the window's range (or returns a fixed or previous monster index for the other window kinds).
ev: Both do a Chance-weighted cumulative pick among monsters filtered by LevelFound, but DrawOne first draws a random monster kind and only checks an upper level bound, while the C++ function handles the RepeatPrevious/KeepPrevious and TableIndex window kinds and uses a [nativeFloor+offsetLo, nativeFloor+offsetHi] range with a fallback to previousMonsterIndex.

what: Decides whether a Charm forces a companion to join the party, returning true when the damage inflicted in combat exceeds the monster's remaining hits (per R13.3 of the game's rules).
ev: No candidate compares damage inflicted against the monster's remaining hits to decide a forced join; the closest, Combat.cs Blow.Credit, only caps inflicted damage at remaining hits for XP and damage events, and Combat.cs at.Charmed builds the companion without any join-forcing rule.

what: Decides whether a monster's spell is accepted for casting, returning true only when both its damage value and its spell effect value are positive (per SRD [c14]).
ev: No candidate has a monster-spell acceptance predicate that requires both Damage2 > 0 and SpellEffect > 0; the nearest, SpellThrown.cs Ask.WhoToAsk and Companion.Apply, test only Damage2 <= 0 while choosing targets, and CastGate.UseOf tests Damage2 == 0 only to classify the spell as combat or non-combat.

what: Advances the game's combat, play, and ailment clocks by a given number of milliseconds, running combat rounds while a fight is on and ticking the play-clock and ailment effects when their time boundaries are crossed.
ev: No candidate advances all three clocks by a millisecond amount; CombatTick covers the combat-clock part (a round runs while a fight is on, gated by minimising), while PlayClock.Tick and AilmentTick cover the play and ailment parts separately, and none has the dispatcher logic that converts ms into tick counts.

what: Looks up the chute on the given floor whose position is one step diagonally down-right of the player's square (x+1, y+1) and has a positive depth, returning its record index or "no record" so a fall can happen (R56).
ev: Its first line does the same lookup as the C++ (first chute at x+1, y+1 with Depth > 0), but it returns the chute object instead of an index and goes on to apply the whole fall, so it is not a standalone equivalent.

what: Returns the gold a character can show, which is their total purse when the party is at dungeon level 0 (town) and only the gold on hand when in the dungeon.
ev: It applies the same rule as shownGold, choosing `c.Purse` when `c.DungeonLevel == 0` and `c.GoldOnHand` otherwise, but it runs over both exchange characters and formats the result into a label instead of returning it.

what: Returns whether the party's map is active, which is true unless the leader is lost (the game's nav.Mapping rule: automapping stops when the leader becomes lost).
ev: NavFor sets `nav.Mapping = !_ch.IsLost` as part of creating a level's navigator, which applies the same rule as `!leader.isLost()`, but it is embedded in a larger method and reads `_ch` rather than the leader, and no candidate is a standalone equivalent of the one-line function.

what: Returns true if any current party member has an alignment opposed to the joining character's alignment, which is the R7 check on whether a joiner may be admitted to the party.
ev: It loops over the members and refuses on the first one whose alignment is opposed to the joiner's (the same R7 check), but it is embedded in a larger function that also tests size, duplicates, death and location, and it returns a refusal string rather than a bool.

what: Computes the minimum cost for a spell-sheet (sheet) casting formula from the initial level, guild modifier, and spell-cost ratio, rounding up and returning 2×ROUNDUP(...) − 1, or 0 when the level is −1 to avoid division by zero.
ev: It uses the same 1.9 factor and a division by a level-derived quantity, but it computes a spell-point price with round-to-even and no ROUNDUP or 2×−1 step, and no candidate handles the sheet minimum-cost formula or its level −1 guard.

what: Resolves a companion's opening spell group at the moment of casting by delegating to spellStartGroup with a -1 argument, which sets the group that the companion's spell takes effect in.
ev: No candidate defines or calls anything like `spellStartGroup` or determines which group a companion's spell starts at; the closest, `Combat.cs` `CompanionCasts`, handles companion casting but never resolves an opening group.

what: Returns true only when a key is missing from settings.ini, so the legacy MORDOR.INI file is consulted as a fallback for that key.
ev: Its doc comment and `IniLayers` construction describe the same rule (each key comes from the port's settings file when present, otherwise from the game directory's MORDOR.INI), but the C++ function is an isolated boolean predicate, while this is the full options loader and the per-key check lives in `IniLayers.For`, which isn't among the candidates.

what: Rerolls a random value from 1 to max using the game's RNG, as used for chest fate (Table F), and returns 0 if max is not positive.
ev: No candidate returns a uniform roll from 1 to max with a zero result for non-positive max; the nearest, `SpellThrown.Apply`'s Fate reroll, uses an unrelated `Int(Rnd * 3)` on the caster, and `Loot.RollCharges` applies a different random shift.

what: Attempts a spell that retrieves a chosen roster character to the caster's square, level, and area and marks them saved, provided the pick is a valid candidate and the character is within reach of the dungeon level; a cancel or out-of-list pick spends nothing.
ev: CastHere's fetch branch offers only dead characters in the rock on the leader's level with area 0 and then (in the truncated remainder, which presumably moves the body) handles the retrieval, which matches the candidate-list and body-moving parts of castFetch. However, the candidate is truncated before the actual move, and it does not contain the castFetch reach test (`isFetchWithinReach`), the R58 cancel-spends-nothing logic, or the explicit caster-square/area/saved assignments, so only part of the function is visible.

what: Computes the friendly-join threshold for a monster, which is the Charisma-based score (CHA×10) reduced by 10 for each level below the first at which the monster was found.
ev: No candidate computes CHA×10 minus 10 per level below the first; the closest, Combat.cs FillGroup, has a join-offer block, but it is truncated before any threshold formula appears.

what: Announces a Hall of Records entry by showing the record holder's name, the record kind's name, and its value as a game message to the player.
ev: Check also builds a player-facing "record set" line from the holder name and record kind, but it returns null in several cases, omits the value, and uses different wording, while HallRecords.Describe shows holder and value without announcing anything.

what: Decides whether a charm spell can add another creature to the party by checking that fewer than the maximum number of companion slots are currently filled.
where: Mordor.Core/Combat.cs, CastDamage (enclosing class not shown in the candidate)
ev: The charm branch returns "No room for more Companions!" when `actor.Companions.FreeSlots == 0`, which is the same room decision as `occupied < kCompanionSlots`, but it is embedded in a larger spell-casting method rather than being a standalone predicate, and no candidate has the bare check.

what: Decides whether a kill counts toward the player's Kills tally, returning false when a companion made the kill (quirk c37 in the Mordor rules).
ev: The C++ predicate returns false for companion kills, and KilledBy implements the same rule by incrementing `killer.Kills` only for a character's own kills (its doc says companion kills skip that step), but it is an inline increment rather than a boolean check, and the companion path is not shown in the candidate.

what: Rolls a random number against the complication chance to decide whether a raise attempt in the game complicates, using a strict less-than comparison.
