ev: Both draw one random roll from 0-99 and report a complication when the roll is strictly less than the chance (`rng.Next(100) < ComplicationChance(...)`), but Complicates also folds in the rock short-circuit and derives the chance from age and race lifespan, which the C++ leaves to its caller.

what: Returns the trimmed name of the party leader (member 1) to sign the clean guild log record, or an empty string when there is no party.
ev: TownLeader also picks the party's leader by position with a fallback, but it returns a Character (the first living member in the city, or null), not the trimmed name of member 1 or an empty string, so it does not do the same thing as glLeaderName.

what: Fate re-rolls a character's current hit points and current spell points, each as a uniform random value from 1 up to its maximum, and announces the new values to the player.
ev: The candidate's doc says it handles Fate by rerolling a single character, but the visible text cuts off before the Fate body, and Candidate 1's doc describes an extra unused `Int(Rnd * 3)` draw that the C++ function does not make.

what: Checks whether a character level falls within the Asmodeus band for an item drop level, meaning two levels below the drop level up to the drop level itself.
ev: It computes the same band, `(ItemDropLevel - 2, ItemDropLevel)`, but returns the bounds rather than testing whether a character level falls inside them, and it is scoped to Asmodeus's chest.

what: Announces to the player that a character has fallen through a chute and then been hurt by the landing, showing the damage taken.
ev: Chute.Land produces a chute-fall line with the hit count and applies the damage, but it returns one conditional line ("You have fallen into a chute for N hits.") instead of the C++ pair of announcements ("falls through the chute!" then "is hurt by the landing"), and it has no per-character name-based announcement.

what: Returns "on" or "off" for a character's boolean option, reading the stored INI value for that member and key (falling back to the default), for display in the character command and option listings.
ev: No candidate reads a stored per-character boolean option from INI and maps it to "on"/"off" with a default; the closest, CharacterPanel.DrawCharPage, paints stat text, and the rest handle keys, help topics, spells, and pack drops.

what: Looks up a race's base resistance to a given damage kind from the race table, returning 0 if the race or the resistance entry is missing, as the first step of the game's resistance calculation.
ev: It takes the race base the same way (`c.RaceDef?.Resistances[kind]`, 0 if missing), but then adds the flat 90 from gear and any spell resistance, so it is a larger function that includes this step rather than an equivalent of `raceResistBase` alone.

what: Returns the gold multiplier for a chest's class (0.5, 0.5, 1.0, or 1.5), which scales how much gold the chest holds.
ev: It uses the same class-to-multiplier mapping (0 or 1 gives 0.5, 2 gives 1, 3 gives 1.5), but it applies that factor to a gold amount instead of returning the factor itself, and no candidate returns the bare multiplier.

what: Checks whether a dead character can be retrieved from the soul list, returning an error if the character is on a different dungeon level or not dead in rock in area 0, and Ok otherwise.
ev: CastHere's Fetch branch applies the same eligibility rule (IsDead, CauseOfDeath == Rock, the leader's dungeon level, SavedArea == 0) to filter a list, but it returns no typed status and has no "not on this level" or "not in rock" error results, which the C++ function returns for a single character.

what: After a fight, the gold the party won is either added to the chest if one is present, or otherwise paid into the gold leader's purse (falling back to member 0 if the leader index is invalid), with a message to the player.
ev: It makes the same chest-or-no-chest decision, but when there is no chest it splits the gold evenly across the whole party (PayGold) rather than paying the gold leader's purse, and when there is a chest it leaves the gold in the fight record instead of adding it to the chest's gold.

what: Validates a typed item-give target by parsing the text as a number and accepting it only if it names a pack slot from 2 to kPackSlots (slot 1 is the Hands), returning that slot or -1 for "No Item to give!".
ev: Both parse the typed number and reject values outside the pack range, but Fn131A also accepts slot 1 (returning index 0), returns a zero-based index where giveSlot returns the 1-based slot, and additionally requires the slot to hold a named item, which giveSlot does not check.

what: Returns true when a square's trap flags include the anti-magic bit, which in the game means that square refuses spellcasting.
ev: SquareTests makes the same `Floor.Has(_nav.X, _nav.Y, Floor.ANTIMAGIC)` square-bit test as the C++ function, but it is a void method that also sets `NoSpellsHere` and `_combat` fields rather than returning a bool.

what: Returns a pointer to the square at the given 1-based x/y coordinates on the requested dungeon level, using that floor's width from the data files, or null if the level or coordinates are out of range.
ev: The C++ function returns the square at 1-based (x, y) on a given dungeon level using the floor's width, but no candidate does that: ForSquare picks teleport destinations, SquareAt converts map pixels to squares, ReadAutomap decodes saved records, and the rest handle sight, morgue, and map-record logic, so none looks up a square by explicit coordinates.

what: Computes a character's thieving ability as a 0-100 score from Dex, Wis, guild level and thieving modifier, normalized against a baseline and maximum (formula F6 / rule R18 of the Mordor SRD).
ev: It computes the same hardcoded maximum as the C++ `z` term (stats 30 and 40, GLvl 999, ThievingMod 9), but it has no baseline subtraction, no 0-100 normalization, and no round-half-even step, and no candidate performs the full `(x - y) / (z - y) * 100` calculation.

what: Computes a character's archive-form Attack/Defence value from Strength, Dexterity, Intelligence and Wisdom using the game's formula 2*(Str+Dex) + Int + Wis - 76.
ev: Both compute a stats-based Attack/Defence value from Str, Dex, Int and Wis, but Rules.StatsAD uses banded weights (+2 per STR/DEX above 12, +1 per INT/WIS above 14) rather than the archive form's flat 2*(Str+Dex)+Int+Wis-76, so it is a different version of the same calculation.

what: Produces the Char-page attack and defense values for a character by taking the raw best guild award and adding the base 10/10 AD, per the game's rules.
ev: It takes the highest guild Att and Def across memberships, matching the raw best guild award in GuildAttDef, but it does not add the 10/10 base, which appears only in candidates that also add stats and gear (Mordor.App/CharacterPanel.cs CharacterPanel.AttackDefence and Mordor.Core/Combat.cs 3.AttackOf).

what: Parses a typed "seer" command and routes it to the Seer's answer or search handlers (creature, item, or person), or replies with usage text or an error when the input is incomplete or unrecognized.
ev: No candidate parses the typed "seer" command or handles the yes/no answers, usage text, or unknown-input reply, but ShowSeer's inner Locate(bool monster) covers the creature/item search handler and LocatePerson covers the person search, which are the branches the C++ routes to.

what: Rolls a 1-100 die to decide whether a chest holds items, capping high rolls unless the item chance is 100 and adding a dungeon-level-scaled bonus when the chest was opened by a charm.
ev: It matches the 1-100 roll, the cap at 90 unless the chance is 100, the Log(level + 10) * 5 bonus for a charm-opened chest, and the `roll <= ItemChance` test, but it adds a chest-class roll modifier the C++ lacks and applies the bonus before the cap where the C++ caps first, so results can differ.

what: Returns the percent chance that an acid spit lands, which is 90 if the character's guild level is more than 25% above the monster's, 10 if it is more than 25% below, and 50 otherwise.
ev: It applies the same 90/10/50 rule with the same quarter-above and quarter-below thresholds, differing only in parameter order (char, then monster, rather than monster, then char).

what: Charges the morgue's rescue fee by deducting it from the paying party member's gold on hand, returning false with an explanatory reply if the rescuers are unpriced, no payer exists, or the gold is insufficient.
ev: The candidate prices a rescue by depth (Rescue.SearchCost), refuses with "Not enough gold!" when CharPay fails, and charges the morgue's fee as the C++ does, but it charges through CharPay, which draws from the bank as well as gold on hand, and it has no payer-selection or unpriced-rescuer branch.

what: Given a dungeon level and a player's skill against an item's difficulty, it determines how much of an unidentified item's identity is revealed: Mostly on dungeon levels 1-5 when skill meets difficulty, Partial when the skill shortfall is under the gap threshold, and Barely otherwise.
ev: It applies the same rule order (Mostly when skill meets difficulty and the floor is 5 or shallower, Partial for a gap under 20, Barely otherwise), but it takes a character and item rather than a dungeon level, skill, and difficulty, and it rounds skill and difficulty to integers before comparing, which can flip the result at the 20-point boundary.

what: Computes the level a character lands on after taking a chute, which is the starting level plus the chute's depth (never less than zero), clamped to the range from level 1 to the dungeon's level count.
ev: The line `to = Math.Clamp(asked, 1, _dungeon.Count)` with `asked = from + Math.Max(0, depth)` computes the same destination as the C++ function, but it sits inside a larger routine that also handles party members, the limited-version denial, damage, and lost-position flags.

what: Rounds a non-negative value to the nearest whole number using round-half-to-even (banker's rounding), following the SRD's CInt convention for the game's calculations.
ev: `(int)Math.Round(d, MidpointRounding.ToEven)` is round-half-to-even returning an int, which matches the C++ `roundHalfEvenNonNeg` for non-negative input (Mordor.App/MazeView.cs MazeView.CInt is an identical copy).

what: Reports whether a companion slot is still active in the game, meaning it is occupied and neither dead nor stoned (in Normal death state).
ev: No candidate returns a live-companion predicate; the closest, Companion.IsDead inside CompanionSlots.Rearrange, is only a refusal check in drag-and-drop, and nothing tests `occupied` together with `deathState == Normal`.

what: Computes a spell's magnitude for a given spell level, returning a blank result when the spell's Base is blank and otherwise the damage and heal modifiers derived from its base and power terms.
where: Mordor.Core/Rules.cs Rules.SpellDamage (and Rules.SpellHeal, which uses the same base/power/level formula)
ev: The candidates share the base-plus-level-log-plus-power formula, but they return a sampled damage or heal amount rather than a damage and heal modifier pair, and none has the blank-Base early return.

what: Computes the gold needed to reach the next level for a character at the given level, using the wiki's formula with the gold-factor multiplier applied to the floored base amount.
ev: Both compute the gold needed for the next level from the guild level and gold factor, but Fn12B2 uses the original VB loop summation with x87 rounding, not the C++ wiki closed-form floor formula, so the outputs can differ.

what: Stores a pending person offer (kind "person", the person's name, and their level) into the session's feature state so it persists until the player answers it.
ev: The C++ function stores a pending "person" offer (kind, name, level) in session featureState so it persists until answered, and no candidate does this: the closest, CityWindow.LocatePerson, runs a locate-character service with a fee and confirmation but never writes any pending-offer state to a session dictionary.

what: Returns true when a character counts as a casualty of a party wipe, meaning their current hits are at or below zero or they are stoned (rule R5, step 2).
ev: The loop skips anyone with `CurHits > 0 && !IsDead && !Stoned` and treats everyone else as a casualty, which embeds the same test as `isWipeCasualty` but adds an `IsDead` check and is not a standalone predicate; SelectNextAble uses the inverse condition for a different purpose.

what: Prunes a single party member who has died or been stoned, removing them from the party and moving the surviving members to the leader's location, with an optional death announcement (R11, R12).
ev: The per-member rules match (stay if alive with hits and not stoned, zero hits, announce only on the leader's level, mark dead, save, remove, move survivors to the leader's position), but RemoveTheDead loops over the whole party instead of pruning one index, and it has no `announce` flag.

what: Resolves one character's turn in combat by retargeting, skipping the action if paralysed, and otherwise announcing the character's standing order (Fight, Defend, or Spell) to the player.
where: Mordor.Core/Combat.cs, CharacterActs (enclosing class name not shown in the candidate header)
ev: Candidate 3 has the same structure as characterAct (paralysis skips the character, then the standing order is dispatched by kind), but it resolves the Fight and Spell actions rather than only announcing them, and the visible excerpt does not show a Defend branch.

what: Skips over one JSON value starting at the given position in a text buffer, handling strings, nested objects/arrays, and bare tokens, and advances the position past it so the parser can continue reading a mod manifest.
ev: None of the eight candidates parses JSON. They cover WinHelp topic decoding, LZMA decoding, and help-window hit-testing, so nothing skips a JSON string, object, array, or bare token in a mod manifest.

what: At the start of a fight, each party member who has no combat order yet is given one derived from the combat setting (currently hardcoded to 0, which maps to no order), following the standing-orders rule R10.
ev: For each member with no order it applies the Combat Setting through ApplyDefault and keeps the aimed target, which matches the C++ loop; the C++ hardcodes setting 0 (which yields None), while the candidate reads the setting from the character and also handles the spell and item branches.

what: Reports whether the party member at the given index is a dead character currently being carried by another party member, which the game's carrying rules depend on.
ev: No candidate returns whether a given member is a dead body carried by another member, but PickUpBody's filter `_party.Members.All(m => m.CarryingCharacter != c.Name)` tests whether a dead character is already carried by a party member, which is only part of isCarriedBody's logic (no carryingSlot check, no index-based self lookup, and a different purpose).

what: Matches a typed option against the declared options case-insensitively, returning its index or -1, with an empty input never matching (the R16 quirk for empty Defaults).
ev: ChoiceOf does the same case-insensitive exact match of the typed value against the declared options, but it returns the option string rather than its index, falls back to the default or first option instead of -1, and has no explicit empty-input rule.

what: Presents a rescue offer to the player by emitting a "rescue.offer" message naming the character, leaving the actual presentation to the host.
ev: This is the host-side presentation of the rescue offer for a dead character, which is the part the C++ comment leaves to the host, but it also stops the combat clock, hides panels, and sets button state, far beyond the C++ single `ctx.say("rescue.offer", ...)` event emit.

what: Computes a critical-hit or backstab chance from a raw roll value by scaling it against the band's divisor k and clamping the result to the band's lo/hi limits.
ev: It computes a crit or backstab chance and clamps it to a floor and cap, the same overall shape as the C++, but its input is guild, monster and weapon levels through a log formula rather than the C++'s raw roll scaled by `k` and clamped to `lo`/`hi`.

what: Decides where a healing spell goes in the companion routine: nobody if the heal target flag is 0, monsters as damage if the heal was passed to a slot, and the party otherwise.
ev: No candidate picks a heal's route from the target flag and slot-passing, but CompanionCasts describes the same rule: a companion's heal is thrown at monsters as damage, and with M5B1D at 0 it reaches no monster.

what: Computes a spell's protection value at cast time as one plus half the caster's spell level, rounded down (Protection = Int(CasterSpellLevel / 2) + 1).
where: Mordor.Core/SpellThrown.cs Companion.Apply (the `Apply` method; its doc comment states Protection is the caster's spell level halved plus one, citing MAINMOD2.BAS:1046)
ev: Both the C++ function and this candidate compute Protection as the caster's spell level halved, rounded down, plus one, and Candidate 1's comment quotes the same `Int(casterSpellLevel / 2) + 1` formula, though the truncated text shows only the comments and not the arithmetic line itself.

what: Saves a party member to the given dungeon level and square by placing them in the occupants of that square's area, which is the rule for where a displaced or teleported character ends up on the floor.
ev: MoveDown sets the character's level, X, Y, and area from the floor's area at that square, which matches the location part of saveOnFloor, but it does not add the character to the floor's occupant list, and it has no level-bounds check or area-range fallback.

what: Returns the level-gap gate percentage (90, 50, or 10) for a given level difference, with the mapping from gap to value being an unconfirmed assumption in the source.
ev: Both return 90/50/10 from a level comparison, but LevelGapChance takes two guild levels and uses a quarter-of-monster-level band, while the C++ takes a single gap and uses fixed cutoffs at 0 and 2, so the thresholds and inputs differ.

what: Rolls a percent chance (currently a placeholder fixed at 50%) for a companion's friendly-fire attack, applying to every companion rather than only spitters.
ev: Candidate 2 makes the same kind of friendly-fire draw for every companion, whether or not it can spit, but it uses the spit mishap odds from CompanionMishap.Victim and picks the victim from the party, not the fixed 50% percent roll that the C++ placeholder returns as a bool.

what: Reads a named integer field for one of the twelve Hall of Records entries from session feature state and parses it into a number, which the hall check and description logic use to compare or show records.
ev: No candidate looks up a named string field for one Hall record from session state and parses it to an integer; the closest, Candidate 2 (OriginalSaves.cs ReadHall), reads typed fields from a save file, and Candidate 8 (HallRecords.cs Fresh) only seeds values.

what: Converts a hall-of-fame stat value into its stored form by multiplying it by kHallStatMultiplier (10000), which the header comment identifies as a death/raise rule (R22) encoding.
ev: No candidate scales a hall stat value by 10000 or encodes it for storage; the closest, Candidate 5's `ReadHall`, reads stored values back without any multiplier, and the others handle records, guilds, or display formatting.

what: Computes the guild-use level a player needs to use an item, as a real number: the item's level-scale factor multiplied by a guild-dependent factor (plus 2.97 times that factor), with a floor of 1.0.
ev: The candidate has the same formula and the same floor of 1, but it rounds to an integer with banker's rounding, while the C++ compares the unrounded real value, so a level like 2.4 is treated differently.

what: Finds the best ability chance across the character's joined guilds, returning the highest per-guild chance for the given ability (per the Mordor guild rules R34.2/R35).
ev: It loops the guilds the character belongs to, computes each guild's AbilityChance with the same dungeon and monster-guild arguments, and returns the highest, or 0 when none apply, which matches the C++ loop over joined guilds and its per-guild abilityChance call.

what: Decides whether a monster is quest-rare by checking that the roll chance is below the kRareChanceBelow threshold (10).
ev: The C++ function is a bare threshold test (chance < 10) for quest-rare monsters, and no candidate does that check; the closest, Rules.cs table.QuestMonster, only describes the quest-rare rejection inside a larger class-selection loop without the <10 test itself, and the other candidates cover chest drops, level gaps, raise, identify, and paralysis rolls.

what: Pauses the combat clock for an encounter in the same area by zeroing its countdown and announcing that the combat clock is paused.
where: Mordor.App/DungeonWindow.axaml.cs if.SameAreaReload (closest context only; it does not pause anything)
ev: No candidate zeroes an encounter countdown or announces a paused combat clock; SameAreaReload is the same-area path, but its doc comment says the original's clock-off is "Not modelled" and "the port's clock goes on," and CombatTick and OfferRescue only gate the clock on the dead screen or minimising.

what: Formats a boolean as the text "True" or "False" for writing to data output, with no game-specific meaning.
ev: It uses the same `value ? "True" : "False"` mapping, but it returns void and persists the text via `Write` instead of returning the string, so the outcome differs.

what: Tests whether a creature's old-age percentage roll has reached the threshold (pct >= kOldAgePct, the 98% rule from R18) for the old-age death check.
ev: It applies the same 98% old-age threshold (`pct < 98` returns false), but it then adds a random 5%-plus-log death roll, whereas the C++ function only returns whether `pct >= 98`.

what: Rolls a percentage check against a companion-derived stone value, and if the roll fails the target becomes stoned and loses all its hits.
ev: The doc comment says a companion's blow runs the stone's constitution test and gates the stone on the companion's CON, which is the caller-side part of companionBlowStones, but the visible body is truncated before any stone roll, so the percent check and the stoned/hits=0 outcome are not shown.

what: When the party's leader moves away, any other party members still standing on the leader's square and floor are hidden, marked dead if they have no hit points left, and have their location set to the area of the floor below (per the chute "left behind" quirk).
ev: MoveDown sets a chute-faller's area to the same square's area on the floor below, which matches the C++ area assignment, but no candidate hides members on the leader's square (`visible = false`) or does the leftover-on-square selection that resolveChuteLeftBehind performs.

what: Splits a chest's gold pot evenly among a number of shares, with integer division that discards any remainder and returns zero when there are no valid shares.
ev: The C++ `pot / shareCount` (integer division, zero when no valid shares) matches `GoldShare.Share`, which returns `CLng(pot / partySize)` with the same divisor clamp to at least 1, though it rounds half to even instead of truncating and does not return zero for a non-positive count.

what: Decides what a buffer does when fired in combat: a spell buffer is cast immediately or kept as a standing order depending on whether monsters are in front, and an item buffer uses its pack item now, with an empty or invalid slot doing nothing.
ev: FireBuffer does the same thing as the C++: an item buffer uses its pack slot now and an empty or invalid slot does nothing, while a spell buffer becomes the standing order during a fight and is otherwise cast, with an out-of-range spell index doing nothing. It differs only in that it acts directly instead of returning a BufferFire value, and the monsters-in-front check is read from state and delegated to CastKnownSpell.

what: Rerolls the who's facing direction at random (0-based, from the rng) and marks the facing as lost, the rotator-loss effect of the game.
ev: It is the rotator-square effect and sets the lost-facing flag, but it gates that on a perception roll and never rerolls the facing to a random direction, which the C++ function does unconditionally.

what: Rolls a percentile check against a threshold to decide whether a character loses one point of natural Constitution during a raise, following rule R26.
ev: It computes the same percentile threshold (`Rnd * 100 < 50 - CON * 2`) that rollConLoss compares against, but it neither makes the draw nor removes a point of CON, and no candidate does both.

what: Reports whether a character's stat part is held, which is false when the character is paralysed and true otherwise, per game rule R6.
where: Mordor.Core/Character.cs Character.Unparalyse (with Character.Paralyse as its counterpart)
ev: No candidate is a bool predicate returning whether the stat part is held, but Unparalyse and Paralyse both key the stat part's removal and restoration on whether ParalysisLevel is nonzero, which is the same paralysed-or-not condition as the C++ function.

what: Reports whether a mod is enabled for a given mod id by reading that mod's stored "Enabled" flag from the settings store, defaulting to disabled when no value is stored.
ev: It calls `ReadFlag(modId, "Enabled", false)`, which reads the mod's stored "Enabled" flag and falls back to false when nothing is stored, the same as the C++ `readStoredFlag(store, modId, "Enabled", false)`.

what: Returns true when one alignment is Good and the other is Evil, enforcing rule R2 that Good and Evil characters cannot share a party.
where: Mordor.Core/Party.cs Party.Opposed (the candidate named `is.Opposed`; the enclosing class name was not shown in the excerpt)
ev: The method has the same two-clause Good/Evil test as `oppositelyAligned` and returns true only for a Good-Evil pair in either order; it differs only in using the `Alignment` enum type and being a static method.

what: Rolls a percentile check to decide whether a character resists a chest's disease, succeeding when a random roll falls below half the character's resistance value.
ev: The disease branch runs the same test as chestDiseaseTakes, `rng.NextDouble() * 100 < ResistancePercent(c, ResistDisease, item) / 2.0`, with the resistance computed from the character instead of passed in, and it sets the disease when the roll succeeds.

what: Reads one monster record from a binary buffer at a given offset, filling in its resistance, item-slot, box-chance and stat words plus the special property, special attack and spell flag longwords, and returns false if any read runs past the buffer.
ev: LoadMonsters reads the same monster record and fills the same resistance, item, box-chance, stat and three special dword fields, but it reads them in a different order, interleaved with many other fields, and it loops over the whole file rather than reading one record at an offset with a bool result.

what: Emits the companion drift message to the player through the event sink, but only when the companion's binding is zero or higher.
ev: Round sets `Drifted` to the "has broken a level of binding!" line when the binding is still at or above zero, which matches the C++ branch, but it also emits a different "is becoming restless!" line when the binding drops below zero, and nothing gates the say on the sign, which the C++ does.

what: Handles the player's town-menu request to join a guild for a chosen party member, refusing if they are already in it or cannot pay or qualify, and reports the outcome as a message.
ev: The C++ `doJoin` refuses an already-joined guild, attempts `joinGuild` (which charges the fee and checks eligibility), and reports success or refusal, and JoinVisitedGuild covers the payment and refusal paths. It differs because it adds a confirm prompt, a cursed-gear check, and re-acquaint switches the active guild instead of printing "already in".

what: Checks whether a character currently has a given game effect active by scanning the character's list of active effect ids and returning true if the effect is present.
ev: No candidate tests whether a character currently has an effect active; the closest, Candidate 8's SpellEffects bit-set update, applies or sets effects rather than checking membership in a list of active effect ids.

what: Reports a companion's kill to the mod/event system by emitting a "companion.kill" message for the owner character, without changing the owner's kill count.
ev: Both report a companion's kill to the mods as a Companion-kind kill for the owner without changing the owner's Kills, but the candidate also skips the report when DamageDealt is unset or the victim is no longer in the fight, which the C++ does not check.

what: Decides whether a group may cast a spell this round, which is only allowed if no spell has yet been used and the group's attack has not ended.
where: Mordor.Core/Combat.cs CombatEngine.CastDamage (candidate 1, which holds the spell-cast flow)
ev: None of the candidates contains a `spellUsed`/`attackEnded` gate. CastDamage is the only one that deals with the per-round spell cast, but it is about damage and captions, not the permission check that R38 defines.

what: Builds the label shown beside a guild log entry ("TODAY: ", "1 DAY AGO: ", or "N DAYS AGO: ") from the absolute number of days between the entry's day and the current day.
ev: It takes the absolute day gap, returns "TODAY: " for zero, "1 DAY AGO: " for one, and "N DAYS AGO: " otherwise, the same outputs as glPrefix for every input.

what: Returns true when a quest item's spawn weight is at or below the threshold kQuestRareItemMaxWeight (4), marking that item as rare under rule R34.
ev: The C++ function returns true when spawnWeight <= 4, but no candidate tests a rarity or spawn-weight threshold of that kind; the closest is QuestItemBand, which computes a tier band for item quests (tier/1.5 + 1), an unrelated calculation that only shares the "quest item" context.

what: Puts down a carried dead body, clearing the carrier's record of it and freeing the party's carrying slot, and announces "You put down the body."
ev: Its character branch clears `CarryingCharacter` and returns a "no longer carrying" line, matching the C++ body put-down, but it also releases a carried companion and returns null otherwise, which the C++ function (with companions deferred elsewhere) does not do, and its message text is not confirmed to be "You put down the body."

what: Finds the port tree root by returning the index of the nearest ancestor folder that contains Mordor.sln (rule R1), or -1 if none does.
ev: No candidate searches the ancestor chain for a Mordor.sln file and returns the index of the nearest match; GameFolder.Raw walks the same nearest-first parent chain but yields candidate game-art folders, and DirectoryDialog.Ask builds an ancestor chain only to display it.

what: Returns true when the number of worn items of a class is below the wear cap, so another item of that class may be worn.
where: Mordor.Core/Character.cs Character.WornOfClass (with Character.MaxWornOfClass supplying the cap)
ev: No candidate performs the `wornOfClass < cap` comparison; WornOfClass gives the count and MaxWornOfClass gives the cap, but the C# treats a cap of 0 or -1 as uncapped, while the C++ would block wearing when cap is 0.

what: Shifts a Seer-revealed spot's coordinates by a random offset within the blur radius, per rule R64 (the blur mapping is unspecified, so the offset range is an assumed interpretation).
ev: Both are random offsets to a Seer-revealed spot clamped to the map, but Seer.Blur uses a spread of Int(Rnd*spread) with a random sign and clamps to 1..size, while seerBlurSpot draws a uniform offset in [-(r-1), r-1] with no clamping and a radius-1 span, so the blur mapping differs.

what: Resolves the R34 melee draw by returning true with probability 100/(living companions + 1), so the character is picked only when a random roll falls under that threshold (negative companion counts are treated as zero).
ev: Its first step gives the character (-1) with probability 1/(count+1) over living companions, the same gate as the C++ draw, but it is written as the complement (count/(count+1)) and then goes on to pick a companion slot, which the C++ function does not do.

what: Clamps a limited-build spell's level to kLimitedBuildTeleportCap when the limited build is active, so the level used for the later fall and rock tests is capped.
ev: Both clamp a level to the limited build's last level when the limited build is on, but Clamp is the level-change check (fn0A0B) that also returns a "Request to go to Level N is Denied" message, and it does not implement the spell-specific kLimitedBuildTeleportCap clamp used before the fall and rock tests.

what: Moves the party to a new location by setting its x and y coordinates and dungeon level from the given Location, as used when a spell (passwall or teleport/displace) relocates the party.
ev: Both set the party's dungeon level, x and y to the given position in one step; PlaceAt takes (level, x, y) and writes them to every member, since OpenDejenol stores position per character rather than on the party.

what: Dispatches the player's typed "pen" command to either the buy or sell handler, and returns a usage message when the command is missing or malformed.
ev: The C++ `cmdPen` parses the typed "pen buy"/"pen sell" words and returns a usage message, but no candidate does this command parsing; the candidates are pen-stock, click-handling, and window-setup methods.

what: When a town autoload runs, it walks the remembered party members, announces each one's outcome to the player (load error, not here, dead, opposite alignment, or joined), adds eligible members to the party, and then prunes the dead.
ev: LoadFor walks the saved party members with the same outcomes (not here, dead, opposite alignment, joined) and the dead-leader check, but it reads from disk instead of taking a remembered list, handles a failed load with a question rather than the "error occurred" line, has no full-party stop, and does not call the prune (that is Candidate 2's PruneTheDead).

what: Decides whether a character can cast a given spell in a guild, comparing the spell's level and the guild's spell maximum against the member's guild level, and computes the spell level shown to the player (floored from level times rate).
ev: CanCast matches the C++ canCast gate (SpellMax > 0, level <= max, rate <= 0 treated as 1, unrounded compare against guildLevel/2 + 0.5), but it does not return shownLevel, which is only in GuildDefs.ShownSpellLevel (same file).

what: After a chest trap, it applies the damage to current hit points with round-half-even rounding, sets hit points to 0 if the result drops below 1, and caps the result at the 32-bit integer maximum.
ev: Spring's Exploding and Fire trap branches do the R4 step, `CurHits = (int)Math.Round(CurHits - dmg, MidpointRounding.ToEven)`, but nothing in the candidates clamps the result at 0 (R5) or caps it at the 32-bit maximum, and the C++ function is a standalone helper that returns the new hit points.

what: Handles a character's attempt to join the party from the city, refusing with the matching message when the leader is dead, the party is full, the character is already in, not present, has the wrong password, or is opposed in alignment, and otherwise restoring the joiner's hit and spell points and adding them to the roster.
ev: It repeats the leader-dead, party-full, password, opposed-alignment and restore-then-join steps, but it is a UI handler that asks the player for the name and password, lists dead characters as joinable instead of refusing them without a pending raise, and does not show the explicit already-in-party or not-here refusals.

what: After a party member dies in a party of more than one, this saves that character, removes the dead from the party, and refreshes the party display for the player, with no rescue offered.
ev: Its party branch saves the character, prunes the dead, and returns with no rescue offer, matching the C++ sequence, but it first runs an extra Sub0930Head (companions, carried body, status recomputation) that the C++ function lacks, and it also covers the solo case.

what: Casts the Sanctuary spell by recording the caster's current party position (x, y, and dungeon level) as the sanctuary point and announcing to the player that sanctuary is set there.
ev: Its Set Sanctuary case records the caster's square as the sanctuary point (with l01B6 = -1 and a "thrown" line), which matches the C++ core, but it is one case inside a larger spell-dispatch method and does not return the point or match the C++ announcement wording.

what: Returns true when a character is dead and the party has been reduced to just that one member, which is the condition that triggers the dead-character screen under the game's rule R4.
ev: Candidates 2, 3, 5 and 8 all read a `DeadScreenOwed` property, but none of the shown candidates defines it or computes "IsDead and party size == 1" itself, so the predicate's definition is missing from the candidate set.

what: Rearranges a companion's party slots by swapping the two chosen slots' records, and moves the carry marker along with whichever companion it was holding, if the command's member/slot arguments are valid.
ev: It is the same drag-and-drop slot swap that cmdRearrange performs (both cite FRMCHAR3.BAS:763-779), but it refuses to move dead companions, skips empty slots instead of swapping whole records, and does not move the carry marker.

what: Handles the player's typed "use" command on a consumable or charged pack item in town, checking the slot and charges, then reporting either the item's use or why it could not be used.
ev: It runs the same `ItemUse.Problem` charge and usability check and then spends the charge and applies the item's effect for non-spell items, but it is a dungeon sheet button rather than a town typed command, and for spell items it casts through `UseItemSpell` instead of refusing with "its spell effect is not wired yet, so no charge was spent."

what: Builds a LiveMod's display title from its manifest, using the mod's name (or id when the name is blank) followed by its version if one is set, per formula F2 of chapter 21.
ev: Describe applies the same rule (manifest name trimmed, or id when the name is blank, then " " plus the version when one is set), but it takes a save-tag string like "id@version" and looks the mod up among discovered mods, instead of taking the manifest directly as modDisplayTitle does.

what: Computes the next award level for a character by adding the step interval to the current level, or returning the current level unchanged when the interval is zero or negative.
ev: It also computes the next level as the current level plus a step, but it uses the absolute value of the current level, caps the result at a Max, and has no branch that returns the current level for a non-positive step.

what: Reports whether the quicksand trap flag is set on the square the party is standing on, which in the game suppresses perception while the character is in quicksand (the party argument is unused).
ev: Look computes `standingInQuicksand = fl.Has(x, y, Floor.QUICKSAND)` and skips the quicksand announcement only when standing in quicksand, which matches the suppression, but it is embedded in a larger look-ahead routine rather than being a standalone predicate, and it still records the quicksand bit to the map.

what: Returns true when a special item type value falls in the guild crest range (500 through 500 + kGuildCount − 1), marking the item as a crest belonging to one of the game's guilds.
ev: It returns true when `SpecialType` is in `[GuildIssuedBase, GuildIssuedBase + GuildData.All.Count)`, the same 500 to 500+guildCount−1 range as the C++ check, differing only in taking an `Item` instead of a raw int.

what: Checks whether a party member number entered for a typed swap falls within the valid range of 1 to kPartyMaxSize, so out-of-range slots can be refused.
ev: Party.Swap refuses out-of-range party positions using 0-based indices checked against Members.Count, but it also performs the swap, and no candidate checks a single 1-based party number against 1..kPartyMaxSize; Character.SwapSlots does a similar 1-based range check, but for item slots with different limits.

what: Reports whether a spell level is the special level 50 reserved for item-only spells, which players cannot cast directly.
ev: The C++ function only tests whether a spell level equals the special item-only value 50, while no candidate performs that check; CastLevel is the closest related candidate but only resolves an item's cast level (falling back to the caster's spell level when SpellLvl is 0), so it does not identify item-only levels at all.

what: Parses a typed gold amount from the "give gold" command into a number, following VB's Val rules (skipping leading blanks, reading an optional sign, then digits and at most one decimal point, and stopping at the first unusable character).
ev: It matches giveVal's leading-blank skip, optional sign, digits, single point, and stop at the first unusable character, but it also skips blanks between digits, so "1 2" gives 12 where giveVal gives 1.

what: Resolves a rock death from the 1995 Mordor rules (R54): when a caster in the party triggers it, the caster and the members after them (plus those before them if the caster is in slot 0 or 1) are killed by rock, with automap records and a "walked into solid rock" message logged.
ev: It builds the same victim list (caster slot onward, plus slots 0 to k-1 only when k <= 1), kills each with the rock cause, records rock on the automap for living bodies, logs "You walked into solid rock!" when it completes, and stops early for a caster in slot 2 or later; the differences are that it passes `Rules.DeathRock` where the C++ passes `DeathCause{}`, and it does not call a party prune step.

what: Resolves a member word typed in a "spells <member>" command to a 0-based party index, accepting either a 1-based party position or a member name, and returns -1 if no valid member matches.
ev: It maps a 1-based party digit to a 0-based index with a range check against the party size, as the digit branch of townMemberOf does, but it works from key presses rather than a typed word and does not resolve member names, which townMemberOf also does via memberIndex.

what: After each turn, if the forced-settle flag bit is set in the game flags, it triggers the area settlement routine (SettleArea) to resolve the forced settle for the party's floor.
ev: The guard `if (_forceSettle) SettleArea();` matches the C++ flag-gated call to settleArea, but the candidate also prints LookAheadLines() after it, which the C++ function does not do.

what: Computes a character's maximum spell points as 5 times the sum of their natural Intelligence and Wisdom (rule R21).
ev: It computes (Stats[Int] + Stats[Wis]) * 5 from the natural stats, which is the same formula and inputs as the C++ maxSP, and its doc comment confirms the natural-stat choice.

what: Decides whether a chest is available at the player's current location: a chest tied to an encounter area is only available in that same area, while chests with no encounter source or a non-positive area are available anywhere.
ev: It returns true when there is no Encounter source or the room's area is <= 0, and otherwise true only when the fight's room equals `_loadedArea`, the area the player stands in, which matches the C++ logic (the only difference is that it compares the full level and area tuple rather than area alone).

what: Applies the chest teleporter trap: if the party has more than one member, a valid opener is moved to a randomly drawn destination square (y set to 0), while a solo opener sees "The room is settled." and nothing moves.
ev: It matches the C++ core (a lone opener is not moved and the room is settled at once, while in a party only the opener moves), but it takes its destination from a precomputed `Teleported` record instead of drawing one, uses 2D coordinates rather than the C++ `location.x = dest, y = 0` mapping, and adds lost-state, log, and area side effects.

what: Computes the gold cost of a level-L combat audit by summing the running total of (2i-1)×30.1 gold steps with per-step rounding, then scaling that total by a guild-gold multiplier of (1 + guildGold/10).
ev: Fn12B2 uses the same algorithm (a running total rounded each step over (2i-1)*30.1, then scaled by 1 + guildGold/10), but it evaluates each step in x87 extended precision, so at level 3 a half-value like 150.5 rounds up to a running total of 271 where the C++ double arithmetic gives 270, and the outputs differ.

what: Rolls a d3000 percentile-style check against the join bar computed from the target's charisma and found level, returning true when the roll is at or below the bar so the creature agrees to join the party.
ev: FillGroup's comment at lines 1948-1967 places the join-offer decision, but the snippet is cut off before any comparison against a bar or a d3000 roll, and no candidate shows a joinBar-equivalent computed from charisma and level.

what: When a fight starts, it applies a member's CombatSetting to set their standing order to fight, defend, or a recorded spell buffer, or clears the order, and reports whether a pack item should be used instead.
ev: ApplyDefault sets the same fight, defend, and spell-buffer orders as the C++ function, but it returns nothing instead of a UseItem signal (that item branch lives in DungeonWindow.CombatSettingItem), it does not clear the order for settings 7..12, and it has no member-exists check.

what: Decides whether a cast's points are spent, returning true only when a target was successfully chosen and the caster was not killed by a teleport (rule R16).
ev: CastAndThrow returns "" without spending when the target box is cancelled and spends points only after the effect, which covers the "target chosen" half of R16, but no candidate has the teleport-death exclusion (Interact.FellFromTeleport only produces the death message).

what: When a chest item is taken, it applies the chest-drop curse, and if the item is cursed with kind 2 and is wearable, it equips itself to the character and announces that the item has attached itself to them.
ev: Candidate 1 matches only the Cursed == 2 test that decides whether the item attaches, and candidate 4 (DungeonWindow.TreasureFrom) calls it during the chest loop, but no candidate applies the chest-drop curse, checks wearability, equips the item, and emits the "attached itself" message as the C++ function does.

what: Rolls a d(kNoticeRange) and returns whether the result is at or below the character's perception value, implementing the game's notice check (R37), though at perception 100 it always passes, which conflicts with the design note.
ev: It makes the same roll, `rng.Next(100) + 1 <= perception`, which matches the C++ `below(kNoticeRange) + 1 <= perception` if kNoticeRange is 100, but it adds a teleporter exemption that always passes, so the outcome differs for that bit.

what: Looks up a combat spell's monster and group targeting caps (numM and numG) from its spell definition, returning zeros if the spell index is invalid.
ev: No candidate looks up a spell's numM/numG targeting caps; the closest, Combat.cs at.CastSpell and CastDamage, handle casting and damage, and SpellHitsOn computes damage and resistance per monster without reading any caps.

what: Decides whether a square's perception check succeeds by taking the chance as perception minus exclusions, always passing at 100 or more, always failing at 0 or less, and otherwise rolling against that percentage.
ev: The C++ function passes when `Rnd*100 < perception - exclusions` with clamps at 100 and 0, and NoticesAnything uses a similar perception roll with a teleporter exemption but has no exclusions term and no clamps, while PerceiveAhead.Look uses the same `Rnd*100 < perception` roll without exclusions or clamps.

what: Serializes a list of guild log entries (guild index, day-serial stamp, and text) into a little-endian byte buffer with a count header and length-prefixed text, for saving to a file.
ev: It writes the same layout as the C++ function (an entry-count header, then per entry a 4-byte guild, an 8-byte day stamp, a 4-byte text length, and the text) to a file rather than a returned buffer, and it encodes text as UTF-8 where the C++ copies raw bytes.

what: Looks up a stored knowledge record for a given monster or item kind and name in the session's feature state and returns the requested field (such as a knowledge grade), or an empty string if no record exists.
ev: No candidate looks up a value by a composite key of prefix, kind, name, and field in a session feature-state dictionary; the nearest, Librarian.cs `holds.SettleMonsterKeys`, re-keys and merges monster entries rather than reading one field.

what: After a peaceful-spell cast succeeds while foes are present and the party is not yet engaged, the party is marked as engaged in combat and the player is told "Party engaged."
ev: The C++ function engages the party after a successful peaceful-spell cast with foes present, and CastInCombat's `!Engaged` branch with monsters waiting likewise runs the gate first and only a passing spell starts the fight (via EngageWaiting), but the C++ engage-on-success rule is not reproduced exactly: CastInCombat engages only for items (not spell orders), and no candidate sets an engaged flag on a successful non-combat cast.

what: When a new character joins the party, places them on the leader's square with the same lost flags, restores their HP and SP to full, adds them to the party, then runs the companion carry and prunes any dead members.
ev: This candidate is the calling join flow, which shares the leader's lost flags via `Party.ShareLostFlags` and restores HP and SP to full per its doc comment, but the visible body is truncated before the append, companion carry, and dead-pruning steps, and it does not show the leader-square copy.

what: Computes the standard price of an item from its ECV score (scaled by a fixed multiplier and rounded half-to-even), using attack, defense, hits, and strength stats.
ev: No candidate computes an ECV score or multiplies it by a constant to get a standard price; they all price items from base value, stock count, charges, or alignment (e.g., `StoreStock.PriceOf`, `Confinement.PriceToBuy`), and `AttDefWorth` only adjusts attack/defence for fit.

what: Returns the electrocution chance percentage (90, 50, or 10) by looking up the band that the character's level relative to the monster's level falls into.
ev: It returns 90, 50, or 10 from the character's level compared with the monster's, using the same quarter-gap bands as the C++ `ratioBand` lookup, though the candidate uses guild level where the C++ comment leaves the engine's level unknown.

what: Decides whether a chute re-runs the square: a chute taken with the TAKE command always re-runs, while a walked chute re-runs only if at least one companion is alive in the party.
ev: The candidate says the square routine is re-run after a chute or TAKE, which is related to the C++ re-run rule, but it has no walked-chute check on companions and no decision function, so it does not match the `aliveCompanions > 0` condition.

what: Re-syncs a companion's stored monster reference by matching its monster ID against the monster table, falling back to the first entry with that ID and leaving the reference unchanged if none matches.
ev: Resolve keeps a valid Ref that matches the Id, otherwise takes the first table entry with that Id and leaves the Ref unchanged if none exists, as the C++ does, but a negative Ref goes to FromId (which uses alignment) instead of the C++ first-Id search, and a MonsterId of 0 has a special case the C++ lacks.

what: Scans the character's pack slots from slot 1 upward (slot 0 being Hands) and returns the index of the first slot holding no item (item ID 0), or -1 if the pack is full.
ev: It scans slots 1 through PackSize-1 and returns the first one that is empty (via SlotEmpty, which also treats a null slot as empty), otherwise -1, which matches the C++ loop over id == 0 from slot 1.

what: Rolls a daily chance each day until a rescue party finds the captive, with the find chance depending on dungeon level and whether the captive is easy to find, and gives up after a day cap.
ev: Candidate 1 has the same loop: the Log(level)² × 100 + 21 threshold, the 10,000/1,000 ceilings, the level-1 area ≤ 18 ceiling of 100, the 0.1 chance floor, the unfloored easy-to-find doubling, the roll-against-chance check, and a day cap, differing only in that the cap is written as the literal 2,000,000.

what: Computes a complicated character's maximum hit points as the base max hits divided by a complication divisor (1.2), truncated to an integer, per the game's R18 rule.
ev: The C++ function is only the max-hits step (MaxHits / 1.2, truncated), and ApplyComplications contains that same step (`c.MaxHits = (int)(c.MaxHits / ComplicationHitsDivisor)`) but also does stat drops, aging, hit refill, and unequipping, so it is a larger function that includes the matching calculation rather than an equivalent one; no candidate computes the divided max hits on its own.

what: When a Control Dragon spell fails, the targeted monster group turns hostile and loses its charmed status, and the player is told the targets respond adversely.
ev: No candidate turns a group hostile and clears its charmed flag after a failed Control Dragon; the closest, CastDamage's "Failed" branch, handles a failed damage spell by setting the order to Fight, and Finish and Capture only build or store group state.

what: Rolls two percentile checks against the character's Constitution-based stoning chance and stone resistance, and returns true only if both fail, meaning the character is turned to stone.
ev: No candidate performs the two-save stoning check (Con-based stoneChance against the stone resistance roll, both rolled, stoned only if both fail); Raising.Resolve and ParalysisPasses only handle raise outcomes and paralysis, respectively.

what: Sets one of eight option flags (no stretch, sound canvas, no party effects, no auto-save, no automap on load, no blinking cursor, no ding, no toolbar) on the options struct, based on the index read from the options file.
ev: Load sets the same eight flags (NoStretch, SoundCanvas, NoDing, NoLoadAutomap, NoToolbar, NoPartyFX, NoAutoSave, NoBlinkCursor) from the options file, but by named key rather than by numeric index, and it also sets other flags (No3d, NoMusic, NoFX, NoHelpSound) that the C++ function does not handle.

what: Reduces the character's age by the requested number of years (365 days each), clamping it at a minimum of 16 years and emitting a "You cannot get any younger." message when the floor is hit.
ev: It subtracts `years * 365` from age, clamps to `16 * 365`, and returns the same "You cannot get any younger." text on the floor, matching the C++; the one difference is that it also returns "You are now {howMany} younger." on ordinary success, where the C++ says nothing.

what: Computes a character's age as a percentage of their race's maximum lifespan (R36), returning 0 when the race has no lifespan, which feeds the old-age death check.
ev: DiesOfOldAge computes the same age-over-lifespan percentage with the same zero-lifespan guard, but only as an internal step of a death roll that returns a bool, not as a value returned to the caller; ComplicationChance is a related version that doubles the lifespan and uses it for a different purpose.

what: Computes the minimum casting cost of a spell as its starting spell level multiplied by a base modifier, rounded half-to-even to an integer.
ev: The candidate computes the spell's cost for a specific character, using a guild-level floor and `Rules.Fn1485Price` with half-to-even rounding, while the C++ function only returns `round(StartSpellLevel * BaseMod)` with no guild logic, so it is a related version rather than the same computation.

what: Raises a companion's binding level by one step at Confinement, charging the owner gold based on the companion's guild level and current binding, and refuses if the companion is already at the life-binding level or the owner cannot pay.
where: Mordor.Core/Character.cs Binding.Cost (with Binding.NextLevel covering the new level)
ev: Binding.Cost computes the same charge as bindingRaiseCharge and Binding.NextLevel the same next level, but no candidate combines the for-life refusal, the gold payment, and the level change that raiseBinding does in one step.

what: Returns true when a character whose top guild level is 5 or lower cannot cover the revival fee from their purse, meaning the guild pays for the revival.
ev: No candidate computes the `topGuildLevel <= 5 && purse < fee` test; candidate 8 (`looked.Visit`) only reads a precomputed `guildPays` flag to skip the charge, and the other candidates cover unrelated guild and identification logic.

what: Reports whether a character is held in place by paralysis, which is true whenever their paralysis level is above zero (rule R16).
ev: It returns the same paralysis level that `isHeld` tests against zero, but it returns the raw int rather than the boolean "held" answer, so a caller would need to add the `> 0` check itself.

what: Rolls a d100 against the target's stoning chance and, if the roll exceeds it, marks the character as Stoned and records a status message.
ev: No candidate rolls a d100 against a stoning chance to set a Stoned death state; Raising.Resolve uses the same `roll > chance` comparator but for raise failure, and CompanionStrikes only reads a stone constitution test inside a companion's blow.

what: Realigns a companion to a chosen alignment if it is offered as an option and the payer can afford the realignment price, deducting that price from the payer's purse.
ev: The candidate computes the same 0.72 cost with doubling for crossing the alignment spectrum (the `priceToRealign` part), but no candidate checks the offered options, charges the payer's purse, or sets the companion's alignment as `realignCompanion` does.

what: Decides whether a buff spell cast during a fight becomes a queued order (BecomesOrder) when monsters are present and a fight is on or the spell is a combat-usable use, otherwise casting it immediately (CastNow).
ev: It returns `MonstersHere && (Engaged || CastGate.UseOf(spell) != SpellUse.NonCombat)`, which is the same condition as the C++ `monstersPresent && (fightOn || use != NonCombat)`, with `true` standing in for `BecomesOrder` and `false` for `CastNow`.

what: Returns whether shelves and pens restock on the party's arrival in town, which happens only when the leader's days-aged counter is above zero.
ev: RestOnArrival handles the town-arrival restock of the store and pens, but its text is truncated before showing the `daysAged > 0` gate, and no candidate has a predicate matching `restocksOnArrival` itself.

what: Settles the party after a level or area change by taking and clearing the forced-settle flag, then either handling a different area, handling a forced settle in the same area, or doing nothing when the area is unchanged and no settle is forced.
where: Mordor.App/DungeonWindow.axaml.cs DungeonWindow.SettleArea (with SameAreaReload as the forced same-area branch)
ev: The candidate takes and clears the forced flag, returns without action when the area is unchanged and not forced, and runs a reload when forced, which matches the C++ branches; but its return value means "a group is waiting" rather than "a settle happened", so the forced same-area case returns false where the C++ returns true, and the C++ floor-lookup early return has no counterpart.

what: Reports whether a square currently has any foe group with members left and a standing front member, which the game uses to decide if the square is still occupied by fighting monsters.
ev: No candidate returns whether any foe group has members left with a standing front member; the nearest, `Combat.cs given.Capture`, recounts living members per group and writes them back into a room record rather than reporting a boolean, and `DungeonWindow.axaml.cs keeps.ShowWaiting` only tests `Any(m => m.Alive)` to pick a display row.

what: When a new game starts, appoints each seeded guildmaster by writing an "appointed" entry for their guild into the guild log, once per session.
ev: Both install each seeded guildmaster who is not yet in place and append an "appointed" guild-log entry for that guild, once on a new game; they differ in that the C++ takes the names as a parameter and guards with a session flag, while Seed uses its built-in table and guards by checking existing holders.

what: Maps the original game's identification code (0 through 3, counting down from All to Barely) to the matching identification level, or Unknown for any other code, which governs how well the player can identify an item.
ev: IdCountdown encodes the same 0-3 countdown correspondence but in the reverse direction (IdLevel to original code, `3 - (int)known`), and it has no Unknown fallback for out-of-range codes, so no candidate maps an int code to an IdLevel the way idLevelFromOriginal does.

what: Picks the target group for a slay-class spell by returning the index of the first group in the encounter that still has living members, or -1 if none do.
ev: RefreshCombat's fallback `groups.FindIndex(g => g.Any(m => m.Alive))` finds the first group with living members, as slayTargetGroup does, but it is embedded in UI code that also rewrites the order target and builds labels, and it does not return a bare group index or -1 as a standalone function (ShowWaiting has the same fallback).

what: Parses a typed party-member number from command text and checks it lies within 1 to the party size limit, reporting failure otherwise.
ev: No candidate parses a typed member number from text and range-checks it against 1..party size; the closest, GiveFlow.Run, chooses a recipient through a name picker and parses gold and item text, not a member number.

what: Picks the chance that a character is recovered from the morgue, using the route taken (their own body or a morgue counter) to choose which chance calculation applies.
where: Mordor.Core/Rules.cs Rules.MorgueRaiseChance (the own-body-style chance; the counter-side chance is Mordor.Core/PendingRaise.cs Morgue.RaiseChance)
ev: No candidate performs the route switch itself, though Rules.MorgueRaiseChance and Morgue.RaiseChance compute chances that look like the two branches (constant +40 versus +10), so the mapping to morgueOwnBodyChance and morgueCounterChance is uncertain.

what: Sends the party list update event to the player-facing output, after recording any newly dead party members so they are counted only once.
ev: CountThenPrune counts each newly dead party member not yet counted, which matches the C++ loop's recording step, and then runs the party-list update via PruneTheDead; but it also logs the death and plays the DIE sound, and it prunes the dead rather than emitting a generic "clock.party_list_update" event.

what: Every swing of a weapon in the monster-round melee counts as one weapon blow by incrementing the character's weaponBlows count, per SRD rule R32.
ev: PlayerSwings loops once per swing of each equipped weapon (`actor.Swings + w.Swings` per hand), which is the swing-counting context R32 describes, but no candidate increments a weaponBlows count, and the C++ function does nothing else.

what: Rolls a random trap bit from 0 to 11, retrying up to a fixed number of times until it hits one of the chest's set trap flags, and returns 0 if none is found.
ev: The core loop matches (draw 0 to 11 and return the first bit set in the trap flags, else 0), but ChestTrap also gates on chest class and a 25/75/90 percent chance, and uses a hard-coded 200-try cap instead of kChestTrapTries.

what: Returns the special-attack share of a monster's range for breath attacks (range divided by the breath divisor) and for acid spit or electrocution (range divided by the spit divisor), using integer division.
ev: Raw uses the same split (range/4 for breath, range/2 otherwise), but only as a floating-point term inside a larger random damage formula, not as a standalone integer-divided share, so it is a related piece rather than the same function.

what: Maps a library knowledge value for a monster (0 for unknown, 1 for seen, 2 for defeated, 3 or more for fully known, with values below 0 treated as unknown) to the matching LibraryKnowledge state.
where: Mordor.Core/Import/OriginalSaves.cs OriginalSaves.Fill (candidate 8) — or, more closely, none maps a stateValue to a knowledge state.
ev: No candidate maps an integer knowledge value (≤0 → Unknown, 1 → Seen, 2 → Defeated, ≥3 → Fully Known) to a state; the closest is Librarian.Merge, which only keeps the max of `Known` values, and OriginalSaves.Fill, which copies the raw `IdLevel` integer without any mapping.

what: Returns the true/false value of an option from the game's INI settings file, treating a missing key as false (SRD rule R2).
ev: Ini.Flag returns false when the key is absent (default "False") and otherwise returns true only when the value equals "True" case-insensitively, which matches the C++ missing-key-is-false rule, though I couldn't see the C++ `parseFlagText` to confirm its exact accepted strings.

what: Finds the index of the last monster in the monster table whose floor is at or above the given tier, which is the boundary used to limit a quest's monster selection by depth, per SRD rule R51.
ev: Its doc describes the same boundary (one before the first monster deeper than the tier, or the class's last monster), but that logic is inlined in a larger random-draw method and searches class ranges rather than scanning the whole table by floor as `endOfTier` does.

what: For a monster's melee attack, applies poison to the victim and then disease, each resolved against the attacker's level.
ev: Spring is the only candidate that inflicts poison or disease with a level, but it is a chest trap (separate traps 1 and 2, each affecting one ailment, rolled against resistance with dungeonLevel), not a monster melee routine that applies poison then disease against attackerLevel.

what: Converts a character's Gold Parameter (GP) into an actual gold modifier using the formula GP/10 + 1 (rule R24 of the Mordor SRD).
ev: Fn12B2 applies the same multiplier shape, `acc + acc * (Gold / 10)`, which equals acc × (Gold/10 + 1), but it is a guild-cost function whose input is the guild record's Gold field, not a character's GP, and no candidate computes `GP / 10 + 1` on its own.

what: Computes the total gold needed to advance from the current character level, summing each level's cost (scaled by the guild gold factor) with per-level rounding, and returns it in currency units.
ev: Fn12B2 takes the same inputs (level and guild gold factor) and builds the same per-level (2i-1)*30.1*(1+gold/10) total, but it rounds the running sum after each level and applies the guild multiplier once at the end, whereas the C++ multiplies each level's step by the factor and rounds that step before summing, so results can differ by a gold unit.

what: Creates a new companion from the front monster in a party, copying its current and maximum Hits, identity, alignment, and level, and marking it as freely joined with the default free-will binding.
ev: AcceptJoin builds each joiner from the front monster's current hits and rolled maximum, binds it at -10 (the free-will binding), and applies the same "all joiners copy the front" quirk, though the visible text is truncated and does not show the level, guild level, or dungeon level copies.

what: Splits a chest's gold equally among the living party members, gives any remainder to a chosen receiver (or the first living member if that receiver is dead), and pays nothing if the opener was killed by the trap.
ev: This is the chest-opening flow that pays the chest's gold and handles an opener killed by the trap, but the equal split among living members and the remainder to a chosen receiver are not in the shown code (the gold split would sit in the unshown OpenChest), and GoldShare.Share only does the equal division, with the dead included and the remainder dropped.

what: Computes the common spell cost for a sheet (spell-sheet charge), using the initial level, guild modifier, school ratio and spell level in a 1.9 multiplier formula, with the result floored at the initial level and returning the initial level when sl is zero.
ev: Both compute a spell cost of the form (level-type value) × (guild/school multiplier) × (rate) × 1.9 / SL, floor it, and clamp to a base value, but Fn1485Price has an extra u4 factor, uses exact BigInteger arithmetic instead of the epsilon, and clamps to `rated` rather than the initial level.

what: Applies damage to a companion by subtracting the amount from its hits, and marks it dead with the Dead death state once hits drop below zero (R27.5, with the threshold taken from R36).
ev: The C++ function subtracts damage from a companion's hits and marks it dead when hits drop below zero, but no candidate does that: the companion-damage paths visible here route damage through the character-only `TakeDamage`, `SetDead` sets character fields, and the truncated `CompanionCasts` loop over companions is not shown far enough to confirm it.

what: Reactivates a previously loaded mod by setting it active again, and for lifecycle-kind mods it announces that the host must call OnEnable and re-note the Harmony patches.
ev: The branch where a loaded, inactive mod is switched on sets it active, calls OnEnable for a lifecycle mod, and re-notes patches, which matches reactivateMod, but Switch also handles unloaded and faulted mods and re-notes patches for non-lifecycle mods, which the C++ does not.

what: Returns whether the Seer can reach a given dungeon level, which is true only for levels at or above the deepest level she can reach (rule R132, where nothing below level 12 is accessible).
ev: Locate rejects any item or monster with `level > Seer.DeepestHeCanReach` as a "Sorry!" message, which is the same depth cutoff as seerCanReach, but it is one step inside a larger search-and-offer flow rather than a standalone predicate that returns whether the level is reachable.

what: Computes the damage a monster's spell deals to a party member, returning 0 if the target is a companion with the magic-immune bit set or if the spell is all-or-nothing and the damage falls short of the target's hit points.
ev: It matches the C++ on the magic-immune companion check (bit 2 zeroes the damage), the all-or-nothing rule for effect 100 (damage is zeroed unless it would kill), and the monster-caster level, though it adds a class-only (effects 75-99) gate the C++ function does not have.

what: Draws a quest level uniformly at random from 1 up to the given cap (inclusive), treating any cap below 1 as 1.
ev: The C++ function draws a uniform random level from 1 to a cap (treating caps below 1 as 1), and none of the eight candidates does a bounded random level draw of that kind; the closest, Rules.QuestMonster, draws a monster class and its tier, not a level.

what: Each tick while the character is not levitating, water (and quicksand) drains hits equal to the dungeon level, and quicksand may also destroy one random pack item via the R71 roll.
ev: It matches the core rule (level-scaled hit loss per tick unless levitating, and a quicksand-only pack-loss roll), but it picks the slot from 1 to PackSlots-1 instead of 0 to kPackSlots-1 and only destroys destructible items, so the outcome differs.

what: Checks whether a character may cast a given spell right now, in order: whether the spell is known, whether the caster's level and spell points suffice, whether an anti-magic area blocks it, whether an item has charges left, and whether an aligned item matches the caster's alignment, returning a refusal reason or None.
where: Mordor.App/DungeonWindow.axaml.cs, CheckCast (labelled box.CheckCast; built from CastGate.Unfit and CastGate.Refuse)
ev: The candidate covers the known, spell-level, points and anti-magic checks in a similar order, but it adds stat, combat-only and non-combat rules the C++ lacks, and it has no item charge or aligned-item check.

what: Computes the worth of an attack or defence (AD) value after alignment fit: full value is kept, adjacent alignment halves it with round-half-even rounding, and opposed alignment negates it.
ev: It maps Fine to raw, Adjacent to `Math.Round(raw / 2.0, MidpointRounding.ToEven)`, and everything else to `-raw`, which matches the C++ Full, Half (round-half-even) and Subtract cases.

what: When the party walks onto a teleporter square, members whose destination differs from the first member's are removed from the party and saved on their landing floor, with any dead members among them marked dead, while the rest stay together.
ev: It implements the same leader-square split (members whose destination differs from the leader's leave the party, per sub0908), but the visible text is truncated before the save-on-floor and dead-marking steps, and it computes destinations itself rather than taking them as input.

what: Returns the trap chance for a chest's treasure class (0 to 3), giving 0 for any out-of-range class, so it sets how likely a chest is to be trapped in the game.
ev: ChestTrap uses the same class-to-chance mapping (25/75/90 percent for classes 1 to 3, 0 otherwise) as trapChanceFor, but it also rolls against that chance and picks a trap index, whereas trapChanceFor only returns the chance value.

what: Checks whether a character may join the party, in SRD order (leader dead, dead joiner in combat, party full, wrong password, opposite alignment, dead without a pending raise), and produces the matching refusal messages for the player.
ev: This candidate is a full UI join flow rather than a pure precondition check, but it covers the leader-dead silent refusal, the full-party message, the dead-in-combat message, and the wrong-password check, while its visible code is truncated before the opposite-alignment and dead-without-pending-raise (R8) refusals.

what: Computes the minimum character level needed to use a guild item, as (use factor + use factor × 2.97) × level scale, floored at 1.
ev: It computes the same `max(1, (f + f × 2.97) × LevelScale)` from the guild's use factor, but it rounds the result to an integer (banker's rounding) where the C++ keeps the unrounded double, so outcomes can differ near level boundaries.

what: Multiplies two 1995 Mordor x87 extended-precision values, rounding the 64-bit mantissa product half to even, with zero short-circuiting to zero.
ev: X87.Round does the same half-to-even rounding of a product to a 64-bit mantissa and returns zero for a zero input, but the candidates do not show the multiply step itself (the product of two X87 values and its sign and exponent handling), which the C++ function performs before rounding.

what: Handles the typed combat command (fight, defend, cast, use), setting party orders or validating and reporting why a spell or item action can't be taken, and returning the reply text shown to the player.
ev: The C++ cast branch refuses a combat cast for a missing spell-point total or a non-combat spell in a fight, and CastSpell makes those same two refusals, but nothing among the candidates parses the typed fight/defend/cast/use command, sets party orders, or resolves the spell name and reachability as combatAction does.

what: Registers the "library" town-screen command, which lets the party look up what it has learned about monsters and items (or search its knowledge) by typed subcommand.
ev: The C++ function only registers a town-screen "library" command with search/monster/item subcommands, and ShowLibrary is the GUI screen that presents the party's learned monster and item records, but no candidate registers a command or parses those subcommands.

what: Given the leader's and followers' float rolls and whether the player chose Yes to Follow Leader, it plans who falls down the chute, who floats and goes nowhere, and whether to ask the Follow Leader question (R57/R58).
ev: The C++ planChuteFall is a pure plan from the leader's and followers' float rolls and the Yes/No Follow Leader choice, deciding who falls, who goes nowhere, and whether to ask the follow question; the closest candidate, DungeonWindow.axaml.cs ChuteFall, carries out the chute fall with rolls, prompts, and level changes interleaved and does not compute a plan from pre-rolled inputs, while Chute.Floats covers only the single-member float check.

what: Halves a character's healing amount, rounding down, while the character has a disease (diseaseLevel above zero), and otherwise returns the heal unchanged.
ev: No candidate halves a heal amount for a diseased character; the closest, Rules.SpellHeal, computes a heal from spell level and power without any disease check, and Companion.Apply only clears disease when a cure spell lands.

what: Returns true when a teleporter draw must reject a given mazeMod value, using a fixed range (1798-1808) taken from the SRD that excludes rock and teleporter squares.
ev: None of the eight candidates handles a teleporter draw, the mazeMod 1798-1808 exclusion range, or rock and teleporter squares; they are all automap display, layout, and mouse-handling code (e.g., AutomapWindow.Draw, RefreshMarks, SquareAt).

what: Rolls a 40% chance, using the context's random number generator, that a neutral lead is peaced.
ev: No candidate makes a fixed 40% roll for whether a neutral lead is peaced; Rules.EngageChance is the closest, but it computes an alignment- and charisma-based chance that a monster attacks, not this 40% peaced roll.

what: Handles the typed "look" command by rejecting extra arguments with a usage message, otherwise returning the Look page text for the current session.
ev: ShowLook renders the Look page's room-occupant list, which is related to what lookText produces, but none of the candidates parses the typed "look" command, rejects extra arguments with "Usage: look", or returns reply text.

what: Raises a companion's Bind level by the given amount, capped at the maximum of 100, and sets the companion to bound and ForLife at that cap, or refuses if the Bind is already ForLife.
ev: BindCompanion also raises a companion's Bind from a spell and sets ForLife for the for-life spell, but it sets the level to a computed value rather than adding an amount, it does not cap at a maximum or refuse on a ForLife companion, and it returns a message string instead of saying through a context.

what: Computes the level a guild member falls back to when forfeiting, subtracting the cost from their current level but never dropping below level 1 (rule R17).
ev: The line `Guild.Level = Math.Max(1, from - cost)` computes the same target level as the C++ function, but it is one step inside a much larger method that also rolls back hit points and unequips gear, and CityWindow.OfferForfeit repeats the same expression only to display the number.

what: Reads a spell's displacement or teleport offsets from a list of values (Right, Forward, and Down for teleport only), failing if fewer than two values are given.
