ev: No candidate parses a list of values into right/forward/down or rejects fewer than two values; `SpellEffect.TeleportTo` uses the same right/forward/down fields but only computes the destination from already-parsed numbers, and nothing else is related.

what: Rolls a random number against the lead monster's box-chance thresholds (with a lair bonus that is currently always zero) to determine which treasure class the chest gets.
ev: With the lair flag false, both take a roll in 0-99 against the two middle BoxChance entries, the higher-indexed hit winning and returning 0, 2 or 3, though the C++ helpers `classFromThresholds` and `lairBonusFor` aren't shown, so their exact behaviour is assumed.

what: Looks up the stored "by" value for a pending rescue of a party member in the session's feature state, returning an empty string if none is recorded.
ev: The C++ `raiseBy` is a plain lookup of the stored "by" value in `s.featureState` that returns an empty string when absent, and none of the eight candidates reads a feature-state dictionary or returns a raiser's name; the closest, `PendingRaise.IsPending` (Candidate 3), only tests `c.RaiseChance > 0`, and `OfferPendingRaise` (Candidates 4 and 5) gets `by` only as an out parameter from `PendingRaise.Accept`, not from stored state.

what: Casting a resistance-raising spell out of combat sets the target's resistance to the matching damage kind to at least 95 percent, and refuses the cast during combat.
ev: It raises the matching resistance kind to a granted value (95) only where it is lower, as the C++ does, but it has no in-combat refusal (that gate sits in the broader Mordor.Modding/ModApi.cs DungeonContext.Cast, which refuses while monsters are present) and it writes SpellResist rather than the resist array.

what: Resolves a pending raise when a body is offered to rejoin the party, refusing if the body can't be raised (in combat or being carried), leaving the raise intact on a decline, and otherwise rolling the stored raise kind and chance to set the character as Raised or Failed.
where: Mordor.App/DungeonWindow.axaml.cs DungeonWindow.OfferPendingRaise (the best match; the combat and carrying refusals sit in the truncated AskToJoin in CANDIDATE 4)
ev: OfferPendingRaise matches the decline path (a No saves the body with its raise intact) and the accept path (it rolls the raise and reports whether the body is raised), but no candidate shows the in-combat and carrying-body refusals or the Declined/Refused outcome structure that askToJoin returns.

what: Returns the character's Constitution score from their ability stats, which the status-effect rules (poison, disease, paralysis, stoning, drain, aging) use as an input.
ev: No candidate just returns the raw Constitution stat, but AilmentTick reads Con as an input to the poison and disease roll, via `EffectiveStat` (which adds gear), not the raw `Stats[Con]` that `baseCon` returns.

what: Registers the town and dungeon player commands "companions", "rearrange", "release", and "carry" so each one can be typed on those screens to list, reorder, release, or carry a party member's companions.
ev: The C++ function only registers the four text commands on the Town and Dungeon screens, and no candidate does that, but CompanionSlots.Release (and the related Rearrange and CompanionCarry.Run candidates) implement the underlying release, rearrange, and carry operations those commands would call.

what: Decides whether buying an item from a shelf, or taking one from a floor, depletes that shelf, which happens when the item comes from a floor or carries an alignment.
ev: The candidate returns `it.Floor > 0 || bought != ItemAlignment.Unaligned`, which is the same boolean expression as the C++ `floor > 0 || bought != ItemAlignment.Unaligned`.

what: Rotates the member, inventory, and companion records for a range of party slots together so that each member's gear and companions move with them when the party roster changes.
ev: No candidate rotates a range of member, inventory, and companion records together; the closest, Roster.Order (CANDIDATE 3), reorders member records by name without moving inventories or companions with them.

what: Computes the spell cost for a character's spell sheet entry as the greater of the initial spell cost (derived from q and r) and the floored value of c, per the SRD's unspecified cost formula that is floored at the initial spell level.
ev: Both compute a spell cost from guild rates and then apply a floor, but Spellbook.Cost derives the cost from the spell level and guild rate and floors it at the smallest rated level, while sheetSpellCost takes a precomputed c and returns the greater of sheetInitialSC(q, r) and floor(c).

what: Rolls the given number of dice with the given number of sides, adds a flat bonus, and returns the total, which the game uses for damage and other random dice results.
ev: No candidate rolls n dice of a given side count and adds a flat bonus; Rules.Fn0DEE draws random numbers but computes a combat damage value with its own formula, not a generic dice roll.

what: Returns the underlying game effect for a party-wide spell variant by subtracting the party-wide base offset (200) from the effect code, and otherwise returns the effect unchanged.
ev: `SpellEffect.Of` subtracts the party offset from the effect when it is at or above `PartyOffset` and otherwise returns the effect unchanged, matching `realEffect`, though it takes a `Spell` rather than a raw int.

what: Computes the join-chance threshold for a monster, starting from the character's natural Charisma and reducing it by the monster's floor level (minus one), never going below zero.
ev: No candidate computes a join-chance threshold from natural Charisma and monster floor; the closest, CompanionInfo.LeaveChance, uses Charisma and binding level for the chance a companion leaves, and Rules.EngageChance uses Charisma for monsters starting fights, so neither matches the C++ formula `max(0, 10*cha - 10*(floor-1))`.

what: Swaps the contents of two pack slots in the exchange window, refusing out-of-range or hand-slot moves (with a "Sorry!" message for out-of-range) and reporting the outcome.
ev: SwapItems refuses slot 0 (Hands) and out-of-range slots and swaps two pack slots between characters, which matches the C++ function's core behavior, but it returns "" silently rather than the C++ "Sorry!" message for out-of-range, and it adds guild-item and worn-item refusals the C++ function lacks; the C++ same-slot and swap logic is also only partially mirrored (SameSlot returns null, a success-like result, not a distinct outcome).

what: Returns the rarity value of the item at the given index in the game data, which the chest-item generation logic uses as a weight when rolling loot.
ev: No candidate returns a single item's Rarity by index; DrawOne and RollDrop read `.Rarity` inline as draw weights inside larger selection logic, and Weight computes a rounded percentage rather than the raw value.

what: Plays the death-cry message "DI-UNDEA" on its own line for the player before the mishap line, unless suppressed.
ev: CompanionCry emits one sound on its own line with no caption under a No Party Sound guard, which matches the shape of mishapDeathCry, but it does not fix the "DI-UNDEA" sound or the death-cry-before-mishap ordering, and no candidate shows that call site.

what: Writes a guild log line recording a character's death, choosing "died somewhere" wording if the level is lost and "died on level N" otherwise.
ev: It writes a guild log entry using `DiedSomewhere` when `LostLevel` is true and `DiedOnLevel` with the dungeon level otherwise, matching the C++ branch, though it also adds the character to `_countedDead`, which the C++ function does not do.

what: Returns the library grade after a read, which is the higher of the current grade and the grade implied by what the character now knows, so the grade only ever rises.
ev: The candidate applies the same rule, mapping All to 4 and Mostly to 3 (else 0) and only raising the stored grade, but it is a store-writing method that also sets the name and Id, not a pure function returning max(currentGrade, grade), and I could not verify the C++ `libraryGradeFor` mapping itself.

what: On a player's move, it grants a free combat round to the party when they are engaged, unless the move stayed in the same area, with the free round for a hostile room arrival and a capped one for leaving or changing level.
ev: SettleArea gives the leave and arrival rounds only when the area or level changes, and skips a same-area step unless forced, but it has no engaged-only gate and no capped round for level changes; the 98 cap appears only in Mordor.Core/MonsterAttack.cs CombatEngine.AttackChance, which computes a chance rather than triggering a round.

what: Each turn, it rolls the party leader's perception (capped at 95) against a random chance to announce a teleporter on the square the party is facing, with no automap check.
ev: Look matches the C++ core (one `Rnd * 100 < perception` roll per feature ahead, no automap check, capped perception), but it announces every feature rather than only the teleporter, and it also writes the automap bit, which the C++ function leaves to noticeTeleporter elsewhere.

what: After a companion casts, the owner's combat order becomes Defend if the companion's Att is 0 or 1, otherwise Fight (per R27.3).
ev: It is the closest match and its docstring describes the same Att 0/1 → Defend, otherwise Fight rule, but the code picks Defend or Fight from the current Kind (None/Fight → Defend) and never tests an Att value, so it does not map an input att to an order as the C++ function does.

what: Counts how many of the given spell IDs are valid and within casting reach of at least one guild, then announces the total to the player with the character's name.
ev: It applies the same reach test per spell record (a joined guild with a nonzero rate for the school, a ceiling at or above the spell level, and the level gate), but it returns a per-spell bool array for the character's guilds instead of counting valid IDs and announcing the total with the character's name.

what: Rolls the old-age death check for a character in the dungeon, and if the roll succeeds, marks the character as Dead and announces it to the player.
ev: It performs the same percent-over-98 old-age roll (5 + Log threshold against rng) but omits the in-dungeon gate, the Dead state assignment, and the death announcement that the C++ function also does.

what: Builds the sanctuary point for the party's current position by offsetting the stored X and Y coordinates by one and recording the party's dungeon level, which is the location a sanctuary spell marks.
ev: Its doc comment says Set Sanctuary records the caster's square, but the body is truncated before the case, so the +1 coordinate offset and the dungeon-level capture are not visible.

what: Makes the exploding chest trap (trap type 4) hit every living party member with its own damage roll, skipping anyone already dead.
ev: Its trap 3/4 case rolls damage separately for each party member, as the C++ does, but it is named "Fire Trap" for trap 4, applies fire resistance, and does not skip dead members.

what: Returns the base protection value for Sorcerer and Wizard guilds (kProtectionBaseSorWiz) and 0 for every other guild, since the base for other guilds is not given in this part of the rules.
ev: No candidate returns a per-guild base protection value (Sorcerer/Wizard base, 0 otherwise); the closest, `Rules.GuildAD`, computes per-level attack and defence from MDATA1, and `Combat.AttackOf` only adds `Rules.BaseAD` to attack.

what: Checks whether two items can be combined in a typed swap, testing identification, class, id, alignment and that the summed charges stay within bounds, and returns the first failing reason or Ok.
ev: Combine covers the class, id, and alignment checks and describes the charge-sum overflow, but it checks identification per item rather than first, has no first-item-is-first-check ordering, and ends the game on overflow where the C++ refuses and changes nothing; Refusal (cannot.Refusal) covers only the identification and combinable-kind checks.

what: Decides whether a character qualifies for the archive route's bonus hit points, which requires Constitution at least 17 and a guild level below the hits cap level.
ev: The CON > 16 and Guild.Level < HitsCapLevel test is inline in LevelUp's hit-gain code, which also computes the level-up hits and sits behind extra gating, so there is no standalone predicate like archiveBonusHpApplies.

what: Builds the starting stat array for a new character by setting each of the six attributes to the race's minimum plus five, capped at the race's maximum, via the rules' createBase function.
ev: Roll sets each base stat to `Math.Min(_race.Max[i], _race.Min[i] + FreePerStat)`, which is the same min(max, min+5) rule as the C++ `createBase` call, with `FreePerStat` presumably 5, though Roll also computes the remaining pool and refreshes the UI.

what: Returns the race definition record for the given race, looked up by the race's enum value, which holds that race's stat ranges and bonus points used in character creation.
ev: It does the same index lookup (`_race = RaceData.All[RaceBox.SelectedIndex]`) but as part of a UI event handler that also resets the alignment box and re-rolls stats, and no candidate is a pure accessor returning the race record by its enum value.

what: Returns true when the given internal item-slot index is the Hands slot (index 0), which the SRD defines as the hands equipment slot.
ev: The C++ function is a pure test that returns true only for internal slot 0, and DropProblem's `if (packSlot <= 0)` check treats slot 0 (the Hands) specially, but it returns a refusal message rather than a boolean and also covers negative indices, so it is not the same function.

what: Returns whether anti-magic or an extinguisher at the position suppresses hostile casting, which is the game's R49.6 rule as inferred from the antiMagicSquare flag.
ev: Refuse takes an `antiMagic` flag and returns an AntiMagic refusal when it is set, which is the suppression the C++ predicate expresses, but it is one step in an ordered chain of refusals (points, Non-Combat, combat-only, peaced) rather than a standalone check.

what: Clamps a raised morgue chance value to the range 10 to 98 percent, using constants that set the minimum and maximum.
ev: The C++ function only clamps an already-computed raw value to 10..98, and MorgueRaiseChance applies the same 10..98 clamp but also computes the raw value from CON, so it is a larger function that contains the clamp, not a match for it.

what: Rolls a poison-resistance check against the victim and, if the victim fails and is not already poisoned, sets their poison level to the attacker's level and posts a "Poisoned" message.
ev: Spring also poisons characters through a resistance roll, but it uses an inverted check (roll under half resistance), sets the level to the dungeon level rather than the attacker's level, and has no "not already poisoned" guard; the candidate list is also cut off mid-method for Spring and Companion.Apply, so a full match could be hidden there.

what: Scales a gold amount by the party's total group count, multiplying it by standing/2.0 and returning the result as currency, per the chapter 14 R4 step 1 gold-scaling rule.
ev: EncounterGold applies the same standing/2 scaling (`gold *= total / 2.0`, where total is the sum of group counts), but only as one step inside a larger function that also adds group gold and applies chest lock and class multipliers, while the C++ function is just the scaling step.

what: Checks whether a given character is currently in the party by comparing names, since characters have no separate id (per R21).
ev: The C++ `isMemberOf` checks whether a character is in the party by name, and `WhyCannotJoin` does this too (`Members.Any(m => m.Name == c.Name)`) but only as one step in a larger join-refusal check, so it is not a standalone membership test; `Buffs.Member` (Mods/Mordor.Mod.Kaizen/Buffs.cs) is the closest standalone name lookup, returning the member or null rather than a bool, with a case-insensitive `Same` comparison instead of exact equality.

what: In the Mordor rules (R27.5), a companion caster who is not a Mage has a fixed percentage chance (kCasterFizzlePercent, half the time) of their spell fizzling, which the function rolls on the context's RNG.
ev: No candidate rolls a percent chance that makes a non-Mage companion caster's spell fizzle; CastSpellHere (candidate 3) draws an RNG value for l01D0 but explicitly never reads it, and the other candidates cover targeting, refusals, charms, and monster-companion damage.

what: Decides whether a spell cast in combat becomes a queued combat order or resolves immediately, based on whether monsters are present and whether the player chose to fight on or the spell is not a non-combat use.
ev: It computes `MonstersHere && (Engaged || CastGate.UseOf(spell) != SpellUse.NonCombat)`, which matches the C++ `monstersPresent && (fightOn || use != SpellUse::NonCombat)` term for term, and returns a bool rather than a disposition enum.

what: Applies a Bind-type spell to a companion: Control adds to its binding level, Bind or Domination raises it to at least the base level for that spell, and the result is capped at the maximum, or the spell does nothing if the companion can't be bound.
ev: Both apply a bind spell to a companion's binding level and report the result, but BindCompanion computes the level from the spell and caster levels (and handles Life Domination), while castBindSpell adds a fixed Control increment, takes the max with fixed Bind/Domination base levels, and caps at the maximum.

what: Under SRD combat rule R6, it returns true when a character's combat order is Defend, which suppresses that character's own attack.
ev: No candidate is a predicate that returns true for Defend, but Combat.Round's doc says a character holding None or Defend does not attack, which is the behavior the C++ function encodes, though inside a whole-round routine rather than a standalone check.

what: When a right-click on the automap is resolved, it shows the collected menu items unless they are all separators or there are none, in which case it discards them and applies the original right-click to re-plot the route immediately (R18.2).
ev: Both return the collected items unchanged when any non-separator item exists and an empty list (the re-plot case) when only separators or nothing remain, though the candidate also gathers the items from each running mod, which the C++ function takes as input.

what: Makes a character advance a guild level by checking membership, experience and gold, charging the advance cost, adding hits and new attack/defence values, clearing an item quest, and refusing with a message when any requirement is unmet.
ev: It runs the same refusal gates (experience, then gold) and the same level advance, with hits, the 999 cap and the full refill coming from Character.LevelUp in candidate 2, but it has no AdGain attack/defence update and no topGuildLevel update, and its quest handling (QuestSatisfied with consume, plus a forfeit offer) differs from the C++ Fetch-clear.

what: Rolls the second modifier for a spell in the Mordor rules (R6 step 2), taking a random value scaled by the first modifier and the spell level, truncated toward zero, and adds 1.
ev: SpellHeal contains the same step-2 expression (`(int)(rng.NextDouble() * (mod1 - ((sl - 1) / (double)(sl * sl))) / 2) + 1`, with SL 0 effectively handled as 1, where the term is 0 either way), but it also computes mod1 and returns the final heal rather than being a standalone modifier-2 roll.

what: Each round a character with disease rolls a cure check, reduced by poison when the poison was not cured this tick; on failure the disease removes hit points, and the character dies if hit points reach zero.
ev: AilmentStep reproduces the disease cure roll, including the poison term set to zero when the poison was cured on that tick, and the one-hit loss on failure, but it combines poison and disease in one step and does not clear the disease, apply the hits, or kill the character at zero hit points as diseaseTick does.

what: Cures a character's disease by setting their disease level to zero and announcing "Disease cured." to the player.
ev: It clears the target's disease state (`Diseased = false; DiseaseLevel = 0`) with no refusal, as the C++ does, but it omits the "Disease cured." message, which must be emitted elsewhere (the message is not in the candidates).

what: Decides whether a creature is still in the fight (R29), returning true only if it has not been removed and either has hit points left or is flagged as at nought.
ev: No candidate computes the R29 alive test (`!gone && (hits > 0 || atNought)`). The closest, `Combat.cs` `LoadRecord`, mentions `AtNought` and sets hits, but it does not read `gone` or return a liveness flag.

what: Makes the combine action available only when the player's combine slot list has at least one item in it, which is the game's rule for when combining can be attempted.
ev: The C++ `combineEnabled` returns whether the combine slot list is nonempty, and none of the eight candidates gates a UI action on a list being nonempty; the closest, `ShelfLine.ShowStore`, only builds the Combine panel and `struct.Combine` performs the combining without any enabled check.

what: Computes the percent chance that an attacker hits a defender in the Mordor archive combat formula, scaling from 50% at parity up or down with the attack/defense difference and clamping the result to the archive's hit-chance limits.
ev: The formula matches (50% at parity, lean by share of the lead, 50% at 0/0), but HitThreshold clamps to 2..98 while the archive function clamps to 1..97, so results differ at the extremes.

what: Ticks the play clock for each party member, adding elapsed real time to their play seconds (with the 86340-second day wrap and pause handling), and returns early when a member's clock has not yet been started.
ev: The candidate has the same early return when a member's start is unset or PlaySeconds is -1, the same pause branch that advances the start without adding time, the same 86340 wrap gap formula, and the same add-then-restamp step; it differs only in using float timers and 4-place rounding, which the C++ notes as a no-op.

what: Grants a starter weapon or armour to a new character at creation, picking the cheapest eligible item (preferring floor 1 or below), marking it fully identified and worn, and deducting its price from the character's gold.
ev: No candidate grants a starter item at character creation or picks the cheapest eligible item, marks it worn, or deducts its price; the closest, Combat.cs WornSum and QoL WearSlot.cs Worn, only read what is already equipped, and the rest handle item use, giving, swapping, or the char page.

what: Checks whether a given square on a dungeon floor, at 1-based coordinates x and y, has a particular floor flag set (such as a trap, wall, or stairs marker), returning false for out-of-bounds coordinates.
ev: Recorded tests a flag bit at a level/x/y/width square like squareHasFlag, but it reads the player's remembered automap flags rather than the floor definition's flags, and it has no bounds checks.

what: Clamps a seer's carrier count to between 1 and kSeerMaxCarriers, so the seer-related game mechanic never uses a count outside the allowed range.
where: Mordor.Core/Seer.cs Seer.Carriers (the overload taking `found` and `rng`, candidate 3)
ev: That method clamps its random carrier count `take` to a 1-to-3 range, which matches the C++ clamp's lower bound and its cap, but it also caps by `found.Count` and is embedded in the sentence-building logic rather than being a standalone clamp.

what: In Mordor: The Depths of Dejenol, the dead screen (R112) is owed only when the lead character is dead and is the sole party member.
where: Mordor.App/CityWindow.axaml.cs looked.ArriveDeadSub0930 (it consumes `DeadScreenOwed` after a `_party.Size > 1` check, but the property's body, which would hold the leader-dead-and-alone test, is not among the candidates)
ev: No candidate defines the leader-dead-and-alone predicate; the closest matches (ArriveDeadSub0930, SyncDeadScreen, and Kill's party-size gate) only call or partly reproduce it, so the match depends on `DeadScreenOwed`, which was not provided.

what: Runs the monster's post-attack effects in a fixed order on the targeted party member: electrocution, then item destruction, then theft, skipping the unimplemented steps in between.
ev: GroupAttacks runs electrocution, item destruction, and theft in the same relative order as the C++ function, but it is a whole group turn that also covers breath, acid, and the ageing, drain, stoning, poison, disease, and paralysis steps the C++ leaves out, and no candidate runs just the three-step post-attack sequence.

what: Returns whether a named toggle is on for a loaded mod, reading the stored flag for that mod and key and falling back to the toggle's declared default when none is saved, or false if the mod index is invalid.
ev: It reads the stored flag for the mod's id and key and falls back to the declared default (`DefaultFor(key)`), matching the C++ `readStoredFlag` with `declaredToggleDefault`; the C++ index-validity check has no counterpart because `ModSettings` is already bound to one mod.

what: Decides whether a bank withdrawal of the given amount is allowed, refusing it when the amount exceeds the gold held in the bank or the bank balance is negative.
ev: Its withdrawal branch uses the same test (`amount > ch.GoldInBank || ch.GoldInBank < 0` returns Beep), but that check is inlined in a larger routine that also parses the typed text and moves gold, whereas the C++ function is only the predicate.

what: Returns whether the automap "been here" flag is set in a packed map word, meaning the party has already visited that square (per SRD c35).
ev: The same been-here test, `(word & (1L << BeenHereBit)) != 0`, appears inline while loading the automap, but it is only one step of a larger loader rather than a standalone predicate that returns whether the flag is set.

what: Rolls a percentile die (0-99) and returns whether the draw falls below the unrounded proc chance, so a player's critical or backstab proc succeeds with exactly that probability.
ev: It rolls `rng.Next(100)` and compares it against a chance, but it adds 1 to the draw and uses strict `<`, so a chance of 5.4 wins five rolls rather than six, and it is a monster-engage check rather than a player proc.

what: When the party is wiped out, it is marked as wiped; if more than one member remains the dead are pruned from the party, and if only one member remains, the owned companions are dropped.
ev: That method covers the size>1 branch by pruning the dead from the party and announcing them, but no candidate sets a wiped flag, and none drops companions in the size==1 branch as `handleWipedParty` does (Candidate 5's `Sub0930` also releases companions, but it does much more).

what: Rolls the pit-hover check from SRD R52 by comparing 5 + pitLevel/4 against a random percentile, returning true if the character hovers over the pit.
ev: The candidate computes `5 + dungeonLevel / 4.0 < rng.NextDouble() * 100`, which is the same R52 pit-hover test as the C++ `rollPitHover` with the same inputs and outcome.

what: Returns the number of squares a blur spread covers, which is 4 for a monster and 0 for characters and items (the latter being an assumed value, since the game's rule for them is unknown).
ev: No candidate maps a monster to a spread of 4 and anything else to 0; Seer.Blur consumes a spread value to jitter coordinates but never chooses that value.

what: Resolves a monster's melee attack against a target by first computing a melee damage modifier from the attack input and then applying the monster's blow with its attack, defense, level, and strength.
ev: MonsterBlow matches the C++ monsterBlow step (attack, target defence, level, strength and modifier passed to Fn0DEE), but no candidate reproduces the meleeDamageModifier step that resolveMonsterMelee runs first, and Rules.MonsterDamage (candidate 3) builds a different modifier from crit, backstab, chest and size inputs.

what: Applies the sequence of checks that decide whether a spell's effect lands on a given creature (magic immunity, charm-proof bit, all-or-nothing and charm sparing based on whether the damage kills, and the class gate), returning the verdict for that victim.
ev: The C++ function returns a per-victim verdict through the magic-immune, charm-proof, all-or-nothing, charm-sparing, and class-gate checks, while candidate 5 applies only the magic-immune bit, the class gate, and the all-or-nothing kill test to a computed damage value, with no charm-bit or charm-sparing logic and no verdict return.

what: Decides whether the item fetch quest is offered to a guild member, which happens only when the guild level is above the threshold kItemFetchMinGuildLevel (15, per the c19 source).
ev: RollQuest contains the same test (`guildLevel > 15` decides fetch versus defeat), but only inside a random quest roll that also depends on QuestPercent, the let-off chance, and a 25% draw, so it is not a standalone predicate.

what: Decides whether the Wait button is offered on the death screen: it is enabled when the party is wiped, or when a party below ground has a dead member awaiting rescue.
ev: OfferRescue shows the Wait button for the dead character whenever they are not in the rock, but it has no party-wiped check and hides the button in the rock, which waitButtonEnabled does not do, and no candidate computes the wiped-or-below-ground-dead-member predicate.

what: Returns the (dx, dy) step for moving forward and the (dx, dy) step for moving to the right from a given facing direction (N, E, S, or W), used to turn relative movement into map offsets.
ev: Delta gives the forward step for each facing, like the first half of facingVectors, but it uses y-up signs (North = (0,1)) where the C++ uses y-down (North = (0,-1)), and it omits the rightward step that facingVectors also returns.

what: Picks which guild a player character uses for a combat proc by choosing the guild with the highest coefficient times guild level, with ties going to the earlier table entry and a zero score winning nothing.
ev: It uses the same selection loop (table order, strict improvement over a zero start, zero-score guilds never win, value = modifier × level), but it returns the winning modifier and level rather than the guild identity, and for ability 4 it uses a different fighting formula instead of coefficient × level.

what: Decides whether a breath attack is stopped, returning true only when it is a cold breath and an earlier breath was already made in the same round.
ev: The guard `Bit(flags,3) || (Bit(flags,4) && !round.Breathed)` skips only a cold breath once an earlier breath has been made this round, and fire is never stopped, which is the same decision as `breathStopped`, though it is inlined in the turn loop rather than a separate method.

what: Determines whether the defeat message uses party wording, treating the player as in a party when the party has more than one member at the time of Asmodeus's defeat.
ev: Ending is the party-or-lone wording consumer for the Asmodeus defeat text, but it takes a `bool inAParty` argument and never computes it from party size > 1 as inPartyAtDefeat does, and no candidate makes that size check at defeat.

what: Approximates the Actual_Exp multiplier from raw experience points for R14 of the SRD, returning 1.0 for non-positive raw Exp and otherwise applying the logarithmic formula.
ev: The C++ function computes the R14 Actual_Exp multiplier from raw Exp via a logarithmic formula with a non-positive guard, and no candidate does that; the closest, Rules.Fn12A1, computes the experience needed for the next level, and Rules.ExpAwarded computes awarded experience from hits, so neither matches.

what: Builds the list of party members in the current room for the Look-around page, counting living members and dead non-leader members separately.
ev: Walk applies the same rule as walkRoom: the leader is never counted dead, a dead non-leader goes to the dead count, everyone else goes to the living count, and each row carries name, guild, level, and hits, with the room filter as the main input-shape difference (Walk filters a full roster by floor and area, while walkRoom iterates the party directly).

what: Checks whether adding two currency amounts would overflow the 64-bit currency range, so a bank transaction can be refused instead of wrapping around.
ev: Both return false exactly when a + b would overflow the 64-bit Currency range, using a different test (the sign-bit check in TryAdd versus the bound comparison in addFits), with the same inputs and outcome.

what: Takes the requested amount of gold from the party's gold on hand, drawing from members in roster order, and returns false without taking anything if the party cannot cover the full amount.
ev: No candidate removes gold from party members' gold on hand in roster order behind an all-or-nothing check; the nearest, ShortfallGift.CoverShortfall, moves gold the opposite way (bank into the payer's hand), and PartyDeposit moves hand into bank.

what: When a character fails a save against a monster's aging attack, it rolls a random number of days (up to 365 times a monster-level-based multiplier, capped at 1825) and adds them to the character's age.
ev: AgeBy does the final step (adds the days to Age and returns a message) and is named as a caller for monster aging, but it takes the day count as input, so it has no save roll, no 1d1825 draw, and no monster-level cap of 365×clamp(M/50, 1, 5).

what: Reports whether an item type is sold by the charge-chunk (such as potions and scrolls) in the General Store, based on its charge count and item type, which is store stock logic from the reference rules.
ev: Both return true only when the item's charges are greater than zero and its type is one of 23, 24, 25, 26, 27, 28, 30 or 31, and false otherwise.

what: Uses an item from the player's pack: it refuses if the character is paralysed or the slot is empty, casts the item's spell or spends a charge and applies its special effect, and removes the item once its charges run out.
ev: It matches the C++ flow (refusal checks, spell items cast via UseItemSpell with the charge spent only on success, other items spend a charge and apply the special, with consumable removal in SpendCharge), but it has no paralysis gate, which its own comment says it leaves out, and the C++ refuses paralysed characters first.

what: Registers the "hall" town command, which opens the Hall of Records screen showing the twelve town-wide bests (strength, intelligence, and so on through thieving, plus deadliest creature, most experience, and wealthiest).
ev: OnHall opens the Hall of Records window (HallWindow) as a modal from a menu button, which matches the screen the C++ command opens, but it is not a registered "hall" town command and does not carry the command's help text.

what: Rolls a random seer band from 0 to 2 for the game's seer mechanic, using the context's RNG.
ev: Carriers draws the same `rng.Next(3)` band as the C++ roll, but then uses it to filter monsters by drop level and returns carrier matches instead of returning the band itself.

what: Lets a player withdraw gold from their bank balance into their on-hand purse, refusing only when the requested amount exceeds what the bank holds (negative amounts are accepted per the CONFLICT-10 port rule).
ev: The withdrawal branch moves the amount from GoldInBank to GoldOnHand, refuses only when it exceeds the bank, and lets negatives through, but it also refuses when the bank is already below zero, ignores zero input, and takes text rather than a Currency amount.

what: Ends the party's lost state for all facings, levels, and position, clears each member's lost status, and announces that the party is no longer lost (the effect of the Depth Perception and Find Direction spells).
ev: This clears the lost level and facing flags and calls FoundYourself on one character, but only by a random roll and without the party-wide loop, the per-member reset, or the "no longer lost" message that the C++ function always performs.

what: In the Mordor spellcasting rules, a zero-level item's spell level is 1 if the item is free, otherwise it is the spell level taken from the spellbook for the acting character.
ev: That line contains the same item-level-0 branch as the C++ (`free ? 1 : Spellbook.SpellLevelFor(actor, s)`), but it is one part of a larger method that also handles positive and negative item levels and performs the whole cast, so it is not a standalone match.

what: Heals a character by a spell-healing roll computed from the spell's base, special effect, and level, capping the resulting current hit points at the character's maximum hit points.
ev: Its doc comment says the heal case rolls each target and caps it at the maximum, which matches healCharacter's roll-then-cap, but Apply is a whole spell-dispatch function covering many other effects, and the candidate's visible text is truncated before the heal body, so the cap isn't confirmed in code; Rules.SpellHeal (candidate 7) matches only the roll, with no cap or state change.

what: Reports whether record 0 of a given Mordor data file must be skipped during loading, which is true only for the monster file, where record 0 is a duplicate "GOBLIE" entry.
ev: The C++ `skipsRecordZero` is a one-line predicate that returns whether a file is the monster file (MDATA5), and no candidate contains a check that skips record 0 for a given data file; the closest, `Mordor.Core/Spells.cs it.Known`, only comments on MDATA2 record 0 and does not skip it, and the MDATA3/MDATA5 readers in the candidates do not contain this record-0 rule.

what: Awards kill experience to a character by rounding the XP value half-to-even, adding it to their experience total, and announcing the gain, with no level-up handling.
ev: GiveExperience adds the award to the character's experience total and announces level milestones, as awardKillXp does, but it takes an unrounded long (no half-even rounding), clamps the total at the pin cap, and emits different messages, with no "Kill experience gained" line.

what: Computes the destination square for a Teleport/displacement effect by offsetting the caster's location right, forward, and down relative to facing, wrapping the x/y coordinates within the 30x30 floor and clamping the dungeon level change.
ev: TeleportTo applies the same facing-relative right/forward offsets, the same 1-based 30x30 wrap, the same down-level clamp, and the same level floor of 0 as displaceTarget, differing only in that it returns a tuple without carrying the facing through (and assumes the clamp limit is 3).

what: Computes a character's thieving score from the dexterity and wisdom terms, a level-based term, and the modifier, then subtracts a penalty, following the SRD's F6 thieving formula.
ev: The level term `(4.5 + Exp(Log(lvl+1)/Log(15))) * (mod/10*14)` matches the C++, but the candidate builds its own `wis/4 + dex/2` stat and subtracts a fixed `against*1.5` penalty instead of taking `dexTerm` and `wisTerm` as inputs and subtracting `thievingPenalty()`.

what: When fog is present during a meeting, the monster loses its identification (R38), though the meaning of the underlying flag M4EEE is still unknown.
ev: FillGroup sets `s.IdLevel = fog ? 1 : 0` when a group is met, so a fog meeting lowers identification, but it sets a level on group creation rather than clearing `identified` as the C++ does.

what: Parses a typed "give" command and routes it to the gold or item handler, replying with usage text when the subcommand is missing or unrecognized.
ev: The C++ function parses a typed subcommand (`w[1]`), routes to gold or item, and replies with usage text otherwise, but the closest candidate, Mordor.App/GiveFlow.cs GiveFlow.Run, is an interactive name, gold, and item prompt sequence with no subcommand parsing, no routing on "gold"/"item", and no usage reply.

what: Computes a companion's effective defence against a melee attack, adding +4 if the hit is a critical and +1 if it is a backstab (per SRD c07p1 rule R25).
ev: The +4 critical and +1 backstab bonuses match the C++ constants, but the candidate applies them to the companion's blow (its damage modifier, via special-attack bits 10 and 11), whereas the C++ function adds them to the target's defence.

what: Decides whether the guild covers the raise fee: it does when the top guild level is at or below the guild-pays maximum and the party's purse is short of the fee.
ev: No candidate computes "top guild level at or below the guild-pays maximum and purse short of the fee"; `looked.Visit` only reads a `guildPays` flag (`if (!guildPays && !CharPay(cost))`) whose computation isn't in the shown text, and `MakeLevel` prices the fee but never checks guild payment.

what: Computes the percentage chance that a creature turns on its master, based on the alignment gap between the creature and the master (0% for matching alignment, 100% for a two-step gap, and 75% or 15% for a one-step gap depending on whether the creature is Evil).
ev: Outcome.Check uses the same creature-alignment gap rule (two or more steps always turns, Evil 75%, Neutral 15%), but it differs from the C++ percentage: an Evil or Neutral creature under a master of its own alignment gets a chance (75% or 15%) where the C++ returns 0, and a Good creature under a Neutral master gets 0 where the C++ returns 15.

what: When a character dies, runs the death routine and, if the party can be rescued, flags the party as awaiting rescue and tells the player someone may be able to find them.
ev: OfferRescue sets `_awaitingRescue = !inRock` and shows the dead screen after the death, which resembles the C++ flag-and-notify step, but it uses different text (`Rescue.DeadInTheDungeon`, not "Someone may be able to find you."), has no separate `deathOffersRescue` check, and the death setup is in Sub0930Head and Kill rather than a `deathHeadRoutine` equivalent.

what: Produces the player-facing message that a teleporter leading past the last dungeon level was used, and does nothing else (no state change).
ev: Clamp produces a denial line for a level past the last one in the limited build, but it is a general level clamp that returns the level to use (so state does change), whereas the C++ function only emits a teleporter-specific message with no state change.

what: Decides whether a monster's spell cast is skipped this turn by rolling a flat skip chance, then a second skip chance if the caster is not a mage class.
ev: ChooseSpell contains the same two skip rolls (a 10% flat skip, then a 50% skip for non-Mage classes), but they are embedded inside spell selection and happen after the school and pool are chosen, so the candidate does not isolate the skip decision as the C++ function does.

what: Rolls a random value of the given minimum plus 1 to the minimum (in game terms, a damage or heal roll per SRD R10/R13), with the span clamped to at least 1.
ev: No candidate computes a value of `minimum` plus a random roll from 1 to `minimum`; the closest, `Loot.RollAlignment`, picks a random option from a list, and the others are UI sizing, stat setup, or raise-resolution code.

what: Under rule R86, a character built as Limited has their level capped at 3, and any other build keeps its level unchanged.
ev: Clamp does the same limited-build cap (levels above LastLevel become LastLevel) but takes no build argument and reads a static `On` flag, adds a denial message, and leaves levels above DeepestLevel unchanged, whereas the C++ always applies min(level, 3) when the build is Limited.

what: Rolls a d3000 percentile-style check against the player's Charisma minus a level penalty to decide whether a monster joins the party.
ev: No candidate rolls d3000 against Charisma minus a level penalty to decide whether a monster joins; Rules.MonstersEngage uses a d100 engagement roll, and Combat.cs FillGroup's join-offer section (closest in context) is truncated before any roll appears.

what: Computes the maximum stat value an item may raise a character's stat to, as the race's natural maximum for that stat plus 5.
where: Mordor.Core/ItemUse.cs ItemUse.ApplyStatMods (box.ApplyStatMods; the enclosing class name isn't shown in the candidate)
ev: The candidate computes the same ceiling inline as `race.Max[i] + 5` and uses it to clamp item-raised stats, but it is part of a larger routine rather than a standalone function returning that value.

what: Deleting a character from the roster blanks its record to an empty Character while keeping the list's length, as the SRD's R3 step 2 requires.
ev: OnDelete deletes the character's save file and then calls `Roster.Removed` to update the record list, which is the step that blanks the record, but `Roster.Removed` is not among the candidates, and OnDelete also clears guildmaster seats and shows UI, so it does only part of what the C++ function does (blanking an in-memory list slot while keeping its length).

what: Returns the percent chance that a breath attack fires, which is 80 for a positive relation, 20 for a negative one, and 50 otherwise.
where: Mordor.Core/Combat.cs, CompanionBreathes (enclosing class not shown in the candidate)
ev: It uses the same 50/80/20 tiers, with 80 when the lead foe's guild level is more than a quarter above the companion's and 20 when it is more than a quarter below, but it computes the chance inline from guild levels rather than as a function of a precomputed relation sign, so it is not a standalone equivalent.

what: Makes a melee paralysis saving throw against a character after a damaging monster hit, and if the save fails while no paralysis rounds are pending, applies paralysis to the character.
ev: The candidates contain no melee paralysis save (no `meleeParalysisChance` roll, no `failed` check, no return value), so the closest match is `Paralyse`, which applies paralysis only when none is held, the same effect as the C++ `paralyse` call that is guarded by `paralyzedRounds == 0`.

what: Checks whether a monster's LevelFound falls within the eligibility window for a target floor, i.e. between the floor minus the spread and the floor itself (rule R12).
where: Mordor.Core/Confinement.cs per.BoughtBinding (or Mordor.Core/Rules.cs Rules.EncounterSpread for the spread term)
ev: The C++ function is a pure window check (floor − spread ≤ levelFound ≤ floor), and no candidate performs that check; the closest candidate is Rules.EncounterSpread, which computes the spread value (the "floor − spread" bound) that such a window would use, but it does not test membership in the window, and the other candidates are unrelated.

what: Computes the base respawn delay for a monster in the dungeon, which is 150 seconds multiplied by the dungeon level, returned in milliseconds.
ev: The 150-seconds-per-level term matches (`5 * (level / 2.0) * 60` equals `150 * level`), but RespawnDelay adds a 1200-second base and subtracts a per-area tally adjustment, floored at 120 seconds, whereas the C++ function returns only `150 * level` in milliseconds.

what: Computes the experience points a character needs to reach a given level, using the guild and race experience factors, and returns that threshold as an integer.
ev: The candidate runs the same level loop with the same fixed-point (Currency-style) roundings for the 2l·guildExp and (l/2)·2 + (l−1) terms and the same final division by 10, with raceExp+1 as the race input; its tail, which applies the race multiplier and the closing round, is cut off in the candidate text, so that part is inferred from the doc comment rather than seen.

what: Brings the named party member who was left behind back to the end of the party, failing if no one by that name is out, the party is full, or the roster has no room, then updates the roster and reports the rejoin to the player.
ev: The C++ function brings a left-behind party member back into the party (checking name, party size, and roster capacity, then rotating records and rewriting the roster), and no candidate performs that rejoin; Party.LoadFor is the closest, auto-restoring saved party members, but it works from the leader's roster file with area/alignment/death checks rather than a named rejoin with rotation and capacity checks, so at most it is PARTIAL, and I judge it NOT_IN_CANDIDATES because the mechanism and inputs differ substantially.

what: Registers the "options" console command in both the town and dungeon screens, so the player can list or change game options from either place.
ev: No candidate registers a text console command or parses `options [name [value]]` in both town and dungeon; the closest, `listed.ShowControlPanel` in CityWindow.axaml.cs, opens a GUI control panel (also reached by F10 in the dungeon) rather than a command.

what: Divides two extended-precision (x87-style) floating-point values, rounding the 64-bit mantissa quotient half-to-even, and returns zero when either operand is zero.
ev: X87.Round does the same half-to-even rounding of a value to a 64-bit mantissa that x87Div applies to its quotient, but it does no division, and the candidate set does not show the X87 division operator (used in Fn12B2) that would be the closer match.

what: Decides whether a character's guild membership is "pinned" (experience has reached the cap just short of the next level's threshold) and so should show the level-up announcement, optionally suppressing it when the level is already at the maximum.
ev: Its Pinned flag comes from Character.IsPinned (experience at or past the cap), which matches the C++ pinned test, but no candidate makes the announcement decision or applies the maxLevel gate, and GiveExperience only announces the transition into pinned rather than the pinned state.

what: Returns the guild level (GLvl) of the character's chosen guild for rule R11, or 0 when no guild has been chosen.
ev: No candidate returns a guild's level from an index with a 0 fallback, but Claim contains that same lookup (`c.Guilds.FirstOrDefault(g => GuildData.IndexOf(g.Guild) == guild)?.Level ?? 0`) inside a larger mastership-claim routine, and Character.MeetsUseLevel reads the current guild's level only for class-restricted items.

what: Quotes a sell price for an item, refusing guild crests outright (returning false) before any price is computed.
ev: SellPrice computes the sell price from the item and slot as sellPrice does, but it has no guild-crest refusal before quoting; the crest refusal exists only as a reference to ItemUse.IsGuildIssued in a comment on ShelvedBySelling, which is not among the candidates.

what: Decides whether a spell cast during combat (monsters present) should be routed to the combat branch, which is the case for any spell whose use is not NonCombat.
ev: BecomesOrder returns `MonstersHere && (Engaged || UseOf(spell) != NonCombat)`, which matches the C++ routing only when not engaged, and when engaged it routes every spell, including NonCombat ones, where the C++ returns false.

what: Computes the maximum monster level a guild's quests can reach, which is its guild level divided by 25 (rounded down) and capped at 10, per rule R48.
ev: It has the same cap at 10, but it rounds guildLevel/25 to even instead of truncating and clamps the minimum to 1 instead of 0, so levels 13 to 37 give 1 where the C++ gives 0 for levels under 25 and 1 for 25 to 37.

what: Decides whether a character may climb up stairs, refusing the climb if they are paralysed or dead (rule R69).
ev: The stairs-up branch checks `!_ch.Paralysed` before climbing, which covers the paralysis half of R69, but it does not check death, and no candidate implements the combined paralysed-or-dead test as a standalone function.

what: Sends a message to the player through the session's context, using a message code, text, and the given name as a substitution argument, which is a display helper for roster messages (such as a member joining or leaving).
ev: LoadFor announces joins by name ("\"Sela\" is now a member of your party.") through a say callback, but it is embedded in save-loading validation and hardcodes its text, whereas rosterSay takes a message code and passes the name as a substitution argument to a context-level say; the generic Say methods (DungeonWindow.Say, DungeonContext.Say) only write a raw line.

what: Resolves a player's stored choice for a mod setting against the declared options, falling back to the default option and then the first option when the stored value does not match, per the mod-choice rule (F6).
ev: Both return stored when there are no options, match the trimmed stored value against the options, fall back to the declared default and then to the first option, and return the matched option; the only difference is that ChoiceOf matches case-insensitively, which the C++ matchOption may or may not do.

what: Reports whether a monster group in the current encounter is still standing, meaning it has at least one living member, and treats any out-of-range group index as not standing.
ev: No candidate is a standalone "group standing" predicate with a range check, but Capture tests `rec.Foes[g].GroupCount > 0` per slot and counts living members per group, which is the same per-group living test buried in a larger routine.

what: When a rescue arrives, it applies the R109 rescue-arrival effect to the dead character's body (which sets its level to 0) and shows the player the message that the body has been brought up from the dungeon.
ev: CarryHome sets the body's DungeonLevel to 0 (the R109 effect), but it also adds days to age and sets Area to -1, and it does not show the "body is brought up from the dungeon" message.

what: Given an item's alignment, it returns the creature reference for Id 307's split: Evil maps to the Shadow Ninja, and Neutral, Good, or Unaligned maps to Morgul.
ev: For Id 307 it returns the Shadow Ninja for Evil and the Morgul for Neutral, Good, and Unaligned, matching the C++ split, though it reaches that result by scanning the table and falls back to the first index rather than returning fixed constants.

what: Checks whether monsters are present in the party's current area, returning true if any party foe is alive, any living foe sits in the leader's area, or the leader's area has a standing monster group.
ev: No candidate computes the R125 presence test (any living party foe, any living foe in the leader's area, or a nonempty standing group in that area); the closest, DungeonWindow.axaml.cs `LoadArea`, generates the area's monster group on arrival and does not return a presence boolean.

what: Checks whether a guild index falls within the valid range of guilds (0 up to kGuildCount), which the guild rules rely on before looking up or assigning a guild.
ev: No candidate checks whether a guild index lies within 0 to the guild count; they look guilds up by name (JoinGuild, SetActiveGuild, MeetsUseLevel) or iterate a valid list (ReachingGuilds, TeachingGuild), so none matches validGuild.

what: Rolls a percent chance, using the RNG, for whether an identification attempt succeeds, with the chance computed from the character's skill and whether the attempt is made in darkness.
ev: It computes the same clamped per-tick identify chance from skill and darkness (skill × 0.75 when dark, plus 20, clamped 10–90), but it returns that number rather than rolling against it with the RNG as the C++ `rng.percent` call does.

what: Parses the player's typed word ("good", "neutral", or "evil", case-insensitive) into an item alignment code for the realign command, returning -1 if the word isn't recognised.
ev: No candidate parses a typed word ("good", "neutral", "evil") into an alignment; the closest, CityWindow.Store.cs Realign, takes an already-typed ItemAlignment, and the others map or price alignments without string input.

what: Makes the 75% placement roll for a lair in an area, returning false without rolling if the area has no LairId.
ev: Locate makes the same 75% lair roll (`rng.NextDouble() * 100 < 75`) gated on `area.LairId > 0`, but it also requires `LairId == def.Id` and then continues into the random spawn-area search, so it is a larger function rather than a standalone placement roll.

what: Returns true when an item's id falls within the guild crest id range, treating crests as items with ids between kCrestItemIdBase (exclusive) and kCrestItemIdBase + kGuildCount (inclusive), though the actual crest identification rule is unknown and not specified in this SRD half.
ev: Both decide whether an item is a guild crest, but the C++ tests a numeric item id range that its own comment calls an unverified guess, while IsGuildIssued tests SpecialType against 500 plus the guild index, a different field and rule.

what: Returns true if any guild the character belongs to, in scope for the item's class restriction, has a level at or above the level that guild requires to use the item.
ev: Both return true if the character's current guild (when class-restricted) or any joined guild (otherwise, limited to the item's guild mask) has a level at or above the item's required level for that guild, with the candidate's `Level <= 0` skip and `Math.Max(1, ...)` floor producing the same result as the C++ comparison.

what: Demotes a character's guild membership by one level (if above zero) and announces the reduced level to the player, per the game's guild demotion rule.
ev: ForfeitQuest lowers `Guild.Level` by the forfeit cost (floored at 1, not 0) as one step of a larger forfeit that also reverses hits, clears the quest, and unequips gear, and it does not announce the new level, so it only partly matches the C++ one-level demotion with its zero floor and message.

what: Decides whether a standing group in an area is still kept, returning true when more than twice the area's respawn time has passed since its stamp.
ev: RefillDue contains the same "more than twice the respawn time since the stamp" test that drops a standing group, but it wraps it in a refill decision, uses Math.Abs instead of the signed difference, and adds a `stamp == 0` case, so it is not the same standalone predicate as standingGroupKept.

what: Reports whether a companion has died, which the game's rules define as happening when the companion's Hits fall to zero or below.
where: Mordor.Core/MonsterAttack.cs of.CompanionFalls (class name truncated in the candidate header)
ev: No candidate is a predicate that reports a companion's death; CompanionFalls handles the consequences once Hits reach zero, and Round and several sweep routines repeat the inline `Hits <= 0` test, but only as a skip or gate rather than a reported death.

what: Returns true when the Good pen count is below the restock cap, which decides whether another item can be added to the Good pen, though whether the comparison is strict or inclusive is still unconfirmed.
ev: Add applies the same strict `n < ShelfCap` test on a pen count before incrementing, but it is a void method that also checks LevelFound and Ref and uses the pen of the sold companion's alignment, not a bool-returning test on the Good pen.

what: Moves a dead party member's body to the raiser's location and, if the raise chance is above 0, records the pending raise's chance, kind, and the raiser's name on the body.
ev: It moves the body to the raiser's X, Y, dungeon level and area, and when chance is above 0 it writes the chance, kind and raiser name onto the body, which is the C++ behavior; the only differences are storage (Character fields instead of featureState keys) and a TrimEnd on the name.

what: Computes the breath attack damage range for a monster of a given level cast against a caster whose guild level is given, using the original game's logarithmic formula and returning false where the original would raise an error.
ev: Kind.Range has the same logarithmic range shape as breathDamageRange, but it takes the attacker's guild level directly instead of computing l046C = VbInt(monLvl * Log(monLvl+1)) first, divides the target level by 10 instead of 20, and has no non-positive guards; GroupAttacks (Candidate 1) repeats the l046C step but its visible portion does not show the range formula.

what: In the Mordor monster rules, the number of attempts a monster group gets per turn is its living count, capped at 5.
ev: No candidate computes attempts per group or applies the cap of 5; the closest, Mordor.Core/MonsterAttack.cs CombatEngine.AliveGroups, only collects living monsters into same-kind groups and never caps a count.

what: Arms the combat clock (sets combatClockRunning) when a fight is in progress, so the combat tick will run the next round of combat.
ev: Sub14CC re-enables the combat clock (`_combatClockOff = false`) after a dead character is raised, but it does so unconditionally and never checks for a fight in progress, and no candidate sets a clock-running flag when a fight starts or before each round as armCombatClock does.

what: Computes a companion spellcaster's mishap chance by multiplying the spell's odds by 1.5 and clamping the result between the game's floor and ceiling of 1 and 40.
ev: It applies the same spell factor of 1.5 and the same 1..40 clamp, but it derives the odds from guild level and body count instead of taking the spell odds as an input, so the inputs differ.

what: Checks whether a character may join a guild, refusing if they are already a member and otherwise testing race, alignment, minimum stats, and gold on hand, and sends the player a refusal message when already joined.
ev: Greeting runs the same race, alignment, and stat-minimum refusals (stat below requirement refuses, so equal passes), but it returns a greeting string rather than a join decision, and it has no gold/JoinCost check.

what: Applies the default combat order to a character with no order set, making them Fight, which implements the engine's default combat setting (c54).
ev: Both turn a None order into Fight when the character's setting is 1, but ApplyDefault reads `c.CombatSetting` and maps other values to Defend, a spell, or None, while the C++ always sets Fight, and ApplyDefault also resets Target to -1 where the C++ keeps it.

what: Returns the maximum character level for the Nomad, Sorcerer, and Wizard guilds (30, 29, and 41 respectively), with 0 for all other guilds as an unknown placeholder.
ev: No candidate returns a per-guild maximum character level; Rules.GuildADSingle reads a `g.AdMaxLevel` field as a loop bound for attack/defence accrual, and CombatEngine.MaxGuildLevel returns the highest level the character holds across guilds, which is a different quantity.

what: Checks a character's typed password against the stored one, and any character with no password set always matches.
ev: It does the same case-sensitive exact comparison, but it lacks the C++ rule that a character with no password always matches (it compares against the trimmed stored value, so an empty stored password only matches an empty entry), and that rule is handled by callers such as TitleWindow's LoadCharacter instead.

what: When a Control Dragon attempt fails, the target creature is flagged as hostile and the player is told that the dragon resists control.
ev: The C++ function sets the target's hostile flag and says "The dragon resists your control" on a failed Control Dragon attempt, and none of the eight candidates handles control-spell failure, hostility, or dragon messages (AttackSound, drag-and-drop, sorting, fonts, Cast-on-Who, window layout, and companion drag are all unrelated).

what: Computes the aging saving-throw chance for a character as 2.5 times their base Constitution minus 2 times the monster's floor level, as a rule from the game's aging mechanic.
ev: No candidate computes an aging saving-throw chance of 2.5 × base CON minus 2 × monster floor; the closest, Character.AgeBy (candidate 7), applies the aging itself and never computes a save.

what: Ends paralysis on a character when no monster occupies the square, as the game's R20 rule dictates, and reports whether it did so.
ev: It unparalyses the owner when the square is empty, which is the same effect as the C++ function, but it has no `monsterOnSquare` guard, returns no bool, and only runs at the companion call sites, while Character.Unparalyse and Rules.ParalysisPasses each cover only part of the rule.

what: Charges a realignment fee to the party by deducting gold from members in roster order, and returns false without taking anything if the party's combined gold cannot cover it.
ev: It is the same realign-fee operation, but it charges only the selected character through `CharPay` (which can draw on the bank), whereas `realignPayFee` takes the fee from the party's combined gold on hand in roster order and returns false when the pool can't cover it; no candidate does that pool-based deduction.

what: Computes the damage of a companion's special breath, spit, or shock attack by rolling a random value within a range, adding a bonus, scaling by 0.7, and halving the effect of the target's resistance percentage.
ev: Raw matches the C++ roll, bonus, and 0.7 scaling, and AfterResistance matches the resistance step, but the C++ applies resistance to the unrounded value and clamps resistance to 0..100, while the pair truncates the raw damage first and does not clamp.

what: Registers four town-screen player commands (quest, claim, forfeit, titles) that let a member show or assign a guild quest, claim a completed quest or guildmastership, leave a guild, or view their guild title.
where: Mordor.App/CityWindow.axaml.cs CityWindow.MakeLevel (with OfferForfeit, GuildInfo, and Character.ForfeitQuest/ForfeitRefusal/ForfeitCost as related pieces)
ev: None of the candidates registers or dispatches the town commands quest, claim, forfeit, or titles, and none shows a member's quest or guild title; the closest matches are the forfeit mechanics (OfferForfeit, ForfeitRefusal, ForfeitCost, ForfeitQuest) and the quest-info display (GuildInfo), which cover only part of what the C++ function's command set does.

what: Handles the player's "inspect" command on a chest in the current square, replying with whether a chest is present, whether it is trapped, and the name of the trap if so.
ev: ShowChest also reports whether a chest is present and shows a trap name, but it is a chest-panel display rather than a text reply, and the name it shows may be the wrong trap, whereas cmdInspect always reveals the true name.

what: Returns true when at least four seconds (kFourSecondsMs) have elapsed since the last tick, which is the game's R73 timing check that decides when the four-second tick fires.
ev: No candidate computes an elapsed-time check against a four-second threshold; AilmentTick (DungeonWindow.axaml.cs) is the every-four-seconds handler, but its cadence comes from a timer interval rather than a comparison like `nowMs - lastTickMs >= 4000`.

what: Pays a whole-gold exchange amount in town by spending gold on hand first and drawing any shortfall from the bank, which may go negative.
ev: Pay also spends gold on hand first and takes the shortfall from the bank with half-even rounding, but it returns false and moves nothing when the purse can't cover the cost, whereas the C++ lets the bank go negative with no check.

what: Raises a character's stat by the given amount, capped at the race's maximum for that stat, and stores the result only if it actually increases.
where: Mordor.Core/ItemUse.cs ItemUse.ApplyStatMods (the class name is not shown in the candidate; the method is `ApplyStatMods`)
ev: It adds a stat modifier and clamps the result to a ceiling, but the ceiling is race max + 5 rather than the race max, it always writes the value instead of storing only when it increases, and it adds reversed-item, Hall-record, and recalculation logic that `raiseStat` does not have.

what: Sets a creature's hit points to a new value and clears its AtNought flag, so that any change to Hits also ends the creature's at-nought (zero-hit-point) state, as rule R29 requires.
ev: TakeRecord also sets the hits and derives the at-nought flag from them, but it sets `AtNought = hits <= 0` rather than always clearing it, so writing 0 hits leaves the flag true where the C++ would clear it, and it also resets MaxHits and Unrolled.

what: Caps the number of attack attempts a monster group gets per round at the lower of its living member count and kAttackAttemptCap (5), per SRD rule R32.
ev: No candidate caps a group's attack attempts at min(living count, 5); the closest, CombatEngine.MonsterAttacks, picks targets by weighted roll per group and AttackChance returns a percentage clamped to 5 to 98, neither of which is that cap.

what: Clears the pending seer person offer (its kind, name, and level) from the session's feature state once it has been answered.
ev: No candidate erases a pending seer offer's kind, name, and level from session feature state; the Seer methods (Locate, ShowSeer, LocatePerson) never clear pending state, and CombatOrder.Clear only resets combat orders.

what: Computes the monster level cap for quests from the guild level, taking the guild level divided by 25 (rounded down) and capping the result at 10.
ev: It computes the same guild-level-over-25 cap clamped to 10, but it rounds (ToEven) instead of truncating like vbInt and also clamps the minimum to 1, while the C++ function has no lower bound and can return 0.

what: Returns true when a spell's level exceeds the ceiling allowed for its category, marking the spell as unreachable under rule R67.
ev: The C++ function is a bare test that a spell's level exceeds its category's ceiling, and CanCast contains that same `spellLevel > SpellMax[category]` check but also applies the rate and guild-level gates, so it does more than the C++ function does.

what: Records a charm kill for the Asmodeus charm by incrementing the caster's kill count and adding the creature's id to their monster kill list, with no damage applied (experience is paid by the caller).
ev: KilledBy increments the killer's kill count like the C++ `caster.kills += 1`, but it also reports damage through `Dealt` and runs `QuestKill`, which the charm kill does not do, and no candidate appends the creature id to a kill list.

what: Awards experience to a character's guild membership, zeroing the award if the guild is pinned and capping the total at the guild's experience cap, then returns the amount actually banked.
ev: It adds the award, clamps the total at the pin cap, and reports the gain clamped at zero, but it is void with no return value, emits pin and level messages, and does not zero a negative amount or explicitly zero the award when pinned.

what: When a valid opener unlocks-chest square has guards still alive, it clears the party's attack orders and starts a chest countdown (R116) if the chest's disarm value exceeds 10, while the function itself returns a default ChestOpenStart.
where: Mordor.App/DungeonWindow.axaml.cs DungeonWindow.OpenTheChest (per-turn countdown step is in Mordor.Core/Combat.cs no.ChestTick)
ev: OpenTheChest, with monsters still standing, reloads the orders, clears the party's orders and starts the chest count, which matches part of beginChestAfterCombat, but it is a player-triggered open with no guards-alive check and no disarm > 10 threshold, and ChestTick only covers the per-round countdown step.

what: Returns true when a standing monster group's last-seen timestamp is more than twice the respawn interval old, meaning the group counts as stale under the game's rules.
ev: RefillDue contains the same "more than twice the respawn time old" test (`Math.Abs(nowSec - stamp) > t * 2`) but embeds it in a larger refill decision and uses an absolute difference, while the C++ function is a plain `(now - stamp) > 2 * respawnT` comparison with no abs.

what: Handles the player's "Yes" choice to exit the dungeon to the title menu by marking the party's members as saved, unloading the party, leaving dungeon mode, and showing a confirmation message (no town arrival; the character stays where it stood).
ev: On Yes it does what the C++ function does (save the character, unload the party, close the dungeon, return to the title with the character left in place), but it also wraps that in a monster-presence check and a confirm prompt, and it omits the "Saving and returning to the title screen." message.

what: Computes how much experience (XP) a character still needs to reach the total required, by subtracting current XP from the XP total.
ev: ToolbarNeed also computes "threshold minus current experience" (`needed - Experience` or `cap - Experience`), but it first chooses which threshold applies and returns a state, while the C++ function is a bare `xpTotal - currentXp` subtraction.

what: Computes experience points needed for a character level under the archive (c103) formula, scaling by race and guild factors and the level number, implemented literally as the source states.
ev: Both compute a per-level experience threshold scaled by race and guild factors, but the candidates use the original game's fn12A1 rule from MAINMOD2.BAS, whose body isn't shown, and none contains the C++ literal `r * g * (n/2) * (266 + (n-1)*177)` form, which the C++ itself flags as unreconciled.

what: Computes the magic sack's slot capacity by subtracting the number of wielded items and a hand-pair deduction from a reported base slot count, with no clamp, so it can go negative if more than 38 items are wielded.
ev: No candidate computes a sack capacity from a count of wielded items minus a hand-pair deduction; the closest, Character.SwapSlots and CityWindow.RefreshPack, handle pack slot swaps and display, not capacity.

what: Shows the player the refusal message for an equip attempt that failed, mapping each refusal outcome (no free hands, too many worn, class or guild restriction, stats too low) to its text.
ev: Both the C++ function and WearRefusal map equip refusals to the same player-facing texts (no free hands, too many worn, guild, guild level, stats, cursed), but WearRefusal computes which refusal applies and returns the string rather than taking an outcome enum and displaying it, and it adds a "too weak" text the C++ does not have.

what: Rolls a pit-style chance check for a dungeon pit, where the threshold is 5 plus the dungeon level divided by 4, and the roll succeeds when a random value scaled to 0–100 exceeds that threshold.
ev: The candidate evaluates the same expression as the C++ function, `5 + dungeonLevel / 4.0 < rng.NextDouble() * 100`, with the same inputs and outcome; it differs only in name and in its levitation doc comment.

what: Clears all three lost flags (level, position, facing) on the party's lost state when a morgue visit occurs, per SRD rule R32, without any message to the player.
ev: It clears LostLevel, LostPosition and LostFacing together with no message, the same state change as the C++ clearLostAtMorgue, though its doc comment ties the trigger to mapped ground as well as the morgue.

what: When a companion's Hits reach zero, if a carry choice applies and nothing is currently carried, the fallen companion is announced as dropped and becomes the carried item in the party's carrying slot.
ev: Run handles the same death-carry case when nothing is carried, but it scans all dead companions and picks the largest MaxHits, gates the carry on a monster-size test, and says "dropped" only when replacing an existing carry, whereas the C++ function handles one fallen companion and carries it unconditionally when the slot is empty.

what: Computes a resisted spell or attack damage by scaling the base damage down by the target's resistance percentage and rounding half to even, as the game's R10 formula defines.
ev: Rules.SpellDamage applies the same step, `dmg * (1 - resist/100)` rounded half to even, but only as the last part of a full spell computation and with an added clamp of resistance to 0-100 and a floor at zero, while Kind.AfterResistance halves the resistance and so does not match.

what: Decides whether a teleporter destination square can be drawn, rejecting any square that is out of range, recorded as rock, or holds a teleporter.
ev: ForSquare redraws random destination squares until one is neither rock nor a teleporter, which is the same rejection rule as the C++ predicate, but it is inlined in a larger routine and has no standalone out-of-range check that returns false.

what: Decides whether a non-engaged monster group may offer to join the viewing party, based on alignment match (or neutral) and whether the group's guild level is within the viewer's top guild level.
ev: FillGroup sets the join offer only when `s.Engaged == 0`, which matches the C++ engagement gate, but the snippet is cut off before the alignment and guild-level test, so the candidate's offer predicate can't be confirmed as the same.

what: Sells an inventory item to the store for its computed price, adding the gold to the character's wallet and clearing the slot, or refuses the sale with a result code if the slot is empty or the gold total would overflow.
ev: Receive does the wallet side (adds the sale gold to hand and refuses the sale on overflow with nothing moved), and StoreStock.SellPrice computes the price, but no candidate validates the slot, clears the item, and returns a result code as sellItem does.

what: Marks a dungeon area as cleared by bumping the floor's cleared-area tally, stamping the clearing time, and setting how long until the area respawns monsters based on how many areas remain uncleared on that level.
ev: MarkCleared stamps the clearing time and adjusts the level's tally for the emptied room, as markAreaEmptied does, but it does not set a respawn delay, and it decrements a remaining-areas tally where the C++ increments a cleared-areas tally. Candidate 1 (DungeonState.RespawnDelay) covers the respawn-delay part only.

what: Makes a bank deposit by moving gold from the character's on-hand purse into the bank balance, returning Beep if the amount is non-positive or exceeds the gold on hand.
ev: With deposit set, it returns Beep when the amount exceeds gold on hand or is at most zero, otherwise it adds to the bank and subtracts from hand, matching depositGold; it differs in taking typed text and guarding overflow, which are structural details.

what: Lays out the picture shown in the game's view: when the "no stretch" option is on, it draws the 100x100 picture centred in the viewport, otherwise it fills the whole view.
ev: Its Asmodeus branch computes the same layout (noStretch gives a 100x100 box centred at ((W-100)/2, (H-100)/2), otherwise a box filling 0,0,W,H), but that logic is embedded in a larger method that also handles the dead-leader check and maze drawing, and it uses integer division rather than `vbInt`.

what: Reports whether a creature still counts as alive, which in game terms is true for a member at 0 hits until its hits are written (per SRD [c5]).
ev: No candidate computes "alive or at nought" (`alive || atNought`); candidate 1's `LoadRecord` only mentions `AtNought` in its doc comment, and the others test `Alive` alone or handle experience, spells, and rest.

what: Cures poison in a character by clearing their poison level to zero and announcing "Poison cured."
ev: It clears both the poison flag and the poison level to zero, matching the C++ clearing, but it does not produce the "Poison cured." message, which the C++ function emits itself and the port leaves to its callers.
