what: Rolls a random slot for an acid attack by drawing Int(Rnd*5), so the result is 0 for the character, 1 to 3 for companion slots, or 4 for the phantom slot that no one occupies (R36/R41).
ev: AcidTarget draws `Floor(rng.NextDouble() * 5)` and returns 0 or 4 unchanged, as the C++ does, but it adds a redraw loop for empty companion slots and a shortcut when no companions exist, so its outcome differs from the raw draw in rollAcidSlot.

what: Decides which screen the player sees (new game, combat, dungeon, town, or game over) by checking whether the party is empty, whether all members are dead, and whether the party is in combat, in the dungeon, or in town.
ev: The C++ function is a pure screen-selection rule (NewGame if party empty, GameOver if all dead, else Combat/Dungeon/Town by flags), and no candidate decides which screen to show from party size, death state, combat, dungeon level, and town flags; the closest, DungeonWindow.Sub14CC and CityWindow.SyncDeadScreen, only handle the transition out of the dead screen and do not cover the full dispatch.

what: Decides whether a rare monster (weight ≤ 9) or rare item (weight ≤ 4) pick should be rerolled, with a 75% chance of rejecting it; non-rare entries are never rejected.
ev: QuestMonster's doc comment describes the same rare-monster rule (the Rnd*100 draw happens on every pass with no short-circuit, chance is the Rarity field, and the test is three in four), and its loop rerolls on a rejected rare pick, but the candidate picks a class and run of monsters and never shows the weight <= 9 cutoff or the 75% reject as a standalone function, so it only partly matches QuestRerollRare.

what: Returns the highest character level among a character's other guilds (excluding the given guild), or 0 if none, which levelUp uses to apply the game's level-progression rules.
ev: The first line of LevelUp computes the same value as highestOtherLevel (max level over guilds other than the active one, 0 if none), but it is inlined inside the larger level-up method rather than being a standalone helper.

what: Returns an item's alignment as an integer, which the item-use code uses in its Mordor game-rule checks.
ev: The C++ function returns a single item's alignment as an integer, but no candidate does that: `ItemAlignments.Possible` reads the allowed-alignment bit flags into a list, `Loot.RollAlignment` picks one at random, and `OriginalSaves.SlotFrom` reads a per-slot alignment from a save record.

what: Returns the spit-attack chance threshold percentage (90, 50, or 10) for a monster, chosen by comparing the active level to the monster's level via a ratio band lookup.
ev: Both return 90, 50, or 10 by comparing a character's guild level to a monster's, with 90 when the active level is more than a quarter above and 10 when it is more than a quarter below; I could not see `ratioBand` in the C++, so the band boundaries are inferred from the candidate's documented rule rather than checked line by line.

what: Checks whether a friendly foe group is currently offering to join the party, which is true when its join offer value is positive.
ev: The C++ function is a one-line predicate returning whether `front.joinOffer > 0`, and AcceptJoin contains the same `group[0].JoinOffer <= 0` check as an early-return guard, but it is only a fragment of a much larger routine that accepts the offer and adds companions, so it does not do the same thing as the C++ predicate.

what: Looks up in the guild grid (table T4) whether a given race is permitted to join a given guild, returning that yes/no answer as data without the engine enforcing it.
ev: Both return whether a race may join a guild from a per-guild race table (the C++ `kGuildGrid` lookup, the C# `RaceMask` bit test), though AllowsRace returns true for an unknown race name where the C++ has no such case.

what: Converts a player's facing direction (N, E, S, W) into the grid step (dx, dy) the party moves one square in when it advances that way.
ev: Both map North to (0, 1), East to (1, 0), South to (0, -1), and West (the default case) to (-1, 0), returning the grid step for a facing.

what: Decides whether a melee weapon chain continues after a swing, returning true only when the swing killed the target and the damage was not a missed swing (engine reading of SRD R27).
where: Mordor.Core/Combat.cs struct.PlayerSwings (closest related, but it only sets the per-weapon swing count and does not decide whether a chain continues after a kill)
ev: No candidate decides whether a melee chain continues after a swing based on whether the target was killed and the damage was not a missed swing; the candidates handle swing counts, single blows, damage, kill credit, and sounds, but none returns a continuation boolean like `weaponChainContinues`.

what: Computes the base experience points a thief earns for disarming a trap, from the thief's value multiplied by half the guard guild level and divided by a factor that shrinks as the party leader's active level rises, then truncated to an integer.
ev: The core formula matches the C++ exactly (disarm chance × (monster guild level / 2) / (1 + first character's guild level / 333)), with differences only in the optional party-size factor (defaults to 1) and the rounding mode (ToEven versus the C++ `vbInt`, which the C++ itself flags as unverified).

what: Splits the gold won from a fight evenly among the party members by floor division, returning zero if the party size is not positive (step 3 of the R46 fight-gold rule).
ev: PayGold splits the fight's gold across the party by calling `GoldShare.Share(total, Party.Members.Count)` and pays every member, the dead included, but it rounds with CLng (half to even) rather than floor, has no explicit non-positive party-size guard, and is embedded in the larger monGetGold routine.

what: Reports whether option flag number idx (0–7, in kNamedFlagKeys order) is set in the player's OptionFlags, returning false for any other index.
ev: No candidate maps an index 0–7 to a named option flag; the nearest, Mordor.Core/GameOptions.cs Ini.Flag, reads a boolean by section and key string from an ini file, not from an indexed flag struct.

what: Computes the damage an archive-form electrocution or acid attack deals to a character, scaling with the monster's guild level, reduced by character level, and cut by the character's resistance percentage (floored at zero).
ev: The candidate applies the same resistance step (`dmg - dmg * ((resistance / 2) * .01)`, with a zero floor), but no visible candidate contains the archive base formula `(ln M + M/15) * 4.55` with its random spread and character-level reduction, and the visible `SpecialHits.Raw` call is for acid spit rather than archive electrocution.

what: Computes a character's experience-point total for a given level as a quadratic in the level, scaled by the guild's XP factor and the race multiplier (the exact Fn12A1 formula is unknown, so this is an assumed one).
ev: Candidate 3 is the same-named function with the same inputs (level, guild EXP, race EXP) and purpose, but it is the actual MAINMOD2.BAS loop with Currency roundings, not the C++ assumed quadratic `88.09*n^2 + 45.45*n + 0.264` multiplied by the race factor.

what: Chest trap 8 (Blackout) wipes every active spell effect from the character who opened the chest.
ev: ClearSpellEffects wipes the character's spell mask and spell-granted resistances and then recomputes, and its doc comment says this is what the Blackout chest trap does (MONSMOD.BAS:3605-3609), though it uses a mask and resistance array rather than the C++ `activeEffectIds` list.

what: Removes one copy of a given item from a shelf, drawing at random among the alignments that still have stock (after first trying the unaligned stock), and reports whether anything was removed.
where: Mordor.Core/StoreStock.cs StoreStock.RemoveOne (listed as at.RemoveOne in the candidate)
ev: It makes the same unaligned-stock check first and returns false if there is none, then draws random alignments 0-3 until one has stock, takes one, and returns true, matching the C++ function line for line.

what: Computes the spell ceiling for a category by taking the largest SpellMax value for that category across all guilds that have a spell table, which caps how high a spell level a character can reach in that category.
ev: No candidate computes a global per-category maximum of SpellMax across all guilds; they all test SpellMax per guild or per character (e.g. Spells.cs it.SpellLevelFor, GuildData.cs GuildDefs.CanCast), so none returns the C++ `spellCeiling` value.

what: Reports whether a monster group still has at least one living member, which decides if the group can keep fighting under the melee rules (R2, R3, R5).
ev: The living-member check appears only inline here (`runs[group].FirstOrDefault(m => m.Alive)`, returning early if none) as a gate on a number-key target, not as a standalone predicate that reports whether the group still has a living member, as `groupStanding` does.

what: Picks a random facing for a rotator (rule R96) by drawing a uniform value from 0 to 3 from the context's RNG and casting it to a Facing.
ev: No candidate draws a random facing from the RNG; the closest, DungeonNav.FaceTowards, only turns to a given facing and mentions the rotator's `Int(Rnd * 4) + 1` roll in a comment without implementing it.

what: Computes the maximum item level allowed for a guild's quest reward, derived from the quest monster level for the guild's level and capped at a fixed maximum.
where: Mordor.Core/Rules.cs Rules.QuestItemBand (paired with Rules.QuestTier for the first step)
ev: QuestItemBand matches the `Int(tier / 1.5) + 1` item-band step, and QuestTier covers the level-to-tier step, but QuestTier rounds (ToEven) where the C++ uses floor, and no single candidate composes the full chain with the cap at 7.

what: Detect Rock spell: when not lost, it marks the rock record of the square one step ahead of the caster as known rock, and when lost, it flags that square as not rock.
ev: Look finds the square ahead (via SquareAhead) and writes its features into the automap, but only for features that pass a random perception roll, it never records rock specifically, and it has no lost branch that flags the square as not rock.

what: Walks the square-effect checks for a floor square in a fixed order, currently applying only the anti-magic refusal of casts and the always-noticed teleporter, while leaving pits, chutes, water and the other effects unapplied because their data is missing.
ev: AfterMove runs the square's effects in the original's sub0835 order (anti-magic, teleporter, pit, chute and the rest) in one pass, but it also handles movement, saves and encounters, and the C++ function applies only the anti-magic and teleporter effects, skipping the rest for missing data.

what: Serializes the current session's game state (party, members, guilds, pack, floors, guildmasters) into the ASCII save text, prefixed by a format version and terminated by an end marker.
ev: No candidate serializes the game state to save text; the closest, GameFiles.DataVersion, only reads a version string from the start of an existing data file, and the other candidates cover window closing, updates, audio, and mods.

what: Rolls a random percentage against the uncapped trap confidence to decide whether a chest trap is shown to the player.
ev: TrapReadout also rolls 1..100 against a confidence figure and shows the real trap when the roll passes, otherwise a random one, but it clamps confidence to 2..98 before adding the guild term and returns a trap index rather than the C++ bool test on the uncapped value.

what: Decides whether a click on a store row is allowed while the store selection frame is open, refusing a different row unless the town mod settings permit row changes.
ev: The candidate returns false by default and true only when a live mod answers that row changes are allowed while the store frame is up, which matches the C++ final `return mods.rowChangeAllowed`; the candidate omits the `!sel.choosing` and same-row early returns, which must be handled by its caller.

what: Returns the slot index of the companion the player is carrying, or -1 if nothing or a body is carried, which the carry-choice logic uses to decide which companion is kept.
ev: No candidate returns the carried slot index or -1; the closest is the inline `CarryingCompanion >= 0 && < CompanionSlots.Slots` check in DungeonWindow.axaml.cs `keeps.PutDownWhatIsCarried` (and CityWindow.axaml.cs `is.PutDownWhatIsCarried`), but that check sits inside a put-down action that also releases the companion and writes a message.

what: Returns true when the room's first foe slot holds the emptied-room marker (ref -1), which is how the game's rules record that a room has been cleared of monsters.
ev: MarkCleared contains the same test, `rec.Foes[0].Ref == -1`, as a guard that skips already-emptied rooms, but it is one step inside a larger method that also writes the room and adjusts the tally, not a standalone check like `roomAlreadyEmptied`.

what: Decides whether a store choice gets cleared when its row is hidden by a mod, returning the hidden flag unchanged (so with no mod, nothing is cleared).
ev: The C++ function is a trivial pass-through of a "row hidden by mod" flag that clears a store choice, and no candidate clears a store choice on a hidden row; the closest, ModSlots.ShowStoreColumns and ModHost.StoreRowVisible, only show/hide columns or rows and never clear a choice.

what: Puts down whatever the party is carrying: if it is a companion, that companion is released from its carrying slot and the party's carry state is cleared, otherwise the carried body is put down.
ev: The companion branch matches (it releases the slot, clears the carry, and returns a line), but the candidate checks the carried character before the companion and handles the body case itself, whereas the C++ takes the companion path first and delegates bodies to `putDownBodyOnly`, and the candidate never sets an occupied flag.

what: Checks whether a cursed item can be uncursed at the clerk's shop, returning the refusal message if the item isn't cursed or isn't equipped, and nullptr when the uncurse may proceed.
ev: Both return the not-cursed refusal first, then the not-equipped refusal, and null otherwise, so the checks and their order match.

what: Rolls a d100 against the character's thieving skill to decide whether a chest trap is successfully disarmed.
ev: The method makes the same d100 check (`_rng.Next(100) + 1 <= thieving`) to decide disarm, but it also sets the trap caption, awards chest XP, and writes to the log, which the C++ function does not do.

what: Searches for a dead body one day at a time, rolling a percentage chance each day (based on level and easy-find) until it is found or the 2,000,000-day cap is reached, and reports the days spent and whether it was found.
ev: It has the same day-by-day loop that returns the days spent, but it uses a different chance model (a ceiling that drops after a threshold, a 0.1 floor, and a 2,000,000-day guard) instead of the C++'s fixed `rescueChance(level, easyFind)` with a negative chance never succeeding.

what: Returns the one-line usage string for the `use` command, telling the player the syntax `use <member> <slot>` and that it uses an item from a pack slot (potions heal, scrolls cast).
ev: The C++ function only returns the usage help string for the `use` command, while the candidates implement the actual use-item behavior (`UseItem`, `UseSelectedItem`, `OnSheetUse`) and none of them returns usage text, so the closest match is a related routine that performs the command's effect rather than the same thing.

what: When a creature is charmed, it is marked as charmed and disengaged from the fight, the caster gets a kill credited for it, and the player is told the creature leaves the fight, with no damage dealt and no experience awarded.
ev: Blow.Credit handles a charm (removes=false) as taking the creature off alive with no damage, which matches the C++, but it awards experience where the C++ awards none and never marks the creature charmed, disengaged, or announced, and no candidate does the kill credit with the charm message.

what: Shifts the "counted" flags for loaded party members down by one slot, starting at the given index, so a removed dead body drops out of the count of bodies that are still loaded, and clears the last slot.
ev: The candidate also removes dead bodies while more than one is loaded and keeps the last one, but it unloads them through `RemoveTheDead` and never shifts a "counted" flag array, so the C++ helper's index-based shift has no direct equivalent.

what: Caps the deepest floor a player has reached at 14 for the town's store stock, so floor 15 is never stocked, which reproduces an off-by-one quirk of the original game.
ev: The C++ function is a one-line cap of the deepest reached floor at 14 (kTownDeepestFloor), and StoreStock.Replenish applies the same cap (`Math.Clamp(deepestReached, 1, DeepestStocked)` with the comment citing the 14 cap at MAINMOD.BAS 1505-1508), but it is embedded in a much larger restock routine and clamps the lower bound to 1 rather than passing values through unchanged, so it is a related implementation of the same cap rather than an exact function match.

what: Casting Passwall moves the party one square forward in the caster's facing direction, then checks the landed square's rock and dungeon level to decide the arrival outcome, and charges the spell's point cost.
ev: StepThrough moves one square forward in the facing direction and then tests the landed square for rock, matching castPasswall's move-then-test, but it wraps at the map edges and does not check dungeon level, charge points, or settle the arrival (Teleporting.cs Outcome.ForSpell covers the level and rock outcome test).

what: When a character dies in a party of one, this marks them dead if they aren't already, runs the lone-death flow and rescue handling, and emits a raise offer if a raise is pending; in a larger party it instead prunes the dead from the party.
ev: Candidate 1 follows the C++ steps in the same order: the head, save, prune-and-return when the party has more than one member, SetDead if not already dead, SaveChar, OfferRescue, and the raise offer when the character is dead with a pending raise.

what: Refuses a Seer's locate-monster request when the target's level is above the deepest level the player can reach, per rule R64 step 2.
ev: Inside the monster/item locate flow it runs the same check, `if (level > Seer.DeepestHeCanReach)`, and refuses with the "too deep" message, though the deepest level is a static property rather than a parameter and the check is embedded in a larger method.

what: Applies the disease-spores chest trap (R38): each party member rolls against half their Disease resistance, and on a hit becomes diseased at the party's dungeon level.
ev: Both roll once per party member against half the Disease resistance (`roll*100 < pct/2`) and set diseased at the dungeon level on a hit, but Spring reads the resistance through `Effects.ResistancePercent`, which may add item bonuses where the C++ reads the raw `resistances.resist` field.

what: In combat, when the CombatSetting is 3 or higher, it decides what a chosen buffer does: items are used at once, spells become a standing order rather than being cast immediately, and anything else does nothing.
ev: For CombatSetting >= 3 with a spell buffer, ApplyDefault sets a standing spell order instead of casting, matching the C++ spell branch, but it returns no item action (items are deferred to DungeonWindow.CombatSettingItem) and it takes the character's setting rather than a buffer number.

what: Rolls a random special-attack damage value for a monster, combining a random component scaled by range with a kind-dependent share and applying the game's 0.7 damage scale, rounded down.
ev: Kind.Raw draws `rng.NextDouble()`, computes `VbInt((Floor((rnd*range+1)/2) + share) * 0.7)`, and uses a breath/other share split that mirrors the C++ `half` and `share` steps, though the C++ `specialAttackShare` helper is not visible, so its share values are inferred.

what: Returns true when a spell's raw effect code is at or above the offset threshold (200), marking it as a whole-party spell effect in the game's magic rules.
ev: It returns `s.Effect >= PartyOffset`, the same whole-party threshold test as the C++ `rawEffect >= kEffectWholePartyOffset`, differing only in taking the `Spell` rather than the raw integer, and it assumes `PartyOffset` is 200, which I did not verify.

what: Runs the SRD victory sequence after a fight, marking the room cleared, paying fight gold, and recording monster kills for each party member and checking the killer against the Hall of Records (DeadliestCreature).
ev: EndCombat marks the room cleared, awards and pays the gold, and records each dead monster for every party member, matching the C++ steps 2-6, but the candidate is truncated before any Hall of Records (DeadliestCreature) check for the killer, so step 7 is unconfirmed.

what: Handles a character's death outside of combat by passing the dying character's slot and the cause of death to killCharacter, which applies the death to the party and companion roster.
ev: The C++ comment states DieOutsideCombat = Kill(_ch, why), which matches candidate 1 exactly, though the C++ passes `false` for killCharacter's last argument while candidate 1 leaves Kill's `sub0930` flag at its default of `true`, so that flag should be checked.

what: Returns a guild's maximum Attack and Defence values by looking them up in per-guild tables, which the header notes are maxed independently and follow the character sheet for Sorcerer and Wizard.
ev: GuildAD returns a guild's attack and defence from the same guild data, but it takes a level and accumulates per-level awards rather than returning a fixed per-guild maximum from a lookup table.

what: Renews a fading Bind on a companion by resetting a bound companion whose binding level is below base back to the base level, refusing if the companion is bound for life or joined freely.
ev: Both write `BindingLevel` on a Bind spell and handle bind-for-life, but BindCompanion raises the level to a spell-derived value and never refuses joined-freely companions or resets a level below base to the base level, so it does not renew a fading Bind.

what: Computes the General Store's buy-back price for an item by halving its base value and rounding to the nearest whole currency unit, with half-units rounded to even.
ev: PriceToSell is the same kind of store-payout-to-the-player with half-to-even rounding, but it computes 0.9 × value divided by a stock term and an ID-level term rather than the plain 0.5 × baseValue, and X87.RoundToLong only matches the rounding step.

what: Computes the casting cost of a spell in the Mordor RPG spreadsheet path as initial spell level × guild modifier × ratio × 1.9 divided by the spell level, returning 0 when the spell level is zero.
ev: The candidate is the engine-path cost (via Rules.Fn1485Price, with a 1.9 constant and floor handling) rather than the spreadsheet formula `initialSpellLevel × guildMod × ratio × 1.9 / spellLevel` with its zero-level guard, so it is a related version with different inputs and rounding.

what: Reports whether a map coordinate on a floor of the dungeon is on the 30x30 grid (1-based), returning -1 when it is off-map and 0 otherwise, though the floor's area layout is not yet implemented so it never reports which area lies there.
ev: It bounds-checks the level and the x/y square against the floor's width and height before acting, but only inside a rock-teleport routine that writes the rock square and kills the party, and it returns nothing like the C++ -1/0 off-map result.

what: Counts the monsters in the current encounter that are still alive, which the combat rules use to decide whether the fight continues.
ev: It collects the same living monsters that `livingFoes` counts (`if (!m.Alive) continue;`), but it returns them grouped by kind rather than as a count, and no candidate returns a plain count of living monsters.

what: Rolls a percent chance (kCasterFailPercent, 50 per the R27.5 note) that a companion's spellcasting attempt fails.
ev: No candidate rolls a percent chance that a companion's spellcast fails; the closest, Seer.SearchFailsEarly, is a similar percent gate but for a seer's search and uses `level * 5`, not a fixed 50.

what: When the party enters a square, it turns the party to face whichever wall-facing bit (north, east, south, then west) is set there, and marks the square as explored if any face bits are set.
ev: AfterMove's comment says it runs "the facing bits" as one step of the square's effects, but the candidate is truncated before that step, so the turn-toward-wall and explored-marking logic is not visible to confirm a match.

what: Checks a target creature against the weapon gates of the melee rules (R13-R15), returning whether the attack is blocked for needing a good weapon, nullified by immunity, or allowed to proceed.
ev: PlayerSwings applies the NeedsGoodWeapon block (a weapon below half the monster's LevelFound is skipped for that hand), but it skips the hand instead of returning a gate outcome, and no candidate performs the immunity nullification check.

what: Computes the protection defence value for a given slot value as the cube-like curve l·(3l), where l is the natural log of the slot value, returning 0 for non-positive inputs.
ev: Both compute Log(p) * (Log(p) * 3) and return 0 when the input is not positive; the only difference is that the port wraps the result in VbInt and takes the Protection value from a Character rather than a raw slot value.

what: Rolls a percent chance, based on the character's CON, for whether a successful raise (resurrection) costs the character a point of CON.
ev: The candidate computes the same CON-based loss chance (`max(0, 50 - CON*2)`) that the C++ function passes to its percent roll, but it returns only the threshold and does not perform the roll itself.

what: Reports whether an item was issued by a guild, which the game uses to decide whether it can be dropped, given, or swapped.
ev: Both take an item and return whether it is a guild-issued crest, with IsGuildIssued identifying it by SpecialType in the guild range where the C++ checks a guildIssued flag or isGuildItem(), a structural difference I could not verify against the port's Item class.

what: Reports whether monsters are still present in an encounter, returning true when combat is not over or when waiting monsters remain to join.
ev: No candidate returns a presence predicate of the form "combat not over OR waiting count > 0"; the closest, Mordor.App/DungeonWindow.axaml.cs keeps.CombatTick, branches on the fight and the waiting group but runs a combat tick rather than reporting whether monsters are present.

what: Builds the list of companion slots that a caster can try to raise from the dead, keeping only dead companions that aren't carried, aren't already pending a raise, aren't the caster, and are on the same dungeon level and area as the party.
ev: PickUpBody applies a similar filter (dead, same level and area, not already carried) but to player characters for the pickup list, not to companion slots for raising, and it has no caster, pending-raise, or companion-slot checks.

what: While the character has a disease (diseaseLevel above zero), any healing they receive is halved, rounded down.
ev: No candidate halves healing based on disease. `AilmentStep` handles disease curing and hit loss, and `SpellHeal` computes a heal amount with no disease check.

what: Counts how many distinct monster types are represented among the party's living companions, grouping live companions by their monsterId so each type is counted once, which determines the number of groups in the Port's roster.
ev: No candidate counts distinct monsterIds among live companions; the closest, DungeonWindow.CompanionsDrift and LetCompanionGo, count distinct `Def.Id` over live combat monsters (not companions) for a different purpose, and none of the candidates implements the C++ dedup-over-companions logic.

what: Checks every version stamp on an imported Mordor file or record against the required "1.1" stamp, refusing the import with a player-facing message if any stamp differs, and allowing it otherwise.
ev: Both refuse an import on a bad version stamp, but StampOk checks one stamp per file, while the C++ checks every stamp in a list against exact "1.1" equality, and VersionAccepted also accepts an empty stamp and any stamp whose first four characters match, which the C++ would refuse.

what: Shows the watched character a message that they were accidentally electrocuted, with the damage amount, regardless of whether they were the one targeted by the caption guard.
ev: Its doc comment lists electrocution among the specials a landed hit allows, but the visible body is truncated before that branch, and the closest caption helper (MonsterAttack.cs Caption) only shows text for the watched character without the electrocution wording or damage amount.

what: Returns the item's own spell level when it is non-negative, or the caster's current guild spell level when the item level is negative, as the R6 engine's rule for item-cast spell strength.
ev: It substitutes the caster's guild spell level for an item level when the level is not positive, but the C++ substitutes only for negative levels, so a level of 0 differs (candidate 3's CastSpell has the same negative branch with a different zero case).

what: Advances the party's play clock by converting the elapsed real time since the last tick into 1/10000-second units and adding it to each member's PlaySeconds, wrapping the time of day at 86400 seconds.
ev: Tick does the same core job (adds the elapsed time since each member's last tick to PlaySeconds, wrapping across midnight, then resets the start time), but it stores seconds rather than 1/10000-second units, adds a pause gate and a -1 reset sentinel the C++ lacks, and its early `return` skips the remaining members after the first uninitialised one, which the C++ does not do.

what: Computes the spit share for a group of living companions as N / (N + 1), returning zero when no companions are alive.
ev: Slot uses the same N/(N+1) share and returns no spit when no companions are alive, but it embeds that share as a random-roll threshold and then draws a slot, rather than returning the share value as spitShare does.

what: Computes how many items a seer takes from a stack of n, as a randomized rounded fraction of n clamped to between 1 and the seer maximum (3) and to n itself.
ev: Carriers computes the same take (half-to-even rounding of n minus a random share of n, clamped to 3, to n, and to at least 1), but it then goes on to draw names and return a sentence instead of returning the count.

what: Moves a dragged pack slot into the first empty vault slot, refusing hands, guild-issued items, and equipped items, and reporting "Out of room!" when the vault is full.
ev: It matches the free-slot search, the "vault full" refusal, and the move that empties the pack slot, but it omits the guild-issued refusal and returns true for an empty source instead of refusing it, and the equipped check and "Out of room!" message live in the caller (CityWindow.Deposit) rather than in this method.

what: Rolls a random percentage against half the character's disease resistance to decide whether a disease takes hold (the T3 disease check, with its exact formula flagged as unconfirmed).
ev: The disease test is the same (`rng.NextDouble() * 100 < resistance / 2.0` decides whether the character catches the disease), but it is embedded in a larger trap-dispatch method rather than existing as a standalone check, and it uses a character-derived resistance value instead of a raw input.

what: Rolls the damage a character takes from falling down a chute (R60), a random amount scaled by dungeon level and the Log(4) factor, or zero if the character is levitating.
ev: The damage formula matches (floor of Rnd times level times 10.5, times Log of the race factor, plus 5, rounded half to even), but Rules.ChuteDamage has no levitating check (the C++ returns 0 when levitating) and takes a race size where the C++ hardcodes Log(4); that gate is in Chute.Land, which also applies the damage and builds messages.

what: Walks a party onto a chute trap, rolling for each member's fall (the leader first, and followers falling automatically if the leader fell and the player chose to follow), and applies each resulting fall to the party.
ev: Both walk the party member by member, leader first, roll each fall, and apply it, but the port asks the follow question only when the leader does not float, rolls for followers even when following, and carries out the landing and party-floor updates itself, whereas the C++ takes `followAnswer` as a parameter, skips the roll for followers when the leader fell and the answer was yes, and leaves the party floor unchanged.

what: When a character's new level qualifies as an attack/defence award level, it adds the guild's configured attack and defence increments to that character's membership in the guild and posts a message saying their attack and defence improved.
ev: GuildADSingle applies the same qualifying-level test and adds the guild's AttPerLevel and DefPerLevel, but it recomputes a cumulative total from level 1 and returns it, rather than incrementing a character's stored membership on a level-up and posting a message.

what: Lets the player pen one companion for sale in town, checking the pen cap and alignment, then pricing the sale from the companion's base worth and pen count and paying the gold to the income payee.
ev: PenOne covers only the pen step (cap check, then increment the sold creature's own-alignment pen), but it does not validate the seller or companion, compute the pre-sale count, price the sale, pay the payee, or report the result, and it always returns true where the C++ penOne can return false.

what: Returns the dungeon level used for the first draw of a teleporter destination, which is the party's current level (the rule about the old versus new level is unresolved).
ev: ForSquare draws the first member's destination level from the level loaded before the move (`fromLevel`), which matches the C++ `party.dungeonLevel` as the current level, but it also applies the Z2 override and other per-member logic the C++ function does not model, so it is only a related version.

what: Returns the respawn time adjustment, as a non-positive number of seconds, that subtracts 5 seconds for each area below the header count that is still empty.
ev: It applies the same 5-second-per-area term, (headerAreas - tally) * 5, but as part of the full respawn time (base 1200 + 150 per level, clamped to at least 120 s) rather than returning the non-positive adjustment alone, and it has no zero clamp when the tally exceeds the header count.

what: Maps a companion's alignment to the monster-table index for Id 307 (Morgul for Neutral or Good, Shadow Ninja for Evil), falling back to the Neutral reference if the table lacks Id 307.
ev: For Id 307 it returns the Neutral creature (Morgul) for a Neutral alignment, the Evil creature (Shadow Ninja) for Evil, and the first table index with the Id (Morgul) for Good or Unaligned, matching id307Ref, though it returns -1 instead of 278 when no creature has Id 307 and finds the indices by alignment rather than hard-coding 278 and 389.

what: Decides whether a store will accept (shelve) an item for sale, letting unaligned items through and otherwise requiring the item's alignment to match the store's alignment, using an assumed rule the comment marks as unconfirmed.
ev: Both decide whether a store takes an item for its shelf, but the C++ rule is only "unaligned passes, else item alignment must equal store alignment", while ShelvesSale also requires the item to be uncursed, passes through an unseen ShelvedBySelling check, and enforces a shelf cap.

what: Applies the R25 companion rule for melee damage, halving the companion's modifier when the target is unseen and otherwise leaving it unchanged.
ev: CompanionStrikes halves a companion's blow against an invisible target, as the C++ function does, but it adds an exception when the companion has property bit 0, and the C++ function has no such exception.

what: Equips a pack item to a party member by validating the wearing rules (hands, guild, stats, and so on) and reporting the result, including a warning if the item turns out to be cursed.
ev: It runs the same wear-refusal check (`WearRefusal`, `IsWearable`) and toggles the equipped state, but it is silent on success and does not produce the C++ result text (empty slot, already worn, cursed-on-wear message, AD line), and it does not use the `EquipProblem` lookup.

what: Rolls a percentile check against the companion breath chance computed from the lead and companion strengths, returning whether the companion's breath succeeds.
ev: The method computes the same 50/80/20 breath chance from the lead foe's and companion's guild levels and rolls a percentile against it, but it also handles the friendly-fire mishap and the group sweep, and it computes the chance inline rather than through a separate `companionBreathChance` function.

what: Clears a pending raise-dead state for a party member by erasing its stored chance, kind, and caster entries from the session's feature state.
ev: Accept's failure branch zeroes RaiseKind, RaiseChance and RaisedBy, which matches the three erases, but it is embedded in a dice roll and the complications path, while Forget clears only chance and caster (setting caster to " ") and leaves kind alone.

what: Stores a party member's combat order setting (the order string keyed by member index) into the session's feature state, which the game's buffer rules read when deciding what that member does.
ev: No candidate stores a raw order string under a member-keyed feature-state entry; the closest ones (CastInCombat via SetOrder, and Sub0BDE via `_party.OrderFor(m)`) set a typed per-member combat order, which covers the storing of a member's order but not the same keyed-string storage.

what: Rolls a percentile die against the breath-fire chance computed from the lead and companion guild levels, returning true when the breath fires (SRD rule R23).
ev: It computes the same breath chance (50, or 80/20 from the lead foe's guild level against the companion's) and tests a percentile roll against it, but only as the opening step of a larger routine that also handles mishaps and the sweep, and it has no standalone roll-against-percent function like `breathFireRoll`.

what: Resolves one party member's combat turn in a round: skips paralysed or dead members, handles Defend orders, and for Fight orders works through each equipped weapon's swings against the front living monster, applying the weapon-floor gate and the kill-continues-chain rule.
where: Mordor.Core/Combat.cs PlayerSwings (candidate 1; enclosing class not shown in the excerpt)
ev: PlayerSwings matches the C++ weapon loop, per-weapon swing count, and NeedsGoodWeapon floor gate that sets Defend and clears the item order, but it does not cover the dead/paralysed early return, the Defend-order suppression, guild selection, or the kill-continues-chain rule, and it adds a no-weapon branch the C++ lacks.

what: Computes the base damage for acid and electrocution attacks by rolling a random value scaled by the monster's modifier and applying the R39 formula (with a 0.7 multiplier).
ev: For the non-breath kinds (acid and electrocution), Raw applies the same `VbInt((Floor((rnd * range + 1) / 2) + range / 2) * 0.7)` formula, with the modifier derived from guild levels instead of passed in, and it differs only for breath, which uses `range / 4`.

what: Converts a typed gold amount into a whole-number gold figure, answering 0 for anything below 1 (negatives included) and otherwise rounding half to even, as the original GiveCommand gold prompt did.
ev: GoldFromTag does the half-to-even whole-number conversion (CLng), but it lacks the typed < 1 → 0 branch, so negatives would pass through as-is; that branch exists only in the separate GiveCommand.GoldAnswer prompt check, which returns the text "0" rather than converting it.

what: Returns the area a character is saved in for game purposes, mapping dungeon level 0 (the town) to area -1 and otherwise using the character's stored area.
ev: It returns the stored M59BB for current saves, as the C++ does, but it adds a square-based fallback for old saves and a rock-death rule via `AreaOr`, and it only returns -1 at level 0 when no stored area exists, whereas the C++ returns -1 at level 0 unconditionally.

what: Caps the depth of the shelf of stocked items at the lower of the deepest level the player has reached and the game's stocking limit of 15 (kDeepestStocked), so the shop's stock depth follows the player's progress.
ev: It applies the same cap, `Math.Clamp(deepestReached, 1, DeepestStocked)`, but embedded in the restock routine and with an added lower bound of 1, so no candidate is a standalone equivalent of `cappedShelfDepth`.

what: Resolves opening a chest during a fight: the disarm roll, trap effects, the deadly-trap check that can kill the opener, and then the split of chest gold and placement of chest items into the party's inventories, leaving any unplaceable items in the chest.
ev: OpenChestBy runs the whole chest-opening sequence and matches the C++ death path, where the opener dies and the chest stays unemptied, but its visible text omits the gold split and item placement, and it adds teleport and prune steps the C++ lacks, while OpenChest (candidate 1) covers only the disarm and trap-effect steps.

what: Computes the spell point cost of a Mordor spell from its start spell level, spell point ratio, and base modifier, divided by the spell level, returning 0 when the spell level is zero.
ev: Candidate 1 computes the same spell point cost from the same ingredients (spell level, rate, base modifier squared, 1.9 factor) via `Rules.Fn1485Price`, but it takes a Spell and Character and adds guild selection, rate lookup, and flooring, so it does not match the C++ function's four-input product-divided-by-level with a zero-level guard.

what: Computes the wiki-listed cost of a spell for a character, scaling the spell's base cost by the ratio of spell level to the character's spell level and the guild's spell modifier (defaulting to 1 when unset), with a zero result when the divisor is zero.
ev: It computes a spell's point cost for a character from the spell's level, base cost, and guild rates, but it uses the source's Rules.Fn1485Price arithmetic (no `- 0.0001` epsilon, no `guildMod` default of 1, and no `level/characterSpellLevel` integer ratio) rather than the wiki R86 formula that wikiSpellCost implements.

what: Arrives the party in town, clearing lost-position and lost-level flags, resting every member (curing ailments and spell effects, refilling hit points and spell points, aging them by rest days), and replenishing town store and pen stock on the first member's rest.
ev: RestOnArrival matches the C++ arriveInTown steps 1, 2, and 5 (clearing lost flags, the Hall of Records check, and the rest for every member with the store and pens turned over on the first member's rest), but the C++ function also clears paralysis, spell effects, and resistances and refills hit points and spell points before aging, and those steps are only in Candidate 1 (Character.RestInCity), which lacks the lost-flag clearing and the Hall of Records check.

what: Applies the item-use rules for Mordor in a fixed order: it refuses silently if the user is incapacitated or the item's special type is negative, reports "no effect", "out of charges", "must be in the dungeon", "Nothing Happens" or "must be equipped" as appropriate, and computes the item's alignment fit against the user before the charge is spent.
ev: Problem reproduces most of the C++ refusal chain (negative SpecialType, no charges, out of charges, must-be-equipped, spell alignment) but omits the incapacitated and dungeon-only checks, the alignment-fit computation, and the charge spend, so no single candidate covers the whole function.

what: Checks whether a character meets a starter item's stat requirements by comparing each of the six character stats against the item's minimum, failing if any stat is too low.
ev: Its final loop compares the six character stats against `it.StatsRequired` and fails if any is too low, which matches the C++ check, but it is one part of a larger equip check that also tests hands, wear limits, guild and guild level, and returns a message string rather than a bool.

what: Handles the town menu's descend command by refusing if the party is already underground or has no living member, otherwise placing the party on the level-1 up-stairs with its members' positions and lost flags set, and reporting the descent to the player.
ev: No candidate handles the town-to-dungeon descent (checking for a living member, placing the party on the level-1 up-stairs, and setting the in-dungeon flags); the closest, `CityWindow.RestOnArrival`, does the reverse trip into town, and `DungeonWindow.SavePos` only records an existing party position.

what: Computes the Beneficial spell's heal range in Mordor (per SRD R4), giving a minimum of ROUNDDOWN(healMod × 0.5 − 1) and a maximum of ROUNDDOWN(healMod × 1 − 1), and returns no range for blank magnitudes or non-beneficial spells.
ev: It computes a heal amount for a spell from the same kind of inputs, but it rolls a random value with a different formula (mod1 − Int(U × …) + 1) instead of returning the fixed min/max range of ROUNDDOWN(healMod × 0.5 − 1) to ROUNDDOWN(healMod × 1 − 1), and it has no Beneficial-only or blank-magnitude check.

what: When the player asks the seer to locate a character, it rolls d100 against three times the character's level, returning the location (plus a note if they are dead) on success, a "lost connection" hint on a near miss, or a failure message otherwise.
ev: Candidate 1 uses the same `level * 3` need, the same `rng.Next(100) + 1` roll, the same near-miss branch (`roll + 10 >= need`) returning the "lost connection" level-only message, the same failure text, and the same success message with the dead-note, matching the C++ function line for line.

what: Checks whether an item can be given to another character, refusing if it is guild-issued, currently equipped, or the recipient has no free inventory slot, in that order.
ev: GiveItem makes the same three refusal checks in the same order (guild-issued, equipped, no free slot), but it also performs the transfer and the read-given step, which checkGive does not, and it returns a message string instead of a refusal enum.

what: Reduces a monster's special-attack damage by a resistance percentage (half the resistance value, applied as a fraction of the damage, rounded down), leaving damage unchanged when resistance is zero or negative.
ev: It returns damage unchanged when resistance is <= 0, otherwise `VbInt(damage - damage * (resistance / 2.0 * 0.01))`, which is the same formula and floor rounding as the C++ function.

what: Checks whether a monster kind is enabled by a spawn bitmask, where bit n set means monsters of class n may spawn, returning false for kinds with no valid class index.
ev: Locate tests `(area.SpawnMask & (1u << def.Type)) == 0` to decide whether a monster's class bit is enabled, which matches the core bit test, but it uses `def.Type` directly with no `classIndexOfKind` mapping and no range check, and it is embedded in a larger placement routine.

what: Decides whether a quest of a given kind (monster defeat or item fetch) is available to the player, based on the guild level threshold for each kind, and treats companion quests as never eligible.
ev: It applies the same level gates (below 5 gets no quest, and item quests need level above 15), but as part of a random roll rather than a pure eligibility check, it uses strict `> 15` where the C++ uses `>= 15`, and it has no companion-quest case.

what: Chest trap 6 ("Fate") rerolls the character's current hit points and spell points to random values between 1 and their maximums, then tells the player.
ev: The C++ chestFate rerolls the character's current HP and SP to random values between 1 and their maximums, but no candidate does that; Candidate 5's Companion.Apply mentions Fate rerolling the caster, which is a spell effect and not the chest trap, and Candidate 3's ChestTraps.Spring covers the other chest traps without trap 6 visible in the excerpt.

what: Blurs a map coordinate on one axis by a random offset of up to `spread`, in a random direction, and clamps the result to the range 1 to `limit`, per game rule R137.
ev: Each axis gets the same sign flip, then an offset of `(int)(NextDouble() * spread)`, then a clamp to 1..limit, which matches blurAxis; Blur just applies that twice (x and y) with separate width and height limits, and it lacks blurAxis's explicit `spread <= 0` guard, which only matters for negative spreads.

what: Clamps a raw item chance value (for Identify, Recognise, Rename, or Destroy) to the minimum and maximum bounds defined for that chance kind.
ev: No candidate is a generic per-kind clamp, but IdentifyChance clamps its result to the same 10..90 band as the C++ Identify kind (Rename and Recognise use matching bounds in other candidates), while no candidate covers the Destroy 25..90 band.

what: Maps the saved identification-level code from a data file (0 through 3, counting down) to the game's IdLevel enum, with codes 1 and 2 inferred rather than sourced and any other value mapped to Unknown.
ev: This is the inverse direction, converting an IdLevel to its countdown code as `3 - (int)known`, and it has no handling for unknown values, while the C++ function converts a saved code to an IdLevel with an explicit switch and an Unknown default.

what: Converts a spell effect code into its charm index by subtracting the first charm effect value, following SRD c56, so the game can tell which charm slot an effect belongs to.
ev: The method computes `s.Effect - 75` and compares it to a monster class index, which is the same charm-offset subtraction as `charmIndex`, but it only uses the result in a check and never returns the charm index itself.

what: Computes a spell's scaled magnitude (damage or healing) from its base value G, the caster's level or spell level S, and a logarithmic growth term, following the Mordor spell-damage and healing formulas.
ev: SpellHeal computes the same deterministic term as scaledMagnitude with base 10 and no log shift (`baseHeal + baseHeal*Log(sl)/Log(10) + (int)((sl/10.0)*(power-1))`), but it then subtracts a random roll and clamps to at least 1, so it returns a sampled heal rather than the scaled magnitude; SpellDamage has the same shape with log base 5 and log(SL+1), plus resistance.

what: Applies a stat modifier to a character's ability score, raising or lowering it by the given amount (reversed for curse-type effects), and caps the result at the race's maximum plus a fixed bonus of 5.
ev: The per-stat logic matches (ceiling is race Max + 5, a reversed positive modifier subtracts, otherwise it adds, and the result is clamped silently to the ceiling), but ApplyStatMods works on a whole item rather than one stat, also applies the race Min floor that the C++ omits, and adds messages, Hall of Records checks, and recalculations.

what: Computes a character's remaining creation points by taking the base pool of 30, adding the race's bonus points, and subtracting the points already spent on stats above the race's minimums.
ev: Roll uses the same formula, `30 + BonusPoints - sum(base[i] - Min[i])`, but it builds its own base (min + 5, capped at max) instead of taking an arbitrary base array as the C++ function does.

what: Rounds a CCur value to four decimal places using round-half-even, so that a fraction like 1/3 becomes 0.3333, as the game's currency rule requires.
ev: Both take a double, round it to four decimal places half-to-even, and return a double; the C++ scales by 10000 and divides back, while per.Cur calls Math.Round(v, 4, MidpointRounding.ToEven), which differs only in floating-point scaling details.

what: Takes the party down a chute to the destination level with no roll, then re-runs the square on arrival, after refusing if the Limited Version forbids it.
ev: The port's TAKE path sends every member down with no roll, clamps the floor for the limited build, and lands them, but it denies with a per-member line instead of refusing outright as takeChute does, and the square re-run after arrival lives in ArriveBySpell rather than in this method.

what: Puts down the companion the party is carrying, clearing the carrying slot and companion index silently, as the rules require when a death occurs (R16.4).
ev: The C++ only clears the carry when it is a companion and never touches the companion slots, whereas ReleaseFollowers also releases every companion slot and clears any carried character, so it does more than the C++ function.

what: Decides whether a theft against a monster succeeds, using a percent chance equal to the thief's score minus twice the monster's level, clamped to 0–100.
ev: No candidate computes a theft success chance from score minus twice the monster level, clamped to 0-100; TheftSlot only picks the pack slot, and GroupAttacks lists theft among its specials but its body is truncated before any theft check, so it may call a success test that is not visible here.

what: When a lone character (party of one) dies, the function saves the character and then offers them a rescue, per rule R48.
ev: For a lone character, Sub0930 calls SaveChar and then OfferRescue in the same order as loneDeathFlow, but it also clears companions and carried items, sets the character dead, and may offer a raise, while OfferRescue alone matches only the second step.

what: Shows the player the Hall of Records by building a header line plus one description line for each of the twelve records and returning the combined text as the reply.
ev: OnHall shows the Hall of Records by opening a HallWindow dialog, which is the same user-facing action, but it does not build a text reply from one description line per record as cmdHall does, and HallWindow itself was not among the candidates.

what: Returns the item-band adjustment for a chest class, which shifts the treasure tier of items found in that kind of chest (for example, -1 for one class and no change for others).
ev: RollDrop applies a chest-class band shift (class 1 lowers both ends by 1, matching the C++ -1 entry), but it also raises the low end by 1 for class 3, which the C++ table (none, -1, none, none) does not do, and no candidate is a per-class lookup that returns the adjustment value.

what: Charms a creature into a free companion slot of the caster, binding it at the starting binding for the target's floor and marking it as not freely joined, or refuses if no slot is free.
ev: Binding.Initial computes the same starting binding for a charmed creature's floor (`min(5 + floor, 10)`), but no candidate has the slot-occupied refusal, the fill from the creature, the `joinedFreely = false` flag, or the message. Combat.cs at.Charmed also builds a companion from a charm, but it takes its binding from the spell level rather than the floor.

what: Ages a character by one unit (ageDays += 1) per call as a placeholder for the race-dependent aging mechanic, which is not yet implemented in the source.
ev: AgeBy does the core `Age += days` step, but it takes a caller-supplied day count and also returns an "You are now X older" message, whereas the C++ unconditionally adds 1 per call with no message.

what: Checks whether a given party member's guild has an open quest, by looking up the stored feature-state flag for that member and guild and testing whether it equals "1".
ev: The C++ function only checks whether a stored feature-state flag for the member and guild equals "1" (an open-quest test), while QuestMark.Of and Progress.QuestStateOf both derive "open" from the guild's QuestType and QuestDone fields rather than a keyed flag lookup, so the closest candidates cover the same open-quest question but with different data and outcomes.

what: Maps a companion's spawn mode number to the window of floor offsets, repeat/keep-previous behavior, or spawn table index used to place a companion monster in the dungeon.
ev: No candidate maps a companion spawn mode number to a floor-offset window, repeat/keep behavior, or table index; Mordor.Core/MdrLoader.cs LoadMonsters only reads the raw CompanionSpawnMode field, and Confinement.Fresh is about starting pens, not spawn windows.

what: Removes the gold amount from the character's on-hand wallet as part of a gold exchange, and if that drives on-hand gold negative, takes the shortfall from their bank balance and zeroes on-hand gold (R23.4).
ev: The candidate's lines `from.GoldOnHand -= amount` followed by the shortfall-to-bank and zero-on-hand block match the C++ logic exactly, but the candidate is a full transfer that also credits the recipient, rejects zero and over-available amounts, and catches overflow, so it is not the same function.

what: For the Asmodeus monster, it reduces the group count by one (never below one) so that Asmodeus does not take up a portrait slot in group 0.
ev: The same rule appears inline (`if (slots.Count > 0 && Fn0C3B(slots[0])) count = Math.Max(1, count - 1);`) but only as one step of a larger method that builds the portrait strip, and it takes a monster list rather than the id and count the C++ function takes.

what: Computes the character's natural Constitution, the stored CON stat with no modifier applied, which the morgue, raise, and revival chances use as their input.
ev: No candidate returns the stored CON stat; the closest ones (RaiseConLossChance, MorgueRaiseChance, CompanionChance, RaiseChance) take a CON value as input and apply a chance formula, and LevelUp only reads `Stats[Con]` inside its hit-gain logic.

what: Applies the effects of a landed blow, possibly stoning the target (if the stone check succeeds) and electrocuting it for damage that is subtracted from its hits, and returns the electrocution damage dealt.
ev: The doc comment says a companion's blow carries its stone and electrocution, and CompanionStrikes (Combat.cs) applies a stone constitution test, but both bodies are truncated before any electrocution damage or hits subtraction appears, so no candidate visibly implements the stone-then-electrocute logic that returns the damage dealt.

what: Computes the percent chance of natural death for a character past the old-age onset, as 5 plus the natural log of days beyond onset (floored at one day), clamped to 0–100, and returns 0 before onset.
ev: It implements the same old-age rule (onset at 98% of lifespan, then 5 + ln(excess), with a roll against it), but it takes the log of the excess in percent points rather than days, and it returns a bool from a roll instead of the chance value.

what: Forces a worn item off the character when it has an equip problem (such as a class or alignment restriction) and the item is not cursed, so the item is unequipped.
ev: Run has the same rule (unequip when an equip problem exists and the slot is not cursed) but applies it across the whole pack and uses the reduced `EquipProblem` check that skips free-hands and worn-count limits, which the C++ `equipProblem(ctx, c, inv, slot)` may include, so the outcomes differ in those cases.

what: Sets the game's Levitate, Sight Veil, See Invisible, or Protection ailment on a character, where the first three become on/off flags when the spell level is above zero and Protection stores the level itself.
where: Mordor.Core/Effects.cs Effects.Recompute (and Mordor.Core/SpellThrown.cs Companion.Apply for the direct-set path)
ev: The C++ function is a simple switch that sets Levitate, Invisible, and SeeInvisible to `level > 0` and Protection to the raw level, while the candidates set these states from the spell mask via Recompute (Protection = Guild.Level/2+1, with a Levitate-to-See-Invisible leak) and Companion.Apply sets the four states per target with Protection as caster level halved plus one, so none matches the level-based setter exactly.

what: Decides whether an emptied dungeon room has refilled yet, treating an unset stamp as always due and otherwise comparing the absolute elapsed time since it was emptied against the wait period.
ev: It has the same stamp logic (stamp 0 means due, otherwise absolute elapsed time against the respawn period), but it uses strict `>` where the C++ uses `>=`, and it adds a standing-group gate the C++ function does not have.

what: When the player presses the wait button, it either ends an awaited rescue or, if the leader is dead, enters the rescue wait, returning true only when the rescue wait is entered.
ev: Both do nothing unless the character is dead or awaiting rescue, both clear the awaiting flag and enter the rescue wait when awaiting, and both enter the rescue wait when dead; the candidate returns void and does UI work (hiding monsters, saving), and omits the C++ party-size check.

what: Builds a new companion from a charmed monster, carrying over its hit points before the spell (and max hits), the spell level as its binding level, and its alignment, per rule R51.2.
where: Mordor.Core/Combat.cs Combat.Charmed (the `Charmed` method; the class name is not shown in the excerpt)
ev: It builds the companion with `Hits = hitsBefore`, `MaxHits`, `BindingLevel = s.Level` and `Alignment` from the monster, the same R51.2 fields the C++ sets, though it omits `level` and `specialPropertyFlags`, which the C++ marks as UNKNOWN defaults.

what: Registers the typed "swap" command (for town and dungeon screens) and the "combine" command, each with its help text, so the player can move or merge items between pack slots.
ev: Candidate 2 implements the core of the typed swap with the same one-based slot numbers, slot-1 (hands) refusal, forty-slot limit, and exchange of empty slots, but no candidate registers the typed "swap" or "combine" commands with their help text, and nothing implements "combine".

what: Attempts to disarm a chest's trap for a thief using the thieving skill: on a successful roll the trap and its flags are cleared, otherwise the result is Triggered if a trap is present (so the caller applies it) or Failed.
ev: OpenChest makes the same single thieving-skill roll, with success showing "Trap Disarmed" and failure leaving the trap in place for the caller, but it also awards chest XP and sets UI captions, and it never clears the trap or returns a DisarmResult the way attemptChestDisarm does.

what: Clears a character's paralysis, poison, disease, and spell resistance levels, implementing the game's EndEveryAilment effect (the stone/DeathState is left alone and the stat part of paralysis is not restored).
ev: It clears paralysis, poison, disease, and spell resistances and leaves stone alone, like cityGateClear, but its Unparalyse call restores the stat part that the C++ quirk path deliberately does not restore, and it also calls Effects.Recompute.

what: Resolves a monster's breath attack before its melee, dealing breath damage from the monster's level to the targeted party member if the monster is a Fire or Cold breather.
ev: GroupAttacks also resolves a fire or cold breath before the group's melee, but it first rolls a percentage chance against the party's top guild level and works on a whole group rather than one victim index, while monsterBreath applies no roll and only takes the single targeted character.

what: Checks whether a character of a given race can wear an item by adding the item's stat modifiers (scaled by alignment fit) to the character's current stats and refusing if any stat falls below the race's minimum.
ev: It runs the same race-minimum check (StatWithMods + StatModWorth against RaceDef.Min for each stat) and refuses, but it first calls EquipProblem and returns a reason string instead of a bool, so it can refuse for reasons canWear never checks.

what: Applies a pit fall to each living party member, dealing pitDamage(pitSize) to their hit points and marking them Dead (with hits clamped to 0) if that drops them to zero or below, while logging a fall message for each.
ev: The pit damage roll matches the `pitDamage` helper that `applyPitFall` calls, but no candidate loops over living party members, applies the damage, marks them Dead at zero hits, or logs the fall; `MonsterAttack.TakeDamage` only shares the floor-at-zero step.

what: Runs the guild hall's Make Level procedure: it checks guild membership, max level, experience, and quest completion, takes the gold fee, then applies the level gain, title, mastership, new quest, and hit increase.
ev: The candidate follows the same sequence as makeLevel: max-level check, experience check with Exp. Info, quest satisfaction with forfeit offer for pinned characters, gold fee check, payment, level-up, and title message, and it is truncated before the hits update. Differences are in details, such as the candidate's `CharPay` versus the C++ on-hand-then-bank split, and the candidate's use of `ActiveGuildDef` where the C++ uses the guild parameter.

what: Returns the percentage resistance a given race has against a given damage or effect category, looked up from the race's resistance table (categories not listed count as 0).
ev: It starts from the race's base resistance for the kind (the same lookup as the C++ table, with 0 for unlisted kinds), but it then adds a flat 90 for equipped resistant gear and a spell-raised value, which the C++ function does not do.

what: Drowning a party member clears their paralysis, poison and disease, then sets them to Dead, with no death text shown here.
ev: It clears paralysis, poison, and disease as the C++ does, but it also zeroes spell resistances and recomputes effects and never sets the character dead, which Candidate 2 (MonsterAttack.cs SetDead) does without clearing any ailments.

what: Maps a companion's spawn mode to a monster table index for the companion spawn rule, returning mode 6 as index 4, modes above 7 as mode minus 7, and the keep-window sentinel for mode 7 and for the unresolved modes 0-3.
ev: No candidate maps a companion spawn mode to a table index; the closest, Mordor.Core/MdrLoader.cs MdrLoader.LoadMonsters, only reads `CompanionSpawnMode` from the file and stores it unchanged, with no 6→4, >7→mode-7, or keep-window logic.

what: Applies a successful raise: adds age days based on the prior death state, returns the character to Alive (clearing the ordinary cause of death), and sets current hits from the raise kind and max hits.
ev: Resolve applies the raise outcome and ages the body by cause of death through AgeDaysFor, but the visible code never sets DeathState to Alive or sets current hits from the raise kind, and Accept only says the hits are "Resolve's" without showing them.

what: Maps a companion spawn mode to its spawn behavior: a floor window, keeping the previous window, or a spawn-table index, with unresolved modes falling back to a floor window.
ev: The C++ function maps a companion spawn mode to a floor window, keep-window, or table index with fallbacks, and no candidate does this; the closest, Mordor.Core/MdrLoader.cs LoadMonsters, only reads the raw CompanionSpawnMode field without resolving it, and CompanionRef.Resolve resolves a companion's Ref by Id rather than spawn mode.

what: Rolls a percent chance (kBypassRollPercent) that always gets drawn, and returns true only if that roll succeeds and the newbie guard is not active, so the newbie guard suppresses the bypass effect.
ev: No candidate draws a percent roll that is always consumed and then returns success only when a separate guard flag is false; the nearest, Rules.RollQuest, uses a level check to force its roll, which is a different mechanism.

what: In the city rest rules, a character who is dead does not get rested, so the function returns true (rest applies) only when the character is not dead.
ev: The C++ gate `!ch.isDead()` decides whether the city rest applies, and Character.RestInCity covers the same city-rest rule for an individual character, but its comments say the original rests the dead too, the opposite of the C++ outcome, and no candidate gates rest on `!IsDead`.

what: Returns the number of dungeon levels shown in the Limitation Notice, which is the full build's cap of 15 levels from SRD gc0182 (the limited build's value is unknown, so the full value is used for both builds).
ev: The candidate counts the dungeon levels from MDATA11.MDR for a folder check, but it never returns a fixed cap of 15 for the Limitation Notice, which the C++ function does.

what: Every four seconds of game time, the ailment and item tick is due, so this advances the last-tick timestamp; the tick's effects on the party and inventory are not implemented in this half of the module, so nothing else happens yet.
ev: AilmentTick is the four-second ailment and item tick that the C++ leaves as an UNKNOWN body, but it performs the full effects on the party while the C++ only advances the clock, and it does not visibly contain the due-check or timestamp update that `runFourSecondTick` does.

what: Decides whether two item alignments can be combined, returning true when they match or either item is Unaligned, a rule the SRD does not specify and this code marks as an assumption.
ev: No candidate tests whether two alignments can combine; the closest, ItemAlignments.Possible and Loot.RollAlignment, only list or pick an item's own allowed alignments and never compare two alignments.

what: Recomputes a guild's protection value as half its guild level, truncated to an integer, plus one, overwriting the earlier cast value per the game's rules.
ev: Its `c.Protection = c.Guild.Level / 2 + 1` line matches the C++ formula (integer division equals truncation for non-negative levels), but it is only one step inside a larger recompute of gear and spell states, and the spell-level-based Protection write in SpellEffect.ApplyToCharacter and SpellThrown.Apply uses a different input.

what: Returns whether a chest disarm earns experience, which it does only when the chest was trapped.
ev: The C++ function returns only whether a disarm awards experience (true only for a trapped chest), and Rules.ChestExp and OpenChest both embody that rule — ChestExp computes the award and OpenChest only grants it in the "Trap Disarmed" branch — but no candidate is a pure boolean predicate, so this is a closely related version with different details (it returns an amount, not a flag).

what: Applies a disease attack to every living party member during a chest trap, with each member getting a resistance check against the Disease kind (Resistances[4]) and taking disease damage at floor strength if they fail.
ev: The case applies the same per-member Disease resistance check to the whole party and sets the disease at dungeon level, but it is one branch of a larger switch, sets the Diseased status rather than the damage the C++ describes, and says nothing about dead members.

what: Computes the Sorcerer spell formula I = G + G·ln(C2)/ln(5) + INT((C2/10)·(H−1)) from the 1995 Mordor rules, returning 0 when C2 is non-positive.
ev: SpellDamage has the same skeleton (base + base·ln(·)/ln(5) + int((·/10)·(power−1))) but takes the log of SL+1 rather than C2, adds a random roll and resistance, and has no non-positive guard, while SpellHeal and SpellHealAverage use log base 10 instead of 5.

what: Looks up the teleporter record placed on a given floor square (converting the 0-based square to the 1-based record coordinates), returning it or null if none exists.
ev: The C++ function looks up a floor's teleporter record by square (0-based to 1-based), which none of the candidates does: ForSquare computes where a teleporter sends the party, LoadFloor only reads records into the floor, and TeleporterSquare receives the record as an argument.

what: Handles the player's typed "rescue <member>" dungeon command by validating the target, delaying the dead member's return by a random number of days, carrying them home to town, and replying with how long the search took.
ev: It does the same core work as the C++ dungeon rescue (computes whether the body is easy to find, rolls the days with DaysUntilFound, adds them to the age, carries the body home, and reports "You have been found after N day(s)!"), but it lacks the C++ command's member-number parsing and the "not dead" and "already in town" checks, since it runs on the already-selected character.

what: Decides whether a given character level awards an attack/defence level bonus, returning true only when the level is a positive multiple of the step and does not exceed the adMaxLevel cap.
ev: The C++ predicate is not in the candidates, but GuildADSingle applies the same test (`l % every == 0`, capped at `AdMaxLevel`, with the step clamped to at least 1) below the hit cap, though it accumulates awards over a loop rather than returning a boolean and uses a different rule above the cap.

what: Serializes a list of member names into newline-terminated text and stores it in the session's feature state under the "left" roster key, which is how the saved roster of departed members gets persisted.
ev: Roster.Write also persists a list of member-name records as the roster, but it writes JSON to a file in the saves directory instead of newline-terminated text into the session's featureState under the "left" key, and it swallows errors.

what: Computes the chance that a monster hits a character by comparing the monster's attack against the character's defense, shifting the base hit chance up or down by a spread proportional to the difference and clamping the result to a floor and ceiling.
ev: Both compute 50 + 50·(atk−def)/atk when attack leads, the mirror formula when defence leads, and clamp to 2..98 percent; the candidate's special cases for zero values (def==0 gives 98 for any positive attack, which the clamp would also produce in C++) do not change the outcome, assuming the C++ constants are 50 and 50.

what: Computes the probability that a monster voluntarily joins the party as CHA minus monster level plus one, floored at zero, divided by 300.
ev: No candidate computes a voluntary join probability from CHA and monster level; the closest, `Combat.cs AcceptJoin`, handles accepting an offer already made, and `CompanionMood.cs Round` and `CompanionInfo.cs LeaveChance` compute leave/drift chances, not `max(0, CHA - M + 1) / 300`.

what: Returns true when a spell effect is a charm effect and its charm index equals the monster's class, deciding whether a charm spell applies to that kind of monster.
ev: The same test appears inline (a spell with Effect 75-99 zeroes its damage unless `MonsterClasses[target.Type].Index == Effect - 75`), but it is one step of a damage calculation rather than a standalone predicate, and the candidate derives the monster class from `target.Type` instead of taking it as a direct input.

what: Reads a guild definition from a parsed JSON object into a GuildDef record, field by field, with each value pulled from a named JSON key.
ev: LoadGuilds builds the same GuildDef fields from the binary MDATA1 record format, not from a parsed JSON object by key, so it is a closely related loader but no candidate reads GuildDef from JSON.

what: Decides whether a companion may cast a spell this round, allowing it only if its owner's side has not already cast this round and anti-magic is not in effect (rule R27.1).
ev: The C++ function gates a companion's cast on "owner has not cast this round" and "no anti-magic," but no candidate implements that exact gate; CompanionTurn handles companion turns and rounds, and CastGate.Refuse and SquareTests cover the anti-magic check, so the closest match is only partial and the one-cast-per-owner-per-round rule is not clearly present.

what: Returns the chute's depth, as an i32, read from the FloorChute record (the depth field name is an unverified assumption).
ev: The C++ function is a plain accessor that returns the chute's depth as an int, and no candidate does only that; ChuteFall reads the same `Depth` field (cast to int) inside a larger chute-fall routine, and LoadFloor only stores `Depth` when loading the record.

what: Decides whether a spell may be cast in the current combat situation, refusing casts above the peaced-cast level limit when the caster is engaged with monsters present, and refusing combat-scope casts when no monsters are present, with the rules depending on whether the cast is combat-only, either, or non-combat.
ev: Refuse covers the same combat-state rules (Combat-only refused with no monsters, Either/Combat refused above PeacedSpellLevel when peaced, NonCombat refused when engaged with monsters present), but it also adds a points check, an anti-magic refusal, and returns a message rather than a bool, and it has no `Either` rule with no monsters or an explicit `!monstersPresent` NonCombat allowance matching the C++ `return !engaged` exactly, so it is a closely related version with different details rather than an exact match.

what: Rolls a d100 for a chest and returns MAGIC_LOCKED if the roll is at or under the lock chance, the chest class is above CONTAINER, and the square allows magic; otherwise UNLOCKED.
ev: No candidate rolls d100 against a lock chance gated by chest class and square magic; `Rules.EncounterGold` takes `chestLocked` as an input and its comment says the caller makes the lock roll, and `Rules.ChestClass`, `Rules.MagicallyLocked`, and `Loot.DropsItem` cover other decisions.

what: Parses a typed town command (help, rest, guild, levelup, join, shop, buy, sell, bank, equip/unequip/use) and routes it to the matching town action, replying with the result or a usage line.
ev: The C++ `townAction` parses and routes typed town commands (help, rest, buy, sell, bank, equip and so on), but no candidate does that; the closest, Party.PartyDeposit (candidate 5), only implements the Bank's party-deposit money rule, not command parsing or the `bank deposit|withdraw <gold>` routing.

what: Clamps a critical-hit chance value into the allowed range of 2 to 50 percent.
ev: The C++ function only clamps an input to 2..50, while this candidate applies the same 2..50 clamp for critical hits but only after computing the chance from attacker level, floor, and defender level.

what: Decides whether the morgue guild pays a raise cost for a character, which it does when the character's top guild level is 5 or lower and their total purse (on hand plus bank) is less than the cost.
ev: No candidate computes the guild-pays rule (top guild level <= 5 and purse on hand plus bank below cost); CityWindow.axaml.cs looked.Visit only consumes an already-computed `guildPays` flag, and CanPay tests the purse without the guild-level condition.

what: Returns whether the party member at the given index is the first member, the only one whose rest replenishes the town's pens and store stock (R4).
where: Mordor.Core/Character.cs keeps.RestInCity (its comment says "As member 0 it also turns the store and the pens over"; the replenish itself is in Mordor.Core/Rescue.cs Rescue.TurnOverTown)
ev: No candidate is the predicate `memberIndex == 0`; RestInCity and RestOnArrival state the first-member-only rule in comments, and TurnOverTown performs the replenishment without any member-index check.
