what: Adds the protection bonus, computed from a character's protection value, to their defence score as set out in the game's rule R36.
where: Mordor.Core/MonsterAttack.cs, ProtectionBonus (the enclosing class name isn't shown in the excerpt)
ev: The candidate computes the protection bonus from the character's Protection value (Log(p) * Log(p) * 3), which is the `protectionBonus` part of the C++ function, but no candidate adds that bonus to a defence score as `defenceWithProtection` does.

what: Returns true when the character's current Hits are zero or below, which under the rules (R28) means the character needs death processing.
ev: The C++ function is a bare predicate (`curHits <= 0`), while the candidates are all larger routines that set characters dead or prune the party. RemoveTheDead and AfterAFall both use the "CurHits <= 0 / > 0" death test that R28 describes, but neither returns the boolean on its own, and no candidate is a standalone check equivalent to `needsDeathProcessing`.

what: Returns the stored true/false setting for a mod's key, falling back to the given default when nothing is stored or the stored text is neither "True" nor "False".
ev: It matches the C++ on a missing key (returns the fallback) and on "True"/"False" (case-insensitive, trimmed), but for stored text that is neither it returns false instead of the default, which is the one outcome that differs.

what: Produces the player-facing message "There is a chute here, but it doesn't do anything in the Limited Version." when the player walks onto a chute on the limited dead-end level (rule R68).
ev: It checks the same walk-on condition (limited build on the last level, MAZEMOD.BAS:1840) but returns a bool and does not produce the "doesn't do anything in the Limited Version" message.

what: When a weapon has proven useless, this turns the character's Defend order on, so they defend instead of attacking.
ev: PlayerSwings sets `Party.OrderFor(actor).Kind = OrderKind.Defend` when a weapon fails the `NeedsGoodWeapon` floor check, which matches the C++ effect, but that happens inline inside the swing loop and the method also handles the no-weapon case, so it is not a standalone helper that takes a "weapon proved useless" flag.

what: Serializes a guild log (a list of records, each with a guild index, day serial, and text) into a little-endian byte buffer, writing the record count and per-record fields for saving to the MDATA9 guild log file.
ev: This is the decode side of the same byte layout (int32 count, then per record int32 guild, int64 day, int32 length, UTF-8 text), but no candidate encodes or writes that layout, since the C++ function serializes and Entry.All only reads it back.

what: Chooses which library page to show for a knowledge entry, sending monster entries to the monster page builder and everything else to the item page builder.
ev: No candidate picks a monster page or an item page from a library entry's kind; the closest, CityWindow.axaml.cs ShowLibrary, is cut off and visibly only fills one list of creatures or items, while IsItemPage only tests a page after it is built.

what: Returns the item-roll adjustment for a treasure chest's class (none, +15, none, or -25), which shifts the odds of the chest's item drop.
ev: DropsItem applies the same class-to-adjustment mapping (class 1 gives +15, class 3 gives -25, others zero) inline within the item roll, but no candidate returns that adjustment as a standalone value the way chestItemRollAdjust does.

what: When a spell is cast, it sets the target's Protection ailment to a level derived from the caster's spell level, without recalculating it at cast time.
ev: Its doc says the four states, including Protection, are set on each target with no recompute, and Protection is the caster's spell level halved plus one (MAINMOD2.BAS:1046), which matches castProtection's `protectLevelOnCast(casterSpellLevel)` with no recompute; the method body is truncated, so I'm relying on the doc comment for the Protection case.

what: Rolls a d100-style draw for a raise attempt (using the rock flag to force a zero roll) and reports whether the raise fails, per rule R12.5.
ev: Resolve has the same roll logic (chance zeroed for rock, then fail if `rng.Next(100) > roll`), but it also applies complications, aging, and Constitution losses, so it is a larger routine that contains the C++ function's roll rather than a standalone equivalent.

what: Rolls a random amount of gold between zero and the victim's whole purse for a thief's take, capping the result at the purse total.
ev: GoldToSteal does the cap-at-purse step (it returns the roll unless it exceeds the purse, then takes the whole purse), but it takes the roll as an input rather than drawing it from the RNG, and it adds rounding and overflow handling the C++ function lacks.

what: Returns whether a worn item's slot may be unequipped, which it may not while the slot's curse flag is set (rule R13).
ev: Both return `!slot.SlotCursed`, so an equipped item can't come off while its slot's curse flag is set, matching R13; the static overload ignores its `Alignment` argument and the instance overload (candidate 6) just delegates to it.

what: Exchanges gold between a character's on-hand purse and bank balance in whole-gold amounts, refusing non-positive amounts or transfers exceeding the source balance, and announces the exchange to the player on success.
ev: BankTyped moves gold between on-hand and bank for one character with a deposit/withdraw balance check, but it accepts fractional amounts, lets negative withdrawals through, returns a BankAnswer instead of a bool, and does not announce the exchange.

what: Checks whether a monster is allowed on a given dungeon level by testing the bit for that level (level minus one) in the monster's floor bitmask, returning false for levels outside the valid floor range.
ev: No candidate tests a monster's floor bitmask against a dungeon level (bit level-1, with range check); Seer.Locate's `SpawnMask & (1u << def.Type)` test is a similar bit test but on per-area class masks, and Combat.cs `Generate` is truncated so it cannot be confirmed to contain the check.

what: Decides whether a companion slot counts as living for the R34 rules by checking that it is occupied, not dead, and in the Normal death state.
ev: It refuses to move a companion when either end is `IsDead` and treats an empty slot as not a companion, which covers two of the C++ checks (occupied and not dead), but it never tests `deathState == Normal` and is a drag-and-drop move rather than a living-companion predicate.

what: Reports the spell point cost a party member would pay to cast a given spell with no item involved, returning false if the member or spell doesn't exist.
ev: The C++ wrapper returns the spell point cost from `castCostSp` at item level 0, and `Spellbook.Cost(s, c)` computes that same cost for a character (Combat.cs `RoundCheckCast` uses it as the cost whenever `itemLevel == 0`), though the C# version has no member or spell existence checks, which the caller handles.

what: Lets a player realign an unequipped pack item to good, neutral, or evil alignment by validating the member and slot, computing a fee from the item's price and the alignment distance, charging the gold, and then changing the item's alignment.
ev: Realign refuses equipped items, computes the fee with StoreStock.RealignCost, charges it, and then sets the alignment, which matches the core flow, but it has no member/slot validation, does not refuse a same-alignment target (it would charge and proceed), and adds a Yes/No confirm that the C++ command does not have.

what: Applies the withering trap by aging the character by a fixed number of weeks (kWitheringDays, 28 days per the SRD note [c4]) through the shared ageBy routine.
where: Mordor.Core/Character.cs keeps.AgeBy (with keeps.DescribeDays for the "4 week(s)" wording)
ev: AgeBy adds the days to Age through the shared mdrcharAddAge non-rest path, and its doc names the chest Withering caller (MONSMOD.BAS:3633), while DescribeDays(28) gives "4 week(s)" as the C++ displays. The C++ ageBy's exact party flag isn't visible, so the message wording is the only possible difference.

what: Raises a character's stats by the bonuses from a stat item, capping each stat at its race maximum plus 5, then runs the hall-of-records check on each stat.
ev: For each stat it adds the item's modifier, caps the result at race max + 5, and runs the Hall of Records check after the cap, matching the C++ on the non-reversed path; it differs in that it skips zero modifiers, adds a race-minimum floor, emits messages, and handles a reversed mode the C++ lacks.

what: Builds the text block shown on the Hall of Records screen for one record, giving its heading, who set it (with the day number or the original holder), and its formatted value.
ev: It builds the same "Set on <date> by" / "Set by Original RecordHolder" line, the trimmed holder, and the value text, but it omits the C++ function's leading `row.heading` line, so the output differs.

what: Returns true when an item is not fully identified (idLevel is not All), so the identify fee applies only to items whose properties are not yet fully known.
ev: No candidate is a plain "not fully identified" predicate, but IdentifyFee returns 0 when nothing is left unknown (`IdCountdown(slot.Known) <= 0`), which is the fee gate's effect, though it also computes a price the C++ function does not.

what: Reports whether a rescue raise is pending for a party member, by checking that its "kind" was recorded in session feature state (which only happens when the raise chance was above 0).
ev: It tests whether a raise is pending by checking `RaiseChance > 0` on the character, which is the condition under which the C++ kind is recorded, but it reads a character field rather than `featureState` keyed by member, so the inputs and storage differ.

what: Returns true when the character's level is below the seer's level gate (original T-L level 12), so the seer refuses service to characters under that level; the deepestHeCanReach parameter is ignored because the source doesn't specify how it factors in.
ev: No candidate refuses seer service when the character's level is below 12; the nearest, CityWindow.axaml.cs `looked.Locate`, refuses when the monster's or item's depth exceeds `Seer.DeepestHeCanReach`, which is a different gate.

what: Given a character's identification skill, the item's difficulty, and the dungeon level, it determines how well the item is identified (Mostly, Partial, or Barely), with shallow-level items fully Mostly-identified when skill meets difficulty.
ev: It applies the same rules: Mostly when skill meets difficulty on a floor at or above 5, Partial otherwise, and Barely when the gap is 20 or more, with Partial as the default. It takes a Character and Item rather than raw integers, and it derives the skill, difficulty, and level from them.

what: Runs the Seer's locate-a-monster service on a dungeon level: refuses levels too deep for the Seer's reach, charges the fee (even when the search fails), then either reports only the level or picks a blurred spot and a 75% frequency line when the search succeeds.
ev: Locate covers the level gate (`level > Seer.DeepestHeCanReach`) and the fee offer, but it never charges the fee, runs the search-failure roll, picks a spot, blurs it, or rolls the frequency line, and the Seer.Fee and Seer.OfferMonster candidates cover only parts of that.

what: Rolls the stone-path CON-loss check for a raise by looking up the character's natural Constitution and running the loss roll against the chance derived from it, per SRD R26.
ev: The candidate computes the same CON-based loss chance (`50 - CON * 2`, floored at 0) that the C++ passes to the roll, but no candidate performs the roll itself, and Raising.Resolve instead always deducts 1 CON for stone with no roll.

what: Computes the Mordor sheet column value K from the SRD R7 formula, rounding up C·Q·R·1.9/(C+1) and returning twice that minus one, though its in-game purpose is unknown.
ev: The closest candidate, Mordor.Core/Rules.cs Rules.Fn1485Price, shares only the 1.9 factor and computes a floored price, not a ceiling-based column value with `*2 - 1`, and none of the other candidates (sheet spell list, cast, and MDI/tab methods) computes K.

what: Returns whether the party's lead character is Neutral-aligned, which is the check the engine uses for the neutral-alignment gate in the game's rules (R?? neutral gate, c7).
ev: No candidate returns whether the lead character is Neutral; the closest, CompanionTurn.cs Outcome.Check, reads the leader's alignment only as one input to a companion-turning roll, and Rules.cs EngageChance uses Neutral only in its alignment-pairing table.

what: Handles a typed "claim <member>" command by checking the named character's Nomad guild membership and attempting to give them the guildmastership, returning the reply text shown to the player.
ev: Claim applies the same seat rule (take it if nobody holds it or the holder's level is below yours) but has no "claim <member>" parsing, member-name lookup, Nomad-membership check, or reply text, and it returns a tuple instead of a reply string.

what: Rolls a percentile check against the special hit chance for the given kind and raw value, using the context's RNG to decide whether the special hit lands.
ev: SwingOnce rolls `_rng.Next(100)` against `Rules.CritChance` and `Rules.BackstabChance` for a blow, which is the same chance-then-percentile-roll pattern as rollSpecialHit, but it is hard-wired to crit and backstab and not dispatched by a SpecialHitKind with a raw value, and no candidate computes a chance for a generic special-hit kind.

what: Returns the rescue ceiling in gold for a level and area, giving a flat 100 for level 1 in area 18 or lower, otherwise 10000 if fewer than the threshold days have been waited (1000 if at or past it).
ev: The ceiling rule (10000 before the threshold, 1000 after, and 100 for level 1 with area 18 or lower) appears inline inside the day-rolling loop rather than as a standalone function, and it uses a Log-based threshold formula instead of the C++ `rescueThresholdDays(level)`, which I could not verify.

what: Handles the player's typed command to take off a worn item from a party member's pack slot, refusing if the item is cursed and otherwise unequipping it and reporting the result as a message.
ev: This is a toggle that both equips and unequips the selected slot and refuses a cursed item with "Cannot unequip! Item is cursed!", but it is silent on success and does not report which member or slot was cleared, unlike the C++ removal message.

what: Computes a treasure class (chest or loot tier) from a random roll and the lead's box-chance thresholds plus a lair bonus, though this pure form hardcodes the thresholds to 0 and so only applies the bonus.
where: Mordor.Core/Rules.cs Rules.ChestClass (the class name wasn't shown in the candidate header, so the enclosing class is inferred)
ev: Both map a 0-99 roll plus a lair bonus to a chest class, but ChestClass reads the monster's real BoxChance thresholds while the C++ stub hardcodes them to 0 and ignores `lead`, so the outcomes differ.

what: Resets the game's music volume, sound-effect volume, brightness, and the two fonts (proportional and non-proportional) to their default values when the player presses the Default button in the options menu, per SRD rule R6.
ev: DefaultFonts resets the proportional and non-proportional faces and sizes to their defaults, matching the font part of restoreOptionDefaults, but no candidate resets MusicVolume, FXVolume, or Brightness.

what: Decides whether the town screen should be shown instead of the dungeon, which is the case when the party is on dungeon level 0 and the leader is still alive.
ev: The same test (`leader.DungeonLevel <= 0 && !leader.IsDead`) appears inline, but it gates service-window updates after a character switch rather than choosing whether the town screen is shown, and no candidate exposes it as a standalone predicate.

what: Rolls a spell's base damage as the minimum value plus a random amount from 1 up to that minimum, per SRD rule R10.
where: Mordor.Core/Rules.cs Rules.SpellDamage (nearest spell-damage routine, but it does not match)
ev: No candidate computes minimum + Random(1..minimum); Rules.SpellDamage is a log-scaled damage formula that subtracts a random share from a power-based total and applies resistance, and the other candidates are unrelated (character stats, window sizes, volume, MDI scrollbars, or a different monster damage function).

what: For a monster spell, it sets the turn's damage total to the spell's damage value, replacing any damage already accumulated that turn rather than adding to it.
ev: No candidate sets a turn's damage total to a monster spell's damage value in place of accumulated damage; the closest, Candidate 1's CastSpell (Combat.cs) handles the player's casting, and Candidate 2's Rules.SpellDamage only computes a single spell's damage without touching any running total.

what: When a town hook is asked, it returns the original rule's amount and flag unless a mod is active, in which case it takes the first OK mod reply in load order as the answer, and logs which path was used.
ev: It follows the same "first mod's answer in load order wins, otherwise fall back to the original" pattern, but it answers a different question (whose bank account gets the gold) and returns a Character rather than the amount and flag, with no status-based reply list or logging.

what: Handles a typed dungeon command by resolving "stairs" to the stairs on the current square, rejecting the command when the player is out of the dungeon or in combat, then moving the party, changing levels, or producing the wall-bump and turn messages.
ev: UseStairs handles the stairs-up and stairs-down part of the C++ function (level change, the level-1 exit to town, and the describe result), but it is driven by the square under the party rather than a typed command string, and no candidate parses commands, checks in-dungeon or in-combat state, or handles moves, turns, and wall bumps.

what: Returns true unless the character is dead, enforcing the SRD rule (R7 step 9) that dead characters cannot rest while waiting.
ev: The C++ `canRest` is a one-line check that a character is not dead, and RemoveTheDead only treats a member as dead when `CurHits <= 0`, `IsDead`, or `Stoned` holds, so it is related but does not implement the rest rule. Candidate 5 (Character.cs keeps.RestInCity) also touches the dead and resting, but its dead-character handling (ages dead bodies, fills their spell points) is a different rule from canRest's "dead cannot rest" check.

what: Converts a character's gold balance into the save-file fields, recording the whole gold amount and setting a flag to store the exact value only when the balance has a fractional part.
ev: No candidate writes a balance into whole-plus-exact save fields with a has-fraction flag; the nearest, VbCurrency.FromSave (Mordor.Core/VbCurrency.cs), is the inverse read path that rebuilds the balance from those fields, and VbCurrency.RoundToWhole only rounds half to even, which is not the same as the C++ whole-part and flag logic.

what: Offers each of the character's six natural stat values to the Hall of Records as a stat-category entry, logging them as solo records for the new character.
ev: It runs the same per-record `CheckAndLog` offer-and-save loop over (kind, value) pairs, but the caller supplies the values and `alone` comes from party size rather than being fixed to true, and the six-stat creation call site (likely in the truncated `CharacterCreationWindow.OnCreate`) is not shown.

what: Blocks a paralysed character from taking the stairs up, while allowing them to go down.
ev: The stairs-up branch is guarded by `!_ch.Paralysed` while the stairs-down branch has no paralysis check, which is the same gating as the C++ `goingUp && paralysed` test, though it is inline in a larger method rather than a standalone predicate.

what: Computes the gold a character must have to reach a given guild level, using the wiki's formula with the guild's raw Gold Parameter as the multiplier.
ev: Fn12B2 computes the same quantity (gold to reach a level from the guild's Gold field) but uses the source's cumulative VB sum with a 60.2 rate and a Gold/10 multiplier, not the wiki's closed-form floor((LVL-1)^2 * 30.1 + (LVL-1)/10) * raw GP.

what: Finds the first living monster in a given encounter group (the one at the front of the line, with hits above zero) and returns its index, or -1 if the group is invalid or everyone in it is dead.
ev: It finds the first living member of the run of same monsters that a given monster belongs to, which is the core of frontLiving, but it takes a monster reference instead of a group index and returns a monster or null rather than an index or -1.

what: Returns the magic resistance percentage (clamped to 0–100) that a victim uses against a spell, or 0 if the spell's resistIndex is negative, meaning the spell has no resistance roll.
ev: It shares the gate that returns 0 when the spell's ResistIndex is negative and then reads a resistance, but it indexes a per-kind `target.Resistances` array inside a full damage calculation, whereas the C++ helper returns the clamped `victim.magicResistance` regardless of kind.

what: Handles the player's typed `buffer` command, listing a party member's buffers or setting or clearing one of their four spell buffer slots by spell name or id, and returns the reply text to show.
ev: BufferValue stores a spell (plus forty) or pack slot into a buffer and empties it for an empty slot, and CharacterPanel.BuffersPage lists buffers with their cost text, but no candidate parses the typed `buffer` command, looks up a spell by name, validates the 1-4 slot, or produces the reply text.

what: Computes a monster respawn delay in milliseconds from 1200 seconds plus 150 per dungeon level, minus 5 per emptied room, floored at 120 seconds.
ev: It computes 1200 + 150 per level, subtracts 5 per room, and floors at 120 s, matching the C++ arithmetic, but it derives the room count as headerAreas - tally rather than taking emptiedRooms directly, so the match holds only under the reading the C++ marks as unconfirmed.

what: Decides whether a character can open a chest during combat, returning false if the character is dead or paralysed or the chest is magically locked.
ev: OpenTheChest applies the same three guards (dead, paralysed, magically locked) and returns early on each, but it is a full open-the-chest routine with fight and loot handling and an extra on-screen check, not a standalone predicate, and it checks only DeathState rather than the C++ isDead.

what: Rolls a companion caster's spell mishap check by discarding one d100 draw, then comparing a second d100 roll against the spell's computed mishap chance and reporting whether the spell misfires.
where: Mordor.Core/Combat.cs CompanionCasts (enclosing class not shown in the excerpt)
ev: CompanionCasts runs a spell-specific mishap check (`CompanionMishap.Kind.Spell`), but it picks a victim via `CompanionMishap.Victim` rather than returning a bool from a spell-odds chance, and no candidate discards a draw before the check as the C++ function does.

what: Equips a pack item for the character if it's a valid, non-refused item, setting its equipped flag and applying any alignment-based curse via fitFor.
ev: Its equip branch matches equipItem (wearable and refusal checks, set Equipped, then ApplyEquipCurse with the alignment fit, with the refusal logged), but it is a toggle that also unequips, uses WearRefusal's extra stat-floor check instead of the plain equipProblem test, and returns silently on an empty slot rather than returning false.

what: Copies the party's dungeon position, level, and facing into the saved game location and game state, and raises the town's deepest-reached-level record when the party goes deeper.
ev: SavePos places the party's level, X, and Y and copies the facing onto the members, which matches part of syncPosition, but it does not update a separate saved location or the town's deepest-reached record, which the C++ function also does.

what: Computes the damage of a companion's R37 breath attack by taking the special hit range from the attacker's and target's levels, adding a quarter of that range, and applying the target's resist percentage.
ev: Raw computes the same range and adds range/4 for breath before resistance, but the resistance step is split out into SpecialHits.AfterResistance, which the candidate CombatEngine.CompanionBreathes calls, so no single candidate does the whole C++ function.

what: Returns the antimagic flag unchanged, so the game's AntiMagicHere state (whether the antimagic effect is active in the current location) is simply reported back to the caller.
ev: The candidate sets `_combat.AntiMagicHere` from `_nav.Floor.Has(..., Floor.ANTIMAGIC)`, which is the same flag, but it derives that flag from the floor rather than returning a caller-supplied value unchanged as the C++ does.

what: Returns the chest on the party's current square if one is present, or nullptr in town or when no chest exists, which the disarm and inspect actions use to find the trap target.
ev: No candidate returns the chest on the party's current square, but OpenTheChest's guard `if (_chest == null || !FightIsHere(_chest)) return;` checks that a chest exists for the loaded area before using it, which is only part of what disarmChestHere does.

what: Each round, a companion's binding drifts toward zero, moving toward unbound by a step set by its hit points (when unbound and below zero) or its guild level relative to the top guild level (when bound), and never drifts if it is ForLife.
ev: Step.Round applies a per-round drift toward zero and skips ForLife companions, but it moves the binding by one level on a random roll, whereas the C++ moves it by a computed step with a minimum of one; Step.Drift computes a step-like magnitude but only returns a threshold and does not apply it.

what: Using Kind 25 (a stat item, possibly a potion) ages the character by 28 days, per SRD c31.
ev: AgeBy adds the given days to Age, which is the same aging primitive as C++ `ageBy`, and its doc names the Kind 25 item (MAINMOD2.BAS:6228) as a caller, but no candidate shows the 28-day Kind 25 use, and AgeBy also returns a message the C++ function does not.

what: Decides whether the breath-weapon sweep effect applies to a non-aimed group attack, which it does when the attack's special-flags bit is set and the attacker's guild level is below the sweep limit of 40.
ev: It tests the same breath bit (bit 3) and sweeps the groups when the breath lands, but it gates on a percentage roll and a lead-foe level comparison, not the guild-level-under-40 limit, so the predicate is not the same.

what: When a character dies, every occupied companion slot is released and the carried item index is cleared, so companions and carried items are lost.
ev: It releases every companion slot via `Companions.ReleaseAll()` and clears the carried index (`CarryingCompanion = -1`), matching the C++ loop and `carryIndex` reset, though it also clears `CarryingCharacter` and the C++ `Inventory.carryIndex` may map to this companion carry rather than an item.

what: Computes the initial spell-point cost of a sheet's common spell as a truncated product of the guild modifier, the spell's cost ratio, and 1.9, using the R33 ROUNDDOWN formula.
ev: It applies the same floored 1.9 product and the same epsilon concern as the C++ ROUNDDOWN formula, but it takes level, u4, rate and SL and divides by 10×SL, whereas the C++ takes only guildMod and scRatio and has no division.

what: Buys the chosen pen row for a party member by taking payment through confinementBuy, then fills the member's first free companion slot with the purchased creature and reports the price paid and remaining gold, or refuses with a message if the row, member, slot, or funds are invalid.
ev: Add does the R67 "first free slot" step, returning -1 with nothing done when no slot is free, but it does not validate the row or member, charge gold or decrement the pen (Confinement.Take does only the pen decrement), set the slot's ref, alignment, or hits, or build the reply message.

what: Records a Hall of Records entry by storing the given value under the record kind, while the holder name, whether the holder is the player, and the timestamp are discarded because the hall has no fields for them.
ev: Check stores the offered value under the record kind, as the C++ does, but it also compares against the current record, stores the holder name and date, and returns an announcement line, none of which the C++ function does.

what: Returns true if the character has joined any guild, checking each guild slot in turn, which the equipment check uses as a gate on equipping items.
ev: No candidate returns whether the character has joined any guild; the closest, Character.MeetsUseLevel and GuildData.CanUse, loop over joined guilds but only as a step toward an item-usability check, and the C++ `joined` flag has no direct counterpart.

what: Registers the "rescue" typed command for both the dungeon screen (lie where you fell until found and carried to town) and the town screen (pay the morgue to send rescuers).
where: Mordor.App/DungeonWindow.axaml.cs DungeonWindow.WaitForRescue (the pick.WaitForRescue candidate; its class name is shown as "pick" in the candidate header)
ev: The dungeon half matches (wait to be found, add days, carry to town, via the dungeon wait and Rescue.CarryHome), and the town half matches CityWindow.axaml.cs looked.RescuersButton (name and coordinates, then morgue cost), but no candidate is a typed "rescue" command registration covering both screens, so the two behaviors are split across candidates.

what: Decides whether a perceive-ahead check succeeds by rolling a random percentage and comparing it against the given chance (R46 in the SRD).
ev: Look contains the same `rng.NextDouble() * 100 < bestPerception` roll as the C++ function, but only as one step inside a per-feature loop that also records the map and builds the message text, and Perception.cs's NoticesAnything (which likely holds the same roll) is not shown.

what: Computes the gold cost of binding a monster to a monster guild, scaling with the guild level and the absolute size of the current binding through a cost factor and a fixed cost unit.
ev: It computes the same formula (monster guild level × 1237 × f × |current| / 4) with f derived from |current|, but it multiplies by the signed `current` rather than the absolute value `a`, and its closed-form factor (a+4, or 12−a near the cap) is not verified against the C++ `bindingCostFactor` table.

what: Stores an integer value for a named field of a rescue-raise state for a party member in the session's feature state, as a string under a key built from the member and field.
ev: None of the eight candidates stores an integer under a member-and-field key in a session or feature-state dictionary; the closest, Sub0930RaiseOffer (Mordor.App/DungeonWindow.axaml.cs), only consumes and forgets pending-raise state, and RaiseChance (Mordor.Core/PendingRaise.cs) computes a value without storing it.

what: Decides whether a dead character's body can be asked to rejoin the party, refusing if combat is ongoing, if the body is being carried, or if no Resurrect-based raise is pending, and otherwise allowing it.
ev: The C++ function is a pure gate (combat → carried body → no pending raise → allowed), and this candidate reproduces the in-combat refusal for a dead joiner ("Cannot raise character in Combat!") and checks the dead-leader case, but it does not have a carried-body refusal or a `raisePending` check as a standalone decision; the refusal logic is interleaved with the name picker and password flow rather than being a separate function returning an enum.

what: Computes a player's quoted share of a gold total split among a number of shares, rounding half up to whole gold, and returns zero when the share count is not positive.
ev: Its displayed share is the total divided by the party size, rounded half away from zero to whole gold, as the C++ does, but it returns a caption string rather than the share value and has no guard for a non-positive share count.

what: Changes a party's location to a different dungeon area by leaving the current area, saving the characters, moving every member to the new area, and loading the new area with arrival handling.
ev: SettleArea runs the same leave, save, arrive, and load-with-arrival-round sequence when the area changes, but it derives the new area from the party's position instead of taking `newArea`, adds a PruneTheDead call, and has a wiped-party branch that skips the save and load.

what: Applies the Kind 25 stat item's age effect by adding the given number of days to the character's age in days, even when the item's fit is reversed.
ev: AgeBy performs the same `Age += days` as duseOlder and is listed as one of the Kind 25 item's callers, but it also returns an "older" message line, which duseOlder does not, and the Kind 25 branch of ItemUse.ApplySpecial that would show the reversed-fit handling is cut off in the candidate.

what: Builds a spell's sheet from its definition, mapping its damage values to base and power, flagging it as blank when both are zero, clamping its kill-effect index into the 0–8 verb range, and classing it as Detrimental or Beneficial by its effect when it has damage.
ev: No candidate derives the sheet's base/power, blank flag, clamped verb index, or Detrimental/Beneficial type from a spell definition. MdrLoader.LoadSpells only copies the same raw fields into a Spell object, and SpellInfo.Paint shows a damage line but does not build the sheet.

what: Serializes one character's full state (identity, stats, vitals, gold, ailments, location, lost-status, pack and guild data) into the save file on write, or restores it on read, through a shared traversal.
where: Mordor.Core/Import/OriginalSaves.cs past.Convert (the candidate's Convert method, which is private, so the name is written as the candidate shows it)
ev: This converts one character record from the original VB format into the port's Character model, covering some of the same fields (name, race, alignment, sex, stats, hits, spell points, location), but it is a one-way import from a different format and omits the save-file traversal, ailments, wallet, lost-status, pack, and guild data.

what: Computes the damage range of a detrimental spell from its magnitude, giving a minimum of half the damage modifier minus one and a maximum of the full modifier minus one, and returns no range for blank magnitudes or beneficial spells.
ev: The C++ function derives a min and max range from the magnitude's damage modifier (trunc(dmgMod*0.5-1) and trunc(dmgMod-1)), but no candidate computes such a range, since the closest ones (Rules.SpellDamage, SpecialHits.Kind.Raw) roll a single damage value.

what: Computes the base worth in gold of a dungeon creature from its attack, defense, hit points, stats, special attack and spell flags, and resistances, scaled by the guild level, and returns it as a Currency value.
ev: The candidate uses the same A/D/hits weights, Stats[0]+Stats[5] with a floor of 1, the log-of-guild-level scaling, the rate×GuildLevel+1 surcharges for special-attack and spell bits, the positive-only resistance sum, and the hits==1 case returning 1 (the visible text is truncated before that last check, and the candidate's doc comment describes it), with only structural differences such as hardcoded rate tables.

what: Handles the town `useitem <member> <slot>` command by forwarding it to the shared item-use logic, which checks the item and applies its effect for the player.
ev: It runs the same item-use logic (`ItemUse.Problem`, then the spell or `ItemUse.ApplySpecial` and charge spending) on a selected slot, but it works on the dungeon's active character with no member/slot arguments, and the town-side candidate (CityWindow `OnPackUse`) only refuses with "Must be in Dungeon to Use items."

what: Returns the index of the first group in the encounter that is still standing (per R5 of the melee rules), or -1 if no group is left standing.
ev: TargetFor picks the first living monster as a fallback when the aimed-at group is gone, which is the R5-style "first group standing" idea, but it works per monster rather than per group and returns a monster rather than a group index, so it is related rather than the same function.

what: Caps the displayed disarm chance for a chest trap at 98%, applied after the confidence calculation, so the cap affects only what is shown to the player and not the uncapped value the caller uses.
ev: The method applies the same `if (disarm > 98) disarm = 98;` cap after the confidence calculation, so the uncapped value feeds confidence first, but the cap is only one step inside a larger function that also computes the trap name and diamonds, and no candidate is a standalone cap.

what: On arrival in town, if mods are live and the player has answered the arrival prompt, it deposits the party's on-hand gold to the bank or pools it, and requests a message line to show only when money moved and the message is non-blank.
ev: Like the C++ function, it returns nothing when no mod is live, lets the first answering mod pick PartyDeposit or PartyPool, and returns a line only when money moved and the message is non-blank, though it also raises an ArrivedInTown event and adds a membership check on the pool target that the C++ lacks.

what: Given an effect code, returns its resist index (0 to 10, offset from the first resist effect) for a resist effect from the Mordor spell rules, or -1 if the effect is not a resist; for mass (party-wide) effects it returns the unclamped index, so callers must bound-check.
ev: ResistKind returns the same index for non-party-wide resist effects but has no realEffect or party-wide branch, so a raw mass effect (200 and up) returns -1 instead of the unclamped index the C++ quirk produces.

what: Checks whether two items can be combined into one stack by testing their type, alignment, and whether the summed charges fit within the allowed range, returning the reason for refusal or Ok.
ev: Combine walks each item against the first on type, identification, and alignment and pours compatible ones, which matches checkCombine's type and alignment checks, but it never checks the summed-charges overflow that checkCombine returns as Overflow, and Refusal in the same file covers only the list-level class and identification refusals.

what: Looks up a spell name against the killed-spell and drained-spell lists and returns whether that spell kills outright, drains levels, or has no such effect.
ev: No candidate maps a spell name to a killed, drained, or no-effect classification; the closest, `Rules.RaiseRefusal`, handles raise refusals by cause of death, and `Spells.IsCure` and `Spells.IsUtility` classify spells by effect id rather than by name lists.

what: Returns true when the encounter spread value exceeds the restart limit, which under R13.2 means the encounter restarts.
ev: No candidate compares a spread value against a restart limit; Candidate 1 (Rules.EncounterSpread) computes the spread value that the C++ predicate would test, but it never returns or checks the `spread > limit` result.

what: Returns true when two alignments differ by more than kAutoloadAlignGap steps on the Good-Neutral-Evil scale, which is the rule that decides whether two party members clash enough to block autoloading.
ev: Outcome.Check computes the same test inline as `Math.Abs(theirs - mine) > 1` on the Good=0/Neutral=1/Evil=2 scale, but only as one step of a larger free-will and turning routine, and it hardcodes 1 rather than using a named gap constant.

what: Returns the standing combat order (none, fight, defend, or spell:<id>) that a party member has set for the combat round, defaulting to "none" when no order is stored.
ev: Both turn a standing order into display text with "None" as the default, but Describe formats an existing order object as "Fight"/"Defend"/quoted spell name, whereas the C++ function looks up a per-member stored value and returns "none"/"fight"/"defend"/"spell:<id>".

what: When a character is engaged in combat, it sets that character's combat order to cast the given spell, so the spell becomes their action for the round; otherwise it does nothing.
where: Mordor.App/DungeonWindow.axaml.cs DungeonWindow.BecomesOrder (and CastInCombat for the setting path)
ev: The C++ function sets the caster's order to cast the spell only when engaged, and no candidate matches that exactly; BecomesOrder only decides whether a spell becomes an order (using monsters present plus engaged or a non-combat check), and CastInCombat actually sets the Spell order, but it also runs the cast gate and has no "do nothing unless engaged" branch, so the behaviour differs.

what: Computes the store's fee for an item from its price by multiplying by 0.8, dividing by 0.5, and rounding half-to-even, per SRD chapter 13's item and equipment rules.
ev: The C++ computes round_half_even(0.8 × price / 0.5), which is 1.6 × price, but no candidate uses that formula; the nearest, StoreStock.RealignCost, is a different store fee that uses 0.72 × price (doubled when crossing the spectrum) with the same half-to-even rounding.

what: Computes the gold fee to uncurse an item by looking up its list price in the item data and applying the SRD's uncurse-fee formula, returning 0 if the item isn't found.
ev: No candidate computes an uncurse fee from the item's list price; the closest are StoreStock.RealignCost and the identify-fee methods, which price different store services with different formulas, and CityWindow.Store.cs ShelfLine.ShowStore only builds the Uncurse panel without computing a fee.

what: Returns the percent chance that a victim of a given level is electrocuted, using the monster-spit percentage bands (high, mid, low) and the monster level as the reference level.
where: Mordor.Core/Rules.cs Rules.LevelGapChance (the class name is inferred from the file, since the candidate header shows only `of.LevelGapChance`)
ev: Both return 90, 50, or 10 percent from a victim-versus-monster guild-level comparison, and the C++ `c14` comment names the same 90/50/10 bands, though `bandPercent`'s exact threshold rule isn't visible, so the match is inferred.

what: Works out whether the party can disband (leave the dungeon or quit) while monsters are present, refusing unless the leader is dead, and flags whether a reload from autoload should be offered when the party has more than one member.
ev: No candidate handles disbanding while monsters are present, the leader-dead exemption, or offering a reload for parties of more than one; the nearest, CityWindow.axaml.cs `listed.AskToLeave`, only refuses the leader's departure in town and has no monster check.

what: Reports whether a monster's blow sequence is ended by a character's state, treating any state other than Alive as ending it (an assumed rule, since the SRD does not specify which states do).
ev: The C++ function returns true when a character's state is anything other than Alive, and none of the eight candidates decides whether a monster's blow sequence ends based on a character's death state. The closest, Candidate 8 (DeathStates.Name), only maps a cause-of-death number to a display name, and Candidate 6 (RoundPaced) only notes that a fight ends when nothing is standing.

what: Returns true once a store restock buy-out has hit 100 empty draws, at which point the attempt gives up.
ev: The candidate's doc comment says the buying-out loop is the only one that gives up after 100 draws (MAINMOD.BAS:1671), which matches the C++ cap, but the method body shown is cut off before that loop, so it is only a partial match and the cap check itself is not visible.

what: If a companion's alignment is still Unaligned (encoded as 0), it adopts the alignment of its creature type, shifted by one to match the CompanionAlignment encoding.
ev: Settle gives an Unaligned companion its creature's alignment via Confinement.AlignmentOf(def), matching the C++ fill, but it also resolves the companion's table Ref and runs over every occupied slot rather than one companion.

what: Computes the R28 audit swing bound for a monster's base hits as the truncated value of Hits × 0.5 ÷ 2, plus one.
ev: The candidate computes the same `Int(… * .5) / 2) + 1` swing expression from the monster's hits, but multiplies it by a random draw (`rng.NextDouble()`) and applies it as a signed change to hits, whereas the C++ function returns the deterministic upper bound with no random draw.

what: Checks whether a new character can be created by testing, in order, that the name is non-empty, contains no forbidden bar character, that a sex and an alignment have been chosen, and that no save file already exists, returning the first failing reason or Ok.
ev: It runs the same checks in the same order (empty name, '|' in name, no sex, no alignment, existing save file) and stops at the first failure, though it reports each refusal through a message box and also contains the later points, password, and character-creation steps that the C++ function does not.

what: Blocks a character from using an item when they are paralysed, unless the use is a buffered one, which skips the paralysis check.
ev: OnSheetUse returns silently when `_ch.Paralysed`, which is the non-buffered half of the C++ predicate, but it has no `buffered` parameter, and the buffered exemption lives in UseSelectedItem, which is not among the candidates.

what: Moves the whole party to a new dungeon level (R64 ChangeLevel), setting the party's and every member's level and then settling the area on the new floor.
ev: The candidate changes the level and then calls SettleArea, as the C++ does, but it also clamps the level, keeps facing, logs first-to-level guild entries, and saves, and it never explicitly sets each member's DungeonLevel.

what: Clamps a backstab chance to the range 4 to 75 so that a backstab attempt's success chance never falls below 4% or above 75%.
ev: Its backstab branch clamps to the same 4..75 range as the C++ function, but it is only one step of a larger monster crit/backstab calculation, and the other candidates use a different floor (2) or no clamp at all.

what: Returns the dungeon level reached by taking the stairs up from the given level, which is one level up but never above town (level 0), so climbing from level 1 leads to town.
ev: UseStairs handles the level-1 stairs-up case by leaving to town (level 0), which matches the clamp, but the shown snippet is cut off before the general one-level-up branch, and no candidate computes the destination level as a standalone value.

what: Picks which party member receives a share of chest gold by mapping a random roll onto a party index, with ties rounded half-to-even and the result clamped to valid range.
ev: `RoundedIndex(rng, n)` computes `(int)Math.Round(rng.NextDouble() * n, MidpointRounding.ToEven)`, the same half-to-even mapping as the C++ with the caller passing `n = partySize - 1`; the C++ clamp and the `partySize <= 1` early return add no behavioural difference, since the draw is in [0,1) and n = 0 yields 0 either way.

what: Decides whether a companion leaves the party to go with a creature, in the game's R41 "Let Companion Go" rule: it runs the turn check, and either stops, joins the creature's live set, or silently releases the companion's slot.
ev: Candidate 1 follows the same branches as the C++ function: it returns early on refusal, drops the companion and joins the fight when it turns, releases it silently on a non-forced Kick Out with no turn, and leaves a forced companion in place when it does not turn, with only small differences such as a void return, a message from the check, and no explicit group-slot test.

what: Handles the typed "companions <member>" command by checking the argument, then replying with that party member's list of up to four companion slots showing each one's name, hits, and whether it is being carried.
ev: Show lists each filled companion slot with its name and hits, but it is a UI routine that writes to labels, not a typed "companions <member>" command that parses the member, returns a text reply, or marks carried companions.

what: Clamps a value to the range between a lower and upper bound, returning the lower bound if the value is below it, the upper bound if above it, and the value itself otherwise.
ev: The method clamps its input to 0-100 with `Math.Clamp(value, 0, 100)`, the same operation clampD performs, but only as one line inside a slider factory, and no candidate is a standalone clamp helper.

what: Marks a square as explored on the automap, except that fog-edge squares are skipped unless a wall bump has been recorded there.
ev: Candidate 4 skips fog-edge squares' walls and doors (`if (foggy) return;`), which is part of the C++ fog-edge gate, but no candidate sets an explored flag, and Candidate 4 has no wall-bump exception.

what: Computes fire damage after resistance, reducing the incoming damage by half the fire resistance percentage per point (fireResistance/2 percent) and rounding the result half to even.
ev: It computes `damage - damage * ((resistance / 2) * .01)` and rounds with `VbInt`, matching the C++ formula, but returns the raw damage early for resistance <= 0, which differs only for negative resistance inputs.

what: Returns the index of the highest set bit in a 128-bit value (or -1 if it is zero), a helper used in the game's currency-normalisation rounding logic.
ev: No candidate returns the index of the highest set bit of a 128-bit value; X87.Round only uses BigInteger.GetBitLength internally to pick a rounding shift, and it returns a rounded X87 value rather than a bit index.

what: Reports whether a special item type (stat modifiers, Potion of Youth, or Dragon's Blood) grants stat modifiers when used.
ev: It makes the same SpecialType 1/13/14 test as the C++ function, but it also returns false for an item one alignment step from the character, and it takes the character and slot as inputs where the C++ takes only the special type.

what: Computes a character's perception gear value as WIS plus a quarter of the WIS stat modifier, per the SRD rule R46.
ev: For ability 5 it returns the WIS term as natWis + (effWis - natWis) / 4.0, which equals WIS + StatMods[WIS] / 4 as the C++ does, but it is one element of a tuple, uses fractional division where the C++ truncates integers, and returns natural WIS alone when no gear lookup is supplied.

what: When a character is given an item, giveRead raises the item's identification level to whatever level the receiver can read from it, if that is higher than the current level, and announces the identification to the party.
ev: It matches giveRead's logic (skip if the level is All, raise the level only when the receiver's readable level is higher, then announce the identification), but it also calls the `filed` callback to file the item in the Library, which the C++ explicitly leaves undone as an unavailable API.

what: Reports whether a character has joined a given guild, returning false for an invalid guild index and otherwise reading the character's "joined" flag, which serves as the availability test for guild-related level content in the game's rules.
ev: That method computes the same "joined" predicate (a guild membership with Level > 0) as a local variable, but only as part of the join flow, not as a standalone availability check that returns false for an invalid guild index.

what: Maps a spell's class (Fire, Cold, Electrical, Mind, Damage, Kill, Banish, Dispel, Charm, Element, Protection) to the resistance category a target uses to defend against it, so the game's resistance rules apply correctly.
ev: No candidate maps a spell class to a target's resistance category; the closest, SpellEffect.ResistKind, maps a resistance spell's effect to the resistance it grants, and the monster-spell candidates pick resistance by the spell's ResistIndex rather than by class.

what: Rolls a percent chance (74%, per the R34 comment) that a rare quest entry gets rerolled.
ev: QuestMonster inlines the same rare-entry test (`Rnd * 100` compared against the Rarity field, which it says works out to about 75% in practice rather than the 74% in the C++ comment), but no candidate is a standalone 74% reroll helper like `rareQuestReroll`, and QuestItem has a similar inline rare test.

what: Rolls a single d100 check for a melee attack, returning true (the attack's hit gate passes) when the roll, Int(Rnd*100)+1, is below the given threshold percentage, per the SRD R18 hit rule.
ev: Fn0DEE contains the same gate, `(int)(rng.NextDouble() * 100) + 1 >= threshold` (a miss when at or above the threshold, which is the inverse of the C++ pass test), but it is buried inside the damage calculation and makes other random draws first, so it is not a standalone one-draw hit check.

what: Checks whether a typed swap slot is a valid target, accepting only slots above 1 (slot 1 being the hands, which never move) up to the pack's slot limit.
ev: The range rule matches (one-based slot must be above 1 and at most PackSize, with the same check applied to both slots), but SwapSlots also performs the swap and is not a standalone single-slot predicate like swapSlotInRange.

what: Charges the gold fee for removing a curse, taking it from the character's hand gold first and then from their bank, and refuses without changing anything if the combined total cannot cover the amount.
ev: Pay takes gold on hand first, then the bank, returns false and changes nothing when hand plus bank cannot cover the cost, matching chargeUncurseFee; it differs only in taking a long cost and rounding the bank's part to a whole number.

what: Computes a companion's caster level from their guild level as one sixth of it (rounded down), clamped to the range 1 to 255.
ev: The candidate computes the same companion caster level (floor of guild level / 6, clamped to 1..255) but only as the first step of a larger routine that also applies resistance, damage, and immunity checks, so it does only part of what the C++ function does.

what: Returns the natural log of the trap-disarm input m, clamped to a minimum of 2, as the logarithmic term in the game's trap disarm chance formula.
ev: No candidate returns `log(max(2, m))` as the trap-disarm term; Candidate 1 (`TrapReadout`) takes a log of a `Math.Max(1, ...)`-clamped guild level, but that feeds the trap-name confidence rather than the disarm chance, and the clamp is 1 instead of 2.

what: Renders the party's automap as a text grid centered on the party, showing explored squares, walls, secret doors, and doors around them, with the party marked and its facing shown as an arrow.
ev: The C++ renderAutomap builds a full text grid (walls, doors, '@', facing arrow, header line) for the party's surroundings, while the closest candidates are AutomapPics.Blit (bitmap blitting), AutomapOverlay.Inside (square pixel bounds), and PerceiveAhead.SquareAhead (single-square line-of-sight), none of which render a text automap.

what: Applies a Table E drain result from a monster's special attack: a pick of 1–5 lowers the matching ability stat by 1, and a pick of 6 lowers the character's maximum hits by the drain amount, with a note logged either way.
ev: The closest candidate, Raising.ApplyComplications, also lowers stats and max hits, but it applies a fixed five-point drop to all stats plus a divide-by-1.2 on max hits from raising, not a single Table E pick that drains one stat by 1 or max hits by a fixed loss from a monster's attack.

what: Decides whether a bank deposit is permitted by checking that the requested gold amount is positive and does not exceed the gold the player is carrying.
ev: Its deposit branch returns Beep when `amount > ch.GoldOnHand || amount <= 0`, which is the negation of the C++ predicate, but it sits inside the full keypress handler that also parses the text, moves the gold, and returns Ignored for zero before reaching that check.

what: When a chest's teleporter trap triggers, the opener is moved to a random square on the same level and the chest's trap is cleared.
ev: The candidate also moves only the opener to a destination square and sets its area from that square, but it takes the destination as an input instead of picking a random square, does not clear the chest's trap flags, and adds lost-position and party handling the C++ function lacks.

what: At a new guild level, it rolls whether the player gets a quest (or is let off), then assigns a defeat-monster or fetch-item target scaled to the quest tier.
ev: It clears the quest, rolls via Rules.RollQuest, handles let-off, and assigns a defeat target (QuestMonster) or fetch target (QuestItem) with the matching QuestType, matching assignQuest's flow; it differs in that it never stores the tier in a level field or sets an Active state, and its messages differ.

what: Produces the guild listing shown in the town menu, reporting each party member's active guild and, for each guild, either their level, experience still needed, and gold for next level, or the join cost if they haven't joined.
ev: The C++ function lists every party member's guilds (active guild, then per guild either level, XP needed, and gold for next level, or the join cost), but no candidate loops over party members or builds that multi-guild listing; the closest, Candidate 1 (NeedState.NextLevel), gives only a single-guild sentence about XP and gold owed, and Candidate 5 (ShowGuild) only opens the guild screen.

what: Computes the spell-casting formula J for a sorcerer from a base value, a power value, and a cost input C2, using a logarithmic scaling term plus a linear term, returning 0 when C2 is not positive.
ev: SpellHeal computes the same deterministic core as J (base + base·log(sl)/log(10) + int((sl/10)·(power−1))) but then subtracts a random mod2 and clamps to at least 1, whereas J returns that core directly and returns 0 for C2 ≤ 0.

what: Scans pack slots 1 to 39 for guild-issued crest items and refills any whose charges are below the crest table value, then announces the recharge to the player with the owner's trimmed name if the character is in the party.
ev: It scans pack slots 1 up to the pack limit, skips slot 0, refills guild-issued items whose charges are below the item's full charges, and builds the recharge message with the owner's name for party members, which matches the C++ loop and messages apart from returning a string instead of emitting through `ctx.say` and returning a count.

what: Runs the monster phase of a combat round, where each living monster in each group in turn rolls to hit a randomly chosen living party member, applies defense and damage, and handles that member's death mid-round.
ev: GroupAttacks is one group's turn against one already-chosen character, with the same monster swing and defense logic, but it adds breath, acid, spells and special effects, and does not do the per-monster random target pick, the per-monster loop over all groups, or the mid-round death handling that resolveMonsterPhase has.

what: Registers the "cast" dungeon-screen command, which lets a player cast a non-combat spell for a party member by typed name or id, and wires it to the dcastRun handler.
ev: The C++ function only registers a "cast" dungeon-screen command bound to dcastRun, and no candidate registers or parses a typed command; the closest, Mordor.App/DungeonWindow.axaml.cs DungeonWindow.CastSpellHere, performs the cast effect but not the command registration.

what: Returns whether the square the caster is standing on suppresses magic, which is true when the square has the ANTIMAGIC or EXTINGUISHER feature, so spells are refused there.
ev: It computes the same flag as the C++ accessor, `Floor.Has(X, Y, ANTIMAGIC) || Floor.Has(X, Y, EXTINGUISHER)` on the party's current square, but assigns it to `_combat.NoSpellsHere` instead of returning it.

what: Computes the base damage of a monster's breath attack by applying the real breath modifier, derived from the monster's and the character's guild levels, to the breath block damage roll.
ev: Raw takes the monster and target guild levels, makes one rng draw, and applies the breath share (range/4) and 0.7 scaling, which closely matches breathBaseDamage, but it does not call a realBreathModifier equivalent or a separate breath-block step, so the match is not confirmed as identical.

what: Computes the spell cost a guild charges for an engine-cast spell from the rated level, a scaling factor and the guild's rate, floored at the spell's initial level, and returns 0 when no guild has the spell.
ev: Both compute a guild-rate spell cost from the rated level, a u4 factor, and the rate, but Fn1485Price uses `rated * u4 * rate * 19 / (10 * SL)` with exact rational arithmetic and floors at the rated level, while the C++ uses `ratedLevel * u4 * rate / 10` floored at the spell level, and the candidate's Cost adds a multi-guild minimum the C++ does not have.

what: Reports how many guild halls exist in the game session, capped at the fixed guild count constant (kGuildCount).
ev: No candidate returns a count of guild halls capped at a constant; the closest, OriginalSaves.cs OriginalSaves.ReadGuildLog, returns the number of guild-log entries read from MDATA9, which is a different quantity.

what: Transfers gold from one character's exchange allowance to another (R23), rejecting zero-amount and over-limit transfers with a "Too Much!" message, and otherwise moving the gold between wallets.
ev: It matches the C++ steps (zero is a no-op, the "Too Much!" check uses the dungeon-aware available amount, then gold moves from one character to the other, with negatives allowed), differing only in returning a string instead of an outcome enum and in its bank-shortfall and overflow handling.

what: Handles the player's "seer yes" or "seer no" reply to a pending offer, charging the fee and then producing the seer's location report for the named party member, or cancelling the offer.
ev: LocatePerson charges `Seer.LocateCharacterFee` for the chosen character, then reports their location through `Seer.LocateCharacter`, which matches the C++ fee-then-report flow, though it uses a confirm dialog instead of the text "seer yes/no" reply and returns silently on decline instead of saying "Cancelled."

what: Handles the Exit-to-Main-Menu request by refusing with a beep if monsters are in the area and the party leader is alive, otherwise showing the exit confirmation prompt.
ev: The candidate uses the same gate as the C++ function (refuse with a beep and "Cannot exit while monsters are in the area!" when monsters are present and the character is alive, otherwise show "Exit to Main Menu?"), but it also performs the confirmed exit, which the C++ function leaves to its caller.

what: Computes the spell Protection value a guild gets on recompute as half its guild Level, rounded down, plus 1 (rule R29).
ev: Recompute sets `c.Protection = c.Guild.Level / 2 + 1`, the same formula as the C++ function (integer division floors non-negative values), but it is embedded in the larger recompute routine rather than standing alone; the other candidates compute Protection from caster spell level or do unrelated work.

what: Computes the dungeon level the encounter window targets, adding one floor when the STUD condition applies, per the game's encounter rules.
ev: Both return the level plus one when the stud condition holds and the level unchanged otherwise, with the same inputs and outcome.

what: Computes the respawn delay in milliseconds for a dungeon level, starting from a level-based base time and subtracting 5 seconds per empty area below the header count (the penalty is not clamped, so a negative tally adds time), with a minimum floor of 120 seconds.
ev: Both compute `base(level) - 5 s × (headerAreas - tally)` with no clamp on the penalty and a 120-second floor, though the candidate takes headerAreas and tally separately where the C++ takes their difference, and its `level / 2.0` is floating-point while the C++ base is unseen.

what: Applies the R29 rotator trap check: if the character's ability-5 chance fails to beat a random roll scaled by dungeon level, the character becomes lost, with position and facing unknown.
ev: It makes the same R29 check (save if the perception chance is at least `rng * 70 + dungeonLevel * 2`, otherwise set LostPosition and LostFacing and leave the floor flag alone), differing only in that it derives the chance from the character and returns a bool instead of emitting the message.

what: Checks whether a guessed location and dungeon level are close enough to the actual rescue target (within the finder range on both axes and on the same level) to count as a successful find in the Mordor rescue mechanic.
ev: It takes the same six inputs and returns `Math.Abs(guessX - x) < 8 && Math.Abs(guessY - y) < 8 && guessLevel == level`, which matches the C++ check against `kRescueFinderRange` (assuming that constant is 8, as the C# doc comment states).

what: Checks whether any monster group still has living members, returning true while the encounter continues and false once none remain so the combat round ends.
ev: No candidate is a standalone "any monster alive" check, but RoundPaced performs the same test inline (`!Monsters.Any(m => m.Alive)`) to stop the round, which is the behaviour of the C++ `roundGuard`.

what: On each four-second tick, rolls d100 against the paralysis wear-off chance for a held character and, if the roll exceeds it, ends the paralysis.
ev: Both compute the paralysis wear-off chance, roll `Int(Rnd*100)+1` and end the paralysis when the roll exceeds it, but ParalysisPasses returns a bool instead of calling unparalyse, and it adds a no-monsters-present shortcut that the C++ leaves to its caller.
